generated_text: Honestly, Chloe, this little one has me completely worn out today. He decided 3am was the perfect time for a party. A very vocal party. Oh, you poor thing, Sarah. Little Leo's definitely got a set of lungs, doesn’t he? My niece, Maisie, was the same. Screamed the house down. Are you managing alright though? Don’t overdo it. I’m managing. Just… existing, really. Mark’s been a godsend, bless him. He took over for a couple of hours this morning, which allowed me to actually have a lukewarm cup of tea and a biscuit! Small victories, eh? How's everything going with you? Still looking at that pottery course? Yeah, actually signed up! Starts next month. A little apprehensive, I'm not exactly known for my artistic abilities, but it’s something to do, something creative. And Mrs. Davies at the community centre seems lovely. Speaking of creative, are you still doing much proofreading work? Things been busy? It's a bit up and down. Some weeks are manic, others… not so much. I had a really long project for a textbook publisher just finished, thankfully. Paid well, though, so I can breathe a bit. Thinking of having a bit of a night out to celebrate. Need a proper catch-up with the girls. Fancy joining me? Absolutely! It's been ages since we properly let our hair down. What were you thinking? The usual haunt, The Red Lion? Yeah, probably. Or maybe somewhere a bit different? I saw that new cocktail bar opened on Gas Street, "The Velvet Curtain." Sounds a bit posh, but could be fun. Ooh, sounds good! Let me check with Liam, see what he’s up for. He's been moaning about being stuck in the house with Maisie. She's started a phase of wanting to wear his slippers everywhere. Everywhere. Oh, kids! They’re something else, aren't they? Leo’s just started trying to climb out of his bouncy chair. I swear, he’s got springs in his feet. We need to get him those baby gates fitted. Mark keeps putting it off. Tell me about it! Liam’s threatened to build one out of cardboard if he doesn’t get around to it soon. Have you thought about your Mum’s birthday yet? It's coming up pretty quickly. Oh goodness, you're right! I've completely forgotten!

Honestly, Liam, you wouldn’t believe the state of the campsite toilets in rural France. Like, seriously, I’ve seen cleaner public conveniences back home in Sunderland. And that’s saying something! Oh, I can imagine. You always find the… unique experiences, don’t you, Maisie? Reminds me of that time we went camping in the Lake District and it rained for three solid days. Aye, but this was different! This was… organised chaos. I’m talking plastic chairs piled near the bins, someone’s dirty laundry hanging on a bush, and a general aroma I’m trying very hard to forget. Still, the croissants were brilliant. Can’t fault the French on their pastries, can ya? True. Priorities. I did find the French bureaucracy a bit… overwhelming, to be honest. Trying to get a vignette for the Swiss motorway was an absolute nightmare. All that paperwork! I swear, the woman at the desk looked like she’d been stamping forms for centuries. Oh, Switzerland! We had a right laugh there. Remember that ridiculously oversized cuckoo clock we saw? Seriously, it was huge! And the chocolate… oh, the chocolate. I’m already regretting not buying more. I’ve got a dodgy tummy, practically living on peppermint tea since we got back. Too much Lindt, apparently. You and your sweet tooth. I was more impressed with the efficiency of the public transport. Every train ran exactly on time. Even in the tiny villages. It was almost unsettling. Makes you wonder what we're doing wrong over here. It does, doesn’t it? We spent ages trying to figure out the tram system in Strasbourg. Keep getting on the wrong one and ending up completely lost. Ended up having a rather brilliant impromptu picnic by the canals though, so it weren't all bad. Found this little boulangerie that did the most amazing tartes flambées. Tartes flambées! See, that's the thing – every country has its own unique culinary delights. We should’ve spent more time focusing on the food and less time wrestling with parking meters. Remember that Parisian parking garage where we spent a good half hour circling, trying to find a free space? Don't remind me! The Parisian drivers! Absolute madness. Honking and weaving, and no respect for pedestrians whatsoever. I nearly got flattened twice. It was like a demolition derby, but with Renaults. They do have a certain… enthusiasm for driving, that’s for sure.

Right, this Monopoly game has officially broken me. I’ve landed on Mayfair for the third time, and honestly, I think I’m going to have to sell my kidneys to pay rent to Leo. You always lose, Mummy! It’s SO much fun! It's  my  fun, actually. I'm winning! I have Baltic Avenue  and  Mediterranean Avenue! Yes, darling, you do. And you’ve charged me £20 for landing on Mediterranean this time. I'm pretty sure that's against the rules. No, it’s not! It says right there! Rent goes up if you have a whole color! Right, fine. You’re absolutely correct. But seriously, I’m almost bankrupt. We need a saving grace. A distraction. A… desert! Desert? Like sand? With camels? No, darling! Dessert! Sweet things! Cake, ice cream, fruit salad…deliciousness! What kind of dessert are we having? Chocolate cake! With sprinkles! Lots and lots of sprinkles! Puddings! With custard! And strawberry sauce! Okay, okay, ambition is good. But we're a bit short on funds at the moment. Remember, I'm practically destitute thanks to Little Monopoly Moguls over here. But I'm  saving  you! If I get all the properties, I can build houses and hotels and… and then  you  have to pay  me  more! It's strategy, Mummy! It's ruthless, darling. But I admit, a strategic victory. Perhaps we compromise and I'll make crumble? That's pretty easy and doesn’t require a massive grocery shop. Crumble is boring! It’s just… apples and sugar! It’s apples, sugar, flour, butter, and a whole lot of love, thank you very much. And it's far cheaper than a multi-layered chocolate cake with industrial quantities of sprinkles. Besides, we can have ice cream with it! Ice cream  with  crumble… okay. But can I still win Monopoly? You already  have  won Monopoly, darling. You've utterly decimated me. Let's just say, in this household, you're the financial guru. Now, help me find the flour, will you? I'll find the sprinkles! And the cream! And maybe a little bit of chocolate sauce… just in case we decide to  add  chocolate sauce to the crumble. You’re incorrigible. Right then, crumble it is. But after this game, we are clearing out the Monopoly money and donating to charity. I can’t handle another round. My blood pressure can’t take it.

Honestly, Liam, this whole thing is just...mad. Absolutely mad. I’ve been wrestling with this data all day, and it’s just screaming at me. What is? You know I hate it when you start with the “screaming data.” It gives me the willies. Is it the Brexit impact report again? You looked proper stressed at dinner last night. It's related, aye. It’s the sentiment analysis on the social media responses to the supplementary trade deal. People are  furious . Like, actual, genuine fury. I’m flagging tonnes of it as ‘highly negative’ but it feels… different than the usual grumbling. It’s angrier, more… pointed. And it's not even just about the trade deal itself. It’s all linked to this thing about the fishing quotas. Fishing quotas? Right, I vaguely remember reading something about that. Something about promises made and not kept, wasn't it? Political muck, as usual. Aye, but it's not just muck when it's reflected in a tidal wave of angry tweets and Facebook posts! The algorithm is picking up this really aggressive language. I’ve had to manually classify hundreds of comments. It's exhausting, Liam. I'm worried it might escalate. Escalating how? Riots in Grimsby? Come on, Elara. Don’t be dramatic. Don't be dismissive. It’s not just Grimsby, it’s all the coastal communities. And it's not just about the fishing, it's about feeling betrayed by the government. It’s about feeling like nobody listens to them. And my job is to identify that sentiment, to categorize it, and frankly, it’s proper unsettling. I flagged one thread that specifically mentioned targeting MP offices. Okay, that  is  concerning. Did you report that one directly to the authorities? I did, of course. But it just feels… like a drop in the ocean. The sheer volume of angry voices is overwhelming. And the company's directive is to simply flag and categorize, not intervene. It's like I'm just documenting a potential disaster. So, you’re feeling helpless. I get it. It’s frustrating to see all this negativity and feel like you can’t actually  do  anything about it. Happens in engineering too, you know. Trying to design a solution that just feels like a stopgap. Aye, I suppose. It's just... different when it's human emotion, innit? Numbers and percentages are one thing, but reading all that raw anger… it affected me today.

Honestly, Maureen, this rain. Proper miserable it is. Been comin' down for days, hasn’t it? Makes you want to just pull the curtains and stay put. It is a bit gloomy, David. But look at it this way, the garden's having a right good soaking. Everything will be blooming lovely in a few weeks. Just needs to stop for longer than five minutes, that's all. Arthur's bringing the lemon drizzle cake over this afternoon, remember? Lemon drizzle? Now you're talkin'. Though I preferred it when Maureen used to make it. She always put a bit more lemon in. Arthur's is a bit… tame, I reckon. Arthur’s cake is alright, Arthur’s cake is alright. Don't be sniffin' at it, Arthur puts a lot of effort in. Besides, it’s the company, innit? A bit of a sit-down and a natter’s good for the soul. Been a long week, even for someone retired like me. Tryin' to sort out these blasted bills… the council tax keeps climbin', you know. Don’t you start complaining about the council tax, David. We all have to pay it. And Arthur offered to help you with those forms, didn't he? You just keep sayin' you’ll get around to it. Honestly, you’re like a man made of stone sometimes. I appreciate the offer, Maureen, I do. Just find it a bit… overwhelming, to be honest. All these forms and online portals. Used to be a simple letter, you know, a bit of paper and a stamp. Now it's all passwords and verification codes. Drives a man mad, it does. Remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road? She couldn't work a television remote. Ended up tryin' to wind it up like an old gramophone. Oh, Arthur! You are terrible. David, drink your tea. It’ll calm your nerves. And please, try to be a little bit more open to Arthur’s help. He worries about you. I know, I know. Just feels like… losin' a bit of control, I suppose. Used to be project manager, used to have teams at my beck and call, all sorts of responsibility. Now it’s just me and a pile of bills. Don't be like that, David. You've earned your rest. And you're not alone. We're all here. It’s not like you’re managing the A14 anymore, is it?

Honestly, Anon, your place is lovely. So much brighter than I remember! Birmingham’s really changed, hasn’t it? And you’ve clearly been busy! How's Honest Skincare going? Last time we spoke, you were just starting to get things off the ground. It  is  going well, actually! Really well! It’s been a whirlwind, to be honest. This little business has completely taken over my life, but in a good way, mostly! See these? These are our new ‘Summer Radiance’ sets. SPF, hydrating serum, gentle cleanser... the whole shebang. They look gorgeous! The packaging is so clean and modern. Much more sophisticated than those initial samples you showed me. Did you finally get a proper website sorted? Yes! That was the biggest hurdle, wasn't it? I'd been putting it off ages. Got a lovely girl from Uni to help me - Sarah. She did a brilliant job, really. Still tweaking it, of course. Trying to optimize for SEO, you know? So people  actually  find it when they Google “natural skincare Birmingham.” It's a minefield! Tell me about it! I used to teach a module on digital marketing, and it’s constantly evolving. What platform are you using for selling? Etsy still, or have you branched out? Etsy’s still bringing in a decent amount, but I’m really pushing towards my own website. It’s just… the shipping! Calculating the postage is driving me mad. I spent  hours  the other day trying to figure out dimensional weight for a larger order going to Scotland. Honestly, it’s enough to make you tear your hair out. Oh, dimensional weight! Don’t even get me started. It’s so arbitrary! You could have three tiny boxes, and because they’re oddly shaped, suddenly the cost is astronomical. How much are you charging for international shipping? That's another nightmare! I'm quoted about £20 to send a single set to France! People just say 'too expensive' instantly. I’m thinking of having a tiered system, maybe. Free over a certain amount… but it's so tricky to calculate a fair price. My mum keeps saying I should just add the postage cost to the product price. That’s an option, certainly. But it'll make you look more expensive than your competitors. Maybe offer a flat rate for certain zones? And really emphasize the  quality  of your ingredients and the ethical sourcing.

Oh, that’s lovely, David. Just lovely. You always make a proper cuppa. Better than that instant stuff I sometimes resort to, I’m afraid. Though, really, it shouldn't come to that, should it? It’s no trouble, Margaret. You’re family. And after that dreadful news about inflation… well, a good cup of tea is sometimes the only comfort. Did you see that report on the BBC this morning? Absolutely shocking. I did. I did. Utterly dreadful, isn’t it? Makes one wonder how ordinary people are supposed to manage. You, with your pension and savings from teaching, you’ll be alright, of course. But for those just scraping by… it's just cruel. It reminds me of the eighties, doesn't it? Though at least then, we had a sense of… possibility, even amidst the hardship. This feels more… bleak. It does, doesn’t it? A sense of stagnation, really. Younger generations are facing a challenge we never imagined. Remember when we were kids? We could get a house with a reasonable salary. A graduate teacher could buy a flat! Now…? It’s a pipedream. A pipedream indeed. And I’ve been thinking a lot lately about… well, about my situation. You know, being… perpetually unemployed, after teaching. It feels even more… precarious now. I mean, I’m on benefits, of course. But what if they’re cut? What if things get even worse? I know I should have done more, planned better. But it’s hard, David, it's hard when you have no income. Don’t beat yourself up about it, Margaret. You did a wonderful job teaching for all those years. You gave so much to those children. And you’ve always been incredibly generous, despite not having much yourself. Don't think for one moment that your value is tied to a job. You are… you are my sister, and that’s worth more than any salary. You always were a good talker, weren’t you? Always knew the right thing to say. I remember when you were applying for that headship at Elmhurst. You were so nervous! I kept telling you you were perfect for it, but you were convinced you’d fail. Oh, I was a wreck! I remember pacing the floor all night before the interview. Your unwavering belief in me got me through it, you know. You always saw the best in people, Margaret.

Right then, everyone! Help yourselves. I’ve gone a bit mad with the Christmas baking, haven’t I? Mince pies, gingerbread, a ridiculously large fruitcake… anything you fancy. It's freezing out there, isn't it? The heating’s on full blast, but it still feels like January. You absolutely have! But no complaints from me. That fruitcake looks incredible. Newcastle's not quite as bad as I thought - actually, well, it  is  pretty cold, but not as brutal as a Yorkshire winter. Glad to be out of that! This is a much nicer way to spend a Saturday. So, how's the research going, Eleanor? Still wrestling with those micro-organisms? Absolutely mental, actually. This spread is already making me feel much calmer, though. Research is... intense. I'm basically trying to convince people that ancient fungal communities could revolutionise sustainable building materials. It’s niche, to say the least! And yes, the southwest is experiencing some nasty winds today. Practically gale force. My flat's rattling! Clive’s trying to fix the draughty window again. Bless him. Sustainable building materials, eh? That’s a big ask. Speaking of materials, I've been wrestling with a particularly stubborn piece of oak for a commission. Making a rocking horse, you see. Tiny details. It's a right pain, but when it’s finished, it'll be lovely. Wales is… well, Wales is doing its own thing weather-wise. Miserably damp, as usual. My workshop's perpetually steamy. I’m thinking about investing in a dehumidifier. A dehumidifier! You’ll have to build one yourself, won't you? Seriously though, Rhys, that sounds lovely. Rocking horses are classic. It reminds me of my grandfather. He always grew the most amazing mulberries. Massive, juicy things. We'd practically live on them in the summer. I miss that. Mulberries! I haven’t had a good mulberry in ages. We had a tree in the garden when I was a kid, but it got chopped down to make way for a shed. Classic story of progress wiping out something beautiful, isn't it? Actually, on the subject of progress… have you guys been thinking about retirement at all? It feels ridiculous even saying it, but I hit 37 last month. Makes you think. Retirement? Rhys is probably already planning his escape to a remote craft village somewhere! I’m clinging on to my PhD for dear life, let alone thinking about hanging up my lab coat.

Honestly, Mum, this roast is incredible. You really outdid yourself. Though… Where’s the good cutlery? This stuff is… serviceable, but not quite the dinner set. You and your cutlery, Elodie. It's dinner at your parents' house, not a state banquet. Use whatever's there. Besides, Dad probably just grabbed whatever was closest. Don’t you start, lad. Elodie’s got a point. That’s just our everyday service. I keep the good silver in the sideboard for ‘special occasions.’ And a dinner with yer grandkids  is  a special occasion, I reckon! Always had an eye for detail, that one. Remember when she was little and insisted on using a pink napkin, even if it clashed with the tablecloth? Pink? She was a little madam, that one. Always had to have things  just  so. I recall she had this phase where she only ate food cut into triangles. Oh, Dad, don't remind me! I was a nightmare. I think it was a control thing. I’ve always liked things… organised, I suppose. It helps me manage the chaos at work. Speaking of, how are you doing, Dad? Truly? You seem… quieter than usual. Just a bit tired, love. The telly’s been showing all these ads for stairlifts. Makes you think, doesn't it? About getting old. Stairlifts! Rubbish! Used to climb mountains, I did. Before my knees gave out, o’ course. Mountains! Now look at me, easing myself into a chair like a doddering old fool. Grandad, you're not a fool. You’re a legend! Remember that story you told me about outsmarting the poachers in the Peak District? Aye, that was a good one. Had to be clever, you see. They weren't expecting an old man with a walking stick to know the hills so well. They were after the grouse, but I was after a bit of mischief! He was always one for a bit of mischief, our Arthur. Though, it usually involved pinching apples from Mr. Henderson’s orchard. Memories. So, Mum, about the cutlery... is there any chance we could use the good stuff? It would just make the evening feel a little more… celebratory. We rarely all get together like this. Alright, alright. Don’t fret. I'll fetch it. Just you wait there. Honestly, the way you young'uns carry on. It's not the end of the world if you have a fork with tines that aren't perfectly silvered.

Honestly, this chicken's lovely. You really nailed the marinade, didn't you, love? Feels good to actually sit down and eat without a little… tornado whizzing around. Tornado? Was I a tornado, Mummy? I was spinning! I was a dancing fairy! You were, sweetheart, you were. A very active dancing fairy. A slightly chaotic one, perhaps. But a dancing fairy nonetheless. How was your painting? Did you finish your sparkly unicorn? Almost! I need more glitter. Lots more glitter. And maybe some rainbow sprinkles? Rainbow sprinkles, hmm? We’ll see about that. Right, now, let's talk about grown-up things for a moment. Work's been… well, work. Absolute madness, as usual. Mr. Henderson's decided he needs a full re-evaluation of the entire marketing strategy. Mid-quarter! Can you believe it? Is that bad, Mummy? Does it mean you have to work more? It means more overtime, yes. But it’s alright, darling. We’ll still get away to the slopes, I promise. It’s practically booked, anyway. Flight confirmations came through today. Skiing! I’m going to wear my new hat! The pink one with the pom-pom! Of course you are! And Daddy will be showing off his snowboarding skills, eh? I keep telling him he needs to practice more than just the one run he squeezes in before work. Daddy falls down sometimes! Sometimes he does. But he always gets back up, doesn't he? That's the important thing. Right, so, Austria. We need to double-check the ski lessons for you, make sure they’re still scheduled. I think they’re for the mornings, so you can spend the afternoons playing in the snow. Can I build a snowman? A really, really big one! Bigger than Daddy! Absolutely. You can build the biggest snowman Austria has ever seen. I'll pack your carrot nose and those silly button eyes. And maybe that little scarf you like. Have you been practicing your snow angel making? Yes! I make amazing snow angels! Better than Grandma! Higher praise I couldn’t possibly receive! This trip is going to be wonderful, isn't it? A bit of sunshine, fresh air, snow… We  deserve  a break. It's been a hectic few months. Henderson’s relentless demands have been wearing me down. I swear, if he asks for another presentation before Christmas, I might… What's 'relentless', Mummy?

Honestly, Maths is just…  ugh . Mr. Davies just keeps piling it on. We’ve done fractions, algebra, percentages… I feel like my brain’s going to melt. Tell me about it. I spent, like, an hour last night just trying to understand quadratic equations. Quadratic  what  now? It sounds like something out of a sci-fi film. Exactly! And then he expects you to be able to solve them in twenty minutes! It’s ridiculous. I’m seriously considering giving up on being a vet. You need Maths for that, don’t you? Yeah, loads. But don’t give up completely yet! Maybe you just need to find a different way to learn it. Did you look at that Khan Academy website Miss Patel recommended? A bit. It’s okay, I guess, but it’s still… Maths. It's not exactly thrilling stuff, is it? At least English is a bit more engaging. I'm really enjoying 'To Kill a Mockingbird'. Oh, yeah! That’s a good one. I’m struggling a bit with the analysis though. Understanding the symbolism and all that. I feel like I’m missing something. I think it's about finding the subtle connections. Like, Atticus’s quiet strength represents… well, it represents a lot, actually! Have you thought about asking Mrs. Davies for some extra help after school? She’s really good at explaining things, even when it's a bit complicated. I might. I’m just a bit embarrassed, you know? Asking for help feels a bit… silly. Don't be! Everyone needs help sometimes. Even Mr. Davies probably needed help when  he  was learning quadratic equations! True. Anyway, what about Spanish? Remember we were talking about studying abroad? I was reading an article about opportunities in Madrid. They have amazing music scenes there. Oh my gosh, yeah! Imagine, living in Spain and being able to order tapas without looking completely lost! That’s the dream, innit? I’m thinking about Valencia, though. It seems a bit more chilled out than Madrid. It does, doesn't it? Still, Madrid’s got so much history. And the football, obviously. What level are you at with your Spanish now? I'm still struggling with the subjunctive. It's so confusing! The subjunctive is a nightmare. But Señora Rodriguez said if we keep practicing, it'll eventually click. I think she’s trying to get us to do a little presentation on Spanish cuisine next month.

Cor, this Cambridge air is a bit chilly, even indoors. Much prefer a good, proper London fog, meself. Though, I must say, ANON’s put on a lovely spread. Everything smells ever so nice. So, films, was it? You were sayin’ something, love? Yeah, Nan. I was just showing Mum and you the trailer for 'Poor Things'. Have you heard of it? It looks…wild. 'Poor Things'? Doesn’t ring a bell, dear. Sounds a bit morbid, doesn’t it? I prefer a nice bit of escapism, I do. Something with a handsome bloke and a happy ending. A good musical, perhaps. Remember 'Singin' in the Rain'? Now  that  was a film. Nan, that's a classic, absolutely. But this is…different. It's based on a book by Alasdair Gray - a Scottish writer. It’s about a young woman brought back to life by a scientist, and she goes on this incredibly strange and liberating journey. Emma Stone is playing her. Emma Stone, you say? Oh, she’s ever so pretty, isn’t she? That ‘La La Land’ was a lovely film. Though a bit too modern for me, all that jazzy music and the…the dancing on rooftops. Give me Fred Astaire any day. But scientist, eh? Bringing people back to life? Sounds a bit like Frankenstein, doesn’t it? Werewolves and mad scientists – not really my cup of tea. It's more…philosophical than scary. It’s exploring themes of autonomy and societal expectations. It's really visually stunning, too. The costumes and sets are completely bonkers - Victorian but with a twist. I think you might actually like it, Nan, despite the weirdness. Bonkers, you say? Well, I don’t want to be seein’ nothin' too scandalous, mind. I’ve got my reputation to uphold, even in Cambridge! Though…I did enjoy that 'Downton Abbey' series. That had a bit of scandal in it, didn't it? All those affairs and whatnot. This isn't quite Downton Abbey, Nan. It’s…more Brechtian in its style, I think. Don’t worry, it’s not all corsets and yearning glances. There's a lot of wit and really clever storytelling. Brechtian? Heavens to Betsy, what's that then? Is that some newfangled American thing? Sounds awfully complicated. No, it's a theatrical style, from a German playwright, Bertolt Brecht. It's… hard to explain, really. It breaks the fourth wall, makes you think about the play itself, rather than just getting lost in the story.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic getting in was  awful . Took me nearly an hour and a half from Hitchin. I swear, the M6 is just a parking lot these days. Oh, you’re telling me! You should try navigating Birmingham rush hour. It’s a beast. Glad you made it though, love. Needed a good catch-up. How’s the teaching going? Still battling teenage apathy? You have no idea! One boy spent the entire lesson drawing dinosaurs. Dinosaurs! It’s Shakespeare week. I tried to explain iambic pentameter, got blank stares. You know, sometimes I wonder if I’m making any difference at all. Don't you start with that now. You're a brilliant teacher, Elara. Remember how much Mrs. Davies used to rave about you when you were little? You always had a way with explaining things. Besides, you’re inspiring those kids. Even if they don't  show  it yet. Thanks, Mum. I needed to hear that. It's just...a lot. And then there’s the cost of everything. I’m thinking about trying to get some extra tutoring gigs on the side, just to ease the pressure a bit. Don’t overdo it, love. You'll burn yourself out. Have you thought about what David says about that online tutoring platform? The one he uses for his mate’s business? Apparently, you can set your hours and charges. Might be less stressful than chasing individual clients. I've looked at it, yeah. It seems alright, but there’s something about dealing directly with students that I prefer. And David keeps going on about the legal contract stuff - apparently, you need to be  really  careful. Well, that's where I might be able to poke my nose in a bit, aren’t I? Been dealing with contracts and affidavits for near forty years at the court. It's all very straightforward, really. Just make sure they cover liability and payment terms clearly. Don't be afraid to ask for changes. That’s brilliant, Mum! You’re a lifesaver! Honestly, I feel slightly intimidated by all the legal jargon. It's not exactly something they cover on the PGCE, is it? No, dear, it isn't. They focus on the Chaucer and the Carol Ann Duffy. Speaking of, did you see they’re showing that new football documentary on the Beeb next week? The one about Villa’s season?

Honestly, this air is just  divine  after being cooped up in that stuffy lecture hall all day. I think I've officially inhaled enough dust to last me a lifetime. You and history. It’s a dangerous combination, apparently. Did you manage to wrangle those essays from the students? They were looking particularly… resistant this week. Resistant is putting it mildly. It was like pulling teeth. Three of them claimed they were struggling to access the library archives – which is a flat-out lie, they're readily available online. I swear, sometimes I think I’m teaching them the art of creative procrastination. Tell me about it. My philosophy students are convinced existential dread is a valid reason for late submissions. I almost felt a pang of sympathy. Almost. Did you confirm with Mei about the translation project? I know you were looking at sending her the draft. Yes, I emailed her this afternoon. She said she could have a first pass done by Friday. Which is brilliant, really. Her English is impeccable, and she understands the nuances of the material so much better than some of the Western "experts" we've employed before. It’s a relief. Though it does mean I need to finish going through it properly by Wednesday, doesn’t it? Urgent. Right. Procrastination avoidance, then. We’re both masters of it, ironically. Speaking of which, we're almost out of tea. Do you want to pop into that little shop on the corner tomorrow? The one with the jasmine pearls? I know you adore those. Oh, that would be lovely. Yes, definitely. And maybe some of those dried plums, too? The ones that are chewy and sweet? I’ve been craving them. It feels so decadent, doesn't it? Buying little treats like that. After months of eating instant noodles in student digs, suddenly we're indulging in gourmet dried fruit. Progress, I suppose. Though I’m still slightly suspicious of the sheer quantity of noodles you consumed during your PhD. Remember that time you claimed you were “experimenting with different sodium levels for academic research”? Don’t remind me! My poor digestive system! It was a necessary sacrifice for the sake of knowledge. Seriously though, the shop is a lifesaver. I’m running so low on everything. I need to restock the spices too. That Sichuan peppercorn I got last month... it's nearly gone.

Right, so, update. Sarah’s confirmed she can do Saturday afternoon for the kids. Four till six. That gives me just enough time to pop over to Chloe’s for a catch-up. Saturday! Can I wear my sparkly shoes, Mummy? For Sarah? Of course, sweetheart! Your sparkly shoes are always wonderful. Just promise you’ll be careful not to trip over them. Can we build a giant castle for Sarah, Mummy? A really, really big one! Absolutely, darling. A giant castle it is. We can all work on it together before Sarah comes. That sounds brilliant. Right, now, Chloe's offered to finally attempt a new dinner recipe – apparently, she’s trying a butternut squash risotto. Sounds ambitious. Risotto? Is that like pasta? A bit like pasta, love. But with rice. And cheese! We'll definitely have to try some when I get back. And hopefully, it won't taste like glue, knowing Chloe! Can we have chocolate cake with it? Please? Let’s not get ahead of ourselves, little man. Risotto first. Then we'll see. Maybe. I was thinking about baking cookies earlier - those ginger ones you both love. Ooh, yes! With the sparkly sugar! Exactly. Now, I have a final thing on my list. I was thinking, Leo, you've got that rather… voluminous haircut. Are you feeling brave enough for a trim? Nope! I’m a lion! Lions have big hair! You  are  a lion, aren’t you? Alright, alright, a lion it is. But we might need to tame it slightly before the photoshoot next week. Remember? The family one with Auntie Emily? I like the photoshoot! Will I get to wear my princess dress? You absolutely will, my princess. You’ll look stunning. And maybe we can get a picture of you and your little lion brother together. Rawr! Very fierce, very fierce indeed. Now, I've been trying to convince myself to read "Little Women" again. It’s been ages, and it always feels so comforting. But finding the time... Can I listen to you read it, Mummy? Just a little bit? Of course, pumpkin. We can snuggle up on the sofa after dinner and I’ll read you a chapter. It’s a lovely story about sisters. Can I build the castle while you read? You absolutely can. A castle for the March sisters, perhaps? They need somewhere grand to live. Right, I need to finish this crumble topping.

Honestly, this uni food is getting on my nerves. Another day, another beige lunch option. Like, is there a single vibrant colour in this whole place? Tell me about it! My mum would absolutely  die  if she saw this. She's always going on about proper, fresh ingredients. This lettuce looks like it’s seen better decades. Though, to be fair, this dressing’s alright. It’s got a bit of a kick. You wanna try? Nah, I’m good. I’m clinging to this latte for dear life. It’s the only thing keeping me going after that lecture on the French Revolution. So much bloodshed! Seriously, all I learned was that Marie Antoinette probably didn't actually say "Let them eat cake." You’re pulling my leg, right? That's such a myth! My history teacher spent ages debunking that. Still, French Revolution – horrifying, innit? Fancy needing a holiday just  thinking  about it. So, are you going out Friday night? Liam’s organising something, apparently. Liam? Ugh, Liam’s "organised" events usually involve questionable music and even more questionable decisions. I don’t know… I was thinking of just heading back to South London and chilling with my cousins. They’ve got that new rooftop bar, apparently. Actual views, not just concrete. A rooftop bar? Ooh, sounds a lot better than Liam's usual dimly lit basement. See, that’s the thing, isn’t it? Kingston's alright, but it's missing that real vibe. It's all a bit… suburban. Exactly! It needs a bit of proper London energy. Though, I’m not saying Kingston’s  completely  hopeless. The riverside walk is pretty nice, especially when the sun’s out. And that little coffee shop near the train station does a decent flat white. True, true. And the theatre’s surprisingly good. Remember that Shakespeare play we saw last year? That was brilliant. But yeah, you’re right. It needs a shake-up. Speaking of shakes, did you try that new smoothie place? ‘Green Goddess’ or something? I saw it. It looked aggressively green. Like, if a smoothie could be radioactive, that’d be it. I'll stick to my latte, thanks. What about your flat? How's the decorating going? Last time you said you were trying to hang up those fairy lights, right? Don't even  mention  those fairy lights! I spent a good two hours trying to get them up yesterday.

Right, so, Germany, eh, Finn? You’re actually going back? Proper jealous, I am. Sunderland doesn’t exactly scream ‘Christmas markets’ does it? More like… grey skies and the smell of fish and chips, if you’re bein’ honest. It’s brilliant, honestly. Mum's side of the family are all there. It’s a proper tradition now, going back every other year. This year's the big one though, apparently they're unveiling a new Christmas light display in my grandfather’s village. It’s supposed to be massive. A new light display? Sounds… intense. My parents are putting up a string of fairy lights this year. Groundbreaking stuff. Fairy lights is luxury, isn't it? Back home, your 'lights' were usually someone's dodgy Christmas tree stuck in their window with a single, flickering bulb. Adds to the charm, mind. What are you up to, Liam? Still wrestling with structural integrity and whatnot? Pretty much. This project in London is a nightmare. The client wants a cantilevered structure that defies the laws of physics, apparently. It's...challenging, to say the least. And the budget is tighter than a drum. At least you lot can relax. Holidays and mulled wine - sounds heavenly. It will be! Though Mum insists on making a hundred different kinds of Christmas cookies. It’s a serious operation, the whole baking process. I'm on gingerbread duty, which involves a surprisingly high amount of spice grating. Oh, I remember those days! My nan used to make these fruitcakes that were… well, they were a fruitcake. Rock solid, proper jaw-breaker material. You needed a chisel to get into ‘em. Still tasted of brandy, though. My grandmother's are… interesting. She’s got this recipe passed down through generations, and it involves marzipan and something called ‘essence of plum’. The results are… acquired. See, that’s what Christmas is about, isn't it? The questionable food you’re forced to eat with people you vaguely like. Aye, that’s the spirit! So, you two seen anything good on telly lately? I’m proper craving a good box set. Been watching that “The Crown” again, but I've already seen it about six times. I've been hooked on "Slow Horses." It's brilliant, really sharp writing and the acting is superb. Gary Oldman  kills  it. "Slow Horses"? Never heard of it. Sounds… slow. It is, but in a good way!

Cor blimey, London. Right posh place it is, innit? Reminds me of… well, reminds me of when I went with me cousin Brenda back in '68. Though then, it felt more… exciting, somehow. Now, just seems a bit frantic. All that rushin' about. Exciting’s right! Though frantic is a fair assessment these days. The price of a cuppa alone will put you off. Remember when you could get a decent tea and biscuit for tuppence? Now? Forget about it! But we need to be realistic, George. It’s modern life. Are you definitely sure about the theatre tickets, though? 'Hamlet', you know… a bit heavy. Morning, you two. London, eh? Fancy that. Been a while since I've been. Used to go down for football matches, back in the day. Villa, obviously! Though, Mrs. Davies - that’s my wife - she’s not convinced. Says it's all building sites and crowds now. Speaking of crowds, how’s the grandson? Still promising to finish that history project? Little rascal. Says he’s researchin’ the Tudors. More like watchin’ telly and playin’ ‘Fortnite’, if you ask me. But history's alright, innit? All those kings and queens. Not like these politicians we got now. Honestly. What’s going to happen with this election? Makes your 'ead spin, eh? Don't even start, George! It's all so dreadful. I’m just sticking to what I know - horses. At least they're reliable. Remember when young Emily was obsessed with ponies? She’d spend all her pocket money at the riding school. Those were the days. Should've invested in a horse farm, really. You know, speaking of investments, have you two thought any more about selling the spare room and turning it into an Airbnb? Could bring in a bit of extra cash, couldn’t it? Especially with the Americans coming over for… well, all the various events. Airbnb? Sounds a bit risky, doesn't it? All sorts of people comin’ an’ goin’. No, I think I’ll stick to me whist drives down at the community centre. Safer that way. Keeps me out of mischief, anyhow. What about that old Ford Fiesta you've been trying to flog on eBay, George? Any takers? No joy yet. It's a gem, really - a classic! But nobody seems to want a ten-year-old Fiesta with slightly faded paint. I did get a nibble on that vintage teapot, though.

Honestly, the sheer volume of research surrounding infant feeding is  insane . You’d think it was rocket science. And everyone has an opinion, don’t they? Like, I was just reading a paper arguing for exclusive breastfeeding for six months, then another saying introducing solids at four is perfectly acceptable, if not beneficial… it's a minefield! Tell me about it. Mum’s been on at me about breastfeeding constantly. "It’s the  natural  way, Elara," she keeps saying. Like I haven’t felt like a leaky, milk-filled cow for the past few weeks! Little Leo just latches on and then… nothing. He falls asleep. Is he getting enough? Or is he just using me as a comforter? Oh, the latch questions! The dreaded latch questions. Look, even the experts disagree. And honestly, every baby is different. Leo's got a strong suck, that's good. As long as he's gaining weight, don't stress too much about  how  he's feeding. Easier said than done, I know. Have you tried expressing? Just to see how much milk you’re producing? Yeah, I’ve tried. Got practically nothing. And then I feel even more useless. I feel like a failure, you know? Like I’m letting him down. Everyone says it should come naturally, but it’s anything but! And because I haven’t worked, I don’t have that confidence, that… professional expertise, I suppose. You’re always researching things, eh, clever clogs? Don’t be silly. Being a mum is  way  harder than any research I’ve ever done. This job pays the bills, but you’re the one doing the actual, important work. And honestly, expressing isn’t a measure of anything. Some women just don’t produce loads, and that's perfectly fine. Formula is  fine . Seriously. It’s designed to nourish babies. There’s no shame in it. Grandma keeps going on about how she fed me on formula and I turned out alright. Grandma. Don't even get me started on Grandma. She keeps saying she fed me on "cow and palm oil" and I'm a perfectly healthy adult. Like that proves anything. She also keeps offering me squash. Squash?! He’s only six weeks old! Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm living in the 1950s. Oh, she’s got a point, actually, about you turning out okay. But yes, squash is a bit… early.

Honestly, did you see that article about the sewage discharges again? It’s just… relentless, isn't it? Right off the coast! Can you believe it? I saw a little boy building a sandcastle down at Hythe last week, completely oblivious. Mmm, saw it. Awful, absolutely awful. They keep saying they're investing, but it doesn't seem to be making a blind bit of difference. The political posturing is wearing thin. Southport’s got its own problems, of course, with the pier needing constant repairs, but this… this is different. This is about public health. Is it all over the news, Dad? I saw something pop up on Twitter earlier, but I didn't really look into it. Seems like everything’s awful these days. Twitter, love? That'll be full of doom and gloom. The Kent Messenger had a whole spread on it. Disgusting. Anyway, about today. I’m finally getting around to tackling the overgrown lavender in the back garden. It’s a jungle out there, honestly. Lavender? Sounds lovely. I’m heading to the hospital early today. Mrs. Peterson’s having a bit of a wobble. She’s convinced the neighbours are talking about her and forgot where she’d put her teeth again. Nurse practitioner training is…interesting, to say the least. It's amazing how much you have to remember. Good luck with that, Brenda. Mrs. Peterson can be a handful. You've got the patience of a saint. And early start, eh? Sarah, are you still thinking of heading out to Richmond this afternoon? We could all go for a wander, grab some lunch. Richmond? Sounds nice, actually. I’ve got to finish a proposal for a new client, but I could probably wrap it up by lunchtime. What’s the weather forecast? I’m not fancying getting soaked. Apparently, it’s supposed to be quite pleasant. Sunny spells, a bit of a breeze. Perfect for a stroll along the river. I might pop down to the garden centre while I’m at it and get some more compost. This lavender's going to need a good feed. Oh, could you grab me a couple of those little succulent plants? The ones in the terracotta pots? I've been wanting to add a few to the windowsill. They're surprisingly robust. Absolutely, Brenda. Consider it done. Though you know, I still think you should get a proper houseplant.

Honestly, this maths test was  brutal . Like, properly, properly brutal. I swear, Mrs. Davies just  loves  making us suffer. Tell me about it! I spent the whole of Tuesday night just staring at fractions. Fractions, Elsie! Who even uses fractions in real life, apart from, like, bakers? And I don't  want  to be a baker. Exactly! And she kept going on about prime numbers being "fundamental to the universe." Fundamental to what, exactly? My Christmas dinner? Probably not. But hey, at least Christmas is coming! Did you get your Christmas cards sorted? Mum's been on at me to address all mine. It's so boring. Nearly. I've only got, like, a dozen left. I’m using those vintage stamps again. You know, the ones my grandad collects? The ones with the birds on? Ooh, proper cool! Are they the ones with the puffins? I love puffins. He's got loads, doesn't he? Is he still obsessed with them? Always! He’s got a whole sheet of puffin stamps from the Falklands. Says they’re scientifically fascinating. He's always going on about their beaks and how they adapt to the sea. Honestly, he'd bore you to tears. I bet! My grandad's obsessed with succulents. He’s got, like, fifty different kinds. My garden is turning into a desert. He keeps trying to give me cuttings. Oh, succulents are lovely! My mum’s trying to grow a Venus flytrap. She read an article in  The Gardeners’ World  magazine. Apparently, they’re brilliant for getting rid of flies. A Venus flytrap! Wow! Science is pretty cool sometimes, isn’t it? Although, I still think art is way better. Did you see the new project the art teacher set? It’s about recreating famous paintings using only natural materials. No! Seriously? That sounds amazing! I was thinking of doing Van Gogh’s ‘Starry Night’. I could use dried leaves and twigs and… maybe crushed berries for the blue? That's brilliant! I was thinking of doing Monet’s water lilies. I reckon I could use moss and pebbles for the stones. It’d look so good! Oh! Ed Sheeran's doing a Christmas concert in Cambridge!  No way!  Really? My mum loves Ed Sheeran. She'd probably die if she got tickets. Do you think it’s possible to get tickets? I doubt it! They probably sold out the second they were released.

Cor blimey, Doris, this rain’s something else, innit? Like someone’s emptied a bath over the garden. Though, it’s good for the roses, I s'pose. It is a bit miserable, Arthur. But look! I finally finished him. What do you think? He's Reginald, the rat puppet. A rat, you say? Bit on the nose, that is, given the state of things. Looks… lively, though. Did you use proper felt? That's always best for the little whiskers. Yes, proper felt! And I made the eyes out of buttons. I thought he needed a bit of character. I was hoping young Leo might like him when he visits next week. He’s got a soft spot for animals, even the, er, less cuddly ones. Reginald, you say? Quite ingenious, Doris. Reminds me of Punch and Judy, really. A bit… subversive. Remind me to tell you about a puppet show I saw in Zurich once. Very avant-garde. Subversive, Rupert? It's just a rat, dear! Though, he does have a rather mischievous grin. Are you having tea? Indeed. Earl Grey, naturally. And I thought we might indulge in a little handbell ringing after. I’ve been practicing "Greensleeves." Got the fingering almost perfect. Handbells, eh? You and your fancy music, Rupert. I wouldn’t know where to start. Remember when Mrs. Higgins down the lane used to ring them for the harvest festival? Used to give me a right headache, that did. Oh, Arthur! Don't be like that. It’s quite soothing, actually. Far less stressful than…well, than trying to get a bus these days. Tell me about it! Last week, I tried to go to the optician’s. The number 28. Absolute chaos. Half the seats were taken by pushchairs, and a fella was blasting music through his headphones. Couldn’t hear a single announcement. Ended up walking the last mile. Eyesight's getting worse, y’see. Need a proper check-up. You really should prioritise that, Arthur. These public transport systems… they're simply not designed for the elderly. I recall lobbying the council about accessibility improvements years ago. Got nowhere, of course. Bureaucracy at its finest. It's awful. I used to take Leo on the bus all the time when he was little. Now, it's a scrum. They need more buses, surely? And better enforcement of those child seat rules. That’s right.

Right, so, plans for today then? I’ve been looking at that Murano glass factory tour, but it looks a bit… touristy, doesn’t it? And pricey. Aye, it does a bit, lass. Always does, round these parts. But the glass is proper beautiful, innit? Remember Old Mrs. Higgins down the lane in Bolton used to have a little glass bird on her windowsill? All sparkly and blue. That was Murano stuff, she swore it was. I do. She always said it brought her luck. But I was thinkin' maybe we could just wander, you know? Get a bit lost. See what we stumble across. There's that little canal boat tour advertised – one that goes through the quieter backwaters? Now that sounds much more like it, pet. Less of the 'click-click-camera' crowds and more of a proper feel for the place. This used to be a proper bustling market, you know, Café Venice. Remember when it was just a tiny kiosk selling chips and gravy? Not this fancy-schmancy place it is now. Chips and gravy? Seriously? I can’t imagine it. It’s practically a landmark now. And the pastries are amazing. Honestly, I'm tempted to buy one of everything. You always were a sweet tooth, weren't you? Aye, but back then, you could get a massive portion of chips for tuppence! Tuppence! And Mr. Rossi, who ran it then, he used to give me extra vinegar, 'cause I was helping him out sometimes after school. Simple times, lass, simple times. Though, not much to eat apart from chips, to be fair. It's wild to think it was so different. My history lecturer mentioned that Venice used to be a major trading hub. Did you ever notice how all the buildings seem to face the water? It must have been all about the boats. It was, love, it really was. Everything came by boat. Spices from the East, silk from China… all landed right here. And the food… oh, the food! They used to have these incredible seafood stews simmering all day. Remember your Gran used to try and recreate them? Never quite got the flavour right, though, did she? Always needed just a  bit  more something. She did try. And she always insisted on using cod instead of proper Venetian fish. She said it was more affordable. Speaking of food, I’m starting to feel peckish.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Proper comfort food after that week. How was your week, Liv? Still battling the world of Bupa marketing? You have no idea. It’s been… a lot. New campaign launch, deadlines, the usual chaos. I’m fuelled entirely by caffeine and sheer willpower at this point. Though, this Nandos is definitely a welcome upgrade. I'm starving! Did you manage to get to the gym this week? I was thinking of trying that new spin class on Thursday. Yeah, I actually managed most of my sessions! Legs were a killer on Monday, naturally. Still feeling it, if I'm honest. I’m trying to be more consistent though, you know? Aiming for at least four a week now. That Pilates reformer class is a game-changer for my back. You should try it, seriously. Pilates reformer? Sounds fancy. I'm just trying to convince myself to  go  regularly, never mind try something new! I've been lacking motivation. Anything exciting planned for the weekend? Well, Chloe's organised a little pre-birthday drinks thing on Saturday. Nothing massive, just at The Eagle. Fancy joining? It’d be good to see everyone. The Eagle? Always a classic. Absolutely! I’m in. I need a decent night out. Things have been a bit… stagnant lately. Speaking of stagnant, have you heard from Tom? Don't even. I saw him on Instagram the other day, posing in front of some fancy restaurant in Barcelona. Looked  very  happy. Which is just… a lot to take in, you know? Especially after… everything. I know, babe. It’s rough. You’re better off without him, honestly. He always seemed a bit… flaky. Remember that time he cancelled on our bowling night last minute? Classic Tom. Oh god, don’t remind me. I wasted an hour waiting for him. I’ve started trying to focus on myself, though. Like, no more dwelling on people who don’t appreciate you. Hence the gym obsession and the slightly unhealthy amount of chicken. Good for you! Seriously. Self-care is key. Honestly, working in healthcare, you see the toll stress and neglecting yourself takes. It's scary. I'm trying to get better about taking breaks myself. I was thinking, after the Eagle on Saturday, maybe we could grab brunch on Sunday? That new place, ‘The Green Table,’ looks amazing. Brunch on Sunday sounds perfect!

Honestly, Bartholomew, the joy! Eleanor had her baby, you know. A little girl. We’ve named her Iris. Iris, you say? A lovely name. Sounds… artistic. Eleanor’s chosen well, then. So, a granddaughter for you, Penelope? Heavens. Time fairly evaporates, doesn't it? It seems like just yesterday you were bringing me those delightful homemade scones. Don’t remind me! I’m officially old enough to have grandchildren. It’s a rather… sobering thought. And quite overwhelming, in the best possible way, of course. It makes you think about the future, doesn't it? About where she’ll grow up. Eleanor’s considering… well, not here, actually. She’s looking at France. France? Running off to France, are we? Escaping the gloom of London? A sensible choice, in many ways. Property’s cheaper, certainly, though the bureaucracy… well, that’s a challenge everywhere, isn't it? Even here with our delightful bollards. Speaking of which, did you see they’ve put those dreadful new ones on Elm Street? Utterly ridiculous! They don’t serve any purpose whatsoever. They’re just... obstructions. You and those bollards, Bartholomew! It's a perennial argument. Yes, I saw them. A complete eyesore. Honestly, the local housing management… they're a disaster under this new landlord. Promises, promises, but no action. It's desperately frustrating. I'm documenting all the issues for a friend who’s a solicitor. Landlords. A necessary evil, I suppose. Though I’ve never quite understood the appeal of owning property when one can simply… exist. I’ve been spending my time productively, however. I’m writing a book, you know. Really? A book! About what? About European history, naturally. Focusing on the Habsburg-Spanish relationship in the 16th century. I spent some time in the Spanish archives a few years back - fascinating place, Madrid. The sheer scale of the documentation regarding Philip of Spain and Mary Tudor... remarkable. You get a real sense of the ambition, the maneuvering, the religious fervour. That sounds absolutely incredible! You should definitely publish it. You have such a wealth of knowledge. Have you considered the British Library archives? They’d be invaluable for cross-referencing. Indeed. I've been utilizing them extensively. Though, you know, it’s a lonely pursuit, sometimes. It’s not like in the old days when historians were larger-than-life figures, involved in everything. Now, it’s just… solitary research, fuelled by endless cups of tea.

Ugh, this is… okay. Not amazing. Mum always makes better spring rolls, honestly. Crispier. Dude, you’re complaining about spring rolls? Look at this Kung Pao chicken! This is  chef's kiss . Slough’s finest, I tell you. Best Chinese in the whole borough. You’re biased, Liam. You live here. My nan says the one in Hayes is better. And she knows Chinese food. She’s practically lived off it her whole life. Hayes? Please. That place is giving 'generic takeaway' vibes. This is proper, you know? Authentic. Feel the ginger! Okay, okay, Mr. Food Critic. I’m just saying, a little more crunch would be nice. And is anyone else noticing a distinct lack of chillies in anything? I asked for spicy. They always dilute the spice for Mrs. Patel next door. Remember last time? She sent back the sweet and sour pork because she said it “tickled her tongue.” Tickled! Seriously! My dad nearly choked trying not to laugh. He’s a proper fire-breather when it comes to spice. He puts scotch bonnet peppers on practically everything. My mum’s the same. Thinks anything below a five on the Scoville scale is basically tasteless. You guys even remember that chilli-eating competition Ben did last year? Oh god, don't remind me. He was redder than a tomato afterwards. And sweating buckets. Did he even finish the ghost pepper? Almost. He made it to, like, three and a half before tapping out. Said it tasted like burning sadness. Classic Ben. Speaking of Ben, has anyone heard from him recently? He’s been pretty quiet on Instagram. Yeah, I saw him post a story the other day. Said he was struggling with the Physics homework. Apparently, Mr. Davies is being a total beast this year. Davies is brutal. I spent all weekend wrestling with those thermodynamics equations. My head actually hurts. I’m seriously considering dropping it and focusing on Art. You? Dropping Physics? You’re the only one in our group who actually  gets  it! Don't be ridiculous. Yeah, think of the uni options you'd be limiting yourself to. Unless you're planning on being a professional comic artist? I saw you sketching some serious stuff in the library last week. Just messing around. But the new 'Crimson Comet' issue is insane. Seriously, the artwork is incredible. You guys should check it out. ‘Crimson Comet’?

Honestly, this is a right state, isn't it? Jonathan's birthday's next week, and we're still wrestling with this… avalanche of belongings. It’s got to be done though, hasn't it? Can’t be having him over to a house like this. Aye, it's a bit of a mountain, lass. But we’ll conquer it! I brought these down from the attic. Thought you might want to have a look. See if there's anything worth saving before we start chucking things. Jonathan'll love a trip down memory lane. Are we talking cake? Because I’m already thinking about cake. Chocolate, definitely. With those shiny sprinkles. Sprinkles are vital, Finn. Absolutely vital. Right, Mum, I've been looking at some branding options for the party. Jonathan’s turning 50, it deserves a decent theme, don't you think? I was thinking "Golden Jubilee" - bit cheesy, maybe? Or something more stylish? Branding? For a birthday party? Oh, that's a bit much, isn’t it, love? Just a good cake and a cup of tea will do. Though, that Golden Jubilee does sound rather… grand. A bit like the Monarchy. Jonathan wouldn’t like too much fuss. Fuss is good, Martha. A milestone like that deserves a celebration. I remember when your dad turned 50. Had a brass band come down to the street and played his favourite tunes. Good times. That  was  something, Elsie! Nearly deafened the whole neighbourhood. But you're right, though, it's a special occasion. Maybe we should have a proper buffet then, not just nibbles? I saw some lovely recipes for mini Yorkshire puddings with beef. Yorkshire puddings! That's a definite yes! But can we get those cheese and onion crisps? The proper ones, not the cheap ones. Right, buffet confirmed. And I’m still wrestling with the banner. "Happy 50th, Jonathan!" is a bit...basic. I was thinking maybe something playing on his love of literature? "Chapter 50: Celebrating Jonathan." Too pretentious? You're overthinking it, lad. “Happy 50th” is perfectly fine. He’s not a book, is he? Though, he does love a good read. He’s always got his nose stuck in a novel. Fancy some tea, dear? I'll put the kettle on. Yes, please, Martha. And I'll start sorting through these photos. Look at this one! Jonathan aged about five, covered head-to-toe in mud after a football match.

Honestly, GCSE choices are stressing me out  so  much. Like, what if I pick the wrong thing and then I can’t do what I want later? Chill, Liv. It's not the end of the world. We've still got ages to decide. My mum’s saying I should definitely do triple science, but I’m dreading it. All those labs… and the equations! Triple science  is  intense. I’m really tempted by photography, though. But then Mrs. Davies said it’s not ‘career-focused’ enough. What does that even mean? Is playing the clarinet a career? She made it sound like a hobby, a frivolous one at that! Seriously? Mrs. Davies is  always  being like that. Typical. She’s probably still stuck in the 80s thinking everyone needs to be an accountant. Photography’s brilliant! Loads of people make a living from it. Think about those travel bloggers, earning loads of money just taking photos of beaches and coffees. Yeah! Exactly! But then my dad keeps going on about needing ‘stable employment.’ He’s always on about jobs where you can’t get made redundant. Like… working in an office. Ugh. Offices are the worst. I saw this video on YouTube last night, this guy was doing a ‘day in the life’ of an accountant. It looked agonizing! Just spreadsheets and grey walls. I'd rather be a YouTuber, honestly. You and everyone else! But that’s so competitive, isn't it? Like, how do you even  start ? And the pressure to constantly create content… I know, right? But look at Charli D'Amelio. She basically dances around and makes millions. It’s mad. Though, my mum wouldn’t let me. She's all about 'perfect duty' and 'respect for elders'. Apparently, filming yourself dancing is disrespectful. Classic. My nan's the same. She still thinks the internet is a fad. Remember when she asked me if I could print out that article about Harry Styles for her? She’d never heard of him before! Oh my god! Harry Styles’ everywhere! Honestly, he's a cultural icon. What about his outfits? They're amazing. Did you see him in that sequined jumpsuit? Yes! Iconic! Speaking of famous people, I saw Sienna Miller at the farmers' market last week. She was just… normal. Looking at tomatoes. It was a bit surreal. No way! Seriously? I love Sienna Miller. She looks so effortlessly cool.

Lovely bit o’ sunshine we’re havin’, innit? Reminds me of a summer back in ‘78. We went campin’ up in the Peak District. Absolute nightmare with the midges, mind you. Swarms o’ ‘em! Nearly drove me da mad. Peak District, eh? Used to go fishin’ up there as a lad. Not much luck, truth be told. More bother than it was worth lugging all that gear. Though, the scenery was somethin’ special. Remember when they built that new bypass through Bakewell? Ruined a right pretty stretch of the River Wye, it did. Oh, you boys and your reminiscing. Must be nice to have memories like that. Mine are mostly of sticky fingers and spilled juice boxes. Though, I did take a trip to Cheddar Gorge once. Absolutely breathtaking. Much better than midges! Did you see that robin in the garden, Anon? Such a cheeky little thing. It  was  lovely, wasn’t it? I was just checking on some research material for my lecture next week – it's on Victorian social structures in Norfolk. Surprisingly complex, you know. And yes, Mum, I saw the robin. I caught it on my phone camera actually. I may put it on my presentation—just to give it some local colour. By the way, Dad, you were saying something about midges? Aye, the midges were a plague! We were pitched next to a bog, practically swimming in ‘em. Da was tryin’ to swat ‘em with a newspaper. Looked like a right fool, he did. Ended up covered in ink. Couldn’t get it off for days! And the tent… let’s just say it wasn’t exactly breathable fabric. Sweat drippin’ somethin’ awful. You oughta’ have tried citronella. Used to keep the mosquitoes away down the allotment. Though, didn’t do much for the midges, I reckon. Mind you, I read somethin’ the other day about some newfangled software that can identify insects by a photograph… can you believe that? Honestly, all these computers… it’s bewildering. I still struggle with my email! My granddaughter, Chloe, spends all her time on that thing. Gets her nose buried in it constantly. She was tryin’ to explain NFTs to me the other day. Absolutely no idea what she was on about. NFTs are… a complicated topic, Grandma. Essentially, they’re unique digital assets. Think of it like owning a rare digital painting. But yeah, they  are  a bit niche.

Cor blimey, it’s blowin' a right gale out there, innit? Glad I managed to get inside before it properly picked up. You drove alright, Brenda? Yes, perfectly fine, Arthur. A bit breezy, but nothing to worry about. Norfolk roads are always…interesting, aren’t they? You’d think they'd tarmac them properly sometimes. Did you see that delivery van struggling down the lane this morning? Nearly ended up in Farmer Giles’ pigsty! Sounds about right. Deliveries are a hazard around here, aren't they? I had a chap drop off a parcel the other day – couldn’t find number 27, ended up knocking on number 32, then 18! Bless him, he looked utterly bewildered. Reminds me of a joke… Why did the scarecrow win an award? Oh, go on then, Derek, spin us a yarn. I’m always up for a bit of a laugh. Me joints ache something fierce today, need a good chuckle. Because he was outstanding in his field! Oh, Derek! You haven’t changed a bit. Still telling those awful jokes. Though, they  are  rather endearing, in a silly sort of way. Endearing, are they? That's a bit strong, Brenda! But it did raise a smile, I’ll give it that. Speaking of things that raise a smile, I was watching that "Great British Sewing Bee" last night. Clever, those girls. Makes you think about your own wardrobe, don't it? Mine’s lookin’ a bit peaky, I must say. Got more holes than a Swiss cheese. Tell me about it! I was thinking the same thing. I've got a cardigan I’ve been meaning to mend for months. It’s got a massive hole in the sleeve. I keep saying I’ll get to it, but… well, you know how it is. Easier to buy something new, I suppose. Though, it does feel a bit wasteful, doesn't it? It does. My wife's quite the whizz with a sewing machine. She's always making things. She's currently attempting to recreate a 1940s dress, apparently. Honestly, it's a project! But it’s lovely to see her being creative. Did you hear about that teacher in Solihull who started a TikTok account? TikTok, is it? That's that tweetin' thing, ain't it? All those youngsters doin' silly dances. Can’t make head nor tail of it. My nephew tried to show me once.

Aye, it’s baltic, innit? Proper snow. Didn’t expect it this early. Makes you want to just hibernate until spring. Did you get much up north? Not as much as you, apparently! Just a light dusting here in Cambridge. Enough to make the pavements a bit slippy though. It's drifted a bit worse on the market square. Fancy a hot chocolate while you warm up? I was just about to put the kettle on. Oh, that'd be brilliant, thanks love. I’m absolutely frozen. This garden is never gonna get finished at this rate. I was hoping to get the last of the bulbs planted today but…nope. Snow. Everything’s put on hold. Tell me about it. I was planning on deadheading the roses later, but I think that's a non-starter now. Though, looking at it, a light dusting of snow  does  look rather pretty on the rose bushes...almost magical. Still, not good for the roses themselves. Aye, pretty for a bit, then it's just a damp, miserable mess. Speaking of miserable, have you seen the latest episode of Come Dine With Me? Honestly, the food looked…questionable. That woman with the pineapple melting situation? I nearly choked on me tea laughing! I caught a bit of it earlier. The pineapple incident was legendary. It's amazing how much drama people conjure up over a simple dinner party. It’s the competitiveness, isn't it? Makes for good telly though. Absolutely! Right. Anyway, back to more sensible topics… have you heard anything more about Liam and Chloe’s stag and hen? They're proper stressed about it, apparently. Chloe’s trying to organise a spa day, and Liam’s got some daft ideas about axe throwing. I did. Liam's parents were joking about him needing to sign a waiver before he even picks up an axe. Chloe's stressing about getting enough bridesmaids booked in. I think they’re both completely overwhelmed. Should we offer to help with anything? Just to take a bit of the pressure off? I think that'd be lovely. I could maybe look at venues for the spa day; Chloe mentioned wanting something in York. And you could have a word with Liam to gently steer him away from the axes, eh? Safety first, lad. Deal. I’ll have a chat. It’ll be a right laugh, though, won't it?

Right then. Lovely bit of chicken, this. Agnes, you’ve outdone yourself, you really 'ave. Better than that time you tried to make the goose… remember that? Nearly set the kitchen alight, it did. Oh, don't remind me, Arthur! I thought I was going to have to evacuate the whole street! It was a disaster, wasn’t it? The gravy was like tar. This lot is much better, though. Proper roast potatoes, crispy on the outside. Did you want some more? It's delicious, Mum. Really lovely. But I'm quite full, actually. All that travelling made me ravenous, though. That A11 is dreadful, isn't it? So many lorries. Tell me about it. We were tailgated by a cement mixer for at least ten miles. Seriously stressful. But at least we made it. This smells amazing, by the way. Smells like…home. That’s what it’s all about, innit? A good home-cooked meal. Fresh veg, too. Agnes always gets the best veg from Farmer Giles. Proper Norfolk grown, it is. Not like that stuff you get in the big supermarkets. Full of… well, nobody knows what it's full of. Don't start on the supermarkets again, Arthur. They have their place. Though I do think Farmer Giles’ parsnips  are  superior. What did you two lecturers get up to this week, then? Anything exciting? Actually, yes. I gave a guest lecture on postcolonial literature to a group of visiting students from Canada. It went really well, I think. They were incredibly engaged – asked some brilliant questions. That sounds fascinating, Elara. I was marking essays all week, sadly. A truly horrifying experience. So many plagiarism cases this year. It's disheartening. I’m thinking of incorporating more in-class writing exercises. Forces them to think on their feet, you know? Plagiarism? That’s a fancy word for cheatin', innit? Back in my day, you got caught copyin’, you got a clip round the ear and sent to stand in the corner. Sorted you right out. Arthur! Honestly! Things have changed, dear. It's much more complex now. It's about academic integrity and understanding intellectual property. Exactly, Grandpa. It’s a really nuanced issue. It’s not just about copying word-for-word anymore. It can be repurposing ideas without proper attribution, too. It’s about ethical scholarship. Elara’s right. The technology makes it so much easier to… well, let's just say it presents challenges.

Honestly, Mum’s roast potatoes are just… legendary. I don’t think I’ll ever manage to replicate them, no matter how many YouTube tutorials I watch. There’s just something about her technique. Don't be ridiculous, Chloe. You're a brilliant cook. Remember that paella you made last month? That was incredible. These are good too, though. Proper good. Paella’s a bit fancy, lad. These spuds… this is comfort food, pure and simple. A good roast potato is a cornerstone of a decent Sunday dinner. Secret's in the duck fat, you know. Real duck fat. None of that vegetable oil nonsense. Duck fat is right, Eileen. Remember when they stopped selling it in the shops? Folks were in a right state! Thought their Sunday dinners were ruined. Had to go to specialist shops, pay a fortune. Thankfully, that passed. Still, speaks to the importance of a good roast potato, doesn't it? Duck fat... used to buy it from Old Man Hemlock down the lane. Used to farm ducks himself. Best fat you ever tasted. Not like this processed stuff you get now. Proper old-fashioned. That sounds amazing, Grandpa. Do you remember what he used to do with the rest of the ducks? Did he sell the meat? Aye, he did. Sold the meat too, mostly to Mrs. Higgins down the street. She made the best pies in Bishop Auckland, that woman. Goose fat and duck fat, used to rub 'em in till the pastry was just perfect. So, Mum, when are you going to write down this potato recipe? You've been saying for years you'd do it. I'd love to have a go. Oh, I couldn’t. It's all in the feel, love. You can't write that down. It's about… knowing when they're crispy enough, when to baste them, when to take them out. Practice, that's all. Years of practice. Besides, I enjoy making them. Wouldn't want to ruin the fun, would I? Don’t be like that, Eileen. Share the wisdom! Though, I suppose that's what makes them so special. Things were simpler back in the day, weren’t they? Everyone had their little secrets. Mine was always adding a pinch of sugar to the gravy. Sugar in the gravy? Dad! That's… sacrilege! Really? I wouldn’t have thought so. Gives it a bit of a caramel note, doesn’t it?

Right, so, thinking back to that lecture I heard last week – the one on neuroplasticity and how we can actually  re-wire  learning pathways… it got me thinking about the whole university structure, doesn't it? So rigid. So…exam-focused. It feels archaic, really. Archaic is a good word. Absolutely. I’ve been saying it for years, haven’t I? It’s like they’re still teaching students  how  to memorize for tests, rather than how to  learn  for life. The pressure on those final exams is just… brutal. And doesn’t always reflect the actual understanding. Remember that brilliant student, Amelia, who froze up completely during her History final? She knew the material inside out. Oh, I remember. Devastating. It’s the performance anxiety, the sheer weight of expectation. So, if we're thinking about re-wiring… what would a genuinely neuroplastic-friendly university look like? My initial thought is less emphasis on standardized assessments, more emphasis on project-based learning, deeply modular courses... Definitely project-based. And personalized learning pathways, absolutely. Tailoring things to individual student strengths and interests. We already do bits and pieces of it, differentiating in the classroom, but it needs to be systemic. And what about ‘passion projects’? Let students dedicate, say, 20% of their time to pursuing something they're  truly  interested in, even if it's tangential to their core subject. Then they present it, defend it... Brilliant! I love that. Imagine the motivation boost alone. It’s like that viral video of the guy who built a fully functional arcade game out of scrap metal, right? Complete passion project. The drive was incredible. It tapped into something primal. We need to cultivate that primal spark in our students. It's not about building arcade games, obviously, but about that intense, focused engagement. Exactly. And it would foster genuine innovation. Speaking of innovation and drive, how's the new AI tutoring platform going? Still hitting roadblocks with the algorithm’s empathy module? I read that piece about it needing a sense of  narrative  to really connect. Frustratingly so. The technical side is solid, the data processing is phenomenal. But the empathy... it's like trying to teach a computer to understand irony. We're leaning on Sarah, our linguistic specialist, quite heavily. She's suggesting feeding it a massive database of storytelling – myths, legends, novels... Essentially, giving it a human cultural context.

Honestly, this week has been  mad . The Henderson project is threatening to swallow me whole. Three different stakeholders, all wanting slightly different things. It’s like herding cats, I swear. Tell me about it. My week's been pretty intense too. Had a really rough time with a patient on Tuesday. Severe anxiety, hadn't slept in days. Took a lot of calming and reassurance. You know how it is. Curry tonight? Thought I'd make a big batch. Need something comforting. Curry sounds  amazing  actually. Thank you! You're a lifesaver. I was just contemplating ordering a pizza and wallowing in self-pity. So, Henderson... anything exciting happening in your world besides battling anxious patients and conjuring up culinary masterpieces? Not really "exciting," more just...demanding. We're short-staffed, which always ramps up the pressure. Did you hear about that Halloween party at The Raven's Claw? Apparently, it's going to be huge this year, themed around spooky English folklore. Ooh, The Raven's Claw! That's ages since I’ve been. Spooky English folklore, you say? Tempting. Though, the thought of navigating a crowded pub in fancy dress after this week... Exhausting! What are you thinking of going as? I was thinking Boudicca. Proper warrior queen vibes, you know? Fierce and independent. It would be awesome to rock that look. I've already found a fab recreation of her headdress online. What about you? Any brilliant costume ideas brewing? Boudicca, brilliant! See, you’re all planned and organised. I’m still thinking about just buying a cat mask and calling it a day. Low effort, maximum resemblance to my current state of mind. Actually, thinking about English folklore... have you ever been to Cornwall? It's supposedly teeming with legends. Cornwall! I've always wanted to go! I’ve seen pictures – those clifftop walks look incredible. I’d love to go down to Land’s End sometime. Properly unplug and just absorb the scenery. It’s ages since I've had a real break. Seriously. It's on my list too. Maybe we could plan a weekend trip? A bit of coastal walking, some pasties… It feels like we both need some serious de-stressing. I'm in! Definitely. We could even check out some of the tin mines, apparently they have some really fascinating history. Right, talking about the future... where do you see yourself in five years?

Right then, love. Let’s 'ave a proper natter, shall we? It's been ages since I’ve seen you all properly. Cambridge is lovely, isn't it? So… different from Lewisham, eh? Much more...calm. Bit too quiet for my tastes, to be honest, but lovely all the same. It is nice, Mum. Quieter than Lewisham, definitely. Though I do miss the buzz sometimes. How was the journey up? Everything alright on the train? Dreadful, darling, absolutely dreadful. Delayed by forty minutes! Forty minutes, can you believe it? Packed like sardines, too. A young man spilled his coffee all down my new scarf. Honestly, the cheek of it! Though he did apologise, bless 'im. Said he was rushing to get to a job interview. Oh no! Poor you! And you were wearing your favourite scarf. What a nightmare. Did he offer to pay for the cleaning? He did, but I told him not to worry, love. What's a bit of a stain between family? Besides, he looked absolutely frantic. Imagine going into an interview looking like you'd been swimming! I'd 'ave been mortified. Anyway, the train was finally here and I got here safe and sound, thank goodness. So, tell me, what 'ave you been up to? Still juggling spreadsheets and making sure everything’s in the right place at the right time, are you? Pretty much! Being a Production Controller is… well, it's busy, that’s for sure.
