I was just looking at those wearable fitness trackers. Seen one that monitors your sleep  and  tells you if you’re snoring? Seems a bit…invasive, doesn't it? Invasive is an understatement! My nan bought one of those, thinking it’d cure her insomnia. Turns out, it just made her self-conscious about her sleep noises. She kept muttering about "being a lumberjack in her dreams." Oh, bless her! My dad’s been obsessed with health gadgets lately. He just bought one of those compression suits – you know, the ones they use for athletes? He's convinced it'll make him run a marathon. He can barely manage a brisk walk to the shops. Haha! My mum's the same. Got herself some of those weird detox teas. Says it's "cleansing her aura." Last time I saw her, she was green around the gills. Honestly, these health trends… Yeah, it's all a bit suspect, isn't it? Marketing hype, mostly. Remember that charcoal toothpaste phase? Black teeth for a 'clean' feeling? Don't remind me! I fell for that one. Looked like I’d been eating coal for a week. Speaking of teeth, have you seen the latest series of 'The Crown'? The portrayal of Charles’ dental work… utterly bizarre. Absolutely! Felt a bit too much like a parody, didn't it? Though, to be fair, the whole thing is slightly ridiculous. I'm more into 'Peaky Blinders' myself. Finally caught up on that. Proper gritty. 'Peaky Blinders' is amazing! I rewatched the whole series last month. It’s insane how stylish everyone is, even in that bleak setting. Speaking of style, did anyone see that hideous floral shirt Liam Hemsworth was wearing on the red carpet the other day? Don't even mention it. My cousin sent it to me with a string of crying-laughing emojis. Looks like something my grandpa would wear to a bowls tournament. I'm sticking with plain t-shirts, thanks. Easier. Simplicity is key.

Right, so we’re doin' the big shop tomorrow, yeah? Gotta make a list otherwise we'll end up with fifteen different types of hummus and nothin' else. Aye, lass, you’re right. Hummus seems to be your downfall. What do we need? I’ve already got a rough idea. Milk, bread, definitely need some proper bacon this time, not that skinny stuff you got last week. Can we get those chocolate biscuits, Mum? The ones with the caramel filling? Please? United won, ya know. Deserve a treat. Chocolate biscuits are definitely going on the list, Ethan. And Mum, we're short on teabags, definitely. And some of those ready meal lasagna things – comfort food for when I'm drowning in essays. Lasagna? Really? Seems a bit extravagant for a mid-week dinner. Is there a budget being considered here, or are we just indulging? Dad! It's not extravagant, it’s efficient. And besides, you always hog the roast dinners. It’s about fairness. Leave the girl alone, David. Sometimes a bit of indulgence is good for the soul. Ethan’s right, he deserves a treat after watching the game. Did you see that goal Henderson scored? Magnificent! Best goal ever! Absolutely screamer. Henderson? Good player. Though I still think Maguire needs to move. Honestly, his defensive record is… concerning. Oh, here we go. Another football debate. Right, let’s get back to the food list. What about fruit? Apples, bananas...? And we’re needin’ some insect repellent. I got absolutely eaten alive in the garden yesterday. Oh, that’s a shame, love. Were you stung? That nettle patch is blooming nicely, mind. I've got some cream upstairs for bites – the good stuff with hydrocortisone. It'll calm it right down. I learned a few tricks during my midwifery days, you know. Lots of little ones get covered in bites. Maybe if you spray the garden with that stuff it'll kill all the bugs? Like, a proper, strong spray? I'd rather not kill everything, Ethan. It’s bad for bees and butterflies. Maybe a citronella candle? Or some of those plug-in thingies? Citronella is a waste of money, honestly. Invest in some proper mesh netting for the windows and doors. Problem solved. And frankly, it’s a far more civilized solution than scattering chemicals everywhere. Your father’s always got a solution, hasn’t he?

Ugh, P.E. was  brutal  today. Mrs. Davies made us do suicides five times! Five! I swear, my legs are gonna fall off. No way! Really? Ours was alright. Just a bit of netball, and Mr. Harrison let us finish early because it was raining. Lucky sods. Lucky? He always lets  you  finish early! It’s like you’ve got a personal charm offensive with him. He barely glances at me, I’m pretty sure he thinks I’m a potted plant. That's not true! He just… appreciates a strategic dribble, I guess. Anyway, have you seen that new science video by ‘CosmicKatie’? It’s about black holes. Properly mind-blowing. CosmicKatie? Nah, I'm more of a 'SpaceBroBen' girl, myself. He does better explainers, like, actually visualises things. Katie just talks  at  you. Plus, his editing’s way slicker. Did you post your Instagram story from the weekend? With the filter? Yeah, loads of people liked it! Chloe commented she was jelly of my new trainers. Yours didn't get much attention, did it? No, not really. I thought it was a decent pic, too. It’s just… everyone’s obsessing over that influencer, ‘Lily Luxe’. She's only like, sixteen, but she’s got like, ten thousand followers. All posing and fake lashes. I know! It’s ridiculous. My mum says it’s just a phase, and everyone will be onto the next thing soon. Though, secretly, I do kinda want a better camera. My phone ones aren't  that  great. Tell me about it. My mum keeps going on about ‘authenticity’ and ‘not needing validation from strangers’. Like, easy for her to say. She doesn't have to compete with Lily Luxe’s perfectly curated life. She’s got a point though, doesn’t she? Remember last week in Biology? When Miss Peterson kept asking you about mitosis? You looked like a deer in headlights. Don't remind me! I’m hopeless at cellular biology. I swear, she just  enjoys  seeing me squirm. She probably highlights my struggles in her teacher’s notes. “Penelope – demonstrates a profound lack of understanding of fundamental cellular processes.” You’re exaggerating. She’s just… thorough. And she’s got a soft spot for weird facts. Remember last year, she was going on about the mating rituals of the Amazonian tree frog for fifteen minutes? Completely irrelevant to the lesson. True! She’s a bit odd, that one.

Honestly, this is minging. Absolutely minging. I feel like a right shipwreck. It does look like you're not exactly thriving, love. Proper peaky. You've barely touched that cup of tea I made you. You need to drink something, even if it’s just water. Tea tastes like sadness at the moment. And smells like sadness. Everything smells like sadness. This cold's properly knocked me for six. I can't believe I’m crashing out like this right before that presentation on Friday. We’ll get you sorted for Friday. Don’t you worry. It's just a cold, right? Not food poisoning again? Remember that dodgy Thai place last month? Don't even  mention  that. I was convinced I was a goner. Honestly, lying on the bathroom floor feeling like my insides were trying to escape... Traumatic, that was. Still, this just feels like a really bad cold, a proper head-stuffing one. Head's banging, nose is running, throat feels like sandpaper. Want to watch some telly? Something daft? Yeah, sounds good. I was just making lentil soup, it's good for when you’re poorly. Trying to use up that tin of chopped tomatoes. Remember when we used to have Lloyd Grossman on a Saturday night? That was peak telly. Oh my god, yes! The "travelling the world in search of delicious food" guy. I was obsessed! Used to try and recreate his recipes, always disastrous. My version of Pad Thai looked like something you'd sweep up off the floor. Mine too. Though I think I’ve mastered a decent chicken korma now. Speaking of health though... have you had your flu jab this year? I haven't yet. It’s on my list. Honestly, with work being so manic, it keeps slipping my mind. Should I go get one? I hate needles, mind. You really should. Especially with this nasty bug going around. And think about it, last time you were properly ill, you were out of action for two weeks. Remember that hospital stay? I was a nervous wreck. Don’t remind me. The food was grim. And those fluorescent lights... I felt like I was in a spaceship. Though, I'll give them credit, the nurses were brilliant. Proper heroes, they were. Absolutely. It’s just… it's a good reminder to keep on top of things. I was reading an interesting article the other day, actually, about advances in body language recognition.

“Quixotic.” Honestly, where do these words even  come  from? It's ridiculous. I’m sure you’ve got some obscure word up your sleeve, haven't you, David? "Not particularly, actually. Though, I was hoping for a 'zygote' - would have been rather impressive, wouldn't it? Quixotic is a decent play, Eleanor. Solid points there.” He adds a "crest" to the board, doubling his score. “Zygote! Good heavens, David, that's hardly appropriate language for a family game, is it? Though, I must confess, I admire ambition. Always did. Used to tell my girls, 'Aim high, even if you miss!’” "Rather like 'quixotic', wouldn't you say, Margaret? A bit of tilting at windmills.” He gently pats her hand. "Exactly! It’s like they’re deliberately trying to make it difficult. Reminds me of the traffic down at the Arndale yesterday. Absolute gridlock. I swear, half the population of Manchester decided to shop for bananas at the same time. Took me an hour to get from Piccadilly to home." "Tell me about it! I was trying to get to that new butcher's - apparently, it's  the  place for a proper Sunday roast. Queue was snaking around the corner. Honestly, felt like I was back in London, not Manchester." “A queue for a butcher’s! Well, that  is  dreadful. In my day, you simply walked in and were greeted with a smile. Quality and service, you see. People don’t seem to appreciate those things anymore.” “They’ve lost the art of patience, Margaret. Completely. Although, I must say, I do enjoy a good roast. Did you see that article in  Melody Maker  about the resurgence of brass bands? Quite surprising, actually. Brings back memories of village fetes and…well, simpler times.” "Oh,  Melody Maker ! I remember that magazine! Used to spend ages poring over the reviews. I saw a post on Facebook the other day about a revival band – they're playing at the Bridgewater Hall next month. Tempted to go. Although, I'm still recovering from that traffic ordeal." "Facebook, eh? I'm not much of a user, Eleanor. Too much pointless arguing and cat videos. I prefer a good book, myself." He looks pointedly at Speaker_3, knowing she’s a passionate reader. “Don't be hasty, David. Facebook can be a useful tool. I use it to keep in touch with former pupils. It’s quite touching to see what they’ve become.

Oh, my aching back! Another pile of flyers sorted, thank goodness. Bit of a scorcher today, innit? You’re looking a bit peaked, Arthur. Sit down, love. Have a little breather. Thank you, Eleanor. It is rather warm. Though, not as warm as some of the halls I’ve been in, I’ll tell you that. Germany, you know. Those exhibitions... they could be brutal. Germany? You spent time in Germany, did you? I always imagined you were a bit of a homebody, Arthur. I mean, you've always been a fixture in Taunton. Never thought of you gallivanting about on the continent! Well, not gallivanting, exactly. Though there were moments… It was all part of the business, you see. I invented – and later marketed – a system for printing multiple colour posters, back in the fifties and sixties. Quite revolutionary, really. Before then, it was all painstaking processes and limited colour range. My system automated a lot of it. Good heavens! Seriously? That’s fascinating! Never would have guessed. I always just saw you at the village fete, selling raffle tickets and looking ever so proper. So, these exhibitions... what were they like? Large, very large. Drupa in Düsseldorf, for example - the largest printing trade fair in the world. And IFA in Berlin. We'd take a booth, demonstrate the system, schmooze the distributors… It could be weeks at a time. The Germans, they appreciate efficiency and precision. They weren't easily impressed. Had to be spot-on. I can imagine! Very different from a Somerset farmers' market, I’d wager. Did you have to learn the language? A bit. Enough to get by, you know. ‘Bitte’ and ‘Danke’ go a long way. My real strength was understanding the technical specifications. That was the language we all spoke. I spent a good deal of time explaining the finer points of the colour registration system, believe me. There were constant anxieties about colour accuracy. People were used to dull, slightly off-kilter posters. Showing them something vibrant and perfectly aligned… well, that got their attention. It must have been quite rewarding, seeing your invention actually making a difference. All that hard work paying off. I always admired inventors, y’know. My late husband, bless him, tried to invent a self-stirring teacup. Never quite got there, poor dear, but he had the right spirit. It was indeed rewarding. One particular incident sticks with me.

Honestly, Dad, English Lit is killing me. Mr. Davies is obsessed with, like, really obscure poets. Who even  reads  Gerard Manley Hopkins anymore? Obscure? He’s a proper Victorian, lass. You've gotta appreciate the effort, the wrestling with language. It’s not about whether you  like  it, it’s about understanding where the language comes from, eh? Like this road we’re on. Been here for centuries, countless journeys taken. Each one contributing to the story of England. Right, profound. Still, I'm thinking about dropping it. Maybe just Contemporary Lit. Less…dusty. I was looking at courses actually, at Manchester, and Exeter… Exeter has a really good Creative Writing program. Think I could do a Masters in that later on? Exeter! Lovely place. Bit further south, mind. Good choice. You’ve got an eye for opportunity, you do. Creative Writing...that’s your passion, isn’t it? Always scribbling away in notebooks. Remember when you used to write those little stories about fairies in our garden? Oh, god, don’t remind me! They were awful. But I’m serious, Dad. I want to write, properly write. But then I start thinking about philosophy... what's the point of writing if you don’t understand the why behind it all? See, that’s the good stuff! Connecting the dots. Philosophy and writing are two sides of the same coin, really. Thinking deeply about the human condition, trying to put it into words. It’s all connected. Right. Need a break. See that service station up ahead? Fancy a quick stretch of the legs? And a sausage roll, perhaps? My treat. Definitely a sausage roll. And a coffee. But quickly, yeah? I want to get to Cornwall before it's dark. Are we still on for Padstow? Padstow and the coastal path. Absolutely. Though, you know, I read online about a farmer's market in St Ives. Supposed to be brilliant. Fresh produce, local crafts… Cornwall's got to be full of amazing produce, right? Though I'm not a huge fan of quinoa. People are always banging on about quinoa. Like it’s some sort of superfood miracle. Honestly, it tastes like cardboard. You're a tough critic, you are. I'll stick to the pasties then, eh? Hold on a sec… “Padstow”. Is that how you spell it, love? With a P? Yes! P-A-D-S-T-O-W. Loads of people misspell it.

Right then, nearly ready for this ratatouille. It’s a bit fancy for a Tuesday, innit? But ANON’s been working overtime, deserves summat proper. You two 'aving a go at setting the table? Yeah, trying to. These napkins are… elaborate. Feels like I’m folding swans, not just putting somethin' on a plate. And this cutlery...so many forks! What’s the point of three forks? Oh, that's just because ANON likes to impress. She's a proper stickler for details, that one. It's always been like that, ever since she was a little 'un. Remember when she insisted her teddy bear had to have a miniature tablecloth? Oh, God, I do! Little Miss Fussy. Well, she’s learned it all from fancy conferences, I reckon. All those power lunches and name cards. Still, it's not a bad thing, is it? Bit of class never hurt nobody. How's your back this evening, Arthur? Not bad, lass. Not bad at all. Got a bit stiff earlier, put some heat on it. Rain's coming, you know. Can feel it in my bones. Reminds me of the winter of '77. Snowed for weeks, it did. Couldn't get the milk in! The winter of '77? Crikey. I wasn't even born then. I’ve only ever known rain. And slightly grey skies. Right, young’un. You wouldn't understand. It was a proper apocalypse. Anyway, Arthur, you mentionin’ the rain reminds me, I need to call Mum. She’s got that dodgy hip again, and I bet she'll be tryin' to battle the wind and rain to get the groceries. Maybe I could pop round tomorrow and do a shop for her? I'm not exactly busy. Would you, love? That'd be brilliant. She’d really appreciate it. She’s so stubborn, won't let anyone help her. Thinks she's still twenty, bless her. Speaking of family, you heard anything from Sarah lately? Your sister? Nah, not for a few weeks. Just the occasional text. Said the new job's hectic. Probably too busy to bother with me. Don't you fret about that, son. She's got her own life to lead. It’s good to see her doing well, though. Remember when she was earning peanuts at that little cafe? Aye, those were the days. She was so miserable then. Glad to see her finding her feet.

Right then, this tea’s a bit naff, innit? Still, beats nothing. Fancy bumping into you here, Chloe! Didn't know you were a regular at the leisure centre. Hi, Liam! It’s good to see you too. I try to come a couple of times a week. Swimming's good for clearing the head after a particularly tough lesson. And the café’s a decent spot to grab a coffee and mark some papers. You? What brings you to this side of town? Just came to use the gym, trying to compensate for all the pints I pull, you know? Gotta keep somewhat presentable. Been a busy few weeks at the pub. Tourist season’s kicked off properly. Loads of stag dos and hen nights. Oh, I can imagine! Must be chaotic. I was just telling my sister the other day about how Birmingham’s really booming with tourists. What pub do you work at again? The Black Swan, down by the canals. You’ve probably walked past it. It's a bit of a lively one, as I said. Bit tiring sometimes, but pays the bills. How’s the language teaching going? Still teaching French? Yes, mostly French. I’ve started dipping my toes into Spanish as well, actually. The school wants to expand its offerings. It's challenging, definitely. These teenagers… getting them motivated to conjugate verbs can be like pulling teeth! What about you? Thinking of doing anything beyond bartending? Honestly? Not really at the moment. I did consider going back to uni, maybe do something with history. I always enjoyed that at school. But it’s a lot of money, isn’t it? And the job market’s… well, you know. I’m just thinking about getting a car, to be honest. A car! That's a big step. Birmingham traffic is something else, though. Are you confident you'll cope? I still remember my first few weeks driving in London… terrifying. Yeah, I’m a bit apprehensive about that, to be fair. Dad's been having a go at teaching me, but he's a bit of a lunatic behind the wheel. Gets right up everyone's back! I think I need some proper lessons. Definitely proper lessons. Driving instructors are there for a reason, you know. They’ll instill some road sense. Which, looking at some drivers around here, seems to be a rare commodity.

Cor blimey, look at the time! Nearly half past eleven, isn't it? We're proper late for our break, we are. Should've got that coffee brewin' ages ago. My bones are tellin’ me they need a sit down, they are. Don't fuss, Arthur. It's just a little late. I was just finishing off these biscuits – homemade, you know. Raspberry and white chocolate. You do like those, don’t you? And honestly, you’re always complaining about being late, then panicking when it actually happens! Indeed. A slight delay is all. The traffic was dreadful coming over. Managed to avoid the M25 chaos, thankfully. Though, the roads around here…holds the memory of the last time I tried to navigate the area when I first started, absolutely abysmal. Traffic, eh? Don't get me startin’ on drivin’. I wouldn't trust those youngsters behind the wheel for all the tea in China. Zoomin’ about like they're on a racetrack. Back in my day, we knew how to drive proper. Slow and steady, that’s the ticket. Remember old Mrs. Higgins and her Morris Minor? She was a marvel, she was. Barely went above twenty, bless her. Oh, Arthur! You're unbelievable. And completely missing the point. Anyway, I was thinking about that trip we discussed to Gambia. Peter – your nephew – said it was lovely. Said the people were so warm and welcoming. It is rather appealing, isn’t it? A change of scenery. Although, I did read something disturbing the other day… about Munchausen Syndrome, affecting children in some developing nations. It’s quite horrifying, really. The deliberate fabrication of illness for attention... Munchausen? That’s a right nasty business, that. People do strange things, don’t they? Makes you wonder what goes on in their ’eads. Still, Gambia’s a beautiful place, from what I’ve seen on telly. Plenty of sunshine, eh? That’s what I need. My old joints are creakin’ somethin' fierce. Exactly! And we have to do something about those children, don't we? I was thinking, perhaps we could make a donation box. Something simple, to leave by the front door. People passing by could pop in a few coins. We could decorate it with some of my plants – those trailing ivy look particularly nice. A charitable initiative? Excellent. I'll contribute something substantial. Perhaps a small banner to publicize it?

Honestly, this new "Ghost Hunt" app is just ridiculous. I spent an hour last night wandering around the park, convinced I was going to capture a spectral image, and all I got was blurry pictures of squirrels. Squirrels, Liam! Squirrels are pretty creepy when you think about it. Those beady little eyes… Besides, you know these apps are all fake, right? It’s just clever algorithms playing on your paranoia. Don't listen to him, Elara. It  could  be real! Remember that documentary we watched about Blackwood Manor? Spooky stuff! We should go see that new horror movie, “Crimson Hollow,” this weekend. Apparently, it’s genuinely terrifying. Oh god, no. Not another one where someone is hunted through a forest by a thing with glowing eyes. I still have nightmares from “The Ritual.” My pizza is too good to risk being ruined by impending doom. True, true. But Liam refuses to watch anything remotely scary with me. He says it "ruins his appetite". Can you believe that? How are you supposed to experience the full emotional range of a film if you’re focused solely on digesting carbohydrates? I prefer my emotional range to be limited to the deliciousness of this pasta, thanks very much. Did you guys hear from Chloe and Ben? They’re supposed to be in Barcelona right now. I messaged Chloe earlier, she sent back a picture of Sagrada Familia! It looked amazing. She said Ben got completely sunburnt on the first day. Classic Ben. Seriously? He always burns. He needs to invest in a proper SPF 50. And a hat. A big, floppy hat. He looks like a lobster in every holiday picture. That’s so Ben. Wonder if they're going to try that paella everyone raves about. I’m already craving some. Maybe we should order some for takeaway tomorrow night? Sounds good to me. Although, I'm still riding high on this pasta. What about you, Freya? Hungry? Absolutely. But I’m thinking Thai tonight. I've been trying this new green curry recipe, and it’s seriously addictive. I might whip it up next week. Ooh, that sounds amazing! You’re becoming quite the chef, Freya. Remember when you burned toast every single morning in sixth form? Don’t remind me! I was a disaster in the kitchen back then. It’s all about measured amounts and not overcooking things, apparently. Much like escaping a horror movie, I’d imagine.

Cor, look at this thing, Marjorie. Honestly. You’d think a car this age would fall to bits faster than a biscuit in a tea. Least it starts, I suppose. Aye, started right up, didn't it, Arthur? Don't you go moaning now. Could be worse. Could be a Reliant Robin. Remember those things? Terrifying. Oh, don’t remind me, Bertram! My nephew had one. Kept overturning in the slightest breeze. Are we still talking about cars? I thought we’d move onto the nice bits, like tea and biscuits! Lovely biscuits, Marjorie. Spot on. But this Fiesta... it’s a trial, it is. Especially getting it back down the A11. All those lorries and speedy young ‘uns. Gives me palpitations, it does. I was thinking, maybe a taxi home after all. Save me the bother. A taxi? Arthur, you'll be spending half your pension on taxis! Bit excessive, innit? Remember what the doctor said – keep active. A short drive does you good. Fresh air, even if it’s full of exhaust fumes. Bertram’s right, you know. Sometimes it’s easier to just get a taxi. No stress, no worrying about roundabouts. And you can have an extra biscuit or two knowing you're not driving. But Marjorie, you know I don’t like being a burden. I feel like I’m puttin’ you out. Burden? Don’t be daft, lad. We’re family. That’s what we’re here for. Besides, it’s a long trek to Norwich Central for you and then all the way back on those buses. You'd be knackered. He does have a point, Arthur. Those buses are a nightmare. Always packed. And waiting in the cold… not ideal. I suppose you’re right. Still… feels a bit extravagant. It’ll be pushing thirty quid, easy. Thirty quid is nothin' these days. Think of it as an investment in your blood pressure. Less stress, better you. And besides, I can give you a hand with that blasted Fiesta when you get back. We'll have a look at that rattle it's been making. Oh, you and Bertram tinkering with that poor car! It’ll be held together with duct tape and wishful thinking by the time you’re finished! Don't you start, Marjorie! Bertram knows a thing or two about engines. He built model trains, remember? Precision work involved. Model trains were a different kettle of fish!

Ah, that’s lovely. A proper cup of tea and a digestive. Just what I needed after all that driving. Though, honestly, I’m starting to think I should've just flown. You and airports, Deirdre. We've been through this. You’d rather wrestle a badger than go through security. Remember that fiasco at Gatwick? Don't remind me. The pat-down… the confiscated hand lotion… honestly! I’m still traumatised. It felt like being interrogated. And for what? A weekend in Brighton! Now, now, Deirdre. It's not  that  bad. You just need to be a bit more… prepared. Know the rules. Don't carry three bottles of hand lotion. Easy for you to say, Arthur. You just sit there, calm as a cucumber, despite being acutely aware we're hurtling down the M6 at seventy miles an hour. It’s my nerves, you know. Always have been. He’s got a point though, Deirdre. And flying  is  much quicker. We need to be in Manchester by Thursday, right? The removals bloke said he arrives at eight. Eight! That’s dreadfully early. I’ll barely have had time to finish my tea! And are you  sure  about the removals? They seemed a bit… rough around the edges when I spoke to them. I checked their reviews, Mum. They were fine. A bit blunt maybe, but reliable. Besides, we’ve got Arthur here to supervise, haven’t we? He’ll keep them in line. I’ll make sure they don't break anything precious. Though, I still think you’re overthinking this whole move. It’s a lovely little cottage in Cheshire. Much nicer than that damp flat in London. It  is  lovely, I’ll grant you that. But moving… it's disorienting. All those memories packed into boxes. I keep finding things I’d completely forgotten about. Like that maths set from school! Still in its original case. You kept that? Seriously? Mum, you were a maths genius, you didn’t need a set! It was a gift from my father. He always encouraged me. He thought I’d be a professor, you know. Said I had a mind for numbers. Imagine that! Me, a professor. You were a brilliant teacher, Deirdre. Those kids loved you. I still remember the Christmas card from that little girl, Emily, she drew you a picture of a giant protractor. Emily… I wonder what she’s doing now.

Honestly, Mum, it’s so boring today. Nothing’s happening. Just endless videos of cats doing silly things. Well, something  did  happen. Something good, actually. Put the phone down for a sec, love. What? Did another influencer fall over? No, nothing like that. Remember how gutted you were when your bike got nicked last week? My bike?! You're joking! Did they… did they find it? Seriously? I am serious! The police called this morning. Apparently, someone reported a bike abandoned down by the old fishing huts. They checked the serial number… it was yours! No way! Really? Mum, that’s amazing! I thought it was gone forever! How…? Apparently, a neighbour, Mrs. Peterson, saw a post on the local Facebook group – "Hastings Lost and Found". Someone had posted a photo of a bike matching your description, asking if anyone recognised it. Mrs. Peterson recognised it straight away and contacted the police. Honestly, social media - sometimes it’s a complete time sink, but every now and then it does some good! That's brilliant! Mrs. Peterson is a star! I need to bake her some cookies. Thank you, Mum! You’re the best. It was like, the only bike I really wanted. I was planning on cycling to college when it’s a bit warmer. Don’t mention it, darling. The police have stored it safely for you. They said they’ll bring it back tomorrow afternoon. It’s a bit muddy and needs a clean, but otherwise, it’s all there. Muddy’s fine, I can deal with that. College… I was actually looking at the cycling club at the college. They have some pretty serious routes they go on. Like, proper hills. Serious hills, you say? You haven’t even managed to cycle up the incline to the park without complaining yet! Okay, okay, point taken. But I’m determined! It would be good to have someone to cycle with, you know? Not just Mum who moans the whole time. I do not moan the whole time! I offer words of encouragement! And sometimes, tactical stops for cake. Speaking of cake… I made a lemon drizzle this morning. You want a slice? It’s still slightly warm. Yes, please! That sounds perfect. So, the police are bringing it tomorrow? What time? Will they need a signature or something? They said around three, they’ll call fifteen minutes before. Rest assured, I’ll be signing whatever they need.

Right, I’m officially declaring Cardiff my next destination. Anyone want to try and block me? Rhys, you look like you’re plotting something. Plotting? Me? Never! Just admiring your… enthusiasm, Chloe. And thinking about chips. I'm starving. Did anyone grab any decent pasties on the way? The train station selection was dire. There was a Greggs at Ludlow. Not exactly artisan, but serviceable. I got one with steak and onion. A Greggs pasty? Rhys, you soldier on. I'd rather gnaw on the board. Seriously though, we need to figure out dinner. I was thinking something simple, like a shepherd's pie. We have potatoes, right? Shepherd’s pie sounds lovely, Chloe. Very comforting. Though, remember that disaster we had last time we attempted one? The potato topping was like concrete. Don’t remind me, Dad! Gareth nearly chipped a tooth. That was a traumatic shepherd’s pie. I'm looking at YouTube tutorials this time, I promise. Oh, that was a right mess! I still recall the look on Gareth’s face. He looked like he’d bitten into a paving stone! Gareth, you remember, don’t you? Vaguely. I was more concerned with securing Antwerp. Speaking of which, I think I can cut you off, Chloe. This route to Munich is looking rather lucrative. You’re incorrigible, you know that? Always thinking about railroads and trade routes. Can't you just think about food for five minutes? The train journey was awful, by the way. Absolutely rammed. I swear, someone was trying to sit on my lap. Tell me about it. Trying to navigate that carriage with my luggage was an Olympic sport. And the crying baby… honestly, you could feel the collective stress of the entire train radiating outwards. Oh, trains. They haven’t been the same since they took away the proper tea service. Remember, back in the day, they’d bring around silver teapots and dainty sandwiches... Now it’s just overpriced coffee and lukewarm sausage rolls. Don’t get me started on the Wi-Fi! It kept cutting out. I couldn't even finish watching my 'Coronation Street' episode! It ruined my evening, practically. See? Terrible train experience. Ruined everything. Now, serious question: Do we have any carrots for this shepherd’s pie? Preferably not limp ones. Carrots, yes. Rhodes pointed out a farm shop near here with supposedly award-winning root vegetables.

Right, that’s it. I’m officially declaring war on Baltic. Three times in a row, I’ve landed on Baltic! It’s just not fair. Now, now, darling, that's the beauty of Monopoly. A cruel mistress, that's what she is. And you chose to develop Baltic, didn't you? Don't blame the game, blame your slightly reckless acquisition strategy. Reckless? It seemed like a good investment at the time! Cheaper than the oranges, more potential! And now…look at me. Drowning in rent. Honestly, I think there’s something fundamentally unfair about the distribution of property in this game. Unfair to whom? The landlord? That's the point! Think about the historical context, love. It’s a satire of capitalist greed. You're supposed to  become  the landlord! I know, I know. It's just… sometimes I find the whole thing a bit… excessive. We're sitting in your parents' lovely, completely non-cutthroat home in Norfolk, and I’m mentally bankrupting you. It feels a bit dramatic. That's the joy of escapism! Besides, your parents are loving it, aren’t they? Look at Mum, she’s practically vibrating with excitement. Remember Christmas at Grandma’s when she insisted on playing? Total chaos. Vaguely. I think I blocked most of those memories. Speaking of culture, I was reading an interesting article the other day about British drinking culture and how it’s intertwined with games like this. The whole competitive spirit, the low-stakes risk-taking… it’s all connected, apparently. Really? How so? Lay it on me. I’m always up for a bit of social commentary while systematically dismantling your property empire. Well, the article posited that the British penchant for a pint after work, the pub quizzes, the slightly aggressive team-building exercises… it's all a release valve. We’re expected to be stiff upper lips and work hard, but we need somewhere to let off steam, to assert ourselves a little, even if it’s over a round of darts or, you know, crushing someone in Monopoly. That's quite insightful, actually. So, failing to land on Mayfair is socially acceptable, but failing to meet a deadline at work is not? The irony isn't lost. It's almost a ritualised form of rebellion. Precisely! And it’s heavily tied to the idea of camaraderie, too. The shared experience, the collective groans when someone rolls a three.

Honestly, Kerrie, this smells absolutely incredible. You’ve outdone yourself! I'm starving. Did you manage to get those new potatoes from the farmer's market? Yeah, they look amazing. Thanks, Kerrie. I'm absolutely shattered. That project deadline was brutal. I’ve been living on coffee and adrenaline for the past week. Always the dramatic one, aren’t you, Liam? Anyway, potatoes look lovely. I’m really glad we could all make it tonight. Been feeling a bit… well, a bit under the weather, to be honest. Not the best week, what with the bins being missed again and that washing machine deciding to give up the ghost. Ruined half my towels! Oh no, Nan! Seriously? A washing machine breakdown  and  missed bins? That’s just relentless. Have you looked into getting a new one yet? I can help with the research if you like - I’m surprisingly good at comparing white goods. I could take a look online too, Nan. There are some really good deals around if you know where to look. What model did you have? Might be something similar on sale. It was a Bosch, a perfectly good one, mind you! Just old. And the bins… honestly, the council. They say they're improving services, but it’s just getting worse! They’ve even started charging extra for green waste. Absolute robbery, I say! Tell me about it. Everything’s going up. Speaking of which, are you still thinking about moving closer to the coast, Nan? You deserve a bit of sea air and fewer bin-related dramas. I am, love. I’ve been looking at places in Tenby, actually. Beautiful little town. But the prices! It's terrifying. I need to keep working for at least another three years to build up a decent deposit. And then there's the moving… the sheer thought of sorting out all my belongings. I've got a lifetime of stuff accumulated! You could declutter a bit, Nan. Seriously. We could help you out with that. No offence intended, of course. Just saying, less stuff, less hassle. Easie rsaid than done, Liam. You don’t know my collection of ceramic thimbles! Each one has a story. Besides, I’ve recently been trying my hand at crafting again. Remember I used to make those little knitted gnomes? Oh my gosh, yes! Those were hilarious! I still have the one you made me with the ridiculously oversized hat.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic is mental. I swear it gets worse every time we have to come up this way. Feels like we're barely moving. It does, darling. It's always busy on the A1, especially heading north. Just breathe, love. Road rage isn’t attractive, you know. Remember what your Uncle Dave said about pent-up frustration manifesting in unfortunate parking choices? Yeah, I remember. He parked on a double yellow line after a particularly bad football result. Still got a ticket, though. This car's not helping either, to be fair. It’s a bit…agricultural, isn’t it? It's reliable, isn't it? And perfectly adequate for getting us from A to B. Honestly, you’d think you’d want a sporty little number, being a young man, but you always seem to prefer something sensible. Like me, then? Not like you. You’d drive a vintage Jaguar if you could. I just… I don’t need all that flashiness. Besides, this thing’s got decent fuel economy. Speaking of, are we still going to France in the summer? Absolutely. Isabelle's already said she's got a week free in August. We booked that little gîte near the Loire Valley, remember? The one with the roses and the incredibly grumpy cat? Percy! I remember Percy. He nearly took my hand off when I tried to pet him. Still, the scenery was amazing. I need to brush up on my French before we go. It's been years since I was truly fluent. You'll be fine. A few Duolingo lessons and you'll be chatting away. It's funny, isn’t it? The way technology is supposed to connect us, yet sometimes I feel more disconnected from actual reading. My work is a nightmare. Publishers keep insisting everything has to be serialised, chopped into snippets for online platforms. It's killing the art of the long-form narrative. So, still fighting the good fight for print then? You and your TLS articles. You’ll be a dinosaur eventually, Mum. Possibly! But someone needs to champion the beauty of a well-bound book. Holding it, feeling the paper, smelling that lovely ink... it's a tactile experience a screen just can't replicate. Though, I must admit, even  I  occasionally succumb to the convenience of an e-reader on the train. Don't tell anyone. Your secret's safe with me.

Right, my turn then! You won’t believe this. So, remember I was saying I was planning on having a relaxing week in Cornwall? Relaxing, I said! Yeah? What went wrong, then? Sounds like you, planning something chilled and it ending in chaos. Chaos doesn't even cover it, Liam! Picture this: first day, gorgeous sunshine, beach walk, all lovely. Then, a seagull – a  massive  one – swooped down and nicked my pasty right out of my hand! Right in front of me! I swear, it looked me dead in the eye as it flew off with it. Oh my god, El! A seagull stole your pasty? That's brilliant! You looked it in the eye? I did! It was mocking me, I'm telling you! Proper smug. And then, the next day, the campsite flooded. Like,  really  flooded. We had to salvage our stuff in the middle of the night. Sleeping bags, clothes, everything covered in mud. Aye, sounds reet dramatic! Cornwall's lovely, but they are known for sudden showers, aren’t they? My nan always said, “Pack your wellies, lass, even if it's sunny!” Serves you right for thinking you could have a relaxing holiday, El. You’re a magnet for disaster. Don’t be daft, Josh! It was just a bit unlucky, innit? Anyway, it gets worse! On the last day, trying to get back home, the car broke down on the M6. Stranded for four hours waiting for the breakdown service. Four hours! You’re having a laugh, yeah? You’re making all this up. Swear to you, I'm not! I’ve got photos and everything! Look. . See? Mucky tent, smug seagull, me looking utterly defeated by the side of the motorway. Oh, no! You poor thing! That’s a holiday story for the ages, though. Proper epic fail. That’s brilliant! You’ve been through it, haven't you? Reminds me of when I went camping with me cousins in the Lake District. Ended up sharing a tent with a family of slugs. Slugs?! You're kidding! No! Big, slimy blighters, everywhere! It was horrific. We tried to sleep, but they kept crawling over us. We just ended up laughing too much to be scared. Right, I’m starting to think these holidays are cursed. Anyone else got a disaster story to share? Let’s make this a competition. Worst holiday ever! Alright, alright, I’ll go.

Right then. So, wild winter camping. Sounds a bit… brisk, doesn't it? I’ve always been more of a pub-by-the-fire sort of chap, myself. Still, Angus seems rather evangelical about it. Tell me, Moira, you’ve seen him out and about in all weathers, haven’t you? What’s the appeal, really? Beyond the obvious madness, of course. Oh, it's not madness, George, it’s… invigorating. Truly. It’s a different kind of beauty, isn’t it? The landscape stripped bare, the snow, the silence… it gets right under your skin. And Angus does get quite passionate about it, aye. He'll tell you it's a fantastic way to clear the head, to reconnect with something real. Being a nurse, you see, I'm accustomed to the artificiality of hospitals. This is just the opposite – pure, raw nature. Exactly, Moira's right. It’s not about  enjoying  the cold, George. It’s about confronting it, respecting it. There’s a certain clarity that comes with pushing yourself a bit. It's a mindfulness practice, practically! Trying to stay warm, find a dry patch of snow to pitch your tent, gather wood… it forces you completely into the present. No room for thinking about spreadsheets or university funding applications, I tell you! University funding applications, you say? Well, that does sound rather appealing, actually. Though ‘respecting’ the cold, that’s a rather grand term for shivering uncontrollably, isn’t it? What about the practicalities, Angus? Surely it’s not just about battling the elements? What gear do you need? You wouldn't want to freeze solid for the sake of a bit of mindfulness. Absolutely not, George. Preparation is key. Layering is everything. Merino wool base layers, a good down jacket, waterproof trousers… you need a four-season tent, obviously, something sturdy that can handle snow loads. And a decent sleeping bag, rated well below freezing. I've got a -15 degree bag, you know. You need to know how to build a snow shelter too, just in case. It’s a skill! And a good stove; a properly reliable one – not your flimsy backpacking kind. He’s been drilling me on fire-starting techniques for months now. Says it’s essential for morale as much as warmth. He showed me how to use birch bark even when it's wet - fascinating, really, the resilience of nature.

Right, so, you're  serious  about this Bergman film thing? Like, actually serious? 'Cause I'm struggling, Liam, I'm really struggling. It's all grey and… sad. And everyone looks like they’re perpetually contemplating the meaning of existence. Give us a break! Serious? Yes. Beautifully, profoundly serious. It’s not supposed to be a laugh-a-minute, Maisie. Bergman is exploring the depths of the human psyche.  Persona , in particular – it’s a masterpiece of fragmented identity and the power of connection. Psyche this, psyche that. I've been trying to figure out why that woman keeps staring at the ceiling for twenty minutes! Is she waiting for the ceiling to reveal the secrets of the universe? I need exploding spaceships, at least. Or a witty one-liner. Something,  anything , to grab me. It's not about the ceiling itself, Maisie. It’s about her internal state. The stagnation, the alienation… It's visual poetry. Think of it like… like a really intense, beautifully written novel, but expressed through visuals and silence. You’re used to quick cuts and special effects, I get it. But try to appreciate the deliberate pacing, the carefully considered composition. Deliberate pacing leading to me nearly falling asleep. Look, I appreciate art, right? I studied literature – remember the endless essays on Chaucer and Wordsworth? – but this… this feels like having your emotions gently squeezed. It's a bit much, innit? I'd rather have a plate of chips and a re-run of  The Great British Bake Off . Okay, point taken. Though, I’d argue there’s a certain artistry in a perfectly crisp chip. Speaking of food, what are you fancying for dinner? I was thinking maybe that new Thai place in town? Apparently, their Pad See Ew is incredible. Thai sounds good! Definitely better than watching people mope around in black and white. But on the film thing… you know I love a good book, right? I devoured  Piranesi  last month. That was proper mind-bending. The imagery, the mystery… Oh, Susanna Clarke! She's brilliant. I read that one too, absolutely captivated. It’s similar to Bergman’s approach in a way, isn’t it? Creating a world entirely through detail and implication, rather than exposition. She builds this labyrinthine house that is also a world, and you, as the reader, are discovering it alongside Piranesi. Yeah, but  Piranesi  had a glimmer of hope.

Right then, story time. You two been good today? Poppy, you haven't been building a Lego fortress on the sofa again, have you? It was a  really  good fortress, Mummy! With a moat! And a drawbridge! A catapult! We had a catapult! It launched marshmallows. Marshmallows? Oh, you rascals. Well, that’s delightful. But sofas are for sitting, not for fortified construction zones, love. Okay, so, story time. I was thinking of telling you about the time I found a typewriter in a charity shop. A  typewriter ? What’s a typewriter? Is it like a PlayStation? No, sweetheart, it’s very different! It's an old-fashioned machine. You press the keys and it types letters onto paper. No screens, no buttons, just… clack, clack, clack! It's how people used to write stories and letters before computers. Did it shoot paper? Like a catapult? Not quite, Leo. But it was a bit noisy. It was a really old one, and the keys were all sticky. Honestly, it felt like a museum piece. I thought about buying it, but then realised I wouldn’t have the space, and frankly, I wouldn't know what to  do  with it. I mean, I use Excel for everything now, don't I? Even writing shopping lists feels like I need a spreadsheet! Excel? Is that a game? Can we play it? Excel isn't a game, darling. It’s… well, it’s a program on the computer for organising things. Numbers, words, lists… your Dad uses it for work, mostly. Remember last night when we were talking about the Brownie Promise? He had to make a spreadsheet to plan all the activities. I remember! The one about helping others! And doing… stuff. Exactly! Helping others is a big part of the Brownie Promise. That’s a good thing to do, isn't it? So, back to my story… The typewriter was a lovely green colour, a sort of pale moss green. It reminded me of the countryside around Dartford, where I grew up. Actually, remembering that, I had a friend, Maisie, who lived down the road... Tell us about Maisie! Right. Maisie had a pet rabbit called Winston, and Winston would  always  try to eat her mum’s prize-winning roses. It was chaos! We used to spend hours trying to stop him... Did Winston use a catapult? To launch roses? No, Leo.

Honestly, David, you look like you've been wrestling a badger. Is that your best shirt? It's got more holes than a moth-eaten tea towel. Morning, Margaret. And a badger, you say? Rather flattering, actually. It's just…comfort. These things are hard to find, you know. Besides, we're amongst friends, aren’t we? No need for Windsor formality here in Bradford. This breakfast is lovely, though. Proper Yorkshire bacon. Aye, it is. I got it from that little farm shop up past Bingley. They've got a new orchard, apparently. Plums, apples, pears…a right bounty. Makes you wonder why we import half our fruit, doesn’t it? It does. Progress, I suppose. Though progress often means replacing something perfectly good with something…less. Remember that trip we took to Northumberland a few years back? All those deserted medieval villages, swallowed by the landscape. Beautiful, but a stark reminder of what vanishes. Oh, aye, Wallington. Haunting, weren’t they? Felt like the stones were whisperin’ stories of folk long gone. Speaking of haunting, the roadworks on the A650 are driving me absolutely spare! Took me an hour to get here this mornin’. Absolute chaos. Tell me about it. Tried to avoid them myself, ended up on some back lane that resembled a goat track. Honestly, they could have planned it better. Trying to lay tarmac in rush hour – it’s madness. At least the coffee’s good. You make a mean cup, Margaret. That’s a compliment I’ll take, thank you. I’ve been experimenting with different roasts. Got a lovely one from a little place in Holmfirth. And I’ve made some plum jam, too. Thought you might appreciate it. It’s got a real kick to it. Plum jam? Excellent. You know I'm rather partial. You're a dab hand at this sort of thing. I'm useless in the kitchen. Completely hopeless. My wife, bless her soul, used to handle all that. I grow my own herbs, you know. Rosemary, thyme, sage... lovely for roastin’ potatoes. Though I’m starting to worry about old Mr. Henderson next door. He’s lookin’ frail. Barely sees him out. Yes, it’s worrying, isn’t it? People disappear, don’t they? Gradually. So many older folks struggling to keep up with the world. Phones baffling them, junk mail piling up… It’s not fair. Exactly!

Honestly, this weather is dreadful. Proper damp chill creeping right into your bones. Reminds me of a Christmas when we were kids - remember, John, the one where the pipes burst? Oh yes, vividly. Mum was in a flap, lugging buckets of water. You were convinced Santa wouldn’t be able to get down the chimney with all the ice. Morning, you two! Smells like Earl Grey in here. Anything exciting happening? Still gloom outside, I see. Did anyone manage to wrangle any Christmas decorations down from the loft yet? Not yet, love. I've been trying to sort out your Gran’s medication. It's a nightmare trying to get that new cream she needs, isn't it? The pharmacy keeps saying it’s backordered. Tell me about it. Everything’s backordered these days. They said at work the paper suppliers are struggling – apparently, everyone’s printing Christmas cards and saving them for the post. A bit old-fashioned, isn't it? So, what's Gran saying about her skin? Is it still flaky? Should I maybe pop to the Boots in town later and see if they have it? I can check online too. She says it’s worse, a bit weepy. And she’s been complaining about her knees again, moaning about needing some of that arnica cream. I’ve ordered some online, but it’s taking forever. Speaking of which, did you manage to find the clever phone stand I asked you to look at, John? The one that sticks to the window? Almost. They’re all plastic, aren't they? I thought you’d want something more…stable. Found one in brushed aluminium, quite stylish actually, but it was a bit dear. Should I order it? Brushed aluminium sounds brilliant, Dad! Definitely get it. Mum’s always dropping her phone when she’s trying to watch those baking shows. It's a hazard, truly. Speaking of shows, did anyone see that one about the Arctic expedition? Absolutely freezing! Makes you appreciate a nice warm bath, doesn't it? I’ve been trying that new lavender and eucalyptus bath bomb. It's divine. Ooh, you must tell me about it, darling. Lavender is lovely. I've been trying that new face serum, the one with the hyaluronic acid. Supposed to plump things up. Jury's still out on whether it actually  does  anything though. Plump things up? Goodness.

Honestly, Chloe, this week has been  bonkers . The agency is rushing me senseless. They want a campaign for this new vegan dog food – vegan dog food! – with a focus on ‘emotional connection.’ How do you emotionally connect with a Labrador about tofu, you know? That  is  ridiculous. Emotional connection with a dog about  anything , frankly. Are they expecting poetic voiceovers? "Oh, Barnaby, my little soulmate, you’ll  thrive  on this kale crisp!"? Exactly! They want quirky, they want heartfelt, they want...wordy. And the client keeps changing their mind. Yesterday it was all about sustainability, today it’s about the dog’s happiness levels. It's exhausting. How’s the programming going? Still neck-deep in surveys? Pretty much. It's actually been unexpectedly fascinating, oddly enough. I'm working on one now that's trying to gauge public opinion on the latest political reshuffle. It's…a mess. People are so polarised. And the questions have to be phrased  so  carefully to avoid leading them. It’s a real exercise in nuance. Much less stressful than trying to sell tofu to a dog. True, true. Politics is always a minefield. Did you see that thing about the new housing development near your parents’ place? Apparently, they're planning to build on the meadow. The one where all the bluebells grow? Ugh, I know! Mum’s absolutely fuming. She's organised a petition and is rallying the local community. Dad’s being quietly furious, which is even worse. He’s the silent treatment type of angry. It’s infuriating. Honestly, this city just keeps swallowing up green spaces. It's awful, isn't it? It feels like we're forgetting what's important. My nan was telling me the other day about how she used to pick wildflowers as a kid in Kent. You don't see children doing that now. They’re all glued to screens. Exactly. It’s just…sad. Listen, did you manage to get tickets to that new Netflix show, "Chronoscape"? Everyone's raving about it. Oh my god, yes! I snagged two for Friday. We’re going to that little Italian place beforehand, remember? I was thinking we could try that pasta carbonara. Perfect! I’m really looking forward to it. It’s been ages since we’ve had a proper catch-up without being interrupted by work or parents. Speaking of which, are your parents still on about you settling down?

Honestly, Fiona, I’m feeling it today. My back is protesting every single squat I did this morning. I swear, I'm getting older, not fitter. You’re hardly ancient, Eleanor. And you’re the one who insisted on joining that ridiculously early Pilates class. It’s seven am! Most people are still dreaming of croissants. It’s good for me! Keeps me moving. Though today, moving feels like a monumental effort. How was your run this morning, David? You looked positively smug at breakfast. It was good, actually. Managed a personal best on that hill near the Meadows. The air was crisp. You should try it sometime, instead of torturing yourself with those yoga contraptions. Croissants and runs… honestly. You two are obsessed with punishing yourselves. Here, have a scone. Freshly baked. Less strenuous, far more rewarding. They’re clotted cream and strawberry jam. Penelope, you absolute lifesaver. Honestly, a scone is precisely what I need. Thank you. David, don’t you dare think you’re escaping. A scone for you too. Don’t mind if I do. These smell divine, Penelope. You're spoiling us. So, Eleanor, this back pain... is it just because of Pilates, or is it that dodgy chair you’re still using in the study? It’s probably a combination, to be honest. That chair  is  dreadful. I’ve been meaning to get a new ergonomic one, but… you know. Speaking of things you’ve been meaning to do, has anyone looked at the market lately? I was chatting to Beatrice the other day and apparently, prices in Richmond have gone absolutely mental. Don’t even start, Penelope. It’s depressing. Trying to find somewhere remotely affordable within commuting distance of London is a nightmare. We’re priced out, utterly. I saw a tiny flat the other day, two rooms, overlooking a bin, for nearly £400,000. It’s insane. Edinburgh’s not much better, though. The new developments are pushing up prices across the board. It's ridiculous. People are paying a fortune for glorified boxes. It’s all about location, location, location, as they say. But honestly, finding a place with a garden that isn't the size of a postage stamp is becoming increasingly difficult. I'm seriously contemplating moving further out, even if it means giving up a bit of independence. Don't you dare! You'd hate living somewhere too quiet.

Blimey, look at the size of that thing! Proper Victorian, innit? Never realised the Botanic Gardens were this big. Reckon we can find a bench somewhere outta this sun? I'm roasting. Definitely. It  is  impressive, though. They've restored a lot of it. And yeah, the sun's brutal today. Come on, I spotted one just over there, near the rock garden. It’s got a bit of shade. So, you’re still drowning in corpora, then? How’s the tagging going? Drowning’s the word, that's for sure. It’s a nightmare, honestly. This new project… it’s all historical shipping manifests. Hundreds of thousands of them, hand-written, faded ink... You can imagine the mess. The tagging schema’s a shambles, too. My supervisor keeps changing his mind. He’s got this fancy new system he wants to impose, but it just doesn't fit the data. Sounds… delightful. Sounds like the kind of thing that would drive anyone mad. Shipping manifests, though? So you’re learning about all these past trades and economies? That's actually quite interesting! It is, in a morbid sort of way. I've been reading about the coal trade from Newcastle and Sunderland. It’s astonishing the amount of stuff that went through the ports. But mostly, it's just repetitive clicking and correcting errors. Honestly, I’m dreaming of spreadsheets and algorithms. At least those are predictable! What about you? Still battling bridges? Is the final design sign-off for the new pedestrian crossing sorted? It’s… complicated. The budget cuts hit us hard. They’ve slashed funding for the entire project, so we’ve had to strip back a lot of features. The original plan was for an integrated lighting system and a smoother gradient for accessibility, but now… it's just a standard crossing with a brighter flashing light. It’s frustrating when you try to create something thoughtful, and then get forced to compromise. Aye, I know the feeling. Government budgets are a right mess, aren't they? I was reading about it online the other day – massive cuts across the board. Makes you wonder where it’s all going. Feels like they're just stripping everything back to the bare minimum. Exactly! It’s short-sighted, in my opinion. Proper infrastructure investment is what builds a good economy and improves quality of life. These cuts will just end up costing more in the long run.

Right then, Paulie, you reckon that shade of terracotta’s working, eh? It's proving a right bugger to get consistent, mind. This Lancashire weather isn’t helping; one minute sunshine, next minute drizzle. Terracotta's alright, Markus. Bit…serious, innit? Could do with a bit of splash, a bit of life. Like that film,  The Bicycle Thieves . Simple story, but bursting with feeling. You ever seen it? Of course! De Sica’s masterpiece. Reminds me a bit of some of the pieces you see coming out of Eastern Europe these days. Raw, honest… not all the CGI nonsense we get from Hollywood. Though, I did enjoy that new Scorsese flick,  Killers of the Flower Moon . The acting was… phenomenal. De Niro, you know? Still got it. Scorsese’s brilliant, definitely. But there's summat about a good, honest bit of acting, like, proper acting, you know? Not all this…posturing. Like that fella, Colin Firth. Good actor, but sometimes he looks like he’s trying too hard. Proper Scousers, they don't need to try. They just  are . Like Ken Dodd. Remember him? Oh, Ken Dodd! Absolutely legendary. He wouldn’t have needed terracotta, that’s for sure. He would’ve needed sequins! Speaking of colour… I was thinking about adding some blues and greens around the edges. Something to contrast. What do you think about all this new development going on down by the docks? They're slapping up these huge, modern apartments. Just concrete boxes, really. No character. Don't get me started on that, Markus. Ruins the whole bloody area, it does. Used to be proper warehouses down there, characterful buildings. Now it's all glass and steel. Nobody cares about history, do they? Just profit, profit, profit. They should have preserved some of the original buildings, turned 'em into studios or summat. Proper art place. Like that old brewery down by Otterspool. That could have been amazing. Precisely! It's the same everywhere, isn't it? Gentrification. It's eroding the fabric of communities. I'm trying to add a bit of that fabric back here, with this mural. A bit of colour, a bit of…memory. You know, I found this old canvas down at the charity shop last week - practically brand new, just someone's cast-off. Going to try a landscape on it. Something calming. Charity shops are goldmines, aren't they? Found a vintage record player there last month.

Honestly, it’s… uniform, isn’t it? Field after field of, well, nothing much. I was expecting more… something. Poland is supposed to be brimming with history, isn't it? But all I can see is yellow. A very repetitive yellow. Aye, it's a bit of a blank canvas at the moment. It's early spring, love. Everything's still settling. Give it a few weeks and it’ll be green and full of wildflowers. Besides, look at those cows! Proper Lancashire cows they look, mooing away. Brings a bit of home to it, doesn't it? They  do  look rather content, don't they? Perhaps you’re right. It's just… I’ve been so cooped up lately, even a monotonous view is a bit overwhelming. This campervan adventure feels so… freeing, but the reality is hitting a bit. Finances are another worry, naturally. How are we managing, do you think? We’re doing alright, actually. I’ve been keeping a pretty close eye on things. We’ve been eating well too - those pierogi we bought in Zakopane were a belter! Remember Sarah saying she booked that new pottery class for us when we get back? That’ll be a nice treat, won't it? Oh, yes! Pottery. That sounds lovely. Sarah's so thoughtful. It’s nice to have something to look forward to. I've been meaning to clear out that mountain of boxes in the spare room. It’s truly ridiculous. I keep thinking, ‘right, this weekend,’ and then… well, you know. Life just gets in the way. Don’t you ever feel overwhelmed by possessions? All the time! Which is partly why I’m loving this trip. Less stuff, more experience, right? I sold half my books before I left. Felt amazing. Remember Mark from uni? I bumped into him last week, online. He’s doing some crazy kayaking expedition in Scandinavia. Makes me feel like I should be doing more adventurous things. Mark! Goodness, hasn’t he always been a bit of a thrill-seeker? It’s impressive, really. Though, I'm not sure kayaking in Scandinavia is quite my cup of tea. I’d rather stick to pierogi and pottery, thank you very much. Did you hear from Liam? He was saying he might try to join us in Krakow. Not yet. I sent him a message yesterday. He said he was swamped with marking.

Are we nearly there yet, Dad? My phone’s almost dead, and I haven’t got any signal out here in the sticks. Aye, lass, nearly. Just gotta turn off at that roundabout there, see? Preston's just a few minutes beyond. You've been glued to that phone all day, haven't you? A bit of fresh air'll do you good. Fresh air is lovely, Elodie. Though I’m glad we're heading to a supermarket soon. I need some things for the new flat. The excitement of moving is dwindling a little, it feels like so much organising! New flat’s gonna be brilliant, though. Loads bigger than the old one, isn't it? Can I finally have a decent bookcase then? I’m running out of space for all me books. Definitely a bigger bookcase, love. You’re turning into a proper bookworm like your mum, you are. Speaking of books, Elodie, did you ever get round to reading that Kerouac I lent you?  On the Road , remember? Um... I started it. Honestly, it was a bit… rambly, wasn't it? Proper long. Trying to fit it in with all the revision is hard. Exams are looming, you know. Yes, sixth form is a beast. But you're amazing, Elodie. You’ll smash them. Remember that essay you wrote on Virginia Woolf? Absolutely brilliant. You have a real talent for writing. I’ve been thinking about going to the Hay festival this year. Maybe next year, if things aren't so chaotic with the move. Would you be interested? Hay festival? Seriously? That sounds amazing! Loads of authors? Like, real authors? I’d love to go. Maybe we could see if anyone we know is speaking. Aye, that'd be somethin'. Though travel to get there… considering all the train strikes at the moment. Nightmare, innit? Try getting anywhere at the moment. I nearly missed work last week because of 'em. It’s a shame. Everything seems to be in upheaval. Do you remember when we went to the Lake District, Dad? We saw a deer! You were so excited. Aye, I do. You were only about six, weren't you? Kept screaming "Look, Daddy, a magic pony!" Bless you. You were a right little thing. Always gettin' into somethin’. Dad! Don’t embarrass me! I was just a kid. Remember when Grandma used to tell us those scary stories before bed?

Oh, my word. This is... quite something, isn't it? Thirsk. Feels a world away from Kendal. Didn't realise Yorkshire was quite so… flat. Nan! You're here! Honestly, you gave us all such a fright. We weren't expecting you until next week! How did you even get here? Did you manage the train okay? Managed the train? Dear me, managed is a strong word. It was a saga, love. A proper saga. The announcements were incomprehensible, the seats were cold, and this young man – all piercings and bright blue hair – kept trying to explain blockchain to me. Blockchain! As if I'd know what that is! It sounds like something you find in a bog. Blockchain? Seriously, Nan? You got the blockchain lecture? Classic. You should’ve recorded it. It would’ve gone viral. Viral? Good heavens, don’t start me on that. I tried asking him what it  did , and he launched into a fifteen-minute explanation involving cryptography and decentralized ledgers. Honestly, it felt like I’d stumbled into a secret society. Oh, Nan, you're precious. Liam, be nice. Your great-grandmother has just arrived after a long journey. And it’s wonderful to have her. We've been having a right clear-out, you know, decluttering the spare room. All sorts of memories coming up. Decluttering? That sounds like an awful lot of hard work. I remember a time when decluttering involved a swift dusting and a cup of tea. Now it's apparently a whole lifestyle. What are you throwing away? Don't tell me you're getting rid of things I might want! Mostly junk, Nan. Old photo albums, boxes of dusty paperwork, and Gran's collection of ceramic owls. They're… intimidating. Ceramic owls? Those were a phase! I liked them. They reminded me of Professor Armitage in my literature class. He collected them too, you know. Rather eccentric fellow. Always quoting poetry. I suspect he had a touch of melancholia about him. You always did have a good eye for spotting melancholy, Mum. You're very observant. It's something I've always admired about you. It also helped you understand people, even when they didn't quite understand themselves. Well, one has to, doesn't one? Life throws a few curveballs, and sometimes people hide their hurt behind a smile. Or a collection of ceramic owls. I’ve seen a lot of hurt in my life, love.

Right, so… this is it then. The shiny new beast. Feels a bit… flimsy, innit? Compared to my old one, anyway. That was a right tank. Yeah, they all feel a bit flimsy these days, don't they? Trend, I reckon. Minimalist design and all that. What’d you go for? Specs seem pretty decent from a quick look. Alright, lads! Is this the thing we were on about? Smells like takeaway in here, though. Serious need for a bit of basil tonight, I tell you. My tomatoes are going mental in the greenhouse. Sorted, mate. Basil’s in the bag, you’ve brought the goods. And yeah, this is the new laptop. Went for a… well, I don't even know the proper name. Something with an i7 processor and 16 gigs of RAM? Sounded good at Currys. Hoping it’ll actually  do  something good. My old one was slower than a snail in treacle. An i7 is solid! You won’t be disappointed. I teach English to Korean students online, so I need something that can handle a few browser tabs and Zoom without crashing. This should blitz it. What operating system did you get? Windows again? Yep. Windows 11. All those flashing lights and options… honestly, they just want you to buy more stuff, don’t they? Remember when you just had a desktop and a recycle bin? Simpler times. Used to spend hours playing SimCity on my Dad’s old Amstrad. Proper retro. Oh, man, SimCity! I was obsessed with that. Used to spend all my pocket money on expansion packs. Remember when games had  actual  manuals? You had to read instructions, learn how to play. Now it’s just ‘press button, win’. No skill involved. True! It's all just instant gratification. Though, I gotta say, the graphics they're achieving now are incredible. Did you see that new MMA game that just came out? The detail in the facial expressions is… unsettling. Speaking of which, you still training, Liam? Yeah, still sticking with it. Got a fight coming up in a few weeks, a local thing. Trying to get my cardio up. Building up to a good distance for hiking too, you know, to actually appreciate the countryside. Reckon I could manage Snowdon next summer. Snowdon? Blimey! That's a proper trek. You’ll need serious boots for that. My mate, Kev, tried it last year, ended up with blisters the size of plums.

Well, this is…something, isn’t it? Tarnow isn't exactly known for its vibrant bistro scene. It’s lovely inside though, all that exposed brick. A bit…French, perhaps? Though I doubt they actually  know  French, do you? Nah, I reckon they’ve just seen pictures. It’s good though, innit? Really good pierogi. Better than the ones I had in Krakow last month. Proper hearty. And the coffee’s surprisingly decent. It’s brilliant they’ve opened something like this here. Tarnow needed a shake-up. A shake-up is a rather mild way to put it. It feels a bit…anachronistic, doesn't it? Like a little piece of Paris dropped in the middle of Poland. I was just thinking about Amelia the other day, you know, my niece. She’d adore this. She’s always banging on about needing somewhere "aesthetic" to take photos. Aye, she would. Always on Instagram, that one. Speaking of which, I posted a picture of this pierogi earlier. Got loads of likes already. You should join Instagram, honestly. It’s a good way to keep in touch with people. Instagram? Dear me. Another app. Another thing to learn. I’m still struggling with this Polish Wi-Fi. It keeps dropping out. And besides, I'm not sure I  want  to document my life for strangers. It makes me think of… well, it makes me think of things I’m trying to move on from. Things I don’t need to broadcast. Like what? You don't have to go into it if you don't want to, but... I'm here to listen, yeah? You know I am. Things have been tough, I get it. And you’ve been working so hard on yourself, haven’t you? The swimming…you look fantastically fit. It’s a discipline, isn’t it? Something concrete I can  do . Something measurable. Unlike...other things. It does help, the exercise. Makes me feel… less adrift. Less like a ghost in my own life. Though sometimes... sometimes I worry I'm just clinging to this version of myself, you know? This 'healthy Sarah' persona, to avoid facing… the rest of me. Being adrift is understandable. Happens to the best of us, doesn’t it? Especially when you’re trying to figure out who you are, or who you  want  to be. I was thinking about my teaching, actually.

Right, so Dorset Steam Fair this weekend, yeah? It looks brilliant, honestly. All those engines, the crafts, the food… I'm really looking forward to it. Have you two managed to sort the tickets? Tickets… aye, I've been looking. Online’s a disaster, keeps saying 'technical difficulties'. Tried ringing, got put on hold for twenty minutes. Ended up just going to the local newsagents. Paid a bit extra for the service, mind you. Got 'em though! Here. Think they went up again this year, didn't they? Everything does, doesn't it? They certainly do, Arthur. Everything's getting ridiculous. But it’s worth it, isn't it? Seeing all those old engines, it’s like stepping back in time. And the children love it. Are you alright for getting a wheelchair for Chloe, love? Last year that queue was dreadful. Yeah, I booked one online, specifically. Should be waiting for us at the entrance. Saves a lot of hassle. They even said they'd bring it to where we are setting up our picnic area. I was a bit worried about it, you know, getting there and it not being available. Picnic area, eh? Fancy. Used to bring a flask of tea and a sausage roll, that was enough for me when I was a lad. Bournemouth’s gone upmarket, hasn’t it? Houses are extortionate now! Remember when you could buy a decent place for under eighty thousand? Don't even start, Arthur! It's terrifying. The prices here... I was chatting to Mrs. Davies the other day, her daughter wants to buy a flat, a  small  flat, and it’s nearly three hundred thousand. Crazy! I’m thinking of moving back to Harlow, honestly. The property prices there are still more manageable. Really, Mum? Moving back? That would be a big change. I’d miss you. Though, I can see the appeal. I'm starting to look at places myself, actually. Somewhere a bit bigger than my current flat. But London prices… Forget about it! See? It's everywhere, isn't it? This whole country's gone mad for property. Remember old Mr. Henderson down the road? Had a little bungalow, could've sold it for a fortune. Said he'd rather stay put, though. Said he'd seen too much change. Wise man, that Mr. Henderson. Speaking of things staying put… how's Mittens doing? I haven't seen a picture of her lately.

Oh, this is lovely, isn't it? Thirsk is… quaint. Much quieter than Kendal, of course. Though I do miss the fells. This rain, though! Is it always like this in Yorkshire? It's relentless. Aye, Nan, it can be. Yorkshire’s got a bit of a reputation for it. Though, truth be told, we’ve had a good spell. Don't let it put you off. And don't worry, we'll keep a good supply of tea brewing! How are your knees feeling after the drive? Gran! Did you bring me that book about Roman history I asked for? I need it for my project. And is there Wi-Fi here? I need to check something for school. Wi-Fi’s plentiful, lad. And yes, your grandmother brought the book. It's on the coffee table. Honestly, you'd think you were invading a fortress the way you charge in. Nan, how’s it been travelling? Anything exciting happen on the way? Well, the young man behind the counter at the service station tried to explain Twitter to me. I confess, I just looked at him blankly. All those little blue birds… what’s it all about? It seems an awful lot of noise for very little substance. Honestly, the world's gone mad with these gadgets. Twitter’s a bit of a rabbit hole, Nan. Best avoided, honestly. It's mostly people shouting at each other. Liam, put your phone down for five minutes and greet your grandmother properly. Alright, alright. Hi, Gran. So, about that Wi-Fi… Speaking of mad… Did you see that article about the artisan cheese maker in Ripon? Apparently, he uses music to stimulate the yeast! I’m seriously tempted to write a piece about it. It’s utterly bonkers. Cheese and music? Good heavens. Whatever next? My sister Mildred used to insist on playing Gregorian chants while she baked her Yorkshire puddings. Said it helped with the rise. Never did work, though. They were always a bit flat. Mildred sounds like a character. Reminds me of my Auntie Mabel, who swore by homeopathic remedies for everything. Once tried to cure a broken leg with dandelion tea. Dandelion tea? Seriously? That’s… weird. Gran, did you go to church this Sunday? Mrs. Patterson’s been asking about you. Says she misses your hymns. I did. Though the new vicar… well, he’s a bit… enthusiastic, shall we say?

Right, deep breaths. Dentist appointments for two small humans. It’s going to be…an experience. Especially with Arthur’s aversion to anything vaguely dental. Do I  have  to go, Mummy? Can’t I just…not have teeth anymore? Then I wouldn’t need a dentist! No teeth! Like a baby! No, darling, you absolutely  have  to go. It's important to keep your pearly whites healthy. And Arthur, stop throwing chocolate! It’s Easter, not a free-for-all. We’re having this later. Anyway, speaking of important, I need to book hearing tests for both of you. Mrs. Davies in class mentioned a few times she thought you might be missing things, Ashaad’s mum said something too. Hearing tests? Will it hurt? No, sweetheart, it won't hurt. It’s just… they make little noises, and you point to the ones you hear. Bit like a game, really. It's more to make sure you're both hearing everything clearly, especially with all the noise in school. Can I have a sticker if I do well? A big one! With a dinosaur! Of course, you can, little man. A huge dinosaur sticker, if you pass with flying colours. Okay, right, birthday planning. Eloise and Liam are sharing a birthday again, clever parents sticking them both in at once to make it easier! It's the 14th of May, isn't it? What are we thinking? Can we have a Monet party? Like the paintings? All swirly and blue? A Monet party! That's a brilliant idea, darling! Very cultured. We could make water lilies out of paper plates. Arthur, what do  you  want? Please say something other than dinosaurs. Cake! Lots and lots of cake! And bouncy castle! Right, cake is a given. Bouncy castles are a bit ambitious for the garden, but we'll see. I was thinking of trying to incorporate a bit of Maths into the party, actually. Maybe a treasure hunt with mathematical clues? Keeps them entertained and practising at the same time. That sounds…boring. Can we play pin the tail on the water lily instead? Boring? My little Monet expert thinks maths is boring? Well, it’s a compromise, isn’t it? We’ll do the treasure hunt  and  pin the tail on the water lily. Speaking of compromise, your Aunt Susan’s birthday is next week. She’s really looking forward to seeing you both.
