Found a lovely, neutral grey corner sofa on that site, Made.com. Seems quite reasonable. But the delivery charges! It's extortionate! I spent ages comparing prices. It’s madness. Online shopping… a necessary evil, I suppose. I’m hopeless with it myself. Far too much scrolling. I prefer a proper browse in a shop. Though, I must admit, I do appreciate the convenience of getting stamps online. Gets the postal worker off my back! He was hounding me for that quarterly payment. You should let me manage your emails, Grandpa. They're probably piling up. You kept saying you'd delete that one from the bank, but I bet you forgot.

Ach, this is the life, eh, Alistair? Just fresh air and good company. Been ages since I’ve had a chance to properly relax like this. Been buried in spreadsheets and press releases, you know how it is. Aye, I ken. Communications isnae exactly a stroll through the heather, is it? Though, I’d say this view is a darn sight better than staring at a screen. So, you said you were reading something… Scottish historical fiction, wasn’t it? I was! "The Rising of '45" by John Prebble. Absolutely gripping. I’ve always been fascinated by Bonnie Prince Charlie and the Jacobite cause. It's brutal, though – Prebble doesn’t shy away from the reality of it all. Makes you appreciate what we’ve got now, doesn't it? Though, a wee bit of romanticism still clings to the whole thing, I’ll admit. Have you read it? I have, years ago. Prebble’s research was impeccable. Remember when we used to argue about whether he romanticized the Highlanders too much? You were fiercely defending the depiction of their bravery, I was moaning about his tendency towards glorification. Aye, and you were practically accusing me of being a tartan-clad sentimentalist! I maintain, though, that their courage was undeniable. Anyway, it got me thinking about travel again. Remember that trip we took to Glencoe? The sheer scale of the landscape just… hit you. It reminded me of some of the scenes in the book. All that wildness, the sense of history… Glencoe was breathtaking. And tragic, of course. Learning about the massacre while standing there, looking out over those mountains… very sobering. We should go back, actually. It's been far too long. Perhaps next spring? I’d be up for that! Though, I was also looking at a map the other day, and I was considering Iceland. I know it's not Scotland, but the landscapes are just… other-worldly. Volcanic, glaciers, Northern Lights… it feels like another planet sometimes. Iceland! Now there's a thought. I've always wanted to go. It's definitely on my list. Though, the price of everything over there is enough to send you running back to Scotland. Remember that disastrous attempt to go to Reykjavik on a shoestring budget back in university? We ended up eating instant noodles for a week. How could I forget? We thought we were being clever, finding that tiny hostel miles out of town.

Honestly, Mum, I don’t know what to do. This application is just...brutal. So much jargon. "Demonstrate proficiency in parametric modelling with a focus on sustainable urban design principles"? I mean, come on! Oh, love. Let me see. Right. Yes, it  is  a bit much, isn't it? But they’re clearly looking for someone specific. This is Grayson & Hayes, isn't it? They do brilliant work, though. Remember that eco-housing project in Hackney? Absolutely stunning. That's the one! Which is precisely why I  want  it. It’s exactly the kind of thing I've been working towards. Sustainable, innovative… but this application feels like they’re trying to catch a fly with treacle. Well, treacle  does  stick, doesn’t it? Look, 'proficiency' just means you’re good at it, yeah? And 'parametric modelling'... you know what that is, don't you? You’ve been using it in your projects at uni and since. Yes, but it feels different writing about it. It's easy to  do  it, designing and problem-solving, but nailing the words… I feel like I’m lying somehow. Like I'm over-selling myself. You're not lying, sweetheart. You're articulating. You’re showing them what you can do, in a way they understand. Let’s break it down. "Sustainable urban design principles" – what do  you  think that means? In your own words. Right, okay. Well, it’s about… designing cities and buildings that minimize environmental impact, focusing on energy efficiency, using sustainable materials, considering community needs, creating green spaces... things like that. Exactly! See? You know it. Now, just write that. Don’t worry about sounding fancy. They want to know you  understand  it, not that you've memorised a textbook. And 'proficiency' - just say you have a strong understanding and practical experience using it. That’s… surprisingly helpful. You’re right. I'm getting bogged down in trying to sound like a textbook definition of an architect. Honestly, darling, they want a person, not a robot. And you’re a brilliant person. This job would be lucky to have you. Now, about that "collaboration and communication skills" section... I remember you saying how you successfully mediated that disagreement between David and Emily on your dissertation project... Oh gosh, yes. That was stressful. They nearly came to blows over the fenestration! Precisely! And you steered them back on course. That’s collaboration.

Cor blimey, Maureen, you look right peachy. Been ages since we’ve had a proper catch-up, hasn't it? This chair's a bit knackered, mind you, springs poking through somethin' awful. Arthur! Lovely to see you too. Don't worry about the chair, it's got character. And yes, it  has  been ages. Life just seems to whiz by these days, doesn’t it? How's your back feeling? Last time we spoke, you were moaning something fierce. Don't you mention it! It's fair playin' up again, I’m afraid. Damp in the bones, that’s what it is. This Norfolk weather, eh? Lovely in the summer, proper miserable come autumn. Should've bought that heated blanket young Barry suggested. But no, stubborn as an ox, I was. Damp’s the devil, that is. Remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road? Lived to ninety-two, she did, but the damp got her in the end. Achin’ joints and a cough that wouldn’t shift. Costessey used to be drier, mind you, before they built all these new estates. Concrete everywhere, no room for the ground to breathe. It’s true, isn’t it? Everything's changing so rapidly. Speaking of changes, have you seen what they're planning for the old airfield? They're going to build hundreds of houses! It's outrageous, really. Where will everyone park? Houses, eh? More concrete jungles. They’ll promise green spaces, of course. A little patch of grass and a few benches, and they'll call it a park. Don't trust 'em, Maureen, not one bit. Remember that "eco-village" they built near Wymondham? Promised the world, and it turned out to be a load of overpriced boxes. Politics, eh? Don't even get me started. Never been so confused in my life. One lot promises the earth, the next lot takes it away. Can't believe they’re still talkin’ about fracking. The planet's bleedin’ hot, and they want to dig it up even more! Honestly, it’s disheartening. And the cost of living! Don't even get me started on the price of eggs. I used to be able to get a dozen for a pound. Now, it’s nearly three! Fancy that. Three quid for a dozen eggs! It's daylight robbery, Maureen, pure and simple. And petrol… don't even get me started on petrol.

Right, so, the yoga studio. It's... progress, certainly. But are we sure about the flooring? It feels a bit…clinical, doesn't it? Less 'inner peace' and more 'operating theatre'. Aye, well, budget was tight, wasn't it? The vinyl was the best we could get for the price which allowed us to keep the cost down, and the landlord was breathing down our necks about getting it finished. It’s wipeable, though, which is important, you know, with all the sweaty poses and whatnot. I know, I know, practicalities. But we need to create an atmosphere, David. And atmosphere doesn't come from practicality alone. We’re aiming to attract a particular clientele—people seeking tranquility, well-being. Perhaps some rugs? Or even just a few colourful cushions? It doesn’t have to break the bank. Rugs, yeah, that's a thought. I reckon we could find something decent second-hand. There’s that charity shop down on Acre Lane, they often get decent stuff in. Something patterned, maybe? Not too garish, mind you. We don't want to frighten the chakras off. Precisely. And speaking of frightening… has the fire escape inspection been booked yet? I mentioned it last week. Urgent. Right, fire escape. Yes, I’ve put a reminder in - booked for next Tuesday morning. Had to chase the company, they were dragging their heels a bit. They need to check the access point from the yoga studio, as well, you know. People could get trapped if there's a blaze. Good. Absolutely crucial. We’ve got that pottery course starting next month, and they'll be stacking clay down there. Speaking of which - do we have adequate storage for the clay? That’s another thing that worries me – the sheer volume of stuff accumulating in this building. We could utilise that alcove by the server room, couldn’t we? It's a bit awkward, but it's space. I’ll measure it up this afternoon and see if it'll do. It’s just… remembering to lock it, isn’t it? Last thing we need is someone nicking a bag of terracotta. Indeed. And what about the bookings for the community garden workshop series? They’re proving very popular. I’ve had three inquiries already for private bookings. Aye, those are good. We need to market those better, I think. Something on Instagram, maybe? Brenda from marketing said she could whip something up.

This is lovely, honestly. Such a change from school lunches. Though, I do miss a proper coffee machine. This instant stuff just isn’t cutting it. Instant coffee? You're a teacher! You're used to surviving on the bare minimum! Remember those staff rooms, Emily? The lukewarm tea, the stale biscuits... Don't remind me, Rhys! Though I've upgraded since then. I’ve almost got a decent espresso machine at home. Almost. Still battling with the milk frother. You should have let me sort the coffee situation! I could have whipped up a proper Welsh coffee. Bit complicated for a week away, though, with all the equipment. Welsh coffee's a right faff, Mark. Too much brandy. Faff, is it? My boy! You've no idea the history behind a proper Welsh coffee! My grandmother used to make them for us when we lived in Singapore. Sweet, strong, and chased away the humidity! A little rebellion, she always said. Your grandmother, Dai, practically invented rebellion. Always stirring things up, that woman. Remember when she organized the protest about the library closing hours? Aye, that was a good day. We got the library open until eight! Worth a dram or two of whiskey, that was. You all are unbelievable. I’m surrounded by Welsh revolutionaries and questionable coffee habits. So, Mark, this roast chicken – it's absolutely delicious! What did you do to it? Apart from, you know, roasting it. A little trick my old mentor taught me. Dry brine it overnight. Just salt, pepper, a bit of thyme. Makes all the difference. The skin gets unbelievably crispy and the meat stays so moist. And a splash of cider vinegar in the last half hour – that's the secret weapon. Cider vinegar, eh? Not bad, not bad. You're learning, chef. Reminds me of my grandmother's Sunday roast. She always used a bit of apple juice. Same principle, really. You’ve put apple in a roast? That is sacrilege! Plain salt and pepper. Nothing else. Sacrilege? Come on, Ethan! A little flavour enhancement never hurt anyone. Besides, I can tell you've been a vegetarian for, what, five minutes? It’s very forgiving. These young ones! Always with the opinions. When I was your age, we were grateful for whatever was put in front of us! And there wasn't much varied, I can tell you. Mostly potatoes and cabbage.

Right, so, you're  serious  about this Florence trip then? Like, actually serious? 'Cos last time you got excited about going to Bruges and we ended up in Skegness, watching a pigeon fight over a chip. That was one time, Liv! And Skegness had its… charms. Look, I've booked the flights. Checked out hotels. It's happening. Florence, Renaissance art, gelato… what’s not to love? Gelato? Aye, that’s the selling point, that is. Still, Florence! It’s a bit… fancy, innit? For us? I were expecting you to want to go back to the Lake District again. Loads of sheep and scenic walks, you know. More our vibe. I love the Lake District, genuinely. But I figured, we've done the 'rustic British holiday' thing. Let's broaden our horizons a bit. Besides, your mum's been banging on about wanting to see the Duomo. Remember? Oh, Christ, aye. She's been showing me pictures for months, haven’t she? Always going on about Brunelleschi and perspective and all that. Sounds like a right headache, to be honest. But if it'll shut her up… I’m in. Are we taking nan this time? We talked about it. It’s likely a bit much for her, wouldn't you say? All the walking and the crowds. I think we should focus on us this time. Giving ourselves a proper break. Aye, that’s sensible. She’d complain about the pasta anyway. "Too much garlic," she’d say. "Doesn't agree with me." Honestly, you could give her a Michelin-starred meal and she’d find something wrong. Exactly! So, bypassing nan then. Right, I was thinking we try and catch that new Wes Anderson film while we're there.  Asteroid City . Your mum adores him, and I’ve heard it's visually stunning. Ooh, yeah! I've seen some clips. Looks bonkers, in a good way. Proper vibrant. You know what I were thinkin' though... while we’re abroad, we should send a ridiculous postcard to Chloe. Remember that advert with the llamas? Which ad? The one with the Renault? Aye! The one where the fella’s driving and suddenly, there’s llamas everywhere. I'm sending her a postcard with a llama on it, and just a wee message saying, "Llamas! Fancy that!" She’ll love it. She's obsessed with those adverts. You're incorrigible. That’s brilliant, though.

Honestly, Sarah, this whole NHS thing is just… a nightmare. I've been trying to get Mum an appointment with the rheumatologist for weeks. Weeks! And every time I ring, it's either “no appointments available” or “put you on a waiting list, call back in six weeks.” Six weeks! Her pain is getting worse, you know. Tell me about it. It's rotten, isn't it? I had to fight tooth and nail just to get my Harold seen about his dodgy knee. Ended up going private in the end, which wasn’t ideal, but at least he got a diagnosis. Not cheap, mind. Though the rheumatologist side of things… my sister, bless her, she's been battling fibromyalgia for years. The waiting lists for that are appalling. Exactly! And it's not just the waiting lists, it's the lack of communication. You feel like you're badgering them, begging for help. Mum’s just resigned to it, poor love. Keeps saying, “Oh, it’s nothing, dear, don’t fuss.” But I know it's not "nothing." She barely sleeps some nights. She's a trooper, your mum. Always has been. Listen, about my Harold… it’s been hard, you know? He's not himself. Went to the funeral for old Mr. Henderson last week, and barely said a word the whole time. Just stared at his shoes. Oh, Sarah, I’m so sorry. Mr. Henderson was such a lovely man. Remember his prize-winning dahlias? It's dreadful, isn’t it, seeing someone you care about grieving so deeply? My brother, Mark, he’s a right mess. Uncle George’s passing… it's hit him hard. He's always been the strong one, you know? The one who holds everyone together. Now he’s just… quiet. Aye, that’s how my husband is. He’s usually the clown, always cracking jokes, but since George went… it’s like someone switched him off. He keeps picking at his food too. Started that ridiculous juicing thing, you know. Green stuff everywhere. Says it’s "cleansing" him. I think he’s just trying to fill the emptiness. Oh, I know that feeling. Honestly, grief does strange things, doesn't it? My daughter, Emily, started doing Pilates. Absolutely obsessed. Says it’s about “releasing” something. I told her it just looks like a complicated way to sweat, but she gave me  the look .

Right then, that was a lovely meal, wasn't it? Mark, your roast potatoes were spot on again. Thanks, love. Just following the family recipe, you know. Years of refinement! Though, I could use a good glass of wine to celebrate my potato success. What are we having? Is it the Malbec? Please say it’s the Malbec! Very well, young man. You've twisted my arm. It is the Malbec. Though, save some for your Uncle David. He’ll want a taste after he’s told us all about his… adventures. Adventures is putting it politely, Sarah. It's usually a tale of near-disaster and corporate bureaucracy. So, about work… Things have been… lively. We're rolling out the new logistics system next month. It’s been a nightmare, honestly. The initial training sessions were a shambles. One bloke nearly threw his laptop across the room. Really? What happened? He couldn’t figure out how to log in. Simple as that. But then it turned into this whole rant about how technology is ruining everything, and he was going to go back to hand-written ledgers. It's the modern world, mate. You can't fight it. Anyway, the project manager, Kevin, had to practically drag him out of the room. Kevin, the one who wears socks with sandals? The very same. Ironically, he’s a tech whiz. Go figure. What about you, Sarah? Still battling rogue commas and misplaced apostrophes? You have no idea. I’m proofreading a textbook on astrophysics for a publisher. Astrophysics! I’m reading about black holes and quasars, and all I can think about is whether the author used ‘affect’ or ‘effect’ correctly. It's mind-bending. But it’s good experience. They're paying me a decent rate, which is always a bonus. I'm actually thinking about specialising in technical stuff; it seems to pay a premium. You're reading about space? Can you tell me about black holes? Absolutely! Well, a black hole is basically a region in space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. Imagine a giant drain… Hold on, hold on. Skiing! Are we going skiing this year? Last year was a washout. Don’t remind me. That blizzard in Austria… We were trapped in the chalet for three days. But it was fun, though! Playing board games and eating marshmallows by the fire.

Right, let’s see… where did we even  find  this thing? It was lurking behind the washing machine, wasn’t it? Like a forgotten archaeological dig. Absolutely. I’m amazed it survived the great decluttering of last summer. You’d think you’d have banished it to the attic. So much for minimalism, eh? Minimalism and I have a complicated relationship. It’s a concept I appreciate in theory, but the practice… well, look at this album. Proof that I’m a keeper of memories, however dusty. Look at this one! Japan, 2010. Remember that trip? Oh my goodness! You look so young! And look at that hair! What  were  you thinking, with that fringe? Don't remind me! It was a phase. A deeply regrettable phase. But look at the temple in the background. Kyoto, wasn't it? We spent hours wandering around there, completely lost, trying to find the best ramen. The best ramen  ever . Honestly, even the mediocre ramen in Japan was better than anything we've had back here. Remember that tiny place we stumbled upon, down a side street? The one with the grumpy chef who didn't speak a word of English? Vaguely. I remember amazing noodles. And feeling slightly intimidated by the chef. I think I stammered something about "oishii!" and he just grunted. Good times. It's funny to think that was nearly 14 years ago. It really is. And look! Here's that shot of the bamboo forest. It was so peaceful there, wasn’t it? I felt like I’d stepped into a different world. I’ve been trying to recreate that feeling in my photography since. You have, actually. Your landscape shots have that same sense of stillness, that quiet beauty. Remember when you started practicing black and white specifically to capture that atmosphere? I do. It was a bit of a obsession at the time. Speaking of photography, do you think we should get a new lens for your camera? The 50mm just doesn't quite cut it for everything, you know? Possibly. Though, to be honest, I'm more focused on trying to capture pictures of  badgers  at the moment. Remember Uncle David's obsession? How could I forget? He spent an entire summer trying to get a decent shot of one. With a professional camera, mind you! He looked ridiculous, crouched in the garden at 3am with a massive telephoto lens.

Right, so, Ireland. Honestly, Galway was mental. Absolutely mental. Like a tiny, beautiful, perpetually-drunken party. Did either of you lot ever make it over? I did! A few years back, with my mum. Dublin was lovely, very… organised. Galway, I’ve heard similar stories. Not my cup of tea, to be honest. Too much potential for losing my phone. And potentially being arrested. Oh, I went! Last summer. With my cousin, Chloe. We went to the Aran Islands, which were breathtaking. Just… windy. Properly windy. We tried skinny dipping on Inis Mór. Skinny dipping? Seriously? In the Irish Sea? You’re a brave woman, love. Bloody freezing! Brave? More like foolish! It was freezing, yeah. But the water was so clear! And just… liberating, I guess. Chloe chickened out pretty quickly though. Headed straight for a pub. Classic. I can picture it. Sounds amazing, though. Makes me want to book a flight. Though I’m not sure about the skinny dipping bit. I'm a bit… delicate. You're more likely to freeze than anything else, Ethan. Anyway, speaking of cold places, how's Australia treating you, Liam? Still slinging coffees in Bondi? Still at it. Gotta pay the bills somehow, eh? And the view's not bad. Although, the relentless sunshine can get a bit monotonous. Honestly, sometimes I miss grey skies and drizzle. You're Aussie to the core, aren’t you? You'd complain about paradise! True, true. But a man needs a bit of gloom. Keeps the existential dread at bay. Speaking of dread… anyone else been watching that new zombie apocalypse series? "Rot & Ruin," it’s called. Bloody terrifying. Don’t even mention it! I had nightmares last night. Woke up convinced my flatmate was shuffling around trying to eat my brain. She was just snoring, actually. Which is a whole other level of terror. Sarah does have a powerful snore. Like a foghorn. I've considered investing in earplugs. Or moving out. My nan snores like a walrus. It's genuinely alarming. But she also makes the best cholent you've ever tasted. Cholent? Seriously? I love Jewish food. My grandma used to make this incredible kugel. It was like a cheesy, eggy noodle dream. My great-aunt Rose was a brilliant cook. Everything was homemade, from scratch. She used  Claudia Roden’s  “The Book of Jewish Food” religiously. Have any of you read it?

Right, so, this border security thing… honestly, it’s mad, innit? I was reading this report, and the amount of time and money being spent on, like, facial recognition at airports... seems a bit performative, doesn't it? Like, it  looks  like they’re doing something, but are they actually stopping anything substantial? It’s a complex issue, Liv. It’s not just about  stopping  things, though. It’s about deterring, about projecting an image of control. Facial recognition has its place, imperfect as it is. The volume of international travel is just… staggering. The potential for issues is immense. Think about it, before these things, a passport wasn't even consistently checked. Aye, I get that, the volume is immense. But the report highlighted a load of false positives. Loads of people being flagged incorrectly. And a lot of the actual serious issues – the human trafficking, smuggling – they’re bypassing these fancy systems completely. They're using more… analogue methods. True, the accuracy is a concern. But the systems are constantly evolving. Machine learning, AI... they’re getting better at identifying anomalies, at spotting patterns even before a human would. It’s a layered approach, you see. Facial recognition is just one layer. Think about the data analytics, cross-referencing passenger manifests with known watchlists… See, that data analytics bit worries me even more! Where’s all that data going? Who’s accessing it? It's ripe for abuse, isn't it? Feels like we’re slowly sleepwalking into a surveillance state. Fancy a game of that new Forza? I finally got it, and I'm properly addicted. Better than staring at endless reports about border controls, anyway. Forza, eh? Tempting. My Sims game's been sucking up most of my time lately. I'm trying to build a proper functioning eco-village. It's surprisingly stressful. You know, optimizing the logistics of renewable energy and sustainable agriculture… far more taxing than my PhD sometimes. You are mental! Sims? Seriously? I’d rather face a border control guard than try and manage a virtual farm. Though, remember Alton Towers last year? We need to go back. The Nemesis is still calling my name. Alton Towers… that was… intense. My stomach hasn't fully recovered. I'm not sure I’m ready for another rollercoaster showdown. Maybe something a little more… sedate? Thorpe Park perhaps? They've got a new VR experience, apparently.

Oh, this is just what I needed. Proper fish and chips. Cambridge ones are surprisingly decent, aren’t they? Better than I expected, anyway. They are, yes. Much better than that dreadful place near the market square. So, how's the rowing going? You were so keen to give it a whirl. It's... challenging. Utterly and completely challenging. I mean, I knew it would be a bit of a workout, but honestly, I feel like I’ve aged ten years after each session. The instructor, bless him, is very patient, but the coordination! Getting the timing right with everyone feels impossible. I can imagine. It does look incredibly complicated from the bank. Remember that kayaking trip we did in the Lake District? That felt simpler, somehow. Just you, a paddle, and a whole lot of water. Don't remind me! I nearly capsized three times! Still, it was lovely, wasn't it? Sunshine, and those incredible views… I need some proper waterproof trousers for rowing though. The spray gets  everywhere . I ended up looking like a drowned rat last Tuesday. Absolutely. Have you looked at Rohan? They’ve got some excellent outdoor gear. A bit pricey, admittedly, but worth it if you’re going to be spending a lot of time getting soaked. I’ve got a good pair of waterproofs myself – bought them for teaching outdoor lessons years ago. I’ll bring them round if you fancy trying them on. Oh, you're a star! That would be brilliant. It's just, everything feels so specialist. I don't want to spend a fortune if I give up after a month. Well, thinking about specialists... it was so lovely meeting your cousin, Eleanor, last week for the first time. Such a sweet girl. I'd no idea your mum had a sister. I know! It was all a bit mad. Turns out, my grandmother had her out of wedlock and gave her up for adoption. Mum only found out about her a few years ago when Eleanor’s adoptive parents tracked them down. Awkward family dinners, anyone? A bit! But Eleanor seems lovely and didn't show any awkwardness. Though, I do feel for your mum – so much to process, decades later. It's incredible that families can carry such secrets. It is. It’s made me think about all the things we  don’t  know about our family history.

Honestly, Dad, it’s like nobody communicates properly anymore. It's all emojis and abbreviations. "LOL" and "OMG" and… I saw someone use "IYKYK" the other day. What even  is  that? IYKYK, love? "If you know, you know." Typical internet nonsense, isn't it? Back in my day, if you had somethin' to say, you  said  it. No need for little pictures and made-up words. You’d be writin’ a proper letter. Remember those? A letter? Dad, that’s prehistoric! It takes ages. A text is instant. Plus, all my mates are like that now. Even Mrs. Davies, my history teacher, sends quizzes over WhatsApp. Aye, well, times change. But a bit of proper communication never hurt anyone. Reminds me, I saw a documentary the other night about Morse code. Fascinatin’ stuff. All those little dots and dashes. Used to be the only way to send messages over long distances. Imagine relyin' on that for your results! Results day… don’t remind me! I’m proper anxious about it. I’ve been scanning UCAS Track every five minutes. Still says “awaiting results”. Trying not to think about the ‘what ifs’ you know? What if I don't get into Manchester? Now, now, don’t you fret. You’ve worked your backside off. You’ll be fine. Got yer student finance sorted, haven't ya? Remember to keep an eye on that, they can be a right pain sometimes. And Manchester’s a grand campus. I drove past it the other day, lookin' for a new stationery shop for you. Found a brilliant place, right near Piccadilly. Loads of proper pens. Pens? Seriously, Dad? I need a new phone more than pens right now. Mine’s practically on its last legs. Vodafone are being a nightmare. Signal’s gone completely dodgy. I'm considering switching. Vodafone, eh? Always dodgy. I've got Three. Seems alright. Remember when you used to collect those glass water bottles? Thought you’d ended up sellin' ‘em on eBay! Oh God, yeah! That was a phase. Had loads of them. Then Mum threatened to throw them all out. I think I did sell a few to fund new shoes, actually. Those Adidas ones I wanted. Remember I was moaning about not getting them for Christmas? Aye, I do. They were a bit pricey, weren't they? Reckon you’ve got more shoes than I’ve got socks!

Blimey, it’s good to be back in a proper living room, innit? This place is a palace compared to student halls. Liam's mum really does go all out with the decor. Tell me about it! Halls were…an experience. And yeah, Mrs. Davies is something else. You want a juice? Got some mango, apple, the usual. Mango, yeah please. Proper thirsty. Feels like ages since I've seen you, man. Last time was that Christmas do, wasn't it? Must’ve been. Time flies when you're dodging deadlines and trying to look vaguely intelligent in seminars. How’s uni going for you, then? Still battling with that computer science degree? You looked like you were about to spontaneously combust last time we spoke. Don’t remind me. Algorithm design is genuinely trying to break me. Professor Davies - no relation to Mrs. Davies, thankfully – is a sadist. Exams are looming, too. Proper stressing me out. What about you? Still coding up a storm? Heard you were working on some AI project. Yeah, it’s…interesting. I’m building a chatbot that can practically write essays. Ethical implications are a bit dodgy, but it's fascinating technically. It's better than staring at a screen all day just trying to figure out why a semicolon is messing everything up. Thinking of a presentation on it for next term. You should come, give me some brutal feedback. Haha, will do. Might need it myself. Listen, have you ever thought about… actually, I was reading something the other day, and it got me thinking. Japan. Seriously. Japan? Don’t tell me you've suddenly developed a craving for sushi and anime? Not entirely, no. But they’re so ahead technologically. Like,  way  ahead. And the culture… I’ve been watching some vlogs, and Tokyo just looks incredible. I'm starting to seriously consider a gap year, maybe head out there for a few months. Wow. That's… ambitious. Serious money, innit? And the travel… I always thought you were more of a pub-and-Premier League kind of guy. That’s me usually, yeah. But I'm feeling restless, to be honest. This whole academic grind is starting to wear me down. A change of scenery, something completely different… It feels right. I get it. I really do. Remember when we were kids, always talking about travelling the world? It’s cool you’re actually doing something about it.

Right, look at this! I found some photos from our Buckfast Abbey trip. Remember how ridiculous Uncle Arthur looked trying to take a selfie with the crucifix? Oh, bless his cotton socks! He did, didn't he? Said he was trying to "capture the majesty." The man’s got no sense of perspective, does he? It was lovely though, wasn't it? Such a peaceful spot. I'm glad we finally went. Been meaning to for years. Peaceful? It was a lot of steps! Nearly knackered my knees, I did. Though that monk giving the tour was a decent chap. Very knowledgeable about the history. Reminded me of old Mr. Higgins, used to come into the office. Sharp as a tack, that one. Absolutely. And the singing! That choir was incredible. I’ve put a few videos on Facebook, actually. Do you want me to send you the link, Mum? Yes, dear, please do. I'm still trying to master Facebook, you know. It’s all a bit much for an old girl like me. Keeps changing! Though I do enjoy seeing what everyone's up to. Bertram keeps reminding me to update my profile picture - it's still from 1987. Facebook, eh? Waste of time, if you ask me. All doom and gloom these days. And these politicians… David Cameron and his tax affairs! Utter disgrace, it is. Dodging taxes, the lot of 'em. Back in my day, you paid your dues! Tell me about it, Grandad. It’s all so disheartening. Speaking of trips, I was thinking, maybe we could do a cruise next year? Somewhere warm, somewhere relaxing. A cruise! Oh, that sounds lovely, doesn't it? Bertram's been talking about a Mediterranean one. But I'm a bit worried about the insurance. Getting older, you see, premiums go right through the roof. I know, it's awful. We'll have to shop around. I looked at some options last week. There are some surprisingly reasonable ones, as long as you declare everything. And we need to get travel insurance too, obviously. Can't risk anything. Cruises! Fancy. Used to be something for the wealthy, those were. Now everyone goes. Though I prefer solid ground, myself. Give me Wolverhampton any day. Remember the chip shop on Victoria Street? Best fish and chips you ever tasted. Not like this fancy stuff they serve now. Oh, Grandad, don’t start reminiscing about Wolverhampton!

Right then! Sorry I’m a bit late, the 27 bus was a nightmare. How were you both? Did you get settled in okay? It’s so lovely to see you both! Ah, there's our girl! Glad you could make it. Brighton’s been... well, Brighton. Usual chaos, innit? We’re alright, love. A bit tired, to be honest. That flight properly knocked us about. We’re grand, sweetheart. Just a bit pooped. Belgium was lovely though, absolutely lovely. Such a change from here. And so much… gentler, somehow. Oh, tell me everything! Seriously, I’ve been living for your holiday stories. Belgium, huh? I'm properly jealous. Did you do loads, Mum? Dad? We did, we did! Bruges was brilliant, you know, just like you see in the pictures. We cycled everywhere, mostly. Tried to avoid the tourist traps, but you can’t really escape ‘em, can you? Still, the chocolate was worth it. Oh, the chocolate! Cycling everywhere? Dad, you and cycling? I thought you'd have practically glued yourself to the cafe chairs the entire time! Well, I had to keep up with your Mum, didn’t I? She’s got more energy than a whippet! Besides, it was a pretty flat country, easy pedaling mostly. Though getting lost a couple of times… that was a bit of a trial. The Sat Nav went completely bonkers. That’s an understatement! It kept trying to take us down cobblestone streets, completely unsuitable for a bike. Honestly, it was ridiculous. We ended up asking for directions from a very patient baker. He drew us a map on a napkin. That was much more helpful than that infernal machine. Oh, goodness! That's hilarious. Did you get to try loads of Belgian food? I’m dying to hear about it. I saw on Instagram you were devouring mussels! Oh, the food! Absolutely wonderful. The mussels were amazing, of course. And the waffles… those were a religion. Crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, covered in chocolate and cream. I’m pretty sure I gained a stone just on waffles alone. And the beer! Don't forget the beer, love. Proper Belgian beer. Strong stuff, that. They know how to brew it over there, they do. You sound like you had a wonderful time! So, the markets? Did you visit any good ones? I’m always looking for little vintage finds.

Right, I think that’s the sauce simmering nicely. It needs another ten minutes, I reckon. Honestly, the smell is making my mouth water already. What do you think, darling? Too much chilli? No, smells fantastic, love. Just the right amount of kick, I’d say. Not enough to set my face on fire, but definitely enough to warm you up on this chilly evening. Did you manage to get those lilies I asked for? Yes, I did. They’re in the living room, in that vase I got from Mum. Aren’t they gorgeous? I went for the white ones, thought they'd brighten the place up a bit. They remind me of your grandmother's garden, actually. Remember how she always had lilies? I do. She had a ridiculous amount. The whole garden smelled like lilies and something else...that strong, powdery perfume she always wore. What was it called? Something French, I think. Chanel No. 5, wasn't it? So strong! Used to give me a headache as a child. Although, I do miss that scent sometimes. It just screams ‘grandma’ doesn’t it? I’ve been trying to find a more subtle perfume myself, something that isn’t quite so… assertive. You and half the women in England, probably. It’s the curse of trying to be effortlessly chic, isn’t it? Speaking of accent, I saw Fiona posted a picture of herself on Facebook yesterday. She's living in Bristol now, and her accent has completely shifted. She sounded practically West Country! Oh, really? That’s surprising. I always thought her accent was pretty standard. It's funny how places change you. I was listening to that podcast about regional accents the other day, utterly fascinating. Apparently, even within London, there are subtle variations. Did you know… Whoa, hold on! Let's not launch into a linguistics lecture while dinner's cooking. I'm starving! By the way, I noticed the fireplace isn't swept yet. It's getting a bit smoky when I light it. Should we book someone in? You're right. We really should. It’s been on my list for weeks. I’ll have a look online this evening. There's that company, "Sweep It Clean," remember? They seemed reliable. And they're local. Sweep It Clean sounds promising. Good thinking. Everything looks perfect. Just needs a little… …bit more salt, I think.

Well, it’s lovely to finally meet you both. ANON was so insistent we get acquainted, said it would brighten her day. It’s quite… eclectic, isn't it? Three complete strangers all chatting away. I'm Penelope, by the way. Harold. A pleasure, Penelope. Yes, it is a bit random, but ANON does have a knack for the unexpected. And you're from Gloucestershire, I believe? Almondsbury, wasn’t it? Seems a world away from Manchester, my roots. I’m Margaret. Good to meet you both too. Harold, Manchester’s not so bad, really. Loads of history. Penelope, Gloucestershire… that's awfully far south for me! I’m a Sheffield lass, born and bred. You wouldn't understand our dialect, I reckon. It’s a right corker sometimes. I’m sure I’d pick up a few phrases. I spent a year teaching English in Barcelona, you know. Picked up quite a bit of Catalan, actually. Though I’m afraid my Spanish is rather rusty now. I always regretted not going to Australia. It’s always seemed so… vast. Australia! Now there's a conversation starter. I spent nearly five years there, back in the eighties. Running a small importing business. Mostly men’s clothing, surprisingly enough. Suits mostly. Businessmen’s attire was their big thing. Queensland in particular. Broad shoulders, wide lapels… a different aesthetic than we’re used to here. Had a lovely house in Cairns. Right on the water. Queensland! Sounds idyllic. I often think about escaping to somewhere warmer. Though leaving Sheffield… it’s a wrench, to be honest. I lecture in philosophy at the University. It’s a good job, keeps me sharp. My sister lives in Brisbane now, she emigrated years ago. Says the sunshine just melts away any worries. It sounds positively heavenly. I always imagined myself teaching there, actually. EFL, of course. But the paperwork… the visas… it all seemed rather daunting. And frankly, in my position, acquiring a bank loan to move halfway across the world… well, that was a pipe dream. My husband… things weren't always easy. Loans. A necessary evil. Building the business in Australia required quite a few, to be honest. Had to convince the banks I was worth the risk. A young man with a plan, they said. Seemed to work. Though, I sometimes wonder if I made the right choice leaving Manchester. My family… It’s always a balancing act, isn’t it?

Honestly, Lizzie, this is lovely. Much better than that dodgy falafel place we tried last week. Vegan food in Poland… who’d have thought it? It’s a bit of a revelation, really. Aye, it is! Rzeszow's got a decent scene, doesn’t it? Better than Bury, definitely. Though, Mum's making a real effort with vegan baking now – her carrot cake is surprisingly good. So, you were saying about Instagram? You’re still finding it baffling, are you? Baffling is putting it mildly. It’s an utter vortex of… of curated happiness. Everyone seemingly has a perfect life, perfect holidays, perfect avocado toast. And I’m just… well, me. Sitting here eating lentil soup. Perfectly pleasant lentil soup, mind you, but still. I tried to follow that Gemma Collins woman, you know, "The GC?" And it was just an endless stream of teeth and sparkling things. Oh, Gemma. Aye, she’s… a lot. You don't have to follow influencers, love. Just follow people you actually know. I’ve got a few of my former students on there, it’s nice to see what they’re up to. And loads of animal rescue accounts - that's good for the heart. Don’t feel pressured to perform, you know? Just post a picture of your soup if you want! I wouldn’t dare! It would require me to  take  a picture, then to  upload  it. The technology frightens me, frankly. It's all so... fleeting. I rather prefer a good book. Have you finished that Naomi Klein book I lent you? Nearly! It's brilliant, honestly. Really makes you think about the climate crisis in a new way. But it’s a heavy read, so I’ve been balancing it with some lighter stuff. I’ve been obsessed with this podcast lately – "You're Wrong About." Have you heard of it? "You're Wrong About"? No, I haven't. What’s it about? I do enjoy a good podcast. I've been listening to that "Desert Island Discs" again. It's so comforting, hearing people talk about the music that shaped them. It’s brilliant. It takes historical events - like the OJ Simpson trial or the Challenger disaster - and re-examines them, looking at the media narratives and how they were wrong. It’s fascinating and really well-researched. It changes how you see things. Quite thought-provoking, actually, like that Naomi Klein book!

Right, you two, settle down a bit, please. We need to sort out this weekend. Swimming on Saturday, definitely. And then…Sunday is a bit trickier. Can we play with ANON more? Please, Mummy? She’s got the sparkly stickers! Yeah! And she lets me build the  very  tall ones! Not like Daddy, who knocks them down. Your Daddy does tend to be a little enthusiastic about architectural deconstruction, doesn't he? Yes, you can play with ANON more. She's brilliant, isn't she? She's such a wonder with you both. We're so lucky to have her. But Sunday... I was thinking we could try and get a photo for your Blue Peter badges. Remember? The one that shows you doing something 'amazing'? We could build a HUGE tea towel tower! Like, bigger than the house! Yeah! And then ANON could take the picture! That's a fantastic idea, Finn! But perhaps a slightly... smaller tower, darling? Something we can actually photograph without blocking out the sun. Speaking of, did you know ANON’s travelling circus is coming to Cambridge next week? A circus?! Really? With clowns and elephants? Well, I don't know about elephants, Pippy. But I'm sure there’ll be something amazing. It might be something to do for your Blue Peter badges. Although, getting photos in a circus might be a bit chaotic, wouldn’t it? Is it the same circus as last year? The one with the man who swallowed a sword? No, darling, that was a different one. This one's a proper travelling circus – tents and everything. It's rather exciting, isn’t it? Although...this reminds me, we really need to look at getting your passports sorted. If we want to actually  go  anywhere exciting. Passports? Why do we need those? Well, darling, you need a passport if you want to go on holiday to places like France, or Spain, or even… China! China? Do they eat spiders in China? ANON said they do. I don't know about spiders, Finn. But she did mention something about eating… old eggs, didn’t she? Apparently,  century  eggs are quite a delicacy. Century eggs?! That’s gross! Are they actually a hundred years old? Not quite a hundred years, sweetie. They’re preserved for a few weeks. Restoring them so they have a... distinct flavour. Don't worry, we're not going to be eating century eggs anytime soon!

Honestly, Liam’s being a right drama queen, innit? Liam? Your Liam? What's he being dramatic about  now ? He’s usually pretty chilled. Aye, well, not so much chilled right now. He’s…he's got himself in a state. A proper state. He won’t tell me exactly what’s wrong, just keeps moping about and saying he's 'feeling off'. "Feeling off"? Yorkshire understatement of the century, I reckon. What’s he  doing  differently? Diet? Exercise? Nah, nothing like that. He's just…well, he's not been himself in bed. You know. And he's getting right wound up about it. Keeps saying he's useless and stuff, which is, like,  not  helpful. Oh, yeah? Like, struggling to… you know… perform? Basically, yeah. He’s mortified. Keeps saying it's all in his head, that he’s just anxious. But then he gets more anxious  about  being anxious, and it makes it worse, doesn't it? Honestly, it's a right circle. It can be, yeah. It absolutely can be. Anxiety  does  play a massive role. Stress, pressure… it all affects things. There are loads of causes, you know? It's not always just about… well, you know. I know, I know. But he’s just so down about it. Keeps saying I won’t fancy him anymore. Right drama, I'm telling you. I’m proper laughing at him, but also worried, 'cause he's genuinely upset. He’s got his knickers in a twist, proper. Don't laugh  too  much! Seriously though, have you told him to see a doctor? Like, a proper one? I've hinted at it. Gently, mind. Don’t want to make him feel worse. He’s got this image of being this strong, capable fella, and I reckon him going to the doctor would feel like admitting defeat, you know? I get that. But it’s not defeat. It’s being smart. There could be an underlying medical thing going on – low testosterone, or something. Even dietary deficiencies. There's a load of possibilities. And even if it  is  just anxiety, a doctor can recommend things like therapy or medication to help. Yeah, you're probably right. He’s just… stubborn. Proper Yorkshire stubborn. He’ll be thinking "I can sort this myself, lass." Well, tell him gently that sometimes, we  need  a bit of help. Even the strongest lads. And honestly, showing you care enough to suggest seeing a professional, that’s a good thing, not a bad one.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a walking Slimming World leaflet. Every conversation revolves around ‘syns’ and Healthy Extras! Did you know a bag of Pork Scratchings is almost 18 syns?! Who eats a whole bag?! Don't start, Elara. I’m battling enough internal demons today. I'm thinking cauliflower cheese with a roast this weekend. Are you in? We could do a Quorn roast – they’ve really upped their game, haven't they? Sainsbury's have the best range now, I reckon. Ooh, cauliflower cheese! Yes, please! Roast potatoes definitely required. And a Yorkshire pudding. But…syns! I’m already dreading calculating them. Can we use Frylight? That's only one syn per spray, right? Absolutely Frylight. And loads of herbs and spices. That’s where you can really bulk up the flavour without adding loads of syns. I’ve got this amazing spice blend I found from Holland & Barrett, it’s…well, it tastes like sunshine and happiness. You and your dramatic descriptions! Right, sunshine and happiness spice blend it is. I need it. This week at work has been… intense. We're behind on our targets and Brenda is breathing down my neck. She's convinced I'm slacking because I'm visibly losing weight, ironically! That's ridiculous! People are just jealous. Have you hit your targets consistently before? Show her the data. Honestly, some people have zero perspective. Speaking of losing weight, these scales are playing up again. I swear they add two pounds when I step on them. Tell me about it! Mine think I’m gaining weight when I'm clearly sweating buckets at the gym. Maybe we should just throw them out and embrace the unknown. Tempting. But then we'd never know if we're making progress. Okay, distraction! Tea? I'll put the kettle on. And you know what would be amazing? A little drizzle of that 0-calorie syrup over the cauliflower cheese. Controversial, I know, but… Oh, please no. Artificial flavouring gives me the creeps. It's just… not right. I'd rather deal with the syn calculations. Though, actually, while you’re at it, Siri, add ‘check tax return’ to Saturday’s schedule. I've been putting it off. Done. And add ‘treat day research’! We need to plan something epic for Saturday. Film? Restaurant? Somewhere with mountains of chips, maybe? Chips would be amazing! But we’re going to be so full of cauliflower cheese that we won’t be able to move.

Right, so, Greece it is? Santorini looks absolutely breathtaking. Though, honestly, after the year we've had, I’m not sure I can handle anything  too  idyllic. I need a bit of grit, you know? Somewhere with a good taverna and a bit of a story. Greece is good. Reliable sunshine, decent food. Santorini is a bit pricey though, isn’t it? We could look at Crete. More varied, a little less… picture postcard perfect. And I’m really craving some proper Greek salad. The ones we get here are just pathetic. You’re right about the price. Crete sounds lovely, actually. More history, too. We should research some walking trails. I'm not going to lie, I'm desperate to get back into hiking. This job... it’s just sitting glued to a chair all day. Absolutely. And a good bit of walking would do us both good. Shake off the cobwebs. Say, about Crete… what if we rented a little villa out in the countryside, somewhere remote? No pool, just a view and a donkey or two? A donkey or two? You’re mad. Though, the idea of being properly remote… it's appealing. No tourist traps, no rowdy bars. Just us, good food, and… donkeys. I’m still leaning towards Crete, definitely. But let’s browse some options with a bit more… practicality. What do you reckon about the whole political landscape at the moment, by the way? It's all a bit grim, isn't it? Don’t get me started. It’s a complete mess. I was reading an article this morning about… . Honestly, sometimes I think it'd be more productive to spend my time learning Ancient Greek and just moving there permanently. You and your drastic measures! Although, a sudden relocation to a Greek olive grove  does  sound rather tempting. It’s just… my mum would have a heart attack. She’d adjust. Eventually. Speaking of drastic measures… you’ve been looking at those tattoo designs again, haven't you? I saw a flash of something floral on your tablet earlier. Just browsing. Don’t be ridiculous. It's just… I've been thinking. A tiny wildflower on my wrist. Something small and simple. A reminder of spring. A wildflower. That’s actually quite nice. Not a giant phoenix rising from the ashes, then? Don’t tempt me! But seriously, it would be nice, wouldn’t it?

Right then, Nigel. Let’s tackle this weekend. I was thinking, perhaps a gentle stroll along the river on Saturday morning? Nothing too strenuous, you understand. My knees aren't what they used to be, you know. Then, a bit of lunch at The Old Bell? Their fish and chips are remarkably good, even if a tad pricey. Sounds lovely, Charles. The river’s a good shout. Better than wrestling with the garden, that’s for sure. The bindweed's taken over the roses again. Honestly, it’s like a botanical siege. The Old Bell is fine, although I still maintain The Swan does a better batter. Just saying. Saturday lunch, sorted then. What about Sunday? Anything planned? Sunday… well, I was hoping we could perhaps look at getting that old gramophone working. You know, the one your Aunt Mildred left me? It's been sitting in the spare room gathering dust. I suspect a bit of elbow grease and your technical expertise might bring it back to life. It would be rather charming, wouldn't it, to have a bit of proper music around? None of this modern… noise. Mildred’s gramophone? Right. That’s a project. Last time I looked at it, it was a tangle of wires and dried-up wax. But aye, I'll have a go. Need a proper toolkit for that job, though. Might have to dig out the old soldering iron. Just promise you won’t start playing those scratchy opera records at full volume. My ears aren't as resilient either. My dear Nigel, I would never! Perhaps some Gilbert and Sullivan, at most. Speaking of things arriving, look what came today! Postcard from Scotland. Absolutely breathtaking, wasn’t it? From that walking trip I told you about. Reminded me of a Turner painting. Aye, that's stunning. You got some decent weather then, did you? I was following the news – looked like they’d had a bit of a downpour. Glad you managed to escape it. Still, makes you think, doesn't it? About all that talk of Scottish independence again. Indeed. A rather thorny issue. I confess, I'm rather ambivalent. On the one hand, I understand the desire for self-determination, the pull of national identity. But on the other, the practical implications... the economic disruption... it's all rather unsettling, isn't it? Especially with everything else going on in the world.

Right then, you two. Are you enjoying your creative afternoon? It’s lovely to see you both so engaged. Look, Mummy! I drew a chair! It's for… for people who need a chair. Mine's a spaceship chair! It goes to the moon! And… and it has a comfy seat for everyone. That’s brilliant, both of you! Absolutely fantastic. You know, we were talking at school today about the Syrian refugees, and how many people have lost everything, including their homes and their… well, their chairs, really. It made me think – what if we each drew a chair and donated them? We could send them to a charity that helps refugees, and maybe they can use the drawings to brighten up a shelter or something? Brighten up? Like… make it less sad? Exactly, sweetheart. Like a little bit of sunshine. What do you think? Can mine be the spaceship chair? So they can go on adventures! Absolutely, darling. Your spaceship chair is the perfect adventure-mobile. But maybe we could also draw some normal chairs too? Like the ones we sit on at the dinner table? This one’s like the dinner table chair! But pink! Is pink okay? Pink is  perfectly  okay! Chairs come in all colours. We’ve got wooden chairs, metal chairs, plastic chairs… all sorts! Do you remember when Gran showed us that antique rocking chair in her house? It was so old! It creaked! And Gran said it was for telling stories. She did! It was lovely. But for our refugee chairs, we need ones that are strong and sturdy. The kind that can hold lots of people and last a long time. Think about it, what makes a good chair? It needs to be… not wobbly! Like mine might be. That’s a very good point! Strong legs are important. And a flat seat! Nobody wants to try and eat their dinner on a bumpy seat, do they? It needs arms! So when you're tired, you can rest. Like when I’m drawing! My arms get tired. You're both thinking like engineers! Absolutely brilliant observations. Now, about school… I know you both have some tests coming up. Have you been feeling okay about those? I don’t like the spelling test. Spelling is hard. It can be, love. But we can practice together. We can do it as a game! Maybe we can even draw silly pictures to help you remember the words.

Right, that was a properly bizarre email from Chloe. Apparently, Mark’s decided he wants to try hypnobirthing. Hypnobirthing! Honestly, I thought that was something Gwyneth Paltrow would recommend. Hypnobirthing? Seriously? Mark? The man who nearly fainted when he saw a spider last week? Exactly! He says he wants to be a "supportive birthing partner" and "tap into his inner zen." It's all very… earnestly awkward. Chloe’s just rolling her eyes, bless her. She said she’s going along with it mostly to keep the peace. Poor Chloe. Can’t imagine navigating that. Though, you know Mark, he's probably read some article online and become utterly convinced it’s the only way to ensure a blissful, pain-free delivery. That's exactly what I pictured. It's just so… not him. Remember when we were at uni and he was terrified of pigeons? He'd practically sprint across campus to avoid them. Oh god, yes! He used to claim they had ‘malevolent eyes.’ It’s a stark contrast to chanting affirmations and visualising peaceful meadows, isn't it? So, how’s your marking going? I was buried in student essays all afternoon. One lad actually cited Wikipedia as a primary source. Don't even get me started. It's a battlefield out there. I’ve got a mountain of dissertations to wade through – mostly regurgitated summaries of rather obscure articles. It’s draining. I’m thinking of incorporating a ‘source credibility’ workshop into next year’s course. That’s a brilliant idea. You should! They genuinely seem to think anything they can find online is gospel. It’s concerning. I’m trying to be encouraging, pointing out what they  did  do well, but sometimes I just want to scream. I know the feeling. It's the relentless effort with so little genuine understanding that gets to you. Did you hear back from Sarah about the weekend? No, haven't. I sent her a text earlier, just checking if she's still up for dinner on Saturday. She mentioned something about needing to confirm with Liam before committing. You know how Liam can be, last minute cancellations are his specialty. Oh, the eternal Liam conundrum. I'm starting to think he operates on a completely different timeline. It would be lovely to see them though. It feels like ages since we all got together properly. It really does. We need to make more of an effort.

Honestly, darling, you’re pulling my leg. Policemen believing in ley lines? Really? It’s straight out of a Benny Hill sketch! No, seriously! I overheard it in the pub last week, down in Wicken Fen. A couple of local bobbies, having a pint after their shift. Apparently, there’s a whole thing about this area, about ancient pathways and places of power. One of them was absolutely convinced it explained why there were so many reports of…  unusual  activity. Unusual activity? Are we talking crop circles and little green men, or just the occasional rogue sheep? A bit of both, apparently. One of them was going on about how ley lines might be influencing the sheep's grazing patterns! You know, making them gravitate towards certain points. Oh, bless them. It’s just… fantastically absurd. It reminds me of my grandmother. She insisted that if you saw a magpie, you had to immediately apologize to it. Something about insulting their ancestors. My mum was the same with black cats! Utterly terrified. She'd cross the street if she saw one. Said it was bad luck. Which, I’m sure, contributed to a childhood of me deliberately seeking out black cats just to wind her up. You scamp! See? Superstition is just… human, isn’t it? A way of trying to make sense of things when things are chaotic. Like, the university are desperately trying to make sense of this ridiculous publicity stunt they’re planning for the anniversary. The one with the giant inflatable brain floating over the campus? The one you said was going to attract more ridicule than celebration? Precisely! They genuinely think it's a good idea. Something about "injecting a sense of playful learning" into the student experience. It looks like a giant, sad, deflated jellyfish. I told them. I pointed out it looked like a brain that’d lost the will to live. They said I lacked vision. Oh, you, the visionary! You’re far too grounded in reality. It’s probably a good thing, really. Someone needs to be. Imagine if you started believing in ley lines and giving apologies to magpies! I'm holding out for the giant inflatable badger. That would be much more Norfolk. Don't give them ideas! Although, with the publicity department, anything is possible. Are you thinking about booking that holiday to Greece? I found a lovely little taverna in Crete, apparently the food is divine.

Honestly, Dad, this new phone update is awful. Everything’s moved around. I can't even find the camera quickly anymore! It’s so frustrating when they “improve” things and it just makes it more difficult. A new phone, eh? Fancy that. These things are all too complicated for me, love. Just want to make a phone call, you know? And even that’s a struggle sometimes. Remember when you just picked up the receiver and dialled? Simple as that. I do, yeah. It's just… everything's online now, isn’t it? Work, uni, the bank… it all needs an app. It's a bit much sometimes. Oh, and speaking of complicated, have you given any more thought to hiring a van for moving? I was looking online, and the prices are ridiculous. Right, the move. Still haven’t sorted it, have we? Keep meaning to look at those removals companies. This place  is  getting a bit… much. All these memories, piled up. A bit like these model boats, really. Too many to keep, but hard to let go of. You’d need a big van to take even half of 'em. I reckon a smaller one'll do, although... did you see that big steam engine at the Great Dorset Steam Fair last year? Now  that  needed a van! Yes, it was incredible! I’m thinking of going again this year. It’s just a shame Nan and Grandad couldn't make it last time. Maybe we could try and get more of the family to go. Auntie Carol and Uncle Dave, at least? Aye, a good idea. Carol’s always up for a bit of a lark. Dave’s a bit quieter though, isn't he? Maybe we could tempt him with a little fishing trip beforehand. Get him out on the river, you know. Freshen him up. Been playing far too many computer games of late, I've noticed. He’s obsessed with that strategy game, it’s ridiculous! Honestly, he spends hours building virtual empires. I tried to get him interested in antique hunting, you know, since we'll be clearing out so much stuff... didn't work. He just said it was “too slow.” Antiques, eh? Now there's a treasurer trove to be found. I've always been partial to a good bit of brass. Got a few bits and bobs myself, tucked away in the attic.

Honestly, David, this is dreadful. They're really going ahead with it, aren't they? The library. Demolishing it for… what? Another block of flats? I saw the article, love. Shocking, isn't it? The council’s arguing it's "underutilized" and "financially unsustainable". Utter nonsense. It’s a community hub. People rely on it. Edinburgh wouldn’t be Edinburgh without those grand old buildings. Exactly! It’s more than just books, isn't it? It’s the reading groups, the children’s story time, the quiet space for students. Where are those people going to go? And the architecture! That Victorian façade is beautiful. It's worth preserving. These developers, they just see pound signs, don't they? They do. Sadly, they often get their way. I was reading an article online just now, actually, about a similar situation in Bath. They managed to rally support and get a historic building listed at the last minute. Maybe we should look into that for the library? Something to fight with, at least. It’s worth a shot. I’ve contacted my local councillor, but… honestly, they were quite dismissive. Said it was "progress" and that the council had already made their decision. The usual spiel. I’m thinking of starting a petition. A petition's a good start. We’ll get ANON to sign, of course. She'll be devastated. Remember how she used to spend every Saturday there as a child? Oh, yes. Surrounded by towering stacks of books, pretending to be a brave librarian battling a rogue dragon. Those were the days. Speaking of which, have you had a chance to look at any of those upholstery samples I left on the sofa? I need to make a decision about the new armchair. I did. Briefly. There were so many! That teal velvet was rather striking, but I thought it might be a bit much for the living room. Too… bold. I liked the linen in that muted grey. It’s classic, and it would go with practically everything. The grey linen  is  a safe bet. But I was hoping for something with a bit more personality. Something to brighten the place up. This weather's been so grey, it's depressing! I was tempted by that floral print, but I'm worried it’ll be too much with the wallpaper. Floral could work, if it’s a subtle one.

Right then, Hampshire countryside, lovely isn't it? Much nicer than battling the M25, I can tell you. Though I'm starting to regret suggesting this impromptu road trip. My back's complaining already. It’s brilliant, Dad! And your back will feel better when you hear what I got you! I’ve been dying to show you. Honestly, the lighting in here is dreadful for critiquing presents. Are we actually near that little antique shop in Beaulieu? I wanted to pop in later if we could. Antique shop, Sarah? You and your… well, everything vintage! Geoff, you’re driving us around the county for a hair stylist and an editor who wants to rummage through old china! Don’t be daft, Peter! It’s a family outing. A bit of fresh air. And yes, Sarah, we’ll try to get to Beaulieu. Although, beating your usual eagle eye to a good find might be a challenge. Now, what have you got for me, love? Ta-da! It’s… it’s a subscription to Classic FM! I know how much you love your classical music, especially when you're working. Thought it would brighten up your commutes. Classic FM? That’s… that’s absolutely brilliant, darling! Truly lovely. You shouldn’t have. Honestly, you really shouldn't have. This is perfect. Thank you. It’s much better than another tie, I can assure you. See? Thoughtfulness shines through, Peter. Sometimes it’s the simplest things. Though, a vintage gramophone would have been… striking. Always with the grand gestures, aren't you, Sarah? I'm surprised you haven't booked a trip to Vienna just for the music! It  is  on my list. What about you, Peter? Still glued to 'Escape to the Country' every evening? There’s nothing wrong with 'Escape to the Country'! It's wholesome entertainment! Besides, it’s inspired me to finally start that vegetable patch I’ve been talking about for years. Got my seeds ordered, even. Trying to grow courgettes, you know. A challenge, apparently. Good luck with that, Uncle Peter! They seem to take over the whole garden! I’m trying to learn a new braiding technique at the salon. Dutch braids, really intricate. Takes hours, though. Dutch braids, eh? Sounds complicated. Anything you want me to pick up while we're out? Hair products, perhaps? Nah, I’m good. Mum gets me everything I need.

Right then, Liam, let’s 'ave a proper look at this car insurance. It's a right pain, innit? This quote from Admiral… it’s lookin' a bit steep, even for a first-time driver. Yeah, it’s pretty crazy, Nan. I saw some others, but they all seem to have loads of extra bits you need to add on. Like, "voluntary excess" and "legal protection." What even  is  legal protection? Sounds like somethin’ out of a spy movie. Spy movie, that's a good 'un! Voluntary excess, that’s the amount you'd 'ave to pay towards a claim if you 'ad an accident. So, if the damage costs £800, and you ‘ave a £300 excess, you’d pay £300 and the insurance would pay the rest. Makes sense, doesn't it? Keeps your premium down a bit, usually. I think so. But what if I can’t afford the excess though, Nan? What if I’m in a minor bump and I just don’t have £300? That's a fair point, Liam, and a good thing to think about. You can get insurance  without  an excess, but it’ll be more expensive. It’s a bit of a balancing act, really. Legal protection… that's a bit trickier. It basically means if you're involved in an accident where the other party is disputing who's at fault, it'll cover your legal costs to fight your corner. Okay, that actually sounds useful. Especially if, you know, someone’s not being honest about what happened. Aye, it can be. But think about it, how likely is that to happen? Most accidents are just a bit of a muddle, aren't they? Now, 'ave you compared quotes from more than just Admiral? I've always found comparison sites can be a bit misleading. They might show you a cheap price at first, then add all the extras on at the end. I’ve looked at CompareTheMarket, GoCompare and MoneySuperMarket. I got a cheaper one with Churchill, but it was offering the absolute minimum level of cover. Like, third-party only. Liam! Third-party only?! You'll be properly exposed there, lad. You've got to 'ave at least third-party, fire and theft. It protects you if you damage someone else’s car, or if your wee motor gets nicked or burns down. Don't be greedy tryin' to save a few quid now, it'll cost you a lot more in the long run if somethin' goes wrong.

Jaysus, this curry’s grand, alright. But the chicken…it’s a bit… rubbery, isn’t it, love? Not the usual quality from Golden Dragon. Nah, it’s fine, Dad. More chicken for me then! You've been quiet all through dinner. Still stressed about that server migration? Quiet doesn’t even begin to cover it, lad. It's been a nightmare. Jenkins decided to implement changes without consulting anyone. I’m left to pick up the pieces, make sure nothing blows up. It’s relentless. You wouldn’t believe the emails I've been getting. Sounds awful, Liam. Seriously, you need to find a way to de-stress. Have you thought about those breathing exercises I showed you? Or maybe a walk on the beach like you used to do? I appreciate it, Sarah, I do. But honestly, just thinking about going back to work sets my teeth on edge. I keep feeling this pressure, like a vise around my head. I'm wondering, is there some proper scientific way to measure this? Like, a gadget or something that says, "Liam's stress level is currently 7.8 out of 10." There are apps for that, Dad! They track your heart rate variability and stuff. Apparently, it’s correlated to stress. I’ve got one on my phone. Heart rate variability, is it? Fancy. Is it any good or just another piece of software trying to convince you it's improving your life? It's a start at least, Liam. And thinking about it, remember what we were talking about last week? The marriage equality vote in Ireland. That was something genuinely positive, wasn’t it? Something to feel good about. Aye, a grand day that was. Seeing people celebrate…it was a genuine moment of pride. You know, I was reading up on it afterwards - the sheer number of people who voted 'yes'… it's just…remarkable. I wonder how many times the word "equality" popped up on Google that day? Probably a  lot ! It'd be an interesting search query. It would, wouldn't it? Still, doesn’t take away from the headache Jenkins is giving me. So…that new Suicide Squad film? Did you see it yet, Ethan? Nah, not really my thing. Too much… shouting. I prefer stuff with, you know, actual plot. Plot? Ethan, you're twelve! What do you know about a proper plot? I know it’s about more than just explosions and bad jokes, Dad!

Right, so, are we nearly there yet, Gran? My phone’s lost signal again. Honestly, these hills swallow everything. It's like being back in the Stone Age. Aye, lass. Not long now. Just past the next bend, then a bit further up. Takes your breath away, doesn’t it? This view from up there's worth all the winding roads. It’s well worth seeing Apperley Bridge. It's boring, Gran. Loads of sheep. And more hills. Why couldn't we’ve just gone to Manchester? There's a new arcade there. Honestly, Liam, you’d complain if you were given a golden ticket. Look around you! It's quintessential England. Think Shakespeare! Rolling hills, quaint villages… it’s practically begging to be painted. Shakespeare? Seriously, Dad? We’re stuck in a car, heading for a village with probably one pub and a very confused flock of geese. Shakespeare's not exactly relevant. I was thinking more about how much longer until I can get a decent signal to look at TikTok. Now, now, love. Don't be like that. There's beauty everywhere, even in a flock of confused geese. Remember when we used to come up here when you were little? We'd chase them in the fields! And your dad would be trying to take pictures, failing miserably, as always. They were artistic failures, I'll grant you. But I was documenting a precious moment! Besides, the light was terrible. You need to understand proper photographic principles, Emily. It's about apertures and shutter speeds... Oh, here we go. Dad’s photography lecture. It’s always a delight. Speaking of things that move, did you see that drone buzzing around earlier? It was nearly hitting the birds. It’s a bit dodgy, isn't it? People flying those things everywhere without thinking. Drones are cool! You can record yourself doing stunts. Aye, but they can be a bother to the wildlife. Reminds me, there were some awful reports about a flock of swallows getting disoriented by a drone near the canal last month. It's all about being mindful. Like when I'm delivering a baby, you gotta be super mindful. One wrong move... well, you know. Absolutely. Precision is vital. It's a fundamental principle in any field – management consulting, midwifery, even photographing confused geese. It's all about mitigating risk. Thinking of the EU referendum, for instance… the lack of considering the actual potential ramifications… Oh god, not the EU referendum  again .

Right, so I’ve been reading this article about cultured meat, you know, lab-grown stuff. It’s wild. Apparently, they're getting really good at it, and it could drastically reduce the environmental impact of farming. Seriously? Cultured meat? Like, actual burger patties grown in a lab? I've seen articles, but I always thought it was years off being commercially viable. Years, probably. But the progress  is  happening. I read a piece about how they’re trying to replicate the texture perfectly now - the marbling, the fat distribution. The ethics are fascinating, though. Exactly! It totally bypasses the whole animal cruelty argument, doesn't it? I mean, theoretically, you’d just need a small biopsy from an animal to get started, and then you're done. No more slaughterhouses. But… what about the environmental impact of  growing  it in a lab? Aren't those processes energy-intensive? And what about the resources needed to grow the cells? It can't be magically produced from nothing. Valid point. The initial energy usage is definitely a factor. But most simulations suggest, even with current energy grids, it could be significantly less impactful than traditional livestock farming. Less land needed, less methane emissions, less water. It’s a complex equation, though. It's just... the idea of not contributing to the suffering of animals is really appealing. I know we both try to be vegetarian, but it's not always easy, especially when you're out somewhere. And it’s not like the hunting industry is any less brutal, is it? At least with abattoirs, there are regulations. Regulations that are often ignored, let’s be honest. I was reading about undercover investigations at some farms - absolutely horrifying. Hunting feels… primal and performative. Like a trophy thing. Though my Grandad used to hunt rabbits. He said it was putting food on the table. My dad did too. He'd always emphasize it was about respecting the animal and using every part. Said he felt more connected to nature doing it than buying meat wrapped in plastic. It's definitely a different mindset than the mass production we see now. The disconnect is the problem, I think. People have forgotten where their food comes from. Absolutely. It's all so sanitised. Which reminds me, I'm feeling a bit depleted. I think I might need to up my Vitamin B12 intake. Anyone else taking supplements?

Right, who's in charge o’ this telly tonight then? 'Cos I reckon I've suffered enough o' yer romantic comedies. They're classics, Liam! And besides, you watched that thirty-hour documentary on… on pigeon racing yesterday. Don’t be givin’ me that. Pigeon racing? Seriously, Liam? That's... really niche. Aye, well, it's fascinating! The training, the navigation… it’s clever, innit? Anyway, I were thinkin’ we could put somethin’ on, like… I dunno, that new Marvel film everyone's bangin' on about. Nah. Too much explodey stuff. My head’s already achin’ enough. You know I get migraines with all that flashing. Remember last time? Ended up lookin' like a right mess. He did. Head throbbing, curtains drawn, moaning about the special effects. It wasn’t pretty. How's it feelin' today, Ben? Still a bit tender? Still a bit… fuzzy, to be honest. I've been tryin’ to do some online courses, see if I can get somethin' sorted, but it’s hard to concentrate with all the noise. It's dead frustrating. Aye, I know the feelin’. Uni's a right headache some days. Speaking o' online, I ordered a new controller for the PlayStation. Got a real deal on Amazon. Reckon it'll be here tomorrow. Perfect for Christmas games. Ooh, a new controller! Good shout, Liam! We're gonna need it. I’ve been absolutely smashed at FIFA lately. Ben's hopeless, though. Hopeless? I'm strategically playing a defensive game! It’s about patience, not frantic button-mashing. You two are just naturally gifted, I swear. Did you see I got me Mum that knitted scarf off Etsy? She'll love it. It's got reindeer on it. Etsy, eh? You're gettin' posh, Ben! Mum’ll be chuffed though; she loves a bit o’ Christmas tat. I’m still thinkin’ about what to get Dad. He's got everything. Maybe a new phone case? His is cracked, and it looks awful. Or a subscription to one of them streaming services he likes? A phone case is a good shout. Fancy one of them foldin' ones? Seen some right clever ones online. Shame I can't afford fancy things, eh? Just sittin' here, wastin' time. Keeps me awake though... keeps the fogginess at bay a bit. Don't talk like that, Ben. You'll get somethin' sorted, you will. Loads o’ opportunities out there.

Honestly, this Alumni Day is a bit much, innit? Four years running! But it’s good to see everyone, especially you, Liv! How was your flight up from Lincoln? Did the trains cause any bother? It was fine, actually. Surprisingly smooth. I pre-booked everything, so avoided the usual chaos. Though, Cambridge itself is  packed . Didn't expect so many people to descend on the Law Faculty all at once. It's like a conference! Are you staying for the evening drinks? Definitely! Mum dragged me into it, said it’s important to network. Networking! As if I need to network  more  at my job. I'm literally surrounded by linguists all day. I’m coordinating research projects, remember? It's not exactly short on talking! You seem to be doing alright in your admin role, then? Anything exciting happening down at the university? It's good, yeah. A bit repetitive sometimes, truth be told, but the team’s lovely.
