We’re actually starting a pilot scheme next month, running workshops for postgraduate students on improving their academic writing. It’s surprisingly high demand, apparently a lot of people struggle with the formal register. Speaking of things being in demand, how are things at Aylesbury? Is your nan still going on about you getting a "proper" boyfriend? Don't even go there. She cornered me earlier and launched into a full-blown interrogation about my dating life. Apparently, "researching linguistics isn't a substitute for companionship." Honestly, the woman! I told her I was busy cataloguing Proto-Germanic verb conjugations. I don’t think that resonated. How’s your dad? Last I heard, he was planning that trip to Italy? He just got back, actually! It was amazing. He went to Tuscany and Umbria, mostly small towns you wouldn’t find on a typical tourist trail. He took loads of photos – mainly of churches and olive groves. He’s already planning a trip to Sicily next spring. He was saying how much he appreciated the slower pace of life, just wandering around, soaking it all in. It made me realise how much I need a proper holiday. Something beyond a long weekend in Brighton. Brighton’s lovely, but it's hardly an escape, is it? I'm desperate for somewhere completely different. I was thinking about Iceland, actually. The language is fascinating – Old Norse influences everywhere – and the landscapes look incredible.

Honestly, Liam, I’m ready to chuck my laptop out the window. This Modernist Literature module is killing me. Killing me, I tell ya! Dramatic as ever, love. What’s got your knickers in a twist now? Another impenetrable poem by T.S. Eliot? Worse! It’s Burgess. A Clockwork Orange. I’ve read it twice and I still don't understand half of what’s goin’ on. All that “Nadsat” rubbish? My brain's melting. And the lecture today was just... a load of pretentious waffle from Professor Davies. Davies, eh? Yeah, he can be a bit much. Remember when he spent twenty minutes dissecting the symbolism of a teacup in  Ulysses ? Don’t remind me! It was excruciating. I swear, half the students were asleep. I was fighting it. I just feel like I’m drowning in literary theory. I thought I’d be enjoying this, you know? I chose it because I liked the sound of it, thought it'd be all creative and interesting. Now I just feel stressed. Look, it’s tough, I get it. Uni generally is. But you’re good at this, El. You always have been. Remember that essay you wrote on  Wuthering Heights ? That was brilliant. It wouldn't have been easy, either. Aye, but that was different! That was passionate. I  felt  Emily Brontë. This feels like...work. Like a job. Okay, so maybe you need a break from the job. Fancy getting a massage? I saw that place, “Zen Zone,” opened up on Otley Road. They've got good reviews, supposedly. Stress-melting massages. Exactly what you need. A massage? Now you're talkin'! That sounds heavenly. My shoulders are permanently knotted these days. But… wouldn't that be a bit of a waste of money? I should be revising, shouldn't I? When’s the deadline? Friday. And you have all day Wednesday and Thursday to revise. A few hours of relaxation will actually probably  help  your focus. You’ll come back to it fresh. Besides, you work hard, you deserve it. Treat yourself. You’re right, aren't you? You always are. Alright, alright. Let's book something. But if I fail, I’m blaming you and your stress-melting massages! Fair enough. I’ll take the blame. And I’ll book us both in, right? You need a bit of me relaxing too, you’re always on edge.

Right, nearly ready then. Bit more salt, I reckon. This stew’s smelling rather promising, wouldn’t you say, love? Though I do wish I’d found those rosemary sprigs I was looking for. Makes all the difference, rosemary does. Smells lovely, Dad. Really comforting, especially with this weather. Honestly, it’s gloomy out there. Did you see that article about the flooding in Yorkshire? Awful. Yes, dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. And the news from Calais…it’s just heartbreaking, isn’t it? Those people…they deserve better than that. All crammed in like that, trying to reach a life. Calais is a disgrace, it truly is. A human tragedy playing out right there on our doorstep. Politicians bleating on about borders and deterrents…it's all so short sighted. Used to deal with international teams back in my day, you know. Looking at the human element was paramount. Now... just numbers, really. It is, Dad. It's hard to wrap your head around the scale of it. I was reading about some of the children... it just makes you want to do something, anything, to help. Though what one person can do... We donated to the Red Cross, didn't we, love? It's something, at least. This bread is gorgeous, Sarah. Did you bake it? Thank you, Auntie Carol! Yes, I did. Tried a new recipe – sourdough with olives. Hope you like it. Olives in bread? Bold. Very bold indeed. Actually, not bad at all! Quite tasty, in fact. You've got a knack, you do. Better than I ever had. My baking used to be… sporadic, let's say. That’s putting it kindly, David! Remember that time you tried to make a Victoria sponge? The kitchen looked like a blizzard had hit it! Those were the days. Simpler days, perhaps. Though I'm not sure simpler is always better. Still, it’s nice to reminisce. Right, stew's ready! Everyone grab a bowl. So, Auntie Carol, have you and Mr. Hughes made any more progress with your plans for the holiday? You were talking about going to Cornwall, weren't you? We are! We’ve tentatively booked a cottage near St. Ives for a week in August. Just a relaxing getaway. The sea air will do us good. And hopefully, some decent cream teas. Cornwall, eh? Lovely part of the country. Shame about the tourists, though. Used to go there with my family years ago, before it got overrun.

Dreadful weather we’re having, isn't it, Rhys? Absolutely relentless. Makes you want to just burrow under a blanket and forget the world. Tell me about it, Alistair! Tredegar's been drowned, practically. More rain than I've seen in thirty years, and I’ve seen a fair few. Though, I suppose, having a bit of dreary makes the sunshine all the sweeter, eh? Keeps things in perspective. Perspective is a fine thing. Though, perspective doesn’t really help when you’re trying to decide on the grout colour for the guest bathroom. Grout? Now you're talking! What’s the dilemma? I’ve just finished the downstairs loo – finally, after months of procrastination. Went for a slate grey. Subtle, you know? Doesn’t scream for attention. Slate grey, you say? Interesting. I was leaning towards a beige, something to brighten the space, you see. It’s rather dreary in there. My wife, Penelope, is adamant that beige is ‘dated,’ though. She has a very definite opinion on these things, Penelope does. Oh, I know the type! My wife, Bronwen, she’s the same. Full of schemes and… suggestions. Slate grey is anything but dated, Alistair. It's timeless. And hides a multitude of sins when it comes to those inevitable splashes. What about the tiles? What are you working with? They're a mosaic, actually. Tiny little squares, mostly whites and creams, with a rather ostentatious fleck of turquoise. I feared beige would clash horribly. The turquoise was Penelope’s idea, naturally. Turquoise, eh? Right. Well, beige  might  look a bit… muted against turquoise. Slate grey will complement it nicely, I reckon. Gives it a bit of depth. We had trouble finding a decent tiler, though, you know. Ended up going with young Gareth from down the road. Bit rough around the edges, but honest as the day is long. Charged a fair price too. Tradespeople… a constant source of anxiety. We’re starting on the kitchen next. Penelope's decided to rip everything out and start afresh. Granite worktops! Underfloor heating! She's gone completely mad. We had a perfectly serviceable kitchen before. Granite! Oof, that's a commitment. Bronwen wanted that too, but I talked her out of it. Too porous, you see. Marble, now that’s something to consider. A bit more sophisticated. But you're right, tradespeople are a bother. We used a chap called Dai for the tiling – reliable, but slow as molasses.

Right then, who’s feeling brave enough for another one? That Vindaloo was a proper kick in the teeth, wasn't it? Nearly took the wallpaper off. Yeah! That was brilliant, Mr. O’Connell! My tongue's still buzzing. Can we have it again next time? It was way better than the korma you made last week. Don’t encourage him, Liam. Honestly. You lot and your fiery curries. Finn’s face was scarlet the whole time, wasn’t it, love? Red! Like a tomato! He cleared his plate, didn’t he? That's all that matters. Besides, strengthens the constitution. Builds character. I read something about it – the capsaicin, you see, boosts your immune system. Like a tiny army fighting off invaders. So, curry is like a superpower? Does it give you super speed too? Could I run really fast after beating it? No, Leo, curry doesn’t give you superpowers. Although, sometimes after eating it, I feel like I need one to deal with the inevitable aftermath! Seriously, Liam, maybe a bit less chilli next time, eh? Alright, alright, I'll ease up a bit. But where’s the fun in that? Thinking about it though, remember old Mr. Doherty down in Ballymena? Used to eat metal spoons, he did. Said it was good for his… something. Digestive system, I think. Mad as a box of frogs, he was. Don’t even start with that, Liam. Honestly, the things you read! Eating metal? That's just… disturbing. Finn, don't you even  think  about it. No! Yucky! Wow! That's like a different kind of superpower – an iron gut! But wouldn't it hurt? Like,  really  hurt? Aye, no doubt it would. He said it felt like… well, he wasn’t too clear on the sensation. Just that he felt… better. Crazy, I know. Speaking of feeling, you alright, Sarah? You seem a bit quiet. Just a bit tired. Looking after Finn all day is exhausting. I've got that ache behind my eyes, you know? And the constant worrying. Have you spoken to the bank about that night deposit box idea? I have. It's… complicated. They’re phasing them out, apparently. Security concerns, they say. It’s a grand shame, though. Used to be such a reliable system. Safer than leaving cash lying around. A night deposit box? Like in the movies? Where you drop the money in a slot and a secret robot takes it away?

Cor blimey, October’s flown by, hasn’t it? Feels like only yesterday we were swattin' away midges in the summer. And now it's Halloween! Remember when we used to dress up proper, Elsie? Not this modern nonsense. I recall a scarecrow one year, I did. Full of straw, I was, and a bucket over me head. Kids loved it! Oh, Arthur, you always were a card. Scarecrows! I was a rather dismal witch, I think. My mum made my costume, all scratchy and purple. But yes, the children did adore the effort we put in. It wasn't all about buying those ready-made outfits now, was it? It was about imagination. And those penny sweets! Remember those? Imagination is key, isn't it? My Year 8s are already planning their decorations. A lot of them just want to buy spider webs and stuff from the shop, but I’m trying to encourage some homemade stuff. I suggested they make paper mache pumpkins – a bit of a mess, admittedly, but good fun. They’re more likely to remember something they made themselves. Though, let's be honest, getting them to focus is a battle in itself. Paper mache sounds messy, Mr. Davies! I'm going as a unicorn. Mum’s helping me make the horn, it's glittery. We're going trick-or-treating in Costessey, but we’re probably going to end up at Auntie Elsie’s, aren't we? That’s right, love. Auntie Elsie here makes a right fuss, she does. Mountains of sweets. Don’t want you missin’ out. Costessey's changed a fair bit, hasn’t it? Remember when all there was was that old brickworks? Before all the new builds. It has indeed. Used to be a village, really. Now they're building houses left, right, and centre. It’s changed the feel of the place, hasn’t it? It's not quite the same. Though I suppose progress is progress. Do you remember riding ponies down by the River Tas, Arthur? We used to go every Saturday! Don’t I ever! Old Farmer Giles' ponies. Bess and Daisy. Little Daisy used to nip at your heels, she did. Scared you half to death, she did! I remember showing you how to hold the reins properly, trying to stop you from nearly fallin' off. Good times, Elsie, good times. My daughter, Chloe, used to be obsessed with horses.

Honestly, this is ridiculous. I thought leaving Maidstone at seven thirty would beat the rush, but look at this! A solid wall of red brake lights. Are we even moving? Aye, it’s a proper jam, love. Should’ve gone earlier, like I said. Dorset’s a popular spot, especially for this sort of thing. Steam engines, you know. Brings ‘em out in force. Don’t start, Bernard. Chloe’s right, it’s awful. At least the radio’s on, though. I like that oldies station. Thank goodness for the radio. At least something to distract from the sheer frustration. Mum, you were saying something about your aunt Mildred and the council housing? Oh, yes. Poor Mildred. She’s been on the waiting list for an 'assisted living' place for nearly two years now. Two years! And she’s become increasingly frailer. You know, she’s got that dodgy hip and the arthritis is worsening. She insists she’s fine in her own little terraced house, but it’s just not safe anymore. Climbing the stairs is a nightmare. Council housing, eh? Don’t hold your breath. They’re booked solid, innit? Always have been. Remember when my Nan needed a better place? Took her forever. Ended up in a private care home, cost a fortune. That's the worry, isn't it? It’s the cost. And the sheer inequality of it all. Aunt Mildred pays her council tax, she deserves a decent place. My friend's grandma is in a similar situation – a tiny flat on the third floor. It's just not right. Shouldn’t there be more affordable, accessible options? There should be, darling, but there aren't. And the waiting lists are ridiculous. They keep telling Mildred she's 'in consideration', but it's all just words. They say she needs to prove she's struggling, fill out forms, get assessments... it's exhausting for her! It’s a right shambles, the whole thing. When I were a lad, you knew you’d get something if you needed it. Now look at it. All paperwork and bureaucracy. And they haven’t built enough social housing, have they? Never have. Exactly! It feels like they’re deliberately making it harder for people. And what about disabled parking? I’m dreading trying to find a space at the Steam Fair. Last time, it was a three-mile walk from the overflow car park.

Honestly, this drizzle is relentless. Makes you really crave a bit of sunshine, doesn't it? Especially when you’re dreaming of getting your hands dirty in an allotment. Tell me about it! I was looking at pictures of raised beds online last night. Suddenly felt very inadequate, like I should already have a thriving vegetable patch. My mum always had the most incredible tomatoes. Oh, tomatoes are a must! Absolutely. Though, I’m a bit nervous about pests, to be honest. I’ve seen some really nasty things on gardening forums. Slugs, aphids... it's a bit terrifying! Don't worry too much! There are ways to deal with all that. Companion planting is brilliant – marigolds, apparently, keep things at bay. And copper tape around raised beds for the slugs. We can research it properly. This isn't a sudden, desperate plunge, remember? It's a project. A lovely, slow, project. Slow is good. I don’t want to feel overwhelmed. I’ve been looking at the council website for allotment plots, and there's a waiting list, of course. A ridiculously long one. Yeah, I knew that. I already checked. It’s about a six-month wait, give or take. But we applied! Got the confirmation email yesterday. Fingers crossed we get one – and a decent one, not some tiny strip right next to the compost heap. Oh, you are thinking ahead! A good plot is essential. Somewhere with decent sunlight, ideally. And water access would be amazing, rather than lugging buckets from home. Remember that time I tried to water my geraniums with a watering can? Nearly threw my back out. I remember! You looked like you were wrestling a particularly stubborn octopus. We'll need a proper water butt, definitely. And we should think about what we actually  want  to grow, realistically. Don't go getting overly ambitious with tropical fruit. No, no tropical fruit! Though courgettes… I’ve read you can end up with an absolute mountain of them. I’d hate for that to be our allotment downfall. True. We could stagger planting. Plant a few courgette seedlings, see how it goes, and then plant more if we need to. What about herbs? I love fresh basil in pasta. Ooh, herbs are a brilliant idea. Mint, rosemary, thyme…Definitely. And potatoes! My grandad used to grow the most amazing potatoes. Crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside. .

Right, so, listen to this. Liam actually… texted me. Liam?  Your  Liam? The one you said was about as romantic as a soggy biscuit? No way! What did he say? Don't leave me hanging, lass! Aye, well, he did. He... he asked if I wanted to go to that new climbing wall in Sheffield next weekend. Apparently, he booked it. For both of us. Seriously? A climbing wall? That’s… surprisingly thoughtful. He's trying, isn't he? See, I told you there was a decent bloke hiding under all that… well, Liam-ness. Did he say  why ? Is there a special occasion or something? Nah, just said he thought it’d be a bit of fun. Said he'd heard I was moaning about needing to get out more. Cheeky sod. But… I think I might go. Go! Go, go, go! You absolutely  have  to go! Even if he is a bit rubbish at conversation, it’s still a date, right? And climbing’s brilliant. It’s good exercise, you get a laugh, and you get to dramatically shout ‘Belay!’ at each other. What’s not to love? Aye, but what if he expects me to be all, like, super-fit and knows all the climbing lingo? I've barely climbed anything since Year 8. I’ll be a right disaster. Honestly, who cares? He knows you, doesn’t he? If he's genuinely interested, he’ll just laugh it off when you’re flailing around like a confused starfish. And if he's not, well, at least you've had a laugh trying. Besides, you're stronger than you think. Remember that time you carried Gran's massive pottery kiln up three flights of stairs? Don't remind me! I’ve got the back pain to prove it. Still, you've got a point. Right, well, I'll text him back then. I reckon I should say something... flirty, but not  too  flirty. Just be yourself, love. That’s always best. Oh! Speaking of being ourselves… remember how we were saying we should actually  do  something with Chloe and Maya this month? It feels like ages since we all properly got together. Aye, it does. We were all saying that last month too. Life's just been… hectic, hasn't it? Exams looming, Liam being Liam, everything. Hectic is an understatement. But we need to make an effort.

Right, listen to this. I’ve been grindin’ on Elden Ring all week - proper obsessed, I am. Managed to finally beat Malenia. Took me, like, twenty attempts, but I did it! Proper satisfying, that was. Twenty attempts?! Seriously, Liam? You’re mad! I gave up on that one ages ago. The Waterfowl Dance is just… cruel. I’m more into Stardew Valley at the moment, peaceful stuff, ya know? Rebuilding my farm, getting married to Shane. Much less stressful. Stardew Valley? That’s… oddly charming. I've been consumed by Cyberpunk 2077. It’s still got issues, but the world-building is incredible. And the fashion! I spent three hours customising my avatar yesterday. Got this absolutely mental chrome jacket. Cyberpunk, eh? Not my thing, mate. Too dystopian. I'm playing FIFA, obviously. Trying to take my Barnsley team all the way. It’s a massive pipe dream, I know, but a lad can hope, can’t he? They’ve signed a decent striker though, got him from Crewe. FIFA? Seriously, Tom? Still? You’ve been playing FIFA since we were kids! Don’t you ever get bored of the same game, year after year? I switched to Elden Ring to challenge myself. Nah, it’s different every year! New players, new tactics. Plus, it’s a good way to wind down after lectures. What about you, Anya? Still obsessed with farming? You should come watch some footie with us sometime, it'd be a laugh. I might, if Barnsley are playing. But my weekend's usually booked solid with uni. Loads of essays due next week. How's your course going, Liam? Still suffering with that module on Victorian literature? Don’t even remind me. Bronte, Dickens, Eliot… I’d rather face Malenia a thousand times than read another page of  Middlemarch . Absolute torture. Though, our lecturer is brilliant, makes it a little more bearable. He’s got this great Yorkshire accent too, proper thick. I know the feeling. My criminology modules are fascinating, but the reading list is insane. So much legal jargon! I spent half an hour just trying to understand the definition of  mens rea  yesterday. I’m thinking of watching the new Line of Duty series to de-stress. Speaking of de-stressing, anyone seen that new Netflix series,  Wednesday ? My sister’s raving about it. Apparently, it's proper creepy but brilliant. I did! I binge-watched it last weekend.

Right then, love. Let’s 'ave a proper natter, shall we? It's lovely to be 'ere in Cambridge, it is. Much nicer than that damp little flat you 'ad in London, isn’t it? Though I know you loved it, dear, you always did. Mum! Don’t start. It wasn’t  that  damp. And I did love it. It was central, and I was close to everything. But yes, this is nice. Peaceful. Did you manage to see that new Ridley Scott film?  Napoleon ? Oh, that! Yes, I did. Went with Doreen on Tuesday. Dreadful, I thought. Utterly dreadful. All that shouting! And the costumes… a bit much, weren’t they? Too shiny. And he didn't seem very nice, that Napoleon. Didn’t seem to care about anyone, did he? All about ‘imself, innit? I thought Joaquin Phoenix was brilliant. And the visuals were stunning, especially the battle scenes. It was long, I’ll give you that. Almost three hours! But it tried to be historically accurate, you know, showing the complexities of his personality and the political landscape of the time. Accurate? Doreen says it was full of liberties. She’s read all sorts of books about 'im, you know, Doreen. Always 'as. Thinks they glossed over the really nasty bits. And the romance! Barely worth mentioning, was it? All that banging and crashing… not very convincing, if you ask me. Give me a good Merchant Ivory film any day.  A Room with a View , now  that’s  romance. You and Merchant Ivory! Always. I get it, though. You like the elegance, the period detail. This was…grittier. It explored the darker side. What about  Wonka  then? Have you heard about that? Timothée Chalamet? Timothee…who-now? Oh, you mean that young man from Dune? The one with the lovely eyes. I saw something about it on the telly. Willy Wonka, innit? But not with Gene Wilder. That was a proper shame. Gene Wilder was brilliant. No one could do Willy Wonka like him. Agreed. This is a prequel, though. It shows him starting out. Apparently, it's much more musical. Think Paddington, but with chocolate. Musical, you say? Well, that  does  sound a bit more up my street. I do like a bit of a sing-song, don’t I? Doreen’s always dragging me to amateur dramatics, you know. We’re doing  Oklahoma!  next year.

Right, so, spill. How was the interview? You were proper nervous about it last week. Did you get the digital content role at 'Welsh Life' magazine? Honestly? It was… weird. Really weird. Like, intensely weird. But… potentially good weird? They loved my editing samples, which was a relief, obviously. But the interview itself… well, let me tell you. Weird how? Elaborate. I'm invested. Okay, so, first off, the interviewer, Mr. Davies – a lovely man, actually, very friendly – starts asking me about my favourite board games. Board games! Like, seriously? I was prepared for questions about SEO, content strategy, the entire digital landscape… but Settlers of Catan? No way! That’s mental. What did you say? You’re good at Catan, aren’t you? Remember that disastrous weekend in Norfolk when you completely wiped the floor with us all? Don't remind me. It involved a lot of strategically placed roads and petty arguments over brick. I mumbled something about enjoying the strategic elements. He seemed pleased. Then he asked me which DVD I’d take to a desert island. A desert island? Seriously? This is getting increasingly bizarre. I know! I panicked and said 'Pride and Prejudice'. It just popped into my head. He nodded sagely and said, "A classic choice. Shows good taste." It felt completely irrelevant. Honestly, the whole thing felt more like a personality test than assessing my suitability for a digital content role. It’s like they’d been watching ‘The Undateables’ and decided to apply the format to recruitment. You’re not wrong! That’s brilliantly bonkers. But hey, maybe they’re looking for someone who can think outside the box. That's a positive, innit? And they liked your work, so that’s huge. That  is  true. And I did get a really nice email later, saying they’re “very impressed” and want to arrange a second interview. See! Progress! So, you’re probably going to get it, then? Celebrating with a spa trip? I was thinking that fancy new one in Shoreditch – the one with the aromatherapy massages and the Himalayan salt room? Oh, that would be lovely. I deserve a treat, don't I? This job hunt has been draining. But first, I need to figure out how to answer the question, "If you were a cheese, what cheese would you be and why?" I’m genuinely worried that will be the next question.

Right, this is ridiculous, isn’t it? Honestly, this washing machine's decided it's on strike. Third time this month it's just… stopped. Mid-cycle. Everything soaked. It’s proper annoying. Problems again with the Whirlwind 3000? You’d think for the price we paid, it'd at least  attempt  to function. Did you try turning it off and on again? The classic. Aye, I did! Turned it off, turned it on, pleaded with it, cursed it… nothing. It just sits there, blinkin’ at me like a judgmental robot. I'm thinking we need to finally bite the bullet and get a new one. I was looking online earlier – the Bosch ones seem decent, apparently. Bosch are reliable. Definitely. Though, Cambridge is a nightmare for deliveries, isn’t it? Remember last time we ordered that shelving unit? The bloke nearly chucked it over the fence! Don't remind me! Sounded like a sitcom. Anyway, new washing machine aside... fancy a bit of lunch? I was thinking we could do that butternut squash risotto we both love. Got a big squash in the fridge. That sounds brilliant. I’m starving, to be honest. Been staring at these numbers for hours. My supervisor wants this section revised by Friday, and I’m not sure I'm even close to where he wants me to be. Apparently, the correlation isn't statistically significant enough. The bane of a PhD student’s existence. Tell me about it. Research is always about chasing a fleeting shadow, isn’t it? Remember when I was convinced that particular marketing campaign was going to be ground-breaking? Turns out, nobody even noticed it. Oh, the disaster with the pigeon-themed social media push? Hilarious, in retrospect. Speaking of disasters... how’s your mum doing? Did she manage to get the tickets for that Stephen Poliakoff play in London? Aye, she did! She's absolutely buzzing! She’s been going on about him since she saw ‘Our Mother’s Milk’ back in the eighties. She’s booked a train down next weekend. She'll be moaning about the price of the tickets, of course, but she'll love it. She says she’ll bring us back some posh biscuits. Good, that’s good. Tell her I said hello. I was thinking, after lunch, we could finally watch ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’. You’ve been wanting to see it for ages, and I’ve heard it's properly brilliant.

Honestly, it’s just… unbelievable. Another scandal. You’d think they’d have learned something by now, wouldn’t you? All that fiddling with the emissions tests. It's a bit like when I marked those student papers, and you find a pattern of outright fabrication. Just… dishonest. It  is  staggering, isn't it? The sheer scale of it. Millions of cars affected globally. And the deliberate deception. I’ve been reading up on it for a new article I’m editing - apparently, the ‘defeat devices’ were designed to detect when the car was undergoing testing and switch to a cleaner mode only then. Defeat devices. Lovely bit of terminology, that. Highlights the entire charade, doesn't it? Right from when I was working in planning, you’d see companies trying to cut corners, just to boost profits. They’d promise the world, and deliver…well, something else entirely. This is just a particularly brazen example. The oil industry has its own share of shady dealings, you know. Less visible, more systemic, perhaps. It’s not just about the profits, is it, Michael? It’s about the environment too. Think about the air quality, the impact on people's health. It’s all connected, isn’t it? Just like with the house prices here. They’re going up and up, driven by people moving up from the South, and it's polluting the character of the place as much as those emissions were polluting the air. There’s definitely a link, Mum. That influx of people from down South is contributing to the rising prices, absolutely. It’s pushing long-term locals out. Everyone's moaning about it. We saw it in Birkenhead too, though on a slightly different scale. Regeneration projects meant pushing people out with one hand, and then trying to entice new residents with trendy cafes with the other. Exactly. It's a cyclical thing. People want a 'rural idyll' - a picturesque village, peace and quiet - but they don't want actual  villagers , I suspect. They want something... curated. Hunsonby is lovely as it is. Losing that community feel, that’s the real tragedy. Building all these new houses, largely occupied by weekenders…it's not sustainable. Not socially, not economically. And the irony is, we're moving here to escape some of that! Dublin was becoming a playground for the wealthy, and I just couldn’t bear it anymore.

Cor, this rain. Proper miserable, innit? Reminds me of that housing development they’re building down by the Wensum. Nothing but grey concrete and damp foundations. Making a right mess of the landscape, they are. You always did have a bee in your bonnet about that, Arthur. Progress, eh? Can’t stop progress. Though I agree, it’s lookin' a bit grim. Remember when that field was all wildflowers? Used to go down there with Mabel and pick posies for the church. Don’t you two start moaning about the weather and developments again! My head’s already pounding. And speaking of unpleasantness, did you hear what Brenda said to Margaret at the shops yesterday? Apparently, she accused her of taking the last custard cream! Honestly, some people. Custard creams? That’s a serious offence, that is! Brenda's always been a bit… prickly. Remember when she complained about the shade of blue I painted my gate? Said it clashed with her roses. As if  my  gate matters! Brenda’s a one, she is. Always has been. Never forgave me for winning the village fete egg-and-spoon race back in '68. Said I was cheating. Ridiculous, really. Still, at least you’re getting things off your chest, Arthur. You’ve been a bit quiet lately. Thinking about the pension, are we? It's hard not to, Albert. This last letter… it's even smaller than the last one. Barely enough to buy a decent loaf of bread. I keep searching online – trying to understand how they calculate it all. This computer is a menace, it truly is. All those pop-ups and demands for passwords... I used to design bridges for a living! Now I can’t even figure out how to check my balance. Oh, Arthur, don’t beat yourself up about the computer. It's designed to be confusing. I’ve had a terrible time with it myself. I booked a doctor's appointment online the other day and accidentally booked a  dental  appointment. Ended up with a mouthful of fluoride! You're a caution, Doris! But Arthur's right to be worried about the pension. It’s frightening, isn't it? Mabel and I were talking about it the other day. She's considering moving into one of those retirement villages. Said it would be easier, someone to do the cooking, the cleaning… Retirement villages? More like glorified prisons!

Honestly, I’m just completely drained. Physics practical today was a disaster. My catapult kept launching the marshmallows at the wall, not the target. Mr. Davies looked like he was going to explode. Classic you, Finn. Remember last year’s biology dissection? You nearly dropped the frog onto Mrs. Peterson’s head. That was an accident! It was slippery! And this catapult thing was a design flaw, I tell you! It’s the fault of the manufacturer, not my projectile accuracy. You guys are still whining about school? The internet is  on fire  right now. Have you seen that cat video? The one where the cat thinks it's a ninja? It's already got like, five million views. Yeah, I saw it. Ridiculous. My little sister’s been playing it non-stop. She thinks it's the funniest thing ever. Five million? That’s insane! What's the point of sharing though? Like, what does it  add  to the world? Just another pointless distraction. Come on, Liam, lighten up! It's a bit of fun. Speaking of adding to the world... did you see that debate online about whether scientists should bring back the woolly mammoth? Oh, yeah. That’s actually pretty interesting. Genetically engineering extinct species... the ethics of it are seriously complex. What’s the point, essentially? Bringing back things that are extinct for a reason? Plus, where would they  live ? Siberia’s got that kind of climate, I guess, but still. It’s messing with evolution, isn’t it? Like, playing God or something. Exactly! And it’s probably going to cost a fortune. Money that could be spent on, you know, actually helping  existing  endangered species. It just feels performative. But what if it  did  work? Think of the scientific advancement! We'd learn so much about genetics and ecosystems... it could revolutionise conservation. It’s a slippery slope though, isn’t it? If we can bring back mammoths, what’s to stop people wanting to bring back dinosaurs? Dinosaurs?! Seriously, Finn? Imagine a T-Rex roaming around Siberia. That’d be… entertaining, I guess, until it eats you. Okay, let's not get carried away. It's a fool’s errand. It's like trying to unscramble an egg. You can’t just rewind biology. So, back to less complicated topics… anyone got a date for the weekend? Don’t even go there. Biology, yes.

Right, well, it's lovely to see you all. Honestly, it's been a mad week. That presentation for Sterling Cooper was a nightmare – thought I’d be pulling my hair out. But thankfully, landed it. So, how are we all doing? Mum, you look… surprisingly bright! Oh, I am, dear. Surprisingly bright indeed. That little Ms. Patel from the pharmacy gave me a lovely cuppa and a chat this morning. She’s a treasure, that one. And Bernard brought over a Victoria sponge. Can’t say no to a bit of sponge, can you? Never! Bernard’s a good sort. Always brings a cake. How’s your knee, Nan? Still aching? It’s a bit grumpy, love. Just a bit. They’ve upped my tablets slightly, you know. These new ones seem to dull everything a bit, though. Makes me feel a little… distant. Everything's dull these days. Not like when I was driving a lorry, eh? Now  that  was living! Remember that time in Belgium, Elsie? Flat tyre in the pouring rain… Dad, you tell that story every time. Honestly! Mum, are you taking all your medication correctly? I know it’s a lot, but it’s crucial. The infection they found last month… we don't want that coming back. I know, dear, I know. I'm trying my best. Sometimes I forget, I suppose. It's all a bit of a muddle. Sarah, you’re always so organised, it’s a wonder you manage all your sales stuff. It's a skill, Nan! Some of us are born with it. Speaking of skills, I saw an advert for a new acupuncture clinic opening up down the road. Apparently, it's good for aches and pains. You could give it a go, Nan. Acupuncture? Ooh, prickly things! I don't know about that… it sounds a bit… alarming. Prickly things? Sounds like a waste of money! Should be doing something useful, like fixing your leaky tap. Oh, Dad, leave her be! You’d just complain it wasn’t done your way. Besides, Elsie's been trying to get you to sort that tap for six months. Exactly! So, anyone got any exciting news? I've been thinking about booking a skiing trip for next year. Fancy it? Skiing? You’re mad! I’d rather stay here and have another cup of tea. My knees wouldn’t cope.

Right then, you two. We were talking about... well, about times that weren't always fair, were we? Remember how we read about knights and castles? Those weren’t always fair either, were they? Some people were treated better than others. But knights were good! They fought the dragons! They were heroes, darling, absolutely. But even heroes lived in a world where some people had more power than others. And sometimes, the way power was used… wasn’t very nice. Let’s talk about something called slavery. It was a long, long time ago, even before knights as we know them. What’s slavery? Is it like when I have to share my Lego with Lily? Not quite, sweetie. Sharing your Lego is a good thing. Slavery was… much worse. It meant people were captured – often from faraway lands – and forced to work for someone else, without being paid, without being treated kindly, and without being free to go home. They were treated like… like property. Like my teddy bear, Barnaby? No, Lily, not like Barnaby. Barnaby is your friend, you care for him, you choose to play with him. People who were slaves didn't have that choice. They didn’t choose to work. They didn’t choose where to live. People owned them, and told them what to do. That sounds awful. Why did people do that? That’s a really good question, Finn. People did it for many reasons, mostly because they wanted more… things. Like more land, more crops, and more money. They thought they could get these things by forcing other people to work for them. It was driven by greed and a terrible lack of respect for other human beings. Did knights do it? Did the dragons make people work? Some knights might have owned slaves, yes. It was a complicated time. And no, the dragons didn’t make people work, darling. These were humans making other humans work. Now, let's move onto something else... a bit more recent, but still very sad. Have you heard of wars? Yeah! Tommy at school was playing war at lunchtime! Pew pew! That’s pretending, Finn. Real wars are… different. They’re grown-ups fighting, sometimes for land, sometimes for power, sometimes for… well, sometimes for terrible reasons that are hard to understand, even for grown-ups. Think of it like a really, really big argument, but with lots of armies and lots of sadness.

Right then, everyone settled? Lovely to have you all. Honestly, this week's been a proper whirlwind at the ward. Three admissions with pneumonia, you wouldn't believe. Sounds like it, love. Always busy on the NHS, isn't it? I swear, the paperwork alone could fill a small library. Though, heading up the department, I don't see as much direct patient contact as you do anymore. Mostly meetings, meetings, and more meetings. Did you catch that article in the Telegraph about the funding cuts? Dreadful, really. I saw something about it, Dad. It's just… frustrating, isn’t it? How can they justify cutting funding when the service is already so stretched? Anyway, speaking of frustrating… did anyone see that new series on Netflix, ‘The Gilded Age’? I did! Absolutely brilliant, wasn't it? All those costumes and the tension... I was hooked. Though, I'm not sure how much of it was historically accurate. A bit fanciful, perhaps? Gilded Age? Sounds a bit posh for me. Give me a good wildlife documentary any day. Saw one on penguins the other night. Fascinating creatures, penguins. Always reminding me of little gentlemen in their dinner suits. Oh, Dad, you and your analogies! Penguins in dinner suits. You’re a treasure. I quite liked 'The Gilded Age' as well, actually. Bit of escapism is what we all need. Sarah, you've been quiet. What have you been up to? Still battling keywords for those advertising campaigns? Yeah, pretty much. It’s interesting work, but this new client is driving me mad. They want me to make dog food sound glamorous.  Glamorous dog food ! How do you even do that? I suggested "Royal Canine Cuisine – fit for a king, approved by his loyal subjects,” and they said it was “too pretentious.” Pretentious? For  dog food ? Honestly, some people. It's like trying to sell sand in the Sahara. Remember Uncle George trying to sell those self-heating blankets at the village fete? Honestly, the sales pitch was… well, let’s just say it involved a lot of waving and theatrical shivering. Oh, Uncle George! He was a character. Always had a scheme going on. Speaking of characters, did you hear about Mrs. Higgins next door? Apparently, she’s adopted a parrot. A  blue  parrot! Can you imagine the noise? A parrot? Oh, dear. Loud, those things. Used to work with a chap who had one, kept repeating swear words it picked up from the pub.

Right, nearly done. Honestly, this dishwasher is a lifesaver. Especially after a chaotic school day. How were you two? Did you have a good afternoon? It was brilliant, Mummy! We were reading about the Patronus Charm! I’m going to be a really good witch! I want to be a dragon! A big, fiery one. A dragon, eh? That’s ambitious! A very fiery dragon. You know, there were some very ambitious people in history too, not just in stories. Like George Stephenson. Who's George Stephenson? Is he a wizard? Nope, not a wizard, sweetheart, although he  did  make some real magic happen. He was an inventor, a really clever one. He invented the first successful steam railway engine. A train? Like the one we saw at the museum? Exactly! That's one of his. He built a whole railway! Think about it – before his trains, people travelled mostly by horse and carriage, or boat. It took days and days to get anywhere. But George Stephenson figured out a way to move people and goods much faster, with these incredible steam engines. But how did he  make  the steam engine work? Good question! Well, you boil water, right? Like when we're making tea. That makes steam, which is really powerful. And he created a system where that steam pushed pistons, which then turned wheels. It’s quite complicated, actually, but the basic idea is harnessing the power of steam to move something. Did he have any helpers? Loads! It was a huge team effort. He didn't invent everything on his own, though his ideas were central. Think of it like building a really, really big Lego castle – lots of people contribute, but you need a brilliant designer to bring it all together. He faced a lot of challenges, too. People didn’t always believe him, thought he was a bit mad to be trying to build these giant trains. Did he give up? Absolutely not! That's the thing about really brilliant people, they don’t give up. They keep trying, even when things are hard. My grandad used to tell me a story about him – apparently, he spent years perfecting the design of his engines, making tiny changes and testing them constantly. He even used to walk miles just to observe other machines and learn from them. Wow. He revolutionised travel, you know. He connected cities and made the world feel a lot smaller.

Right, so, I’m thinking this chilli needs a  serious  kick. Anyone got any thoughts? Beyond "more spice, Liam"? Honestly, Liam, you're always going for the nuclear option. Remember that vindaloo you made last time? People were crying! A little smoked paprika could add depth without incinerating everyone. And maybe some chopped chocolate? Chocolate in chilli? Liv, are you mad? That's… well, it's unexpected. I'm with Liam on the spice front, though. I need some warmth on a cold evening. I'm exhausted from dealing with that leaky roof at the cafe all day. Honestly, it feels like I’m constantly patching things up. Chocolate in chilli? Actually...not a bad shout. My Nan used to chuck a bit of dark chocolate in her beef stew. Gives it a richness. But yeah, Liam, ease up a bit on the heat, yeah? Don't want anyone needing an ambulance. Alright, alright, I hear you. Less volcanic, more… pleasantly warming. Smoked paprika it is. Speaking of things needing patching up, how are things with the legal stuff, Chloe? Still battling that landlord? Don't even ask. He’s claiming I owe him over a grand in unpaid rent, which is absolute rubbish. I've got bank statements proving I paid everything. He’s being completely obtuse. I sent the council a letter, hoping they can intervene, but… feeling pretty stuck. It’s just so stressful trying to keep the bakery afloat  and  deal with this. That’s awful, Chloe. You should definitely pursue this. Don’t let him bully you. Are you using a solicitor? I can’t afford a solicitor, Maya! That’s the problem. I’m barely making ends meet as it is. I’ve been looking online, trying to find some free legal advice, but it’s a minefield of dodgy websites. Anyone know a decent, affordable lawyer in East London? I might. My mate’s sister is a paralegal over in Shoreditch. She does pro bono work sometimes. Let me see if I can get her email for you, Chloe. Honestly, those landlords are a nightmare. Back home, you wouldn't get away with half the things they try here. That’s brilliant, Finn! Massive help. So, while we're on the topic of dodgy online stuff, has anyone tried that new supper club website, "Flavourful Nights"? I saw an ad pop up the other day.

Honestly, this coronation chicken is exactly what I needed. Bit soggy, mind you, but a good, solid lunch. How’s your day going, Anya? You look like you've been wrestling a printer again. You have no idea, Sarah. Printer 3 decided it wanted to eat all the magenta toner. I spent a solid hour trying to coax it back to life. At least it's quiet now. Salad’s… fine. I’m trying to be healthy, you know? Little Sergei is obsessed with sausage rolls, though. It’s a constant battle. Sergei? Is that your little one? He must be… how old? Three and a half. A whirlwind of energy, I tell you. He’s also decided that dinosaurs are the centre of the universe. Every conversation revolves around them. "Roar! Where is the T-Rex, Anya?" It's tiring, but adorable. How are Emily and Tom doing? Still at football and ballet, are they? They are indeed! Emily’s showing promise with her ballet, actually. Her teacher thinks she might be able to audition for a summer program. Tom’s just relentlessly energetic on the football pitch. He’ll probably end up tackling someone into next week, bless him. It's expensive though, all the kit and the travel. Are you managing alright with Sergei’s interests? Dinosaur toys aren’t cheap, I imagine. Not at all! Especially when he wants  realistic  ones. I found a website – Jurassic Outfitters, I think it’s called – they do incredibly detailed replicas. A bit pricey, but worth it for his little face. What do you do to unwind after all the cover supervising? It can't be easy, dealing with everyone's different personalities. Oh, it’s a trial sometimes, I won’t lie. My hobbies are blissfully quiet, mostly. I’ve taken up pottery. It’s fantastically therapeutic. You get covered in clay, but it's strangely calming. I'm currently attempting a rather ambitious vase, but it keeps collapsing. Do you have any hobbies, Anya? Besides battling printers and dinosaur enthusiasts. Actually, yes! I do a bit of coding in my spare time. It's a different kind of problem-solving than IT admin; it’s more… creative. I’m working on a small app to help parents track their kids’ activities and appointments. Sergei needs it more than anything, honestly. It's surprisingly relaxing after a day of fixing network problems.

Are we nearly there yet, Grandad? My legs are killing me after lugging all that baby stuff. Mum’s gone mental for blankets, hasn't she? Like the little one's gonna be wrapped in a duvet from day one! Now, now, lass. Your mum's just being prepared. You’ll understand when it’s your turn. And it’s a good job she got ‘em, mind. Remember that time your cousin, Leo, ended up with a rash from that cheap blanket? Nearly had to take him to A&E! Besides, we’re nearly there. Just past this roundabout. Honestly, the amount of blankets! It’s like nesting on a grand scale. But, a soft blanket for a baby is very important. It reminds them of the warmth and security of the womb. It is good your mother is thinking about this. And did you pick up the steriliser, darling? I specifically asked you too. Yeah, yeah, got the steriliser. And the travel cot. So many bits and bobs! It’s madness, innit? Makes you think about moving house again, doesn’t it? That damp patch in the bedroom still proper bothers me. Did the surveyor say anything about it being serious? He said it needed addressing, love. Nothing to panic about, but new plastering is a must. And likely some ventilation improvements. Your mum's looking into getting someone in next week, isn't she? Yes, I've got quotes from three builders. We need to decide which one to go with. The one with the lowest price is also the one with the best reviews, surprisingly. But, sometimes you can't just go for the cheapest. Right, proper hassle. Still, at least it'll be done before the baby comes. Speaking of which, Mum, are you still thinking about having a little nursery? Like, with painted animals and stuff? Of course, darling. I’ve already started collecting ideas. I saw a beautiful mobile at that shop in Chorley the other day. Little wooden sheep. It was gorgeous. It makes you think back, doesn’t it? When I was a little girl, I had a blanket with embroidered bears. My grandma made it. Aye, I remember your grandma's blankets. She were proper talented. Used to make ‘em for all the grandkids. Best blankets you could get yer hands on. Warmer than a hug. So, you grew up in Slovakia, yeah?

Honestly, this game is driving me insane. I’ve been trying to beat this level for  hours , and I just can't. It’s like, the AI is actively mocking me. What game is it, love? Still that space one, isn't it? The one with all the flashing lights that gives you a headache? Yeah, Stellar Conquest. It's brilliant, but this final boss… He’s got, like, three different attack patterns and shields that regenerate. It’s ridiculous! I think it's deliberately unbalanced. Three attack patterns? Sounds intense. You’ve been at it since you got home from school. You alright? You seem a bit… wound up. Wound up is an understatement! I'm bordering on furious. And Mum, you know I get frustrated easily. It's not  just  the game. It's been a long week. Maths test was awful, and Chloe's being extra annoying in history. Right then, enough of that. Biscuits and tea. That always helps. Chloe's always been a handful. Remember when she used to draw all over your bedroom walls with crayons? Don't remind me! Dad nearly had a heart attack. But seriously, I think I need to understand the psychology behind these game designs. Why do they make bosses so deliberately hard? It's not fun, it’s just… frustrating. It's like they’re exploiting our need for reward. It's often about engagement, isn’t it? Keeping you playing longer. It's a whole discipline in game design, ‘flow state’ and all that. They want you to keep trying, to feel that sense of almost-achievement, even if you never actually get there. Think about Skinner boxes, the reward and punishment cycle… same principle. See! This is what I mean! It’s manipulative! It's… it’s making me angry. Maybe I should take a break and read about dark matter again. At least  that  is genuinely fascinating and doesn’t artificially try to irritate me. Dark matter, eh? Sounds a bit heavy for a Friday night. Are you still hoping to go to Cambridge to study astrophysics? Absolutely. It's the only thing that keeps me going some days. Although... I'm a bit worried about the application process. So competitive. You've got a good chance, honestly. Your grades are brilliant, and you're clearly passionate about it. Remember that science fair project you did last year?

Right, so, diamonds are obviously the best, aren't they? Everyone knows that. But did you know Netherite is even  better ? It's like, diamond’s older, tougher, cooler sibling. Nether…ite? Is that like, gold, but stronger? Rawr! Netherite is  fire ! It melts everything! Nearly, darling. It’s not quite as dramatic as melting everything, though it  is  strong enough to withstand lava. It’s found in the Nether, you see, so you need to be very careful. It’s a proper adventure to get it. Much tougher than finding diamonds, which are, relatively speaking, all over the place. Now, what about fabrics? What's your favourite, love? Velvet! It's so squishy and soft. Like a hug! Wool! Sheep give wool! And you can make blankets! Excellent choices. Velvet’s lovely, so luxurious. It's woven, you know, although modern velvet is often cut rather than woven. Then you have wool, which comes from sheep. It’s a natural fibre, brilliant for keeping warm. Did you know they used to dye wool with all sorts of things? Beetroot for pink, woad for blue... Really? Wow! Did they dye velvet too? They did! And silk. Silk is probably one of the most luxurious fabrics there is, and it comes from silkworms! Tiny little caterpillars that spin a cocoon - that's the silk. It's incredibly strong though, for something so delicate. Much stronger than cotton, surprisingly. Now, I was reading about iron the other day… Iron is everywhere, isn’t it? In our kitchen, in the car… It’s super useful, but it rusts. Rust? What's rust? It’s when iron meets water and air, and it turns orange and crumbly. Not very good, is it? You need to coat it with something else to stop it - like paint, or even another metal, like tin. We call that galvanising. Keeps it nice and strong. Now, I was thinking... let's invent a legend. A Minecraft legend! Ooh! I like legends! Me too! Mine needs dragons! Alright, let’s build on that. How about this? Long ago, before even diamonds were discovered, there was a hidden island made entirely of shimmering Obsidian. And on this island lived the Weaver-King, who could spin threads of pure starlight into fabrics stronger than Netherite and more beautiful than velvet. Starlight fabric?! That sounds amazing! But… but what about the dragons? The Weaver-King didn’t  have  dragons.

Honestly, Liam, I’m tellin' ya, this band – 'The Rusty Spanners' – they're proper awful. Like, ear-bleedingly bad. I thought you said they were gonna be good! Nowt's ever good enough for you, is it, Maisie? They’re alright! A bit rough around the edges, yeah, but they got a decent energy. Better than that manufactured pop stuff you listen to. Decent energy? They sounded like a cat fightin' a bag of nails! And don't you dare bring up my music taste. At least I appreciate a good vocal range, unlike those…those  growlers . It's just noise, innit? Proper noise. You're just being dramatic. They were tryin' somethin', alright? A bit experimental. Reminds me a bit of early Muse, bit chaotic. You just gotta let it wash over ya. Muse? Liam, you're stretchin’ it. Muse are proper talented. These lot...they need a good tuning and a lesson in rhythm. Seriously. Speaking of rhythm, how's your guitar playin’ goin'? Still tryin’ to learn that riff from 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'? Yeah, alright. It's tricky, innit? Those power chords are deceptively hard to get right. My fingers are bleedin'. You know I'm not a natural like you are with the bass. Bleedin' fingers are a badge of honour, love. Come on, that riff is practically the anthem of a generation. You’ll get it. Just gotta persevere. You should play it for me tomorrow, maybe? I’ll give you some pointers. Alright, alright. Maybe. But we’re not talkin' about music all night. I was readin’ somethin’ awful online earlier…it was about…well, it was about some bloke online groomin' kids. Proper sick. Oh, Liam. Don’t. Don’t tell me that sort of thing. It’s…it’s just too much. Why do people even  do  that? It makes my blood boil. I know, right? It's just...disgusting. It makes you think, doesn't it? About how easy it is for these sorts of people to hide behind a screen and do terrible things. My mum was saying how they’re gettin’ stricter with online safety lessons at school, but it still feels like it’s not enough. It’ll  never  be enough, will it? They'll always find a way. It’s just…makes you want to shake every single one of ‘em. I read a thing about – I won’t go into details – but it’s just makes you feel so helpless.

Ugh, half-term’s already halfway done. Feels like it just started. Anyone got any plans for the rest of it? Besides, you know, the usual homework grind. Nah, nothing major. My mum’s trying to drag us all to that Van Gogh exhibition in London. Apparently, it’s ‘immersive’ or something. Sounds intense. You going, Liam? Immersive sounds pretty cool, actually. I’ve been wanting to see Van Gogh. My nan's obsessed – she’s got prints of all his sunflower paintings scattered around her flat. I’m going, yeah. Maybe we could all go together? Less embarrassing parental hovering. Yeah, that'd be good. My dad’s already lecturing me about needing to catch up on my EPQ. He's got this whole 'productive half-term' thing going on. Tell me about it. Mine’s on the socio-economic impact of Esports. It's horrifyingly boring, honestly. I’m just churning through reports. What’s yours, Liam? I'm doing mine on the historical context of philanthropy. It's... interesting. A lot of it is surprisingly depressing when you consider how much poverty there still is. Makes you wonder what’s actually changed, you know? Totally. Like, you read about Victorian philanthropists and their motivations, and then you look at food bank usage now… It’s just… frustrating. My history teacher, Mrs. Davies, did a really good lesson on it last week. She talked about how the systems themselves often perpetuate poverty, not just a lack of kindness. Yeah, she's sound, Mrs. Davies. My mum’s a social worker, so I hear a lot about that stuff at home. It’s not always about helping people, sometimes it’s about managing a broken system. Anyway, enough depressing stuff for one afternoon. Fancy grabbing some ice cream? There's that new vegan place just down the road. Vegan ice cream? Seriously? What's that even like? It’s surprisingly decent! They do this salted caramel one that's… addictive. I had it last week. It’s way better than it has any right to be. Exactly! Plus, it's slightly less guilty when you're demolishing a huge portion. Speaking of which, my grandma’s been trying to teach me how to make her Montenegrin cheese pastries. They're insane. They involve filo pastry, loads of cheese, and some sort of secret spice blend. Montenegro? Wow. That's a long way from Slough.

Honestly, this kitchen is a disgrace. Like, permanently. I’ve never seen so much dried pasta stuck to the cooker. It's been there since bloody October! Tell me about it. I swear, someone used the hob as a pizza oven and just… abandoned it. I found a rogue pepperoni under the microwave this morning. A pepperoni! Pepperoni? That’s… a dedication to culinary neglect. My mum would have a fit if she saw this. She’d be scrubbing and organising for hours. You know, like she does with the whole house. She’s a whirlwind of disinfectant and order. Did someone say pepperoni? I’m starving! What’s for dinner? Just a depressing cup of tea, love. And the general ambience of a student kitchen that’s been declared a biohazard. You hungry, Liam? You could be earning some brownie points by aggressively cleaning this place. Nah, I’m good. Mum made lasagne tonight. Massive portions. I smuggled some out. . Liam, you are a lifesaver. Seriously. Uni food is… barely food. Thanks! Lasagne? That smells incredible! My nan used to make the  best  lasagne. Layers and layers of pasta and meat. This is making me homesick. It's pretty good. Mum’s been practicing. She’s trying to win the village bake-off next year. Apparently, Mrs. Higgins has held it for like, twenty years. She’s proper competitive. A village bake-off? That sounds wonderfully quaint. My grandma used to enter flower shows, bless her. She'd spend weeks coaxing roses into blooming just so. It was all very… Cornish. Speaking of quaint and family… my cousin Sophie just got engaged! To… wait for it… a  dancer . Like, a professional dancer. I nearly choked on my tea when Mum told me. Sophie? Dancing? She’s more of a spreadsheet kinda girl. A dancer? That’s… quite the leap! What does his family do? Bollywood choreographers, maybe? Funnily enough, his dad’s a solicitor. Proper posh solicitor. It's a whole saga. Apparently, they met at a Salsa class - can you believe it? Salsa! My mum’s already planning the wedding, naturally. It's going to be a  spectacle . A salsa-themed wedding? Oh, that's brilliant. Though knowing Sophie, it’ll probably involve colour-coded seating charts and a strict dress code. My dad wants me to start learning the drums. He keeps going on about how good it'll be for my coordination.

Honestly, Mum, you wouldn’t believe the chaos at school this week. Little Timmy Henderson tried to convince everyone Santa was a drone. A drone! I had to spend twenty minutes explaining the magic of Christmas to a five-year-old. He wasn’t buying it. Bless him. Kids are marvellous, aren't they? So inventive, so delightfully daft. Reminds me of your cousin Gareth when he was that age. He was convinced the reindeer ate sugar cubes from the elves’ pockets. Said it’s why they could fly so fast. Oh my goodness, Gareth! He always had the wildest stories. It's the same with my lot. Little Poppy is already planning what she’s going to ask Santa. She wants a miniature pony. A  miniature  pony, Mum! Where would I put one? Well, that's Christmas spirit, isn't it? Big dreams, even if they’re slightly impractical. Still, it's better than wanting another iPad, I suppose. How’s David coping with all this festive frenzy? He’s…patient. Mostly. He's got a new project at work, though. Something to do with sustainable tourism in the Lake District. Apparently, he’s working with a group trying to reduce the environmental impact of all those coach tours. David, that sounds wonderful! He's always had a good head for that kind of thing. Remember when he organised that recycling scheme at university? Everyone thought he was mad at the time, but look at us now, obsessing over reusable shopping bags. He was always ahead of the curve. Speaking of travel, are you still planning that trip to Portugal next spring? You mentioned something about a language course. Yes, I am! Booked it, actually. A little Portuguese course in Lisbon. I've been wanting to go for years. It's purely for pleasure, you know. Just wanted to challenge myself. It's good to keep the brain ticking over, especially as the freelance work slows down a bit over Christmas. I’m doing a bit of training for a local charity next week, but no big consultancy projects on the horizon at the moment. That sounds lovely, Mum. Lisbon is beautiful. Maybe I’ll have to pop over and visit you. A little break from the school chaos. Although, I'll probably end up teaching Portuguese to a group of bewildered tourists. To bewildered tourists! And to you escaping the school for a little while.

Wow, Crayford hasn’t changed  that  much, has it? Still all the same terraced houses. Feels…surreal being back, to be honest. Two years is a long time. Aye, it hasn’t. They've put a few more speed cameras up though. Properly sneaky ones they are. Nearly got caught last week, you know. Had to really watch myself. You got your license renewed, then? Yeah, just before I left for teaching. Renewed it and everything. Though I’m still debating whether I need a car in Brighton. Public transport seems pretty decent. Not like relying on a rusty old Ford like this! Don't you be sayin' that about Bessie! She’s served us well. This is the same car I drove you back from uni, remember? Though, speaking of Brighton, you seem a lot calmer about the move than you were a few weeks ago. I am. It’s finally felt…real. I had a really good meeting with the Head of Department at the school. They seem really happy with me. Plus, finding a flat didn’t take as long as I feared. Small, but it’s mine. How’s work been for you, Dad? Still dealing with the endless customer complaints? Same old, same old. Though Brenda called in sick again today. Third time this month. Honestly, I’m starting to think she’s faking it just to get out of doing reports. They’re thinking of letting her go, you know. That's rough, that is. I hope it doesn't come to that. Still, moving to Brighton has got me thinking about Tanzania. Remember that incredible trip? I’ve been looking at some photos. The wildlife was just… breathtaking. Aye, that was something else. Took your mother’s breath away, that. Though I do think you've been putting on a bit of weight. All those fish and chips you've been eating, I wager. Oh, come on! It’s just a bit of holiday fluff. Teaching's been stressful, I've been comfort-eating. It'll come off. Anyway, enough about me. Remember Uncle Barry used to say, "Always talk about the other person’s ailments first, then slip in your own!" Your Uncle Barry… a legend. Speaking of legends, did you ever finish Game of Thrones? I know you were hooked. I never got into it myself. Too much… bloodshed for an old man like me.

Honestly, that Anthropologie trip was  brutal . You wouldn't believe the queue. It snaked all the way down the street. I swear, half the women in Surrey were there. Anthropologie on a Saturday? That's practically a pilgrimage. Did you manage to find anything worthwhile amidst the chaos? Eventually. Found this gorgeous linen dress, perfect for summer. Though, it cost a small fortune. I’m starting to think I need a designated Anthropologie budget. It’s… insidious. They lure you in with beautiful displays and then  bam , your bank account is weeping. They’re masters of the aesthetic. Tell me about it. I had a surprisingly intense meeting today. Professor Davies is convinced we need to launch a full-blown PR campaign for the Archaeology department. Apparently, our public image is, and I quote, “dire.” Dire? How so? You're unearthing Roman mosaics, for goodness sake! That's hardly lacking in public appeal. Apparently, we’re perceived as dusty academics who spend all their time poring over pottery shards and muttering about stratigraphy. He wants us to do open days, social media campaigns, even… …influencer collaborations. Influencers? Seriously? Imagine, “Hey guys, check out this perfectly preserved burial urn! Sponsored by… Lush Cosmetics?” Exactly! The thought alone is horrifying. But Davies is adamant. He says we need to "modernize our brand.” Apparently, having a leading expert on Anglo-Saxon burial rituals follow on Instagram isn’t considered modern enough. Oh, the absurdity of academia. Right, well, I’m starving. Are you thinking of ordering in tonight, or should I attempt something vaguely resembling cooking? I’m still recovering from wrestling for a parking space outside Anthropologie. Let's order. Thai sounds good? I'm feeling lazy. And… about the PR thing, I've been thinking. Instead of influencers, perhaps we could partner with the local museum? They’re always looking for ways to showcase local archaeological finds. It's a more organic connection, you know? That's a far better idea. Much less performative. It feels more authentic. Plus, you’re brilliant at that sort of thing - networking, building bridges, making things happen. I'm better at lecturing on Beowulf and avoiding crowds. Glad to hear it. Speaking of things happening... did you hear about Fleet Foxes playing at the Roundhouse next month? No! Seriously? I've been waiting ages to see them live. How did you find out? A friend sent me the link.

Right, I think the lentils are nearly ready. Smells alright, doesn’t it? Though I'm still not convinced about adding that much cumin. Are you sure it’s not a bit…overpowering? It'll be fine, love. Don't fret. Cumin gives it a proper warmth. Besides, you're always tempering things down. Remember that time you tried to make chili and barely used any chili powder? Disaster. That was one time! And I didn't want it setting everyone’s mouth on fire. It’s supper, not a competition. Speaking of which, did you get chance to look at the shower curtain? The current one is absolutely hideous. The blue and green striped one? It's perfectly functional. Functional and visually offensive are not mutually exclusive, David! It clashes with  everything  in the bathroom. I was thinking something neutral. Maybe a grey? Or even a very pale blue. Something calming. This current one looks like a tropical nightmare. Calm is boring, Eleanor. A bit of vibrancy never hurt anyone. Besides, we have bigger fish to fry than a shower curtain. How’s the beanbag coming along? You’ve been knitting for weeks now. That's the other thing! The beanbag. It's…a project. A  long  project. I swear, each row takes an hour. And I keep having to frog things back. It's a monumental undertaking. I was hoping to have it finished by the weekend for when your sister comes, but at this rate… Don’t stress about it. Your sister isn’t expecting a perfectly formed beanbag. She’s just happy to see us. And honestly, a half-finished one is probably more you – delightfully chaotic. Delightfully chaotic, you say? That's a very generous description. I'm just trying to create something cozy and nice. It's supposed to be a little haven in the corner of the living room. It will be. You always do a good job. You've got a knack for making a house feel like a home. You know, I was actually thinking about repainting the bathroom while we're at it. Just freshening it up. That magnolia colour is starting to look a bit…tired. Don't you dare! Magnolia is a classic. It goes with everything! You can’t just start ripping up perfectly good paint! We  just  talked about the shower curtain! One home improvement project at a time, please!

Right then, Doris. Another Tuesday, eh? Feels like they all bleed into one these days. Rain again, I see. Proper Norfolk drizzle. Doesn’t half soak ya, it does. Yes, Arthur. Dreadful. I was hoping for a bit of sunshine. It would do the roses some good. Did you see the news this morning? About the price of electricity? Absolutely scandalous, it is. Scandalous indeed, Doris. They're squeezing every last penny out of us. The sheer audacity of it all. I was just reading about the latest boardroom salaries… the chaps are practically laughing all the way to the bank. Boardroom salaries, eh? You know, I never did understand all that fuss about money. Always seemed a bit… unnecessary to me. Never had much, mind you. But I always managed. A bit of gardening, a bit of fishing… kept me occupied. Arthur, you’re such a simple soul. Not everyone's had the same opportunities as you to… well, to potter about. David here knows all about these corporate shenanigans. He practically  lived  them. Potting about is a skill, Arthur. A valuable one. Self-sufficiency. Something this generation has lost. And opportunities? They’re largely manufactured, you know. A clever strategy, a bit of luck, and having the right connections. It's not all meritocracy, believe me. I've seen the games played. Connections, you say. My old man used to say, “It’s not what you know, but who you know.” Sounded a bit unfair to me. I always thought hard work was all that mattered. Oh, Arthur. You and your old man. You were both raised on that. But the world doesn’t work like that. David and I have had to navigate all sorts of tricky situations. Networking, schmoozing… it's all part of the game. Schmoozing is a polite word for it, Doris. It’s often about knowing who to flatter and when to hold your tongue. I remember one particular deal... involved a rather influential politician and a very expensive bottle of claret. It's not pretty. Claret, eh? Never been much for fancy drinks. Give me a good pint of bitter any day. Now that’s a proper drink. Something with a bit of backbone. You and your bitter, Arthur! You're incorrigible. David, what do you think about all this? About the unfairness of it all? It’s endemic, Doris. Built into the system.

Right, that roast was  divine , wasn’t it? Honestly, Mark, you’ve outdone yourself this time. The gravy… oh, the gravy! Well, thank you, love. Years of practice, you know. Though, I think a little help from Sarah with the sprouts didn’t go amiss either. They were perfectly al dente, weren’t they? They were pretty good, Dad. Better than last year, definitely. Though I still think Brussels sprouts are inherently evil. Seriously, who invented them? Don't be ridiculous, Sarah. They’re a classic! Though I agree, they  can  be disastrous. Anyway, speaking of classics… did you see that Marks & Spencer advert for Christmas? The one with the twinkly lights and the overly enthusiastic orchestra? Oh, I did! It was a bit much, wasn't it? All a bit… manufactured. Still, it does get you in the mood, doesn’t it? I was thinking, we should book that trip to the Christmas markets in Bath this year. We talked about it last year, didn't we? We did. And it's a good shout. Need to do it soon, though, before they sell out completely. We’d need to get accommodation sorted, that's the main thing. Thinking a weekend trip, say the second weekend in December? Hmm, that sounds lovely. Though, I’m a bit strapped for cash at the moment. Freelancing can be… unpredictable. That big campaign I was working on got cancelled at the last minute. Oh, sweetheart, that's awful! Don't worry about the trip, though. We'll sort it. We always do. Mark and I can cover it this time. It’s Christmas, after all. It’s good of you both. Honestly, it’s just… frustrating. I’m trying to save up for a deposit on a flat, and these little setbacks make it feel like an impossible dream. It’s so different from when I was younger. It is, isn't it? The housing market’s gone mad. When I was your age, Sarah, you could pick up a decent flat for a song. Now… forget about it. It’s all about inflated prices and bidding wars. Remember when we went to Bruges, Mark? That little chocolate shop, with the hand-painted boxes… How could I forget? You practically bought the entire store! We had chocolate for weeks after that. You guys are reminiscing again! While I’m over here stressing about finances.

It’s just breathtaking, isn’t it? I still can’t quite believe we’re here. Dorchester feels a million miles away, all grey skies and drizzle. Indeed. Quite a change of scenery. Though, I must say, the heat is a bit… relentless. Took me a while to adjust. Dorchester, even in winter, had a certain… bracing quality to the air. Oh, I know what you mean. It's lovely in the evenings, absolutely delightful, but mid-day… you need to be glued to the shade. So, you've been here a little longer than I have, haven't you? How are you finding Northern Cyprus in general? Oh, yes, a few years now. Came out after… well, after things weren’t quite working out back home. It's been… an education. Different. The people are very welcoming, you know. Though the bureaucracy… …the bureaucracy is something else. Don’t even get me started on trying to sort out residency. A complete and utter shambles, it is. Oh, I’ve heard whispers about that. I’m trying to navigate it slowly, piece by piece. My husband, David, he's tackling most of it, thankfully. Being a teacher, I’m not exactly used to paperwork over deadlines! What about the food? Have you explored much beyond the usual Turkish restaurants? The food? Excellent. Honestly, some of the best I’ve ever had. Forget the fancy restaurants; go to the local  lokantas . That’s where you find the real gems. Simple, hearty, and incredibly cheap. Try the  kleftiko  – slow roasted lamb. Just melts in your mouth. And the fresh bread! Oh, the fresh bread. I used to complain about supermarket bread in Bushey; suddenly, that seems like a luxury now. You’re making me terribly hungry! David's a massive fan of kebabs, so we’re already on a mission to find the absolute best. He's bringing a little portable grill with him, planning on having impromptu barbecue nights. A portable grill? Here? You’ll be needing a permit for that, you know. The authorities are very keen on enforcing regulations. Though, I suppose a few kebabs probably won’t draw too much attention. I once tried to grow tomatoes in my garden… ended badly. Apparently, I needed permission for that too. Oh, dear! You're putting me off a bit, I must admit. But a few kebabs don’t seem like quite the same scale of offense.

Honestly, another day, another layer. I feel like I’m perpetually swaddled here. Did you see the AQI this morning? It was… concerning, to say the least. Yeah, appalling. Eighty-seven, wasn't it? I checked before leaving the office. It’s getting ridiculous, isn’t it? Remember when we first moved here, we were so excited about the food, the culture… we didn’t fully appreciate how pervasive the pollution would be. Don't get me wrong, I still love it, mostly. It’s just… the cumulative effect is starting to wear on me. My throat feels scratchy constantly. And I’m worried about little Leo. He’s still so young, his lungs… I know, darling. Me too. I’ve been looking into those air purifiers again, the really good ones. The ones that filter out the PM2.5. Think we should bite the bullet and invest in a few more? We’ve only got the one in his room. It's definitely worth considering. It's just… another expense, isn't it? And honestly, sometimes it feels like putting a plaster on a gaping wound. It’s a local problem, exacerbated by a national one, and... well, you know the rest. Speaking of expense, how did the grant proposal go? For the digital humanities project? Not brilliantly, to be honest. The review panel raised a lot of concerns about the long-term viability. They think we’re being too ambitious, trying to integrate AI into the historical analysis of Ming dynasty poetry. Said it’s “borderline fantastical.” Oh, those academics. Always needing to kill the fun, don’t they? Fantastic to them means impractical, apparently. But you argued your point well, didn't you? I tried. I stressed the potential for uncovering previously overlooked patterns and nuances in the poetry. Showed them the preliminary analysis. But they kept coming back to the resources needed, the training of the algorithms… They wanted something more… grounded. Less… me. It's alright, love. Rejection is part and parcel of academia. Besides, they're often just resistant to change. The older guard clinging to their dusty tomes and their established methods. Honestly, sometimes I think they’d rather publish a footnote than a groundbreaking thesis. How's David handling it? He's surprisingly supportive. He kept saying, "Don't let their negativity get to you. You were brilliant." David, bless him. He usually just pretends to understand exactly what I’m talking about.

Right then, Nigel, are you sure you want shepherd’s pie? You had a massive lunch at the office, didn't you? Head of Department life, eh? All those meetings must take it out of you.
