Don't be daft, love. A bit of comfort food never hurt anyone. And yes, the lunch was substantial, but it was mostly protein bars and lukewarm coffee. I need proper sustenance. Besides, Chloe will be thrilled. She adores shepherd’s pie. Did she send any more of those funny cat photos today? Just sent one, Dad! Look, this one's perched on the toaster. Ridiculous, isn’t it? Oh, bless its little socks! She’s got a flair for posing, that cat. You know, I had a proper day at the ward today. Mrs. Henderson finally came around – you remember, the one who’d been so anxious after her surgery? She was actually laughing with me. Felt good to make a difference, you know? That’s brilliant, Sarah. You always do. I was bogged down in budget reports all day. Thrilling stuff, I tell you. The joys of management. Chloe, did you manage to finish that copywriting brief for the pet shop? The one with the overly enthusiastic Dachshund? Almost finished! Just tweaking the final paragraph. They want me to emphasize the ‘joy’ of puppy breath. It’s...a challenge. I showed Mark the initial draft, and he nearly choked on his coffee laughing. Puppy breath! Honestly. The things you youngsters deal with. Right, potatoes are nearly done. Nigel, could you check on the gravy? I put a bit of red wine in – thought it might elevate it slightly. Gravy’s bubbling away nicely, Sarah. Added a teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce, just like your mum used to. Speaking of Mum, did you see that repeat of "Call the Midwife" last night? That storyline with Sister Julienne and the young doctor was rather poignant, wasn’t it? Actually, I've been completely hooked on "Succession" lately. It's dark, but so clever. The writing is just phenomenal. You wouldn't be into it, Dad, too stressful, I reckon! "Succession"? Sounds dreadful. All that arguing and backstabbing. Give me a good historical drama any day. Something with bonnets and handsome lords. You and your bonnets, Nigel. Chloe, you really should recommend something a bit lighter. My brain needs a rest after a day of administering medication and dealing with relatives.

Right, so this new bus route… honestly, it’s a disaster. They’ve cut the 7 every Saturday morning! Every Saturday! How am I supposed to get to the market now? It's not like Cambridge has pavements long enough to  walk  there and back, you know? My feet were killing me last time. The 7? Seriously? I hadn’t noticed. Cambridge transport is a constant source of bewilderment, isn’t it? You'd think with all the money floating around here… Bewilderment is putting it mildly! It’s a conspiracy to keep us poor Northerners from decent vegetables. I mean, honestly, a Saturday morning market is a lifeline for someone on my budget. Did you hear about that protest outside the University Press bookshop yesterday? Briefly. Something about the pricing of academic journals, wasn't it? I saw a few people with banners. Seemed quite spirited, actually. Spirited? They were  livid . Apparently, they're saying the Press is profiteering and making research inaccessible. It's a good point, to be fair. Can you imagine trying to access a proper academic paper? Murder. Reminds me of struggling with the library at Sunderland Uni - always a battle for a decent computer. Well, Cambridge University Library is… considerably more advanced than Sunderland’s, I imagine. Although, it still has its quirks, you know. The sheer scale of it can be overwhelming. Have you been in at all? Briefly. Once. It's like a labyrinth! All those dusty tomes… It smelled like old socks and regret. Sunderland's was smaller, but at least you could find what you were looking for. And the librarians actually knew what they were talking about, not just furrowing their brows and pointing you towards a vague section marked "History." Sounds charmingly chaotic. Cambridge librarians are generally quite helpful, though…perhaps slightly pretentious. Speaking of universities and chaos, how are things at your work? Anything exciting happening with the corpus? Honestly? A bit dull. Mostly it’s just cleaning up the data, flagging inconsistencies. Tedious stuff. Though, Mrs. Higgins did bring in her prize-winning marrows yesterday. They were enormous. Proper whoppers. You'd need a bus to transport them! Sounds like a highlight, then. You know, I was chatting to a colleague from Imperial the other day. He was complaining about the pressure to publish, the endless grant applications... it’s relentless. Makes me glad I chose engineering, comparatively less drama.

Honestly, this is lovely. Just… lovely. A bit of sunshine, decent coffee, and good company. Something I haven’t had enough of lately, I must say. Retirement’s proving… different than I imagined. Different good, though, isn't it, Moira? You always said you'd travel, take up painting... what's been stopping you? The painting ended after the third slightly lopsided landscape. Let's just say my talents lie more in proving mathematical theorems than wielding a paintbrush. And travel… well, travel requires money, doesn’t it? Something I seem to be perpetually short of, even after thirty-odd years of seemingly doing nothing. Don't tell the kids I said that. Don't worry, your secret's safe with us. You dedicated your life to them, Moira. That's plenty worthwhile. Speaking of the kids, how’s Finn doing at university? He sounded absolutely stressed on the phone last week. Finn is... Finn. Always has been, always will be. A brilliant boy, don’t you doubt that, but procrastination is practically his middle name. He’s pulling all-nighters now to catch up on readings he should have done months ago. He says he’s applying for a linguistics course next year, can you imagine? Linguistics? Really? That's fascinating. What sparked that interest? He says he’s found it utterly compelling. Apparently, the way languages evolve and influence each other is far more complex than he ever realised. He was telling me about the influence of Celtic languages on English – something I never fully appreciated when I was teaching. Honestly, the things he learns! Makes me feel quite ancient. He often corrects my grammar, you know. The audacity! Sounds like he’s inherited your love of detail, then! My little Leo’s obsessed with Minecraft. Honestly, a world built entirely of blocks. What will they think of next? Leo's a sweetheart. He's getting so big. Are you still planning that trip to Disneyland for him next summer? Absolutely! Ben’s managed to get a few days off work, so it’s a go. Though I’m slightly terrified of the crowds. I need a serious cup of tea after thinking about it. So, Moira, Ben’s brother, Daniel, is coming down next weekend. Any chance you could pop over? He's been wanting to catch up properly. Daniel! Oh, I’d love to. It’s been ages.

Brr, it’s colder than I thought it would be. You’d think being this close to the water, it’d be more… humid, at least. That’s London for you, love. Damp and delightful, all in one. Right, nearly to the Millennium Dome, are we? Always seems bigger from this angle. It does, doesn’t it? Remember when it first opened? Everyone was so obsessed. The Millennium Dome. Bit of a silly name now, really. They should have just called it the O2. More practical. Practicality isn't always the name of the game, is it? Though I agree, the Millennium Dome does sound a bit… gauche. Still, it’s iconic. You know, it’s funny how we've lived here for years, and we still marvel at things like this. We never get used to it. Never. And it just highlights how utterly ridiculous it is that we don't own a car. Imagine being able to just… hop in and go. Drive out to the coast, maybe. Don’t start this again. We’ve been over it. The cost, the parking, the sheer inconvenience. It's much easier to rely on public transport. And honestly, the peace of mind is worth it. Being stuck in traffic… no thank you. But freedom! The freedom to just…  go . We wouldn't even need to go far. A weekend in Cornwall. It would be lovely to get the kids out of London for a couple of days. We  do  get them out. Remember that camping trip to the Lake District last summer? That was a holiday, wasn’t it? It was… an experience. Though I still find it baffling why Americans measure everything in cups. Like, half a cup of flour? Really? It’s all so imprecise. Give me grams or ounces any day. It’s just different, isn't it? Different cultures, different ways of doing things. It's fascinating, in a slightly exasperating sort of way. It makes you think about how arbitrary our own systems are, really. Why  do  we do things the way we do? Where did all this come from? Gets you thinking, doesn’t it? It does. I was reading something the other day about the history of the Thames, surprisingly. Apparently, for centuries, people used to wash their laundry in it! No wonder it smelled so dreadful. Blimey. They weren’t overly concerned with hygiene back then, were they?

Honestly, Mum, it’s absolutely chucking it down. Another grey day. I swear, Kent is permanently drizzling. Ruining my mood already. Don't be daft, love. It's just a bit of rain. Keeps the garden going, doesn't it? You teenagers always make such a fuss. Remember when you were little and would still want to play outside, even with wellies and a raincoat on? That was different! I was wearing a bright yellow raincoat with ducks on it. This is just… depressing. Did you manage to get any photos at Leo’s sports day yesterday? Oh, the sports day was a right laugh, wasn’t it? Loads of chaos. Little Elsie kept trying to eat the egg-and-spoon, bless her. And Leo… well, he tripped over the finish line. Proper, spectacular fall. I got loads of pictures, yeah. I’ll show you both later. Elsie’s been obsessed with her teddy bear, Barnaby, all day. Won't let me put him down. Barnaby, huh? Still? Seriously, she’s nearly three. Shouldn't she be moving on from the cuddly toys? I’m still traumatised from having to build a ‘Build-a-Bear’ with her last Christmas. Honestly, the stuffing getting  everywhere … Don’t be knocking the cuddly toys, dear. They’re comforting. I still have a little rabbit my mum gave me. Hidden away, of course, don't want anyone laughing! And Leo will be fine, tripping over the finish line is practically a rite of passage. Elsie doesn't want to move on! She sleeps with him, takes him to the toilet - yes, even  that ’s an experience. Potty training is going… okay. It's less like steady progress and more like two steps forward, three giant puddles backwards. Oh god, potty training. I remember helping you with that with Charlie. Nightmare. Speaking of disasters, my phone keeps cutting out. I'm pretty sure it's the signal in this area. It’s ridiculous. I'm paying for premium data and can barely load Instagram. You and your phones! Always glued to them. Back in my day, if the signal was bad, you just accepted you couldn’t have a conversation. Simpler times. Have you tried turning it off and on again? That usually does the trick. Mum, that’s the solution to  everything  according to you, isn’t it? Turning it off and on again! Elsie’s been asking where the fishes go when they swim.

Right then, sunshine. Let's tackle this. We’ve got a whole six weeks here, and honestly, I'm feeling restless already. Just lounging around isn’t really… me, you know? No, it absolutely isn't. You'd be climbing trees and rescuing koalas by day three. Which, by the way, would be delightfully mad, but probably not appreciated by the owners. Six weeks is a good chunk of time though. What did you have in mind, specifically? Beyond avoiding boredom, of course? Well, I've been thinking a lot about that online course I mentioned – the one on scaling a business. It feels like a crucial step if I’m serious about expanding "Coastal Creations." The Kiwi market's good, but I really want to crack the US. It’s a bit daunting, but six weeks gives me some focused time. That’s a brilliant idea, love. Really proactive. It’s a big investment, though, both time-wise and financially. Have you researched fully what's involved, the tutors, the workload? Not just the glossy promotion, the nitty-gritty? I have! I’ve looked at a few already. This one’s got some impressive testimonials, and the curriculum seems practically built for what I need. Plus, they offer mentorship calls. I reckon if I can dedicate a solid four hours a day, I can actually make decent progress. What about you? Any teaching CPD you've been eyeing up? Remember that online module on inclusive education practices you mentioned? I did, yes. And it's still relevant. It's not as vital as your course, though. Honestly, at this stage, I'm more focused on the 'lifestyle' aspect of this house-sitting gig. A chance to recharge, you know? Though, I  have  been thinking about volunteering at that local community centre. They need a literacy tutor. It could be a really rewarding way to spend some time. That sounds perfect! Seriously. You'd be amazing at that. It’s far more fulfilling than endless marking, isn’t it? I’ll look into it for you – see if they have a website or contact details. Speaking of fulfilling... remember we talked about getting everyone together? Liam and Chloe, and the rest of the crew? Oh, absolutely! That was the whole point of suggesting this house-sitting adventure, wasn't it? A proper catch-up. They're only in Perth for another few months.

Right, I’m proper bugged out by this TikTok thing. Everyone’s doin’ these accent challenges, like it’s some kind of laughin' stock. I saw one where someone was tryin’ to do a posh accent, and it was just…awful. Like, genuinely offensive. Aye, they are a bit much aren't they? People think they’re bein’ clever mimickin’ accents. Remember when we were kids and Jamie used to try and do a pirate accent? Sounded more like a strangled pigeon. Oh God, I do! He was dreadful. But, you know, at least he wasn’t tryin' to be mean about it. This TikTok stuff… it's just lookin' for a reaction, innit? Tell me about it! I saw one where someone was takin' the mickey out of a proper broad Yorkshire accent. Honestly, I nearly spat out me pint. Folk don't understand there's a skill involved in speakin’ like this, and it’s not somethin’ to be laughed at. It's got history. Exactly! It's like, they romanticise other accents, but when it's a northern accent, it's suddenly a joke. Speaking of jokes, did you see that guy in the park yesterday, trying to catch a pigeon? He ended up chasing it right into a bush! Absolute comedy. Oh, I wish I’d seen that! I were proper stressed after that meeting with Mrs. Henderson. She was going on about depreciation schedules again. Honestly, it’s enough to make you want to run away and join a Pokémon Go league. You and me both. I’d be Team Mystic, easy. Always were. Remember when we used to camp out at Rylands Park tryin’ to catch 'em all? Midges everywhere, but worth it for a shiny Charizard. Those were the days. Now I just feel like hidin’ in a duvet fort. Speaking of comfort, anyone fancy some After-Eights with their coffee? I brought a packet. Aye, you don’t need to ask twice! Honestly, those are proper good, aren't they? Much better than those cheap mints you get at service stations. Remember that awful Costa we stopped at on the way to Alton Towers? The coffee tasted like burnt tyres. Don't remind me. My Fitbit would’ve had a heart attack. I swear I lost five years off my life just from the smell of that place. Right, let’s not dwell on service station horrors.

Cor, this gravy's a bit thin, innit? Needs a bit more cornflour next time, I reckon. Still, tastes alright. Though I ain’t got much of an appetite these days. The telly's been filled with nothing but gloom and doom, you know. Politics, bah! Don't you start, Arthur. Gloom and doom is your default setting. It's a lovely dinner, isn’t it? And you’re eating plenty. Stop fussing. Honestly, you’d think you were being starved. Where's Benji? He’s usually dive-bombing the table the moment the potatoes are on. He's upstairs, Mum. Playing some ridiculous game on his tablet. I told him dinner was ready, but he’s in a vital level, apparently. Typical. He’ll be moaning later he’s hungry. Did you see the Norwich match yesterday, Dad? Aye, I did! A right nail-biter, that was. Should’ve put the game away in the first half though. Kept giving the ball away. Makes a fella’s blood boil, it does. Never understood why they kept that young lad Johnson on the pitch so long...waste of a space, ‘e was. You always say that, Arthur. Every game. You're a permanent fixture on the complaining seats at Carrow Road. It’s part of your charm. I thought their midfield was looking pretty solid, actually. Johnson created that chance for Sargent. Chance? A lucky fluke, that was. Fluke or not, Sargent needs to be quicker. Should’ve slotted it away. Should’ve, could’ve, would’ve... that’s all we ever get with Norwich, innit? Oh, Arthur and football! It's a never-ending saga. Now, about Sarah’s party… Have you decided on a theme yet? I was thinking a fifties theme? We could all dress up. A fifties theme is good! I can get some vintage records. And maybe some decorations. It would be nice if Benji actually participated for once. He'll probably come as some superhero. I'm perfectly happy being a greaser. Little black shirt, jeans, slicked-back hair. Easy. Though, finding a decent pomade these days is proving tricky. . You wouldn’t happen to have any, would you, darling? Very funny. I’ll look into it. Dad, you could be Elvis. You’ve got the voice, at least. Elvis? Me? I'd make a right mess of "Hound Dog," I would. More like "Hound…rattling knees and a wheezy cough."

Right, I’m officially stating it. I’m thinking about dropping out. Dropping out? Seriously, Maisie? What brought this on now? You were all bright-eyed and bushy-tailed about Archaeology just last week. You were practically buzzing about Roman pottery. Well, the pottery's still pretty buzzing, innit? But...everything else feels… rubbish. The lectures are boring, the seminars are terrifying, and I'm spending more time panicking about essays I haven’t started than actually enjoying anything. Plus, I keep having these flashbacks to sixth form. Remember how utterly miserable I was doing A-Levels? Yeah, you were a right grumpy bean. But that was different, wasn’t it? Sixth form was just... a necessary evil to get you here, to uni. This is meant to be the good stuff. What about the digs you were looking forward to? You were talking about volunteering in Cornwall next summer. Cornwall's lovely, but I can volunteer in Cornwall whilst working at the Crabshack, can’t I? At least then I'd be earning proper money and not drowning in debt. And honestly, I feel like I'm just… existing here. Trying to force myself to fit into a mould that doesn't suit me. You know, Mum’s been on at me about it too, keepin’ things tidy, proper shoes in the hallway and not trackin’ mud everywhere. It makes me think of being a kid at Nanny’s. Oh, Nanny’s. Don’t even get me started on Nanny and her shoe obsession. She used to spray our shoes with disinfectant. Said they were “breeding grounds for germs.” She’d skin us alive if she saw those trainers you’re scrubbing now. Speaking of which, why are you cleaning your trainers at 10 o'clock on a Tuesday? Because they're filthy, obviously. Got caught in a puddle earlier. Made my socks all soggy. It reminded me… Remember when we were little, and Dad called me "Maisy-Muddy-Puddles"? Oh, god, yes! And he used to film you splashing about in every puddle you could find. He’d narrate like a nature documentary. “Here we observe Maisie-Muddy-Puddles in her natural habitat…” He was mental. Where did “Maisie” even come from, anyway? My mum always says it's an old Cornish name, but I've never really looked into it. It is, apparently. Gran did some digging. Means something like "pearl."

Honestly, it’s  so  good to see you, Liv! Ages, hasn’t it? Like, properly ages. This place is lovely, isn’t it? A bit fancy for a Tuesday, but hey, we deserve it. What are you thinking of getting? I'm tempted by the scallops. Chloe! You too! I know, it feels like a lifetime ago we were crammed into tiny lecture halls at uni. This  is  lovely. And yes, we absolutely do deserve something nice. Scallops sound amazing – I might have to steal your idea. I'm eyeing up the roasted duck; it smells divine. How’s everything been? Work still a whirlwind? Work’s...work. It’s alright, you know? Lots of spreadsheets and meetings. Nothing  terribly  exciting, but it keeps me busy. Coordinating those social media campaigns is a bit more fun than I anticipated though. Definitely a learning curve. What about you? Still thriving in the Pearson marketing world? Are you conquering the corporate ladder? Conquering is a strong word! It’s…interesting. The campaigns themselves are great – lots of creativity involved, which I love. The office politics, less so. Honestly, it can be a bit brutal. Some of the senior people…well, let’s just say they operate on a different level of passive-aggression. You wouldn’t believe the email chains! But salary's good, and the office has a decent coffee machine, so I can’t complain  too  much. Ugh, I hate office politics. Makes everything so needlessly stressful. It’s lucky I’m mostly working from home these days. At least I can avoid the drama entirely. Have you heard from Maya and Ben recently? I haven't seen them posting anything on Instagram for ages. Wonder if they're still together. No, actually! That’s what I was going to ask you. They’ve gone completely radio silent. Their last post was…what, a cute picture of them hiking in the Lake District? It feels like years ago. I’m a bit worried, to be honest. Remember how dramatic they used to get? I hope no one’s ended up crying over someone else. I know! I've got this nagging feeling something's up. I saw Ben liked a photo on someone's Instagram - Sarah, I think? Don't tell his girlfriend! They were clearly flirting. Maybe it's nothing, but it doesn't look good. Should we try and track them down?

Right then, Thomas. Let’s 'ave a proper look at this, shall we? You've been at this Amazon business all afternoon, haven't you? I can hear the clicking away from the kitchen! Honestly, you’d think you were trying to win the lottery, the amount of things you're puttin' in your basket. It’s not just random things, Auntie Maureen. I'm researchin’ for my History project. And it’s really useful to compare prices, you know? Like, this model railway track is £35 on Amazon, but £48 on the hobby shop website. Model railway track? Fancy that. When I were a lad, we played with sticks and a rusty old tin can! But comparing prices is fair enough. Still, be careful, love. Amazon's alright, mind, but you need to look at the seller, aye? 'Ave you checked if they're a proper business, or some lad down the street sellin' somethin' he bought in bulk from China? Yeah, of course. It says "Fulfilled by Amazon" so it's gotta be legit, right? They wouldn't let dodgy sellers use their warehouse. "Fulfilled by Amazon" doesn’t mean it’s  made  by them, Thomas. It just means they’re handling the delivery and returns. The actual seller could still be a right rogue. You need to read the reviews, see what other folk are sayin'. And look at their star rating, that’s important. Right, okay. Good point. What about eBay then? You’re always on eBay, Auntie Maureen. Buying antique teacups and whatnot. Is that safer? Well, eBay's a different beast altogether, isn't it? It’s more… unpredictable. You're dealin' directly with individuals, and whilst most of 'em are honest as the day is long, some aren’t. You gotta be extra vigilant. Look at their feedback score. Anything under 98%, I’d be wary. And read  every  single review, not just the good ones. So, like, if someone's sold 500 things and only has 490 positive feedback? That’s a red flag? Aye, that's a reason to be cautious. And look at the  type  of feedback. "Fast delivery, well-packaged" is good. But "Item not as described," or "Seller didn't respond to messages" – steer well clear! And always, always pay with PayPal. They offer buyer protection, you see. If somethin’ goes wrong, you can make a claim.

Rain again. Seems like it's been raining non-stop since we got here to Cambridge. Not exactly the sunshine I was hoping for when I booked this little getaway. It’s Cambridge, Dad. Don't expect the Mediterranean. It’s charmingly grey, isn’t it? And we're inside, warm and dry. Much better than being out in it. How's your knee feeling today? Dr. Patel seemed optimistic last time. Optimistic, is he? He always is. Says I need to “manage the inflammation.” Easy for him to say, sitting in a warm, dry office. It twinges somethin' awful when I get up from the chair, you know. Makes me feel my age, it does. Sixty-eight, and creaking like an old gate. You're not that old, Dad. And it just means you’ve lived a long life. Remember you used to climb trees when you were a kid? That probably had something to do with it. Aye, I did. Reckless little tyke, I was. Climbing the old apple tree in the garden back in Modern. Didn't think about knees then, did I? Just wanted to reach the best apples. Sometimes I miss those days, you know? Simpler. I get that. But things change, Dad. And it's not all bad. You get to relax, enjoy your time. You should be sketching, doing the things you always said you'd do when you retired. Remember you were going to paint that watercolour of the Thames? I know, I know. It’s just… motivation’s a funny thing, isn’t it? Seems to have packed its bags and left. Besides, the light's never quite right. Always a cloud in the sky. Like today. Don't be like that. Look, I've booked you a pottery class next week. Just one session. It's supposed to be really relaxing, and you can make something practical. A nice mug, perhaps. Pottery, eh? Never thought I’d be messing about with clay. Sounds a bit…frivolous, if you don't mind me saying. Frivolous? Building something with your hands isn't frivolous, Dad. It's therapeutic. And it's something different. Think of it as a challenge. Plus, it’s something to  do . Alright, alright. You’ve worn me down. Pottery it is. But if I end up covered in mud and looking like a right fool, I’m blaming you.

Right, so Christmas Day. Proper chaos, innit? Mum’s already on the warpath about sprouts. Says they're essential. Essential! Like they’re some sort of medicinal requirement. Sprouts are fine. I don't mind 'em, especially roasted with bacon. It’s the cranberry sauce I’m dreading. Last year it tasted like sugared vinegar. Honestly, a crime against Christmas. Oh, cranberry sauce? My nan makes the  best  cranberry sauce. It’s got orange zest and a hint of ginger. Completely transforms the whole thing. Anyway, about Christmas Day…are we  actually  going to try and fly out to Oz on the 25th? That sounds mental, even for us. Mental, yeah, but doable. Got the flights booked, anyway. They were surprisingly cheap. Early flight, too. Like, 6am. Brutal. But think of the sunshine! And my mum beating me up about it if I don’t show. She’d never let me hear the end of it. 6am on Christmas Day? You're a saint, mate. Or seriously sleep-deprived. I can’t even fathom it. We're staying put this year. Mum's insisted. Said we need to appreciate the…authenticity of a proper British Christmas. Authenticity? She means hours of forced festivities and Dad trying to tell the same three jokes. And Aunt Susan inevitably bringing that weird fruitcake that smells like car exhaust fumes. Oh, bless Aunt Susan. It  is  a unique fruitcake. My café's going to be rammed on Boxing Day. People needing a serious sugar fix after all the Christmas Day dramas. I’ve ordered extra mince pies, though. Got a lovely supplier down in Brighton. Really good pastry. Mince pies, excellent! See, that's the Christmas spirit right there. Speaking of wildlife suffering… did anyone hear about that poor deer that got hit on the A40 last week? Awful sight apparently. Yeah, heard about that. Proper sad, innit? Makes you think. All the foxes about too. Mum’s putting out extra scraps for them this year. Says they have a tough time over Christmas. Mum's always looking out for the animals. Remember when she tried to rescue that badger from under the car? Took two neighbours and a lot of shouting to get it out. Oh, my god, yes! She ended up with scratches all over her arms. And blamed the council for not providing proper badger signage. Sounds like a classic.

Right then, Cambridge is…still a good hour away, isn’t it? Traffic's a bit sluggish just outside Milton Keynes. Should’ve left earlier, really. You said that half an hour ago, Ben. Relax. We'll get there. And besides, look at this hilarious thread someone’s started on Twitter about regional accents. Apparently, people in Norwich genuinely think their accent is the standard. Norwich? Seriously? It’s barely distinguishable from a bog-standard East Anglian drawl. The absurdity of them thinking it’s superior… it's brilliant, in a deeply irritating way. I’m putting together a sound compilation for the next game, you know? Different accents, for NPC voices. Makes them feel more believable. Right, because you need  more  ways to immerse players. You’re already building a whole sentient universe, Liam. NPC accents are just another layer of complexity. You’ll be coding for weeks! It's brilliant though, isn't it? Creating realistic voices. Remember that documentary we watched about forensic linguistics? How they can pinpoint origins just from a few words? It’s fascinating. I’ve started noticing accents more, actually, since I started editing. You pick up on the nuances. Definitely. For the game, I want to avoid just slapping on generic ‘Northern’ or ‘Scottish’ accents. I’m aiming for micro-regions. Like, someone from Burnley sounds different to someone from Lancaster, even though they're practically next door to each other. It’s all about the subtleties. That’s taking it a bit far, isn’t it? I mean, I struggle to tell the difference between a Coventrian and a Dudley accent half the time, let alone multiply that by every town in Lancashire. You're just hopeless, Ben. You're a Birmingham boy through and through. Blending in is in your DNA. There’s nothing wrong with blending in! Although… Actually, thinking about it, someone from Birmingham does have a kind of…neutrality about them, doesn't it? It absorbs a bit of everything. It's a melting pot, for sure. Which is probably why you struggle to differentiate. It’s all been diluted. Anyway, speaking of journeys, are we still firm on dropping me off at the tech hub? I’ve got that late meeting with the investors. Yeah, you’re good. We’ll drop you off and then head straight to my aunt’s. Remember she’s got that ridiculous collection of porcelain dolls?

Physics was brutal today. Mr. Davies was on one, going on about quantum entanglement for a solid hour. My brain feels like mush. Nah, entanglement’s proper interesting, innit? Like, spooky action at a distance, Einstein called it. It's mental. Physics is alright when it’s not just endless equations. You two still dissecting Davies’ lecture? I think I accidentally fell asleep during the bit about superposition. Woke up with a textbook imprint on my cheek. Not my finest moment. Sounds about right. I was trying to visualise it, honestly. Two particles linked across… well, anything. It's just…weird. Anyway, physics aside, what’s everyone been listening to lately? Anything decent? I've been rinsing Central Cee’s new mixtape. "No Thanks." Proper banger. You heard it, Liam? Yeah, yeah, I've heard it. It's alright, very catchy, but it all sounds a bit samey after a while, doesn’t it? Like, the beats are great, don't get me wrong, but I’m craving something a bit different. Central Cee's good for a vibe, definitely, but I’ve been properly obsessed with Khruangbin. They’re an instrumental trio from Texas. It’s amazing, just proper chilled and groovy. You wouldn’t think you’d like it, Liam, you're usually all about the energy. Khruangbin? Never heard of them. Instrumental? Hmm... doesn't sound thrilling. What kind of music  is  it, exactly? Like, what genre? It’s like...a mix of soul, funk, and psychedelic rock, innit? Really chilled out though, perfect for zoning out. Think summer vibes. Exactly. And their basslines…they just  melt  you. Listen, I’ll send you a track later, "Maria Tambien" is a good starting point. Honestly, it's a massive change from the stuff you usually listen to. Alright, alright, you’ve piqued my interest. But if I hate it, you’re buying me a chocolate bar. Speaking of music, did you see that new film, ‘Babylon’? Baz Luhrmann, right? Nah, didn’t see it. Heard it’s mental though. Massive, loud, all over the place. Is it any good? I’m trying to decide whether to go with my cousin next week. It’s… a lot. It's three hours long, and it hits you with  everything . The acting is brilliant, Margot Robbie is phenomenal, but it’s…intense. It's like they threw every single idea they had at the screen.

Right, so, Balanceability. Honestly, it’s been a saga. Leo, you’re absolutely refusing to wear the helmet today. And Maisie, you're wobbling more than you were yesterday. What’s going on? It’s wobbly, Mummy! And it tickles! And I keep falling over. It's boring! Bikes are better! Boring? Leo, it's about building confidence! It’s about succeeding at something, even if it's just staying upright for a few seconds longer. Remember how hard you found learning to ride your scooter? Balanceability is basically the same principle. But Bethany at school got a sticker for being good at something today. That’s lovely, darling. Everyone deserves a sticker for trying their best. And you  are  trying. It's all about perseverance. Like when Mrs. Davies was showing us how to write a persuasive argument. It took me ages to get it right, didn’t it? Lots of scribbling and starting over. Bethany's got a new house! And it's being renovated. She said her dad is building a swimming pool. A swimming pool! Fancy that. Apparently, they're even having a man-made waterfall. Though, we absolutely mustn’t be diving in, you two, ever! Remember what we talked about? Always check the depth and be careful. It's not worth a risk. I read a really scary article about diving accidents once... Scary! Like in the movies? Sort of. Just, much less dramatic and a lot more serious. Anyway, back to Balanceability. We'll take it slow. Five minutes, and then we can have pizza. That's a promise. Pizza?! With pepperoni? Definitely pepperoni. And maybe some pineapple for you, Maisie? Remember how you said pineapple and ham is a really good combination? Eww, pineapple on pizza is yucky! Sausage is better. Alright, alright, sausage for you then, champ. You know, I heard some interesting things at school today. Little Freddie was telling me about National Cat Day in Japan. Apparently, they give cats lots of treats and special toys. Cats get presents? Do you think Mittens would like a present? I'm sure she would, sweetheart. Maybe we'll get her a little feather toy. Speaking of which, I need to remember to get some fish food. She's been eyeing up the goldfish tank with a very suspicious look. Back to assessments though… Mr. Henderson’s made it clear the Year 2 reading comprehension tests are looming.

Right then, spill. You’ve been all quiet since you got 'ere. Everything alright, love? You look like you've seen a ghost. Just…a bit stressed, I suppose. Work's been mad, honestly. Production deadlines are looming and Gareth’s being Gareth – you know, completely incapable of remembering anything without a five-page spreadsheet. Gareth, eh? Sounds familiar. My Uncle Barry's the same, bless 'im. Can't put a pint on without a diagram. But stressed enough to be quiet? You're usually a right chatterbox. It's more than just work, I think. It's... dating. Ugh. Oh, let me guess. Another one bites the dust? Who was it this time? That nice accountant from the pub? No, it was Liam. We’d been seeing each other for, like, three months. He seemed… promising. Smart, funny, stylish… all the right boxes. So what went tits up? Don't be shy, love. We've all been there. He... ghosted me. Just completely vanished. Stopped replying to texts, blocked me on social media. Nothing. Like I never existed. It’s just… so cowardly. That’s rotten, that is. Proper rotten. Some lads have no backbone, do they? Honestly, that’s a low blow. You deserve better than someone who can’t even have the guts to say, 'Look, I’m not feeling it.' I know, logically. But it still stings. And I’m starting to think I’m just attracting the wrong sort. Don't you think that, love. It's not you, it's 'em. Trust me. I've had my fair share of dodgy chaps from Yorkshire. Most of 'em are lovely, mind, but you definitely have to weed 'em out. Anyway, right, posh dating problems aside, tell me about your exercise routine? You were saying you were trying something new? Yeah, I signed up for a Pilates class. Honestly, it's brutal. I feel like I'm being slowly dismantled bit by bit. My core muscles are screaming. Pilates! You, a production controller who probably spends all day hunched over a computer, are trying Pilates? You're brave, lass! I tried yoga once. Ended up looking like a pretzel someone had sat on. It’s supposed to be good for posture and flexibility. I keep thinking about my grandma, who used to do Pilates religiously. She was ninety-two and could still pot a mean game of snooker.

Well, that was a grand Domino Drive, wasn’t it? Doreen’s still moaning about losing at Rummy – bless her cotton socks. She blamed young Thomas, you know. Said he was “cheating with his little games.” Honestly, the woman! She always blames someone else, Auntie Jean. It's just how she is. I won a couple of games though, beat Brenda fair and square. She did look a bit put out. Aye, she did. Brenda’s got a right competitive streak, that one. Still, it’s a good laugh, isn’t it? Gets us all out and about. Though my hips are screaming now, I can tell you that! Did you see old Mr. Harrison trying to get a handle on that new scooter of his? Almost ended up in Mrs. Patterson’s rose bushes, he did! Harrison and that thing! I told him it was too much for him, but did he listen? No. Said he wanted to "keep up with the times." More like causing havoc! He nearly took out my trailer on the way back from Thirsk last week, that man. A close call, that was. Nearly took out your trailer?! What were you doing in Thirsk? Hauling sheep, lad. Always hauling sheep. Business is steady enough, can’t complain. Though the price of diesel is enough to make you weep, it is. Speaking of which, are you having another slice, Jean? That pepperoni looks rather tasty. I might just, Arthur. Though I’m trying to be good. Easter’s not far off, and I’m needing to squeeze back into my favourite skirt. It's a bit snug at the moment, you know? This pizza isn't helping! You look alright, Auntie Jean. Don't worry about the skirt. Besides, you deserve a treat. You've been working hard marking those essays, haven't you? Oh, lad, don’t remind me. Those Year 11s are a handful this year. All angst and phones. Trying to get them to look up from TikTok and appreciate some good literature is a constant battle. Still, someone’s gotta do it. Have you been practising your cricket, Thomas? The club's looking for new players. Cricket, eh? Should be getting you down to the nets, Jean. Good for the fresh air. Better than sitting cooped up with those teenagers, I reckon. Though, I’ll tell you what, I need a haircut.

Right, then. Earl Grey it is. Standard, innit? Fancy a biscuit, love? Got some ginger snaps. Ginger snaps sound perfect, thanks. This Cambridge air is proper chilling, even indoors. You know, I was thinking about that pub we went to last week, The Cambridge Blue. The food was… interesting. Interesting is a kind word, Andy. The cauliflower cheese was basically just cauliflower and a lot of grief. I swear, they’d never 'eard of nutmeg. Proper grim. But, the beer was decent, eh? At least they got that right. The beer was the saving grace, absolutely. Though I’m still wondering about their approach to vegetables generally. It's like they've declared war on flavour. Remember the carrots? Pale, almost translucent… Don't remind me! Like something you'd find in a forgotten corner of the fridge. Honestly, you’d think with all the fancy restaurants about here, they’d manage a decent carrot. Up North, even the pub grub has more personality. My mam would have a right go at them! She'd be like, "Look at this! No colour, no flavour! Where's the butter, the herbs, the love?!" Your mam sounds like a culinary force of nature. She'd probably sort out their whole kitchen. Speaking of food, I saw that article about Tom Holland apparently opening a pie shop. A pie shop! Can you believe it? Tom Holland? Spiderman? Doing  pies ? That's… unexpected. Like, he’s known for swinging about, not pastry. What kind of pies, then? Keep-fit pies? Apparently, traditional British pies. Steak and ale, chicken and mushroom, that sort of thing. They’re saying he’s got a real passion for baking, came from his gran. Now that's a story! A Hollywood actor obsessed with pies. I'd go. I’d pay good money to watch Spiderman wrestle a suet pudding. It'd be brilliant! Though, could he actually make a decent pie? I’d be judging, you know. Expertly. He’s apparently been learning from a top pastry chef in London. They’re saying his crusts are to die for. Though, I'm still trying to picture him covered in flour. It’s a good image, isn’t it? All those muscles and he’s trying to crimp a pie crust. I reckon he’d be surprisingly good, though. Strong fingers. Good for getting that pastry nice and even. Maybe he'll inspire other celebrities to pursue niche culinary passions.

Right, okay, my turn! "Abstraction." Hmmm… “A brave tractor is stealing onions!” Gareth, come on! That's ridiculous, Seren. Seriously? "A brave tractor is stealing onions?" That’s barely articulate, love. I thought it was brilliant! Very imaginative, considering the letter constraints. It’s the spirit of the game, Rhys! Not just being… sensible. Now, now, Gareth, be fair. It’s a bit loose, isn't it? But I’ll give Seren points for effort, the girl's trying! Back in my day, we’d have been strictly adhering to the dictionary. No made-up words, no nonsense! Oh, Dai, you’re always going on about 'back in your day'! Things have moved on, haven't they? It’s supposed to be fun, isn't it? I think Seren's response was lovely, full of character. My turn! “Elephant.” Hmm... "Eleven penguins are eating lentils." That’s even worse than Seren’s! Lentils? Who eats lentils with penguins? Don’t be silly, Gareth. Penguins are probably very cultured. They appreciate a good lentil! And it fits, doesn't it? It definitely fits, Mum! Though I maintain my tractor is more believable than penguin-lentil combinations. You’re taking this far too seriously, mate. Lighten up! My turn. "Violin." Right... “Very intelligent owls love ice cream." Owl ice cream... Honestly. We're lowering the bar drastically here. Right, my turn. "Butterfly." "Big blue butterflies flit furiously." See? That's a proper sentence! Yes, that's much better, Gareth. A proper sentence. Although, flit furiously? Sounds rather energetic for a butterfly. It’s poetic license, Dai! He's being artistic. Remember, this is  Articulate , not a grammar lesson. Okay, next word… "Pancake!" Oh, this is tricky. It is a bit. Pancakes are deceptively difficult to articulate in a pinch. You're thinking too much, Geraint. Just say something! Alright, alright. "Persistent penguins play poker patiently." You're obsessed with penguins! They’re clearly your animal of choice. I just… they're amusing, aren’t they? All waddling about. Penguins. The world has gone mad. When I was a boy, we played with marbles. Marbles! Not penguins and… persistence. You'd get lost in a penguin convention, Dai. Right, my turn again. “Cloud.” “Crisp clouds create colourful corners.” That’s lovely, Mum! Quite evocative. See, Gareth? That's how it's done. Feeling the pressure now, are we? Your turn. "Rhythm.” “Radiant roses rhyme relentlessly.”

Right then, everyone settled? I’ve shuffled properly this time, Gareth, no cheating! Last time you were trying to palm a Queen - blatant! Oi, now! Just admiring its craftsmanship! Besides, you were winning anyway, Chloe. Luckily for me, this time, I'm feeling my luck’s about to change. A bit of  sus wedi bod  - some good fortune coming! You say that every game, Rhys. And it never changes. Honestly, you’d think you'd have learned by now. Don’t listen to him, Rhys. He's just jealous you've got more patience than he does. Remember that time he threw his cards at the table because he didn't get a straight flush? That was one time, Mamgu! And it was a very exasperating straight flush situation. This game’s supposed to be relaxing! Relaxing for  me  is winning. Seriously though, is anyone playing this seriously? Because I’m aiming to bankrupt you all. Oh, I’ll play seriously enough to beat you, Chloe. Don't underestimate me. I've been studying Bridge. Bridge? Gareth, you couldn't remember the basic rules of Bridge if I wrote them on your forehead. Let him dream, Chloe! It’s good for him. Besides, he's been reading a rather intimidating-looking book. Maybe he’s trying to become a card shark in secret. It's called "Advanced Card Strategy." It outlines psychological warfare. Psychological warfare? Over a game of Hearts? You’re a card! Right, right. Enough with the theories. Let's  play . Rhys, you’re lead. Don't start any nonsense. Seven of clubs. Nice and safe. See, I'm already thinking strategically. Ten of clubs. Trying to get rid of the higher cards. It's a classic move, Rhys. Very original. Jack of diamonds. Testing the waters. Queen of diamonds. Trying to trump you, darling! Ha! I don’t have any diamonds. Clearly, my strategy is working wonders. Your strategy is being incredibly lucky, that's all. I'm just saving my strength. I’ve got a few tricks up my sleeve, believe me. Just wait until  that  card comes out. You're always saying that, Rhys. Remember when you tried to bluff at poker with that two of hearts you were convinced was an ace? Oh, it was a spectacle! We still laugh about that. Okay, okay, point taken. It was a dodgy bluff. But I’ve learned from my mistakes.

Honestly, Bridgerton is getting  so  predictable. Like, do they think we're all that easily fooled? The romantic tension is just… staged. Nah, I love it. It's pure escapism. And the costumes are amazing. You can't deny that. Besides, it's not like you're exactly bursting with better suggestions. What have you been watching, Miss "Highbrow Literature"? I’ve been watching documentaries, thank you very much. And reading. Unlike some people who spend their evenings swooning over dukes. So, have you heard anything back about those care assistant jobs you applied for? Ooh, mince pies! Perfect timing. And yes, I had an interview! It was actually really good, surprisingly. They asked about handling difficult situations, which was a bit nerve-wracking, but I think I managed to pull it off. Difficult situations, huh? Want me to give you some pointers? I deal with a  lot  of that in my work. Not exactly the same, obviously, but... adapting and thinking on your feet is a skill they appreciate. Seriously? You would? That'd be amazing, Liam. I’m just worried about… you know, things getting too emotional. It can be. But you learn pretty quickly how to manage your own emotions and focus on what the person needs. And honestly, seeing someone's face light up when you help them? It's the best feeling. Did someone say mince pies?! So, is everyone stressing about uni applications? Because I'm officially panicking. I still haven’t actually written my personal statement. Seriously, Chloe? Christmas Eve and you  still  haven't? I finished mine weeks ago. Though, honestly, I’m starting to think my first draft sounded like a robot wrote it. Don't worry, Chloe. Everyone procrastinates. Mine was a disaster zone until last week. I basically just wrote a brain dump and then spent three hours trying to make it sound vaguely coherent. It’s probably still terrible, but at least it’s  something . What are you even applying for? Fashion design. Which is incredibly ambitious, I know. But I just… I love it. My parents keep saying I need something more "practical" though. Like accounting, apparently. Fashion design  is  practical! People always need clothes! And it's a genuinely creative field. Don’t let your parents crush your dreams. My mum keeps going on about apprenticeships. Keeps saying they're the future. Like university is a waste of money.

Lovely dinner, Anon. Really lovely. You’ve outdone yourself, dear. Though, honestly, a bit more gravy wouldn’t have gone amiss. Never can have too much gravy, eh? It was good, Nan. Thanks! I tried to follow your recipe, but I think I might have slightly burned the Yorkshire puddings. Luckily, there were loads of potatoes to compensate. And you're right, a little more gravy would have been perfect. Yorkshire puddings were alright. Could’ve been crispier, though. Everything’s gotta have a bit of crunch, innit? Crunch, schmunch. It's the flavour that matters, Liam. You've got a peculiar palate, you do. So, Anon, you were saying about getting a car? Really? After all this fuss about being environmentally conscious? Well, it’s not  entirely  about being environmentally conscious, Nan. Remember how long it took us to get home last week after that concert? Two buses and a thirty-minute trek in the pouring rain? My feet were absolutely killing me. And it’s not like I’ll be driving every day. Mostly just for weekend trips, and maybe getting the shopping. Weekend trips, eh? Where are we talking about? Brighton? We haven’t been to Brighton in ages. Maybe Brighton. Or somewhere a bit further out, like the New Forest. Somewhere we can actually go walking without having to rely on public transport that runs on a questionable schedule. Walking! That's what you should be doing. Lovely walks in Cambridge. Right on our doorstep. Don’t need a motor car for that. I used to walk everywhere when I was a girl. Ten miles to school and ten miles back! In all weathers! You young people… no stamina. Nan, I walk to work every day! It’s a good hour’s walk. And I enjoy it, but sometimes… sometimes it's just easier. Especially when the weather’s like it was last week. You could get a bike. Much better for the environment than a car. And you can cycle pretty much anywhere. I thought about it, Liam, but then I remember that time I cycled up that ridiculously steep hill near Steyning and nearly ended up in a ditch. Plus, the rain… not a fan. Cycling in the rain is no fun at all. Always ending up soggy. Now, driving…  that’s  a skill. Learned to drive on a Morris Minor, I did. Little thing it was.

Oh, hello! Didn’t realize there were so many people here for Alumni Day. Quite a buzz, isn't it? I’m Eleanor, by the way. Language Research Co-ordinator with the department. Hi Eleanor! I’m Amelia. Language Research Administrator, also with the department, though I'm relatively new. It  is  rather lively. I was just admiring the architecture - this Law Faculty is stunning. Charming, isn’t it? I’ve been coming to these things… well, for a few decades now, I suppose. John Davies here. I used to lecture in Linguistics, now officially retired, but they keep dragging me back for these events. John Davies! I remember your lectures on sociolinguistics, actually. They were brilliant. So much insightful thinking. Really? My supervisor mentioned you. Said you were instrumental in shaping aspects of modern linguistic study. Oh, well, I wouldn’t go  that  far. Just paddled about a bit in the shallows, I think! But it’s lovely to be remembered. So, you’re both in Language Research? Splendid! What sort of things are you working on? I'm currently involved in a project looking at the evolution of regional dialects in Eastern England – tracing the impact of historical migration patterns. Rather fascinating really, how language shifts and adapts. We’ve been delving into some quite old parish records. I spent rather a lot of last week deciphering 18th-century handwritten notes. My Aylesbury accent is constantly being challenged by the older forms! That sounds incredibly detailed. My project’s a bit broader, looking at language acquisition patterns in multilingual children specifically. We have a grant to explore how exposure to different languages impacts cognitive development. I was just back from a conference in Spain actually - presenting some initial findings. Spain! Wonderful place. I spent a good few years there researching Basque. A truly remarkable language, isn't it? So isolating, so ancient. Did you get any time to venture beyond the conference? Not much, I’m afraid! Mostly Barcelona, some quick trips to Madrid for meetings. I'd love to spend more time there; the culture is so vibrant. Honestly, I'd love to visit the Basque Country one day. The linguistic isolation is just so compelling. I've heard incredible things. My grandmother on my mother’s side always wanted to go, but never managed it. Heard it's beautiful. Do you speak any Spanish, Amelia? Enough to get by, I suppose.

Right, well that was… a lot. Two years is a  long  time to not see family, isn’t it? Especially when they’re as chaotic as Sarah and Chloe. Chaotic is putting it mildly, Liam. More like a delightful hurricane! Honestly, seeing them both, all grown up… Chloe’s practically a teenager now! Remember when she used to dress up as a fairy and chase us around the garden? I do! She was obsessed with fairies. And Sarah… bless her heart, she kept trying to dress  me  in fairy wings. I was thirteen! I told her I wasn't a fairy, I was a recruitment consultant in the making. Which, apparently, didn’t impress her at all. You were always ambitious, weren’t you, Jess? Seriously though, it's good to reconnect. Mum was proper chuffed. Although, she did spend a good fifteen minutes telling Auntie Maggie about that Facebook post I shared about the grammar errors in that advert. Oh, Mum and her grammar policing! Don’t tell me she went on about passive voice again? “Liam, darling, the correct phrasing would be ‘Applicants  should  submit…’ not ‘Submissions  are required from  applicants!’ Honestly, it’s a public service, apparently.” Classic Mum. At least it gave her something to focus on. She's been a bit worried about Uncle George and his hip, hasn’t she? I heard he's refusing to do his exercises. That’s George all over. Stubborn as an ox. He’s convinced the physio is plotting against him. We’ve been trying to convince him to do the ice bucket challenge for charity, but he says it’s “frivolous nonsense.” The ice bucket challenge? Really? Hasn’t he heard about the funds it raises for ALS research? Seems a bit… insensitive. Plus, it's a bit chilly for it now. We're heading into October! I know! I tried to explain that to him. It’s not just about the cold, it’s about raising awareness. But he just grumbled something about drafts and rheumatism. Speaking of charity, I'm involved in a fundraiser for a local animal shelter next month. Thought you might be interested, Liam? They're hoping to raise enough for a new enclosure. Absolutely! I’d love to help. I've got a few contacts through the university. Maybe I could donate a language lesson or two as an auction prize? That’s brilliant, love.

Honestly, this thing. It's more complicated than a quadratic equation! I spent a good fifteen minutes this morning trying to program it to make a simple cappuccino. Fifteen minutes! And it still came out looking like dishwater. You're exaggerating, Mum. It’s a pretty standard machine. Did you try the manual? Manual? Don't be absurd, darling. Who reads manuals these days? Besides, the font is smaller than a flea's eyelash. Honestly, the modern obsession with… complexity for the sake of it. It’s quite infuriating. Morning, ladies. What’s all the fuss about a coffee machine? Sounds like another existential crisis brewing. You alright, love? Just the usual, Michael. Struggling to function in a world dominated by technological horrors. And speaking of horrifying, have you had a chance to look at those quotes for the removal and storage? They’re outrageous! I did, yeah. They’re high, definitely. But not  insane . We’re moving a full house of contents, Mum, and storing it for six months. It's not going to be cheap. I’ve emailed a couple more companies though, just to get some more comparisons. Six months… that's a long time to be paying storage fees. Are you sure that's the best option? Could we look at downsizing some things? There's a  lot  of chintz in that house, love. Don’t you dare criticize my chintz, Michael! Each piece has a story! And downsizing isn’t an option. This is our family history, preserved in cushions and teacups! Right. Family history. Look, let's table the chintz debate for now. What do you think about Starmer's recent pronouncements? He seems to be trying to appeal to the middle ground. The man's a grey pudding! No conviction whatsoever. It’s all focus groups and careful phrasing. Where's the fire? Where's the passion? It’s not what we need right now. Where’s the idealism? It's all so... safe. I agree with your mother, to a point. He is a bit bland. But you've got to appreciate the stability he provides. Labour needed that after…well, you know. But isn't stability bordering on complacency? People are angry, Dad. They’re struggling. They need  something  to believe in, something more than just… incremental change. Precisely! Remember when Blair used to talk about a "new dawn"? A bit daft, looking back, but at least he was aiming for something!

Honestly, Mum, I’m already feeling a bit overwhelmed with Christmas plans. It’s barely November! The school nativity is booked solid, I've got three different Christmas markets I'm supposed to be helping with, and then, you know,  actual  Christmas itself. Oh, darling, don’t start with the drama already! It always happens. You become a festive whirlwind and then collapse in a heap on Boxing Day. Remember when you were little and you insisted on making every single Christmas decoration yourself? We were knee-deep in glitter and paper chains for weeks! And Dad nearly divorced you over the tinsel! I do remember that. The workload feels different now, though. Back then, it was fun, a project. Now it feels…obligatory. Like I  have  to do all these things to maintain some image of festive cheer, and I'm exhausted before it even begins. It’s a modern affliction, isn’t it? This pressure to curate the perfect Christmas. Social media doesn't help, with everyone showing off their flawlessly decorated homes and artisan gingerbread. Forget about it. Focus on what  you  enjoy. What’s giving you the most stress right now? It's Jamie's family, mostly. They’re suggesting we all go to their place in Cornwall for Christmas this year. Which sounds lovely in theory, but… it's a  lot . It's a long drive, his mum likes to micromanage everything, and his aunt Brenda will definitely corner me to discuss my "life choices" again. You know, the whole "when are you settling down" routine. Oh, Brenda! Bless her heart. She means well, she just lacks a filter. Cornwall for Christmas, though...it  is  beautiful. Any chance you could suggest somewhere else for Christmas day? Maybe a smaller gathering at your flat this year? You could cook a roast, invite a few close friends… I’ve floated the idea, but his mum seemed…disappointed. She’s already started plotting the Christmas menu and sending out Save-the-Dates. It’s a bit much. And then there's Liam. He’s hinting about wanting a proper Christmas with his girlfriend this year, too. I feel pulled in two directions. Liam’s just starting out, isn't he? He probably wants to show off his domestic skills and impress his girlfriend. That's perfectly normal. You can't be everything to everyone, love. Set some boundaries. Explain that you appreciate the invitations, but you need to prioritize your own well-being this year.

Right, so, has anyone heard owt from Liam lately? I haven't seen 'im since that dodgy kebab we all had after the bowling last month. Proper gave me the runs, that did. Liam? Nah, been quiet as a mouse. He's probably holed up in his mum's, still trying to convince her he needs a new gaming rig. Seriously though, he seemed a bit down last time I saw him. Said he was struggling with uni. Yeah, poor lad. I messaged him briefly last week, just to see if he was okay. He said he was battling with a module on Victorian literature. Said he couldn’t tell a Dickens from a Thackeray! Victorian literature! Cor, that sounds a nightmare. I’m doing medieval history, and even that’s a challenge. At least knights in shining armour are a bit easier to picture than some fella writing poetry about gloomy London. Still, at least he’s trying. He just needs to get out more. Maybe a Richmond sausage roll would cheer him up. Waterfields makes the best ones, don't they? Proper meaty. Better than them cheap supermarket ones, anyway. Oh, Waterfields! Don’t even get me started. Their Richmonds are legendary. I got some last week for me dad – he’d been moanin’ all day about the terrible supermarket ones. He practically inhaled them. Me dad's the same. Used to get ‘em every Saturday for breakfast. Proper treat, that was. Remember when Grandma used to keep a huge pile of handkerchiefs in her sewing box? Always had one tucked up her sleeve. You'd get a right telling off if you sneezed and didn't grab one! Oh my god, yes! Grandma was a handkerchief tyrant. I remember trying to hide when I felt a sneeze coming on, just to avoid the lecture. She'd say, "A proper lady always carries a handkerchief, Eliza! Don't be a heathen!" My nan was the same, bless her. Always had a crocheted one on her. I still have one she made me. It’s terribly floral, mind, but I keep it just in case. You never know when you’ll need a good handkerchief. Speaking of things that are a bit grim... has anyone noticed Dave’s snoring lately? It’s been louder than ever. I stayed over at his last weekend, and I swear I thought a walrus was living in the next room.

Oh, that was lovely, Dad. Honestly, just sitting in the garden with a cuppa and a good book… exactly what I needed after this week. Project Phoenix nearly killed me. Aye, well, you earned it, lass. Sounds like you were runnin’ ragged. Glad you got some peace and quiet. Did you finish that book, then? The one about the seaside town? Nearly! Just the last chapter. It was really charming, actually. All about secrets and second chances. Bit cheesy, admittedly, but a nice distraction. What about you? Did you manage to actually relax this weekend? I know the harvest reports were due. Relax? A bit, I suppose. Got most of the reports done, thankfully. Old Farmer Giles had a bit of a disaster with his combine harvester. Right mess, it was. Took me a good afternoon to sort him out. He's a stubborn one, that Giles. Thinks he knows everything. Giles! You’re always dealing with someone’s drama, aren't you? It's a wonder you ever have time to breathe. So, combine harvester troubles… anything more exciting happening in the world of agriculture this weekend? Now that you mention it… young Emily Pritchard, Giles’ granddaughter, she’s entered the village flower show. With dahlias, of all things. Apparently, she's been workin’ on ‘em for months. Says she's got a real chance this year. Emily? Little Emily who used to dress up as a bumblebee for Halloween? Good for her! That's rather sweet. And impressive, dahlias are tricky things, aren’t they? Aye, they are. Takes a steady hand and a keen eye. Reminds me of your Auntie Carol - she had a prize-winning rose garden back in the day. Remember those roses, love? The deep crimson ones? Of course! The 'Black Baccara' ones. Mum used to make rosewater syrup with them. That was the BEST. I wish I’d paid more attention to Auntie Carol’s gardening tips… I can barely keep a succulent alive. You've got to start somewhere, haven’t you? Though, I suppose your world involves spreadsheets and Gantt charts, not soil and seeds. Different kind of nurturing, I s'pose. Exactly. Although, sometimes I think Project management feels more stressful than pruning roses. Did you catch the football on Saturday? Briefly. Didn't make a dent in the report-writing, though. Always the reports… Villa lost, didn't they? Shockin’ performance.

Honestly, this is  lovely . Thank you for having me, Anon. It’s so nice to actually sit down and chat without a classroom full of teenagers vying for attention. How are you really doing, though? Still loving the primary school thing? It is lovely to see you, Chloe! And yes, I’m still at Oakwood Primary. It’s... chaotic, of course, but in a good way. The kids are brilliant. Year 3 this year, and they’re a particularly energetic bunch. Much more energetic than my little Leo, actually. He’s going through a very quiet phase at the moment. Just sits and observes. It’s a bit disconcerting, to be honest. Is everything alright with you? Still battling the teenage French existentialism? You have no idea. They’re convinced that learning grammar is a personal attack on their freedom. Apparently, the subjunctive mood is  clearly  a plot by the government. But yeah, mostly alright. I'm actually thinking about maybe doing a short course in Italian. Always wanted to, and I figured if I'm not using my French as much these days… plus, it’d be nice to learn something just for  me . Italian! That’s fantastic! It's such a beautiful language. I’ve always fancied learning Spanish, but the thought of all those rolled ‘r’s terrifies me. Seriously. I’d probably end up sounding like a seal. Did you find Duolingo helpful when you were learning French initially? I considered having a go at it for Leo, even though he's only ten months old, just to expose him to different sounds. Duolingo is… fine. Good for vocabulary, I suppose. But honestly, I think immersing yourself is key. I spent a summer in Montpellier - that's when I really started to pick it up. Trying to order a croissant without butchering the pronunciation was surprisingly effective motivation. Maybe a weekend trip to Italy wouldn't be a bad idea? Although, with my finances the way they are… holidays feel like a distant memory. How's the maternity leave gone? Has it been as… taxing as everyone says? It’s been a rollercoaster, to be honest. Beautiful highs, and utterly exhausting lows. The first few months were a blur of feeding schedules and sleep deprivation. Leo definitely keeps me on my toes! Financially, it’s been… interesting, let’s say. My husband, Mark, is amazing, and he’s been taking on extra shifts when he can.

Blimey, look at that, Arthur. A right proper nest. Bigger than last year’s, innit? Must've taken them robins ages to build it. Thought they’d be struggling with the wind we've been having. Aye, it is a whopper. Them robins are clever little things, though. Persistent. Reminds me of your sister, Elsie, always getting on with things, no matter what. Remember when she had that scare with her hip? Didn’t let it stop her, did she? Elsie was a marvel. Speaking of which, I’ve put the cake on. Hope you both like it. Bit more sugar than I usually use, a treat for a lovely afternoon. Though, I do feel a bit guilty, given... you know. Guilty? Don't be daft, Maureen. A bit of cake never hurt anyone. Especially when it's as lovely-looking as that. Though, with my glucose levels… Doctor’s been on at me again. Said I need to watch it. Doctors always say that, don’t they? “Watch it.” As if it’s that easy. This diabetes… it's a right nuisance. Limits you. Can’t just pop over for a slice of cake without worrying about it. Used to be we'd have cake every day! Well, we can have a small slice, both of you. And I've made sure to have some sugar-free biscuits too. Just in case. Look, the blue tits are back at the feeder! Are they? Let’s have a look! There they are, bouncing about like little feathered tennis balls. Always a favourite. You know, I was thinking, I might build a bigger feeder. Something more robust. The squirrels are becoming absolute bandits, emptying it in a matter of hours. Squirrels are crafty devils, alright. Remember old Mrs. Higgins down the lane? She tried everything to keep them off her bird feeders. Grease, netting... nothing worked. They just found a way. It’s quite entertaining, actually. Watching them try to outsmart each other. They're like little acrobats. It reminds me of the puppets I used to use when I was childminding. I had a cheeky little squirrel puppet, he was always trying to steal the other characters' nuts. Puppets, eh? You were always good with the kids, Maureen. Remember little Thomas? Always insisted on playing the crocodile. Scared the life out of the other children! Aye, Thomas was a terror. But a good lad, deep down.

Honestly, John, this place is charming. And the view! Absolutely stunning. I'm starving though. What are you thinking of having? I’m leaning towards the grilled octopus – it smells divine. Octopus, eh? Bit chewy, if you ask me. Though, I suppose when you're on holiday, you ought to try the local delicacies. I fancy the kleftiko. Lamb, slow-cooked in the oven with potatoes and herbs. Can’t go wrong with that. Are you going to have a starter? They have some lovely halloumi here. Halloumi does sound tempting. Right, okay, halloumi it is. And a large Mythos beer, please. Excuse me! Two halloumi starters and two Mythos beers, please. So, did you manage to speak to Eleanor about her foot? She sounded so worried when I last called. Yes, spoke to her yesterday. Turns out it’s a rather nasty infection. Doctor’s put her on some strong antibiotics. She’s quite down about it, can’t walk properly. Reminds me of Aunt Millie, you know, with her arthritis. Crippled her in the end. Dreadful business, illness. Makes you think, doesn't it? About, well, about everything. It does. Sometimes it’s just relentless, isn't it? Though, Eleanor’s a fighter. She’ll bounce back, I'm sure. It’s amazing how resilient people can be. Speaking of resilience, did you notice that woman over there, by the window? The one with the bright pink scarf? She’s been staring at us since we sat down. Now you mention it… rather intense gaze. Probably just admiring your hat, dear. Don’t take it personally. You do attract attention, you know. Remember that chap at Brenda’s wedding? Kept trying to engage you in conversation about… what was it? Rare orchids? Oh, goodness, yes! Terribly earnest. I think he thought I was a botanist. I told him I taught history. He looked utterly deflated! It's funny, isn’t it? How you meet people you’d never expect. Though, that reminds me, poor David's still single. He’s so shy, it breaks my heart. He needs to get out more. David? Yes, a good lad. Always fussing over his cats. Little monsters, those Persian chaps. I remember young Timmy – my granddaughter – used to try and steal their food. Absolute chaos. Reminds me of that dowsing incident a few years back… Oh, here we go. Don’t tell me you’re still convinced your friend Bernard found water with a bent stick.

Right, okay. That was a journey. The M1 was absolutely packed. Honestly, Mum, you wouldn’t believe the amount of lorries… Oh, you’re here! Lovely to see you, love. Did you have a good drive? I did tell you to leave earlier, didn't I? Eastern England traffic is a beast, especially on a Sunday. I know, I know, you did. But I was trying to finish that last report, you know how it is. And honestly, the rugby was on! Couldn’t miss it. Did you see the try in the first half? Ridiculous skill. Rugby? Pah! All running about. Give me a good herd of cattle any day. Now  that's  a sport. And your mum made a cracking roast, didn't she, love? Best one yet, I reckon. Don't you start, Arthur. Leave the girl alone. And it’s a lovely roast, isn't it? Yorkshire puddings were a bit flat, I’m afraid. I couldn’t quite get the oven right. They were lovely, Mum! Honestly, don’t worry about it. Better than anything I'd manage, anyway. Dad’s right, it was fantastic. So, how are you both doing? Anything exciting happening? Just the usual. Sheep are doing well, the barley’s coming along nicely. Bit worried about the rain we're getting forecast for next week though, that could do a number on the harvest. Arthur worries about everything. I'm fine, dear. Sorting through some old photos today - found a picture of you in your little football kit, you used to be all knees and elbows! Oh, God, please don’t show anyone that! I'd kill you both. Seriously, anything new with the house? Have you had a chance to look at those quotes for the kitchen renovation? I’ve got them here, actually. They’re a bit steep, aren't they? Especially Mr. Henderson's. He seems to think gold plating the taps is a necessity. Henderson’s always been a bit over the top. I have a mate who used him for his bathroom, cost him a fortune and the shower still dribbles. Right, okay. I can have a look through them later. I've been swamped at work, honestly. They want me to project manage the Carter account restructure. Which basically means I'm running around like a headless chicken making sure everyone else is doing their jobs.

Right, so, Chloe, you were sayin’ about this… this bloke online? Sounded a bit dodgy, didn’t it? Like summat outta Jeremy Kyle. Dodgy is an understatement, Hattie! It was a full-blown catfish, love. A proper, grade-A catfish. I was properly fooled for, like, a month! He was this gorgeous, muscled surfer dude, right? Had this amazing profile, loads of followers… All fake, obviously. A month? Seriously? That's a long time to be chatting without, you know, meeting up or a video call? I’d be suspicious pretty quick. That's what I thought afterwards! But he had all the excuses. "Oh, I’m travelling," "Oh, my camera broke," "Oh, I'm in a really remote area with bad reception." He was brilliant, honestly! Played the whole thing perfectly. He’d send me these long, heartfelt messages. Said he loved my sense of humour, thought I was 'a ray of sunshine'. Massive red flags now, aren't they? Aye, reet enough. Sounds awful, pet. Did you have any suspicions before you found out? Like, did summat just… not feel reet? A few things, yeah. He always avoided talking about his family. Said they were "complicated." Very convenient backstory. And he kept sending me pictures, like,  really  glossy, professional-looking pictures. Like something from a catalogue, rather than someone’s personal photos. I just brushed it off, though, because I wanted to believe it was real. You know how it is. Absolutely. It's easy to get invested. Were you ever tempted to do a reverse image search or anything? My mum's always telling me to do that. I did! Eventually. After about three weeks of being convinced I was falling for him. I ran a few pictures through Google and…bam! There he was. Modelling for some sportswear company. Names and faces didn’t match up with anything he’d told me. Felt proper silly, to be honest. I felt like I'd been right daft. That’s mortifying, lass. Were you ever threatened or anything? Like, did he get narky when you questioned him? Some of them do, don’t they? You see it on Jeremy Kyle all the time – folk gettin’ proper aggro when they get busted. No, thankfully not. When I confronted him with the evidence, he just… vanished. Blocked me everywhere. Pretty anticlimactic, actually. No dramatic argument, no tearful confessions, just  poof . Gone.

Right then, Nana, dig in. Made your favourite, carbonara. Hope it's alright. Bit of a faff with the oven today, kept tripping out. Honestly, these new appliances… you wouldn't believe the drama I had getting it working. Oh, darling, you shouldn’t apologise! Carbonara is  always  alright. Especially when made with love. And yes, modern technology. It's a curse, truly. I remember when a good lamp was the height of innovation. This computer… ...it's been giving me absolute grief. Can't even import my latest sketches. Ridiculous. Tell me about it. Uni’s a nightmare with the IT department. They promise updates, and it just makes everything worse. I had a lecture essay due last week, and the whole system crashed! Luckily, I saved it on my phone. Speaking of, I was thinking about that trip we talked about, to Paris. Fancy it in the spring? Paris! Oh,  Paris . Always a good idea. The light, the art... the pastries! . I remember when I first went, with your grandfather. 1968. The whole city felt...electric. We practically lived in museums and cafes. Did you know I used to speak quite fluent French? Before I dabbled in German, ironically. No way! Really? I’m rubbish at languages, to be honest. Classics at uni is interesting, all the Latin and Greek, but actually  speaking  it? Forget about it. I struggle to order a coffee in French. You were fluent? What happened? Life, darling, life happened. I became an artist. Words took a backseat to colours and textures. Though, when I was younger, and living in Italy for a while, I picked up a bit of Italian too. It’s all interconnected, isn’t it? Languages. Cultures. Like a giant, beautiful tapestry. You should really try. It opens up worlds. I might. It's just… daunting. Especially after struggling with GCSE German. Still have nightmares about the subjunctive tense. Remember when you were teaching me German when I was a little kid? I used to hide under the table because it was so confusing. Oh, you little rascal! You always were a tricky one. But you have a good mind, you know that. You're delving into the Classics, that's no easy feat. Reminds me of my own studies, you know. Classics were a foundation for me, a way of understanding the world. And it gave me a love for languages, even if I didn’t stick with them all.

Honestly, Dad, you were tailgating that lorry for ages! It was terrifying. I thought he was going to have to brake suddenly. Now, now, love. Just keeping the pace. Wouldn't want to hold you up on your way to Dorset. Besides, he was dawdling, wasn't he? Should've been doing a bit more than seventy, that one. Arthur, please. You’re stressing the girl. And honestly, it’s pouring. Visibility’s awful. Let’s just ease up a bit. Remember that time you nearly took out a postbox in Margate? That was different, Brenda! That was… well, it was a bit windy. And the postbox jumped out in front of me! These lorries just… they go so slow. They're allowed to, Dad! They're carrying heavy loads! It’s a legal requirement to go slower. And I’m doing a dissertation on Victorian urban planning, I don’t need my anxiety levels spiking because of dodgy driving. Want to jeopardise my future? Speaking of things needing attention, have you remembered to book the MOT for the Astra, love? It's due next month, isn’t it? Urgent. Blimey, how did you remember that? I’ve got so much on! Solicitors are bleeding me dry with these legal fees over Grandma’s estate. Honestly, it's ridiculous. I might have to start selling furniture to pay them. Solicitors! Don't get me started. A complete waste of money. My brother went through the same thing with his mum. Dragged on for ages. You know, I’m dreading Monday. Another double shift at the care home. Mrs. Peterson is convinced I’m secretly replacing her dentures with plastic ones. Honestly, the things people come up with. At least I get a day off on Wednesday, though. Thinking I might pop down to Mantiques. They've got some lovely old chests of drawers in at the moment. Mantiques? Properly kitsch, isn’t it? Remember when I tried to convince you to get Windows 8?
