Though spreadsheets can be their own form of madness, I suppose. Biscuits? Chocolate digestives, your favourite, Chloe. You're a star, Liv! Oh, and spreadsheets are evil, pure evil. Don’t get me started. But at least they don’t involve explaining to a frantic German delegate why the Yorkshire pudding isn’t “substantial enough.” Only you, Chloe! Tell me, how's the new guy doing at the centre? Ethan, wasn't it? Ethan… yeah. He's alright, I suppose. Bit quiet. Very eager to please, which is both a blessing and a curse. He keeps asking if I need "further assistance" every five minutes, it’s a bit much. I’m trying to be patient, he's obviously just starting out, but I'm used to running things myself, y'know? Always a challenge, managing new people. You’ve got to let them find their feet a bit, though. Otherwise, you risk stifling them. Remember when I started my admin job? I was terrified of making a mistake! Took ages to feel truly comfortable. True, true. I just… sometimes I feel like I’m doing  everything . It’s not all action man stuff, you know, a lot of the time it’s just a constant stream of little problems. It sounds relentless. So, change of subject – how’s things with Daniel? Still going strong? Oh, yeah. He's good. Actually, he's coming down next weekend. We're thinking of going for a walk in the fens, if the weather's decent. He's really keen on birdwatching. Birdwatching? That’s quite the shift from your usual Friday night pub trips! Don’t you start! He’s broadening my horizons, right?

Honestly, David, I’m fuming. Did you see the plans for the library? They’re actually going to demolish it and put up luxury flats. Luxury flats! In Plumstead! Who even  needs  luxury flats in Plumstead? Saw them. Dreadful, isn’t it? They’re calling it ‘redevelopment.’ The usual euphemism for ‘destroying something useful and putting something expensive in its place.’ I was reading about it in the local paper online. Apparently, the borough council claims it's financially unsustainable. Unsustainable?! It’s the only decent space we have left for community groups, the children's reading program, Mrs. Higgins’s knitting circle! And the free Wi-Fi is a lifeline for so many people. You know Liam uses it to do his online courses. Precisely. And let's not forget, it's got a remarkable collection of local history books. Stuff you can't find anywhere else. They just want to maximise profits. Anyway, you're working late again tomorrow, aren’t you? Another double shift? Yes, unfortunately. Tuesdays and Wednesdays are brutal. They’re trying to cover for someone who’s apparently gone off sick. I'm starting to feel like I’m going to collapse. I was thinking we need to really push this petition. I’ve already drafted something, but it needs some proper oomph. We need signatures, and we need to get the local press on our side. Already on it, love. I sent an email to the  Plumstead Chronicle  yesterday. Gave them all the details. And I’ve started a change.org petition. Got a few signatures already, mostly from my colleagues. It’s surprisingly difficult to get people engaged, though. They’re all so busy. Tell me about it. Speaking of busy, how’s that new filing system going down in the office? Still swimming in paperwork? Don’t remind me. Utter chaos. They’ve implemented this new software, supposedly to streamline things. It's just created more work! It's so unintuitive. I swear, the person who designed it should be forced to do customer service for a week. I'm trying to use mnemonics to remember all the different functions. Like, ‘F’ for file, ‘M’ for mail, ‘S’ for… something ridiculous. Oh, you and your mnemonics. It’s quite clever, actually. It’s how I remember all those obscure legal phrases when I'm transcribing. I use the  method of loci , you know?

Right then, Barry. That parking at Great Yarmouth, eh? Absolute nightmare it was last week. Paid a fortune just to leave the car five fields away. Five fields, I tell you! Used to be able to park right by the sea, proper close. Aye, it's gone right downhill, hasn't it, Arthur? They’re bleedin’ you dry. Remember when you could just pull up and drop your wife off for a paddle? Simple times. They’ve got those automated barriers now, confusing the life outta you. You two are always complaining about parking! It’s progress, isn't it, in a way? Keeps the cars away from the beach, a bit safer for the children. Though, I must admit, those prices  are  ridiculous. Did you see that article in the Eastern Daily Press about the council taxes? They're going up again! Council taxes! Don't even get me started, Margaret. Robbery, plain and simple. Where's all that money going? Potholes, that's where. Mattishall’s roads are a disgrace. And this new speed limit! Thirty miles an hour through the village? Ridiculous. Slows everyone down for no good reason. I didn’t vote for them, of course. Never do. Pointless, really, with the way things are. Votin’s a waste of time, Arthur. Doesn’t change a thing. They all say what you want to hear on the doorstep, then do what they want once they're in. It’s the same every time. Remember old Mr. Higgins? At the village hall? Always going on about voting. Died last year, didn’t he? Didn’t change a blinkin’ thing. Oh, you two! Always so cynical. Well, I still believe in trying. Every little bit helps. Speaking of the village hall, did you hear about Mrs. Peabody's prize-winning dahlias? They’re magnificent this year, apparently. Practically glowing. Dahlias? I'm more concerned about pigeons, I am. The flock that's taken up residence on my shed roof. Constant cooing and mess. Makes you wonder why they bother. They’re a nuisance, those pigeons. Always scavenging for scraps. You should try putting up some shiny things to scare ‘em off. My Uncle George used to do it with foil. Drove ‘em right away. So, Barry, how’s your back doing? You were mentioning the other day you had a bit of a twinge. Still a bit stiff, Margaret.

“Right then, Mum, settle in. More tea? And Dad, would you like a biscuit? I managed to get some proper fudge from that little shop in the village – you know, the one we were talking about last time." "That's very thoughtful, dear. Thank you. Fudge is always welcome. Though I do hope it's not overly sweet. Are you managing to keep the log burner going alright? It was freezing up here last time we visited.” “Freezing? Now, Mother, don’t exaggerate. It was a bit brisk, perhaps. But the logs are lovely, aren't they, ANON? Such a satisfying crackle. Better than those electric fires, any day.” “Everything alright here? Just sorting through the post, mostly bills. Speaking of which, we really need to have a proper chat about the budget this weekend. That Tokyo trip certainly put a dent in things.” "Tell me about it. Between the flights and the ridiculously overpriced souvenirs, it was… an experience. But worth it? Debatable. I'm still finding tiny origami cranes in my handbag. Honestly, I'm starting to feel like I have an infestation!” "Tokyo, eh? Fancy seeing that. I’ve always wanted to go to Japan. Though the thought of the long flight… well, I wouldn't manage it now. Did you at least eat some decent sushi?" "The sushi was incredible, Mum. Absolutely incredible. Though I’m not entirely sure what was in it all. One of them looked suspiciously like a tiny, pickled octopus." “Octopus? Good heavens. I'm a simple man, dear. Give me a good roast beef and Yorkshire pudding any day. Better than all that foreign fancy stuff.” “Speaking of decent food, have you tried that new restaurant, 'The Hearth'? It opened down the High Street. Apparently, they do a rather good mashed potato. Creamy, buttery, the whole shebang.” “I haven't! I’ve been meaning to, but with everything else… Still, I could do with a good mashed potato. It's the one thing I can never quite nail at home. It’s always either gluey or watery." “Mashed potato is a skill, dear. You need to use the right sort of potato, and not overwork it. And plenty of butter, of course. You know, back in my day, we used to have a dedicated potato masher. It was a family heirloom.” “Indeed. We had one like that. My mother swore by it.

Right then. This bleedin’ council tax, eh, Arthur? It’s a right cheek, isn't it? Feels like they're takin’ more and more every year. I were lookin' at the details online, proper headache it gave me, all them percentages and bands. Makes you wonder where it's all goin', doesn't it? Aye, Harold. It is a worry, it is. Remember when we were young, you could practically buy a pig for what we pay in council tax now. Piffle, I call it. Absolute piffle. And don’t even get me started on the bin charges! They're tryin’ to bleed us dry, I tell you. Honestly, gentlemen. You two could complain about a sunny day. It’s a necessary thing, paying taxes. Keeps the roads open, the schools running… though I do agree, it feels excessive sometimes. Back in Harrow, we had a lovely little library. Used to take the children there regularly. Now, everything’s online. Roads? They haven’t fixed a pothole in this village in… well, since I moved in five years ago! And online? Bah! I tried to sort out my pension online the other day - ended up more confused than when I started. Grew up with slide rules and set squares, I did, not these blinking computers. Gave me a right headache. Slide rules! That's a trip down memory lane, Harold. You remember Mr. Finch at the school, didn't you? All stern looks and complicated sums. Though I must say, that Sat Nav Anne got… that's a blessing. Remember gettin' lost tryin’ to find Mrs. Pringle's nephew's wedding in Ipswich? Nearly ended up in France! Oh, Sat Navs! I put my faith in one once and it took me down a single-track lane for miles. Ended up having to reverse half a mile to get back out! Nearly flattened a sheep. Terribly distressing. Though, I must admit, I do prefer a proper map. You can see where you are in relation to everything. Aye, maps are better. More…reliable. Though, I tell you what's really gettin' on my nerves...this new housing development they’re building on the edge of the village. They're callin’ it ‘Meadow View’. Meadow View! It's all brick and concrete, not a meadow in sight. Ruining the countryside, that’s what it is. They're buildin’ 'em everywhere, aren't they?

Right then, so, Liam, you were saying about your laptop? The one that went belly-up at school? Yeah, Mr. Davies said it just…stopped. Wouldn’t turn on at all. He reckons it's probably something serious. It’s got all my coursework on it! My history essay's due next week. Oh, that’s awful, love. That's a really stressful situation for a young lad. Has the school got any IT support that could take a look? Not really, Mum. They’ve got one teacher who’s a bit techy, but he's already got loads of computers to look at. He just told me to bring it home. Aye, well, bring it over here then. I’ll have a poke around with it tonight. Might be something simple, just a loose connection or a dodgy power supply. These things happen. I had a similar glitch with my work laptop last year, turned out to be a fried capacitor. Easy fix, really. That’s lovely, isn't he? Little Finn, demanding his dinner already. You’re a hungry one tonight, aren’t you? It's amazing how you can fix these things, isn't it, Conor? I could barely switch a computer on correctly when I was your age, Liam. It’s just logic, really. Follow the wires, find the fault. And, Liam, before I start hacking away at it - do you know if it's still under warranty? Important to check that before I go poking around inside. Don't want to void anything. I  think  so? Mum, did we keep the paperwork? It was one of those fancy gaming laptops, you know, with the flashing lights and everything. Gaming laptops... Let me see... I  might  have a box of old receipts and paperwork in the attic. It’s a right mess up there, mind you. Haven't been up there in ages. Don’t worry about it, love. It's grand. If it's not under warranty, no harm done. I’ll just be careful. Now, about the rugby later… Are you still up for coming down to the clubhouse with Finn and me to watch the match? Yeah, definitely. Is Uncle Seamus coming too? He promised he'd bring some of that homemade fudge. Oh, Seamus! He's a gem. He'll bring enough fudge to feed the whole town, I reckon. Rest assured, it’ll be in abundance.

Right then, pizza’s nearly ready. Who wants pepperoni? Or shall we stick with veggie for Maisie and Finn? Pepperoni! Pepperoni! Please, Mummy! Me too! More pepperoni than Finn! Oh, you two. Alright, alright. A little extra for you, Finn. Maisie, are you sure you don’t want just  one  little pepperoni? Nope! Veggies are better! I like the peppers. They’re… are they spicy, Mummy? A tiny bit, sweetie. Just enough to give them a little kick. So, while this bakes, let's talk about something a bit different. We were talking about Nessie yesterday, weren't we? The Loch Ness Monster! Did he see me, Mummy? I highly doubt it, love! He’s a very shy monster, I hear. But, Maisie, do you think Nessie uses… well,  phones  to talk to his friends underwater? Monsters don’t have phones! Do they not? Think about it. It's a very big loch! Maybe he has a special, waterproof phone. A… a Nessie-phone! “Hello? Is that you, Angus the Giant Squid?” Angus! That’s silly! Silly is good! See? Communication is important, even for monsters. It's like when I’m trying to explain to you both why you can't do handstands on the kitchen table. But it’s fun! Look! Whoa there, speedy! See? That's not a good way to communicate. You’re telling the table, "I'm going to fall!" instead of asking me politely if you can practice somewhere safer. Can we make a fairy garden after pizza? With sparkly rocks? Absolutely! We talked about that. We'll use those shiny pebbles we found last week. Remember, we need to be very quiet when we build it, so we don’t scare away the fairies. We need to communicate  with  them, not shout at them. Will there be a tiny pond for the fairies to swim? We could try making one with a little dish and some blue pebbles. That’s a good idea, Maisie. Okay, let's see... what else does a fairy garden need? We need to plan this! Let’s see... two fairy gardens need five sparkly rocks each. How many sparkly rocks do we need in total? Five… five… ten! Ten sparkly rocks! Brilliant, Finn! You're a maths whiz. That’s excellent communication – you understood the question and gave me the right answer. Although, we'll probably need to find more than ten!

"Dead reight this is, isn't it? Proper lush. I keep lookin' at that water, just want to jump straight in! It’s hotter than a badger’s bottom today, though. Meltin'." "Aye, it is, love. Lovely and warm. Much better than that drizzle we had back home last week. I were nearly gettin’ the winter blues in August! And this wine… honestly, this Teran is champion stuff. Did you try the Fuzi with truffles, Elara? Absolutely divine.” "It's alright, Mum. The Wi-Fi's a bit dodgy, though. Can’t even load a TikTok properly. Did you see that new filter everyone's using? It makes you look like a cartoon." “Remarkable location, truly. Istria just keeps getting better and better. The history is fascinating, you know. Roman ruins, Venetian influence… I stayed in Rovinj a few years ago, absolutely charming. Reminded me a bit of Dubrovnik, albeit on a smaller scale.” “Rovinj? Is that where all the boats are? I saw some pictures online, looked proper picturesque. Dad, you should’ve booked us somewhere like that. This villa's nice, don't get me wrong, but no pool, ya know? And the swimming’s a bit nippy down at the beach.” “We talked about Rovinj, Elara. It was booked solid. Besides, I wanted somewhere quieter, closer to Pula. And the pool’s not  that  nippy, you just need to toughen up a bit! Remember when you were little and used to shriek about paddling in the bath?” “Speaking of stuff that's scary, did you see that documentary about Ebola? Proper creepy. They were talking about how fast it spreads. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Schools are teachin’ us about food technology now, too. We had to design our own 'sustainable burger' – it was mostly lentils and beetroot, tasted like sadness, honestly.” “Ebola… yes, a grim reminder of the fragility of things. Food technology is vital, though. We need to find sustainable solutions, especially with the growing population. It's an interesting problem, almost on the level of designing a truly intuitive operating system… like Steve Jobs tried to do.” "Steve Jobs? He was alright, wasn't he? Made phones people couldn't live without. You ever had bother with immigration officers at airports? My mate, Liam, got pulled aside in Barcelona last year. Apparently, they thought he was tryin’ to smuggle something. All over some herbal tea!"

Right then. Another lovely lunch, Brenda. Though I could do with a bit more gravy, couldn't I? Feels a bit dry today. There's more in the jug, Arthur. You always say that, though. Always needing more gravy. Speaking of things needing attention, did you hear from those debt collectors again? They’re relentless, aren't they? Aye, relentless they are. Gave me a right telling down on the phone. Said they’d be sending someone round. Frightful cheek, the lot of 'em. Just readin’ off a script, they are. Don’t seem to care a jot about yer situation. Makes a man feel right small. Honestly, it's appalling. These debt collection agencies… they operate with such a lack of empathy. I was reading a fascinating article in  The Economist  last week – rather complex, naturally – about the regulatory loopholes that allow them to behave in this way. Of course, you shouldn’t be responding to their calls, Arthur. Document everything, but don't engage. Reginald always has the  Economist  lying around. You’d think it’d be full of financial advice, wouldn't you? Still, easier said than done, Arthur. Ignoring them doesn't make the debt go away. Remember when we were dealing with that PPI claim, Arthur? Took ages to sort that out. PPI! Don't even remind me. Nearly drove me round the bend. All those forms, the waiting… and for what? A pittance in the end. Though I must say, that telly show last night was a decent distraction. That new detective series – “The Shadowed Coast.” Quite gripping, that was. Oh, I loved that! The scenery was lovely. Reminds me of that holiday we had in Cornwall, doesn't it? We could go back, could we not? Though, driving… that’s another thing altogether, isn’t it? Arthur, are you still feeling up to it? Well… I took Elsie to the shops yesterday. Bit wobbly, I’ll admit. The traffic was a bit much. Might be best to stick to shorter trips for a bit, I reckon. Less stressful for everyone. Perhaps public transport then? Or even better, someone else could drive? Sarah, have you considered offering to take them out? Absolutely. I'm happy to drive. And speaking of getting out and about, has anyone started thinking about the village fete planning yet? It’s only a few weeks away now. Do you think we should try and convince Mrs. Higgins to sing again?

Right, that’s the last lot through for today. Honestly, the frustration levels were palpable in that last case. Seems everyone's feeling the pinch, doesn’t it? Aye, you're tellin' me. You see it in their faces, dear, the worry. I’ve been ushering here for fifteen years now, and I've never seen so many people struggling. The bailiffs are busier than ever, bless ‘em. It’s heartbreaking, really. It absolutely is. I was explaining some English grammar to a student this morning, and he mentioned his mum’s working two minimum wage jobs just to keep a roof over their heads. Education feels almost… irrelevant sometimes, when the basic necessities are so precarious. It is a shame, isn't it? A good education should be the foundation. My wee brother, Hamish, he’s a carpenter up in Aberdeen. Proper trade, that. Wish I'd learned something like that instead of just… well, history and geography at school. Not that I didn't enjoy it, mind you, but it doesn’t put food on the table these days. How's your own family doing? Still in Hertfordshire? Yes, still in Hitchin. My parents are getting on, you know? Mum’s particularly worried about the energy bills. Honestly, it's a constant conversation at Sunday dinners – how to shave another pound off somewhere. It’s distressing for them, and they've always been so financially stable. It just feels like things are…shifting. Aye, shifting big time. I read in the paper the other day about the flooding up north. Terrible stuff. The climate’s gone mad, hasn’t it? The summers are hotter, the winters are wetter. Makes you wonder about the future, especially for the grandchildren. You got any little ones? Not yet. We're talking about it, but with everything going on, it doesn't feel like the right time. Part of me feels guilty even  thinking  about having children when the world seems so unstable. It’s a selfish feeling, I know. Don’t you feel guilty, dear. It’s a sensible feeling. Times are hard enough without adding the responsibility of a bairn. Though I do love seeing the wee ones. Remember young Thomas Miller, always used to wave at me from the gallery when his father was on trial? Lovely boy, he was. His father kept his nose clean after that, I'm glad to say.

Right then, little ones. We were talking about happiness, weren't we? What makes you both feel properly, ridiculously happy? Puppies! And ice cream! And… and when Mummy reads me stories! Dinosaurs are happy when they eat leaves. Big, juicy leaves! Roar! That’s brilliant, darling. Puppies, ice cream, stories, and leaves for dinosaurs! You’ve really nailed it. It's lovely to hear. But sometimes, happiness isn’t about things like puppies or ice cream, is it? Sometimes, it’s a feeling inside. Can you understand that? A feeling? Like when I cuddle you, Mummy? Exactly! Like that warm, fuzzy feeling. That's a kind of happiness. Like when I build a really,  really  tall tower with my blocks and it doesn’t fall down? Absolutely! That sense of accomplishment, that little burst of pride... that’s happiness too. Want to play a game? Let's think of rhyming words for happy. Happy… shappy? Is shappy a word? No, sweetheart, ‘shappy’ isn't a word. Let's try again. Happy… snappy! Like a snappy dog! Happy… flappy! Like a bird's wings! Flap, flap, flap! Brilliant! See? You’re both little rhyming geniuses. Now, let’s talk about something else. Imagine you had  loads  of money. Like, enough to buy anything you wanted. What would you do? I'd buy a pony! A sparkly pink pony with a rainbow mane! And a castle made of gingerbread! I’d buy… a  real  dinosaur! A big one! A T-Rex! And a giant pile of leaves for him to eat! Wow! A pink pony, a gingerbread castle, and a real T-Rex! That's quite the shopping list. Do you think having all that money would make you happy? Yes! Because I’d have my pony! Yes! Because the T-Rex would have lots to eat! And I'd ride him! But… and this is a big but, darlings… imagine you didn’t have all that money, but you had each other, and you had a warm home, and we could go for walks in the park, and I could read you stories. Would that still be happy? Yes. Because I love cuddles with you, Mummy. And walks in the park are fun. And dinosaurs like cuddles too. Roar! A happy roar! That’s right. You know what? Real happiness isn’t about sparkly ponies or even giant dinosaurs. It's about feeling loved, feeling safe, and having people to share your adventures with.

Honestly, Mrs. Davies’ careers talk was a bit…meh. Everyone just saying ‘follow your passion’ - like that’s actually helpful. My passion is gaming, does that mean I should become a professional gamer? The lifespan of those is like, three years, max. Tell me about it. She spent fifteen minutes talking about coding bootcamps. Like  everyone  wants to be a software developer. It's not exactly revolutionary, is it? Though, I guess it’s secure. My dad was saying something about AI being the real money-maker now. AI is everywhere, obviously. But the patents… that's what I find genuinely fascinating. Did you know Tesla has, like, hundreds of patents? Musk just gave them all away. Imagine the implications of that! It’s like… democratizing innovation. Yeah, but you need serious cash to even  do  innovation. Like, building something? Testing it? It’s not just scribbling on a notepad. My uncle's got some weird gadget he's been working on for years – a self-watering plant pot with sensors. He’s sunk a fortune into it. Still hasn’t sold a single one. That's the risk, isn’t it? But if he  did  patent it and get it right… boom! Think about China. They’re patenting everything. All those new technologies… They’re snapping them up faster than anyone. Exactly! My mum’s been reading up on China’s technological advancements. Apparently, their AI is catching up fast. They've got insane amounts of data to work with. It’s kind of scary, honestly. Like, are we all just going to be working for Chinese companies in ten years? Don’t say that! But it's a legitimate concern. We need to be ahead of the curve. Maybe that’s where investment comes in. Like, putting money into companies that are developing genuinely novel tech. My gran keeps going on about investing in property. Apparently, it's "safe" and "reliable." But that feels…stuck in the last century. I'd rather try and invest in something new, you know? Something that has potential. Right? Property is just…bricks and mortar. It’s not exactly groundbreaking. Although, sustainable housing could be a big thing. Eco-friendly materials, smart home tech integrated… That could be a growth area. See,  that  I could get behind. Something that actually changes the world, not just helps someone make a quick buck. You know what I was reading about?

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Proper sunshine, decent food… and a break from proofreading legal documents! My eyes were starting to cross. Tell me about it. I think I’ve aged five years just watching you wrestle with those contracts. You were practically vibrating with stress on the phone last week. Glad you managed to drag yourself away. Bansko is lovely, isn’t it? Much nicer than that place in France we tried a few years ago – remember how awful the food was there? Don’t remind me! Those snails were a culinary crime against humanity. This is far superior. And the skiing! I didn’t expect Bulgaria to be so good. Nkosi cleared a path brilliantly yesterday. Nkosi was amazing! He's clearly a natural. I felt like I was clinging on for dear life at times, though. My knees are  singing  today. Think I might just stick to the bunny slopes for now. You should! No point in pushing it. Did you hear from Mum this morning? She was asking about your skiing lessons. Just a quick text. She’s worried, of course. She always worries. Said she hopes I’m not going to break a hip. She’s practically planning my recovery time already. Honestly, she’s got a whole spreadsheet dedicated to potential injuries. Typical Mum. She likely has a spreadsheet for  our  potential injuries too. Has she spoken to David at all? I know they were supposed to be finalising those travel dates for the summer. Not yet. She said he’s been swamped at work. Apparently, that Henderson account is causing absolute chaos. She’s been hinting considerably that she’s getting a bit lonely though. Maybe we should suggest they book something soon? Their anniversary is coming up, isn’t it? Oh, yes, early June. Definitely. I'll give her a nudge. Perhaps a week in Cornwall? They both love walking the coastal paths. Or maybe… Remember how they used to talk about going to Italy? Florence, maybe? Florence! That's a brilliant idea. They’d absolutely adore it. Imagine them, wandering around, eating pasta… Mum would be in heaven. We need to float that suggestion. Actually, while I’m thinking about it, I should text Sarah. I haven’t heard from her in ages. She mentioned wanting to come out and visit us on this trip. Oh, brilliant! Would she enjoy it?

Honestly, Bernard, this is the third one this week. They’re snapping like dry spaghetti. What are we going to do? We can’t charge people a reasonable price if the string keeps failing us. Right, right. Frustrating, isn't it? We’ve talked about thicker string, haven't we? But that’s a bit expensive, and it adds weight. Remember Mrs. Peterson complaining about the feel of the last racket we re-strung? Said it felt like hitting a brick. Yes, but the snapping is the core issue. Thicker might help marginally, but the point of failure is still… here. I was thinking… cable ties. Cable ties? Penelope, you can’t be serious. Are we going to hand out badminton rackets held together with plastic ties? They’ll look ridiculous! And won’t they interfere with the swing? Hear me out! Not  just  cable ties. We’d use them as reinforcement. After we re-string, strategically placed along the vulnerable points, hidden as much as possible. Small ones, black ones, almost invisible. It’d add strength, wouldn’t it? We'd need to experiment with the length and thickness, naturally. And the positioning is vital - particularly around the T-bar, that's where they mostly seem to snap. Hmmm. Interesting. It would certainly be... novel. What about the cost? Cable ties are cheap enough, I suppose. But the time spent incorporating them… and guaranteeing the racket’s performance… That’s a different matter. Well, a packet of 100 decent ones is under five pounds. We’d only need a few per racket. Much cheaper than replacing the string repeatedly. And as for performance… we need to test it thoroughly. But I reckon it could work. Think of the marketing! "Badminton Rackets - Reinforced for Maximum Durability!" We could even offer different 'levels' of reinforcement. "Standard" with two ties, "Pro" with four… You’re already imagining the Dragons' Den pitch, aren't you? "And our secret ingredient, Penelope, is humble, yet mighty, cable ties!” Don’t mock! It’s a perfectly viable solution! Though, I suppose “fleet” isn't quite the right word for a bunch of cable ties. More like a… collection? A squadron? No, that's silly. Okay, okay, let's consider it. We need to assess the weight impact. We wouldn’t want to add considerably. And what about application in different schools? Primary versus secondary... the power used in a school setting will be considerably varied.

Cor, this is a lovely brew, Annie. Proper builder's tea, just how I like it. Been ages since I've had a sit down like this, proper relaxed. You wouldn’t believe the damp getting into me bones these days. It's good to see you comfortable, Arthur. I’ve got digestives today, your favourite. And it’s lovely to have you all here. It’s been too long. This Norfolk air does wonders, doesn’t it? Though I do wish we’d seen a bit more sunshine. It’s lovely here, Mum. Really lovely. Dad, you’ve got such a fascinating collection of prints. This one, the Turner seascape… it's incredible. The way he captures the light… Absolutely, Eleanor. Turner was a genius. Untamed. He just threw the rule book out the window. You look at some of the Romantics, and they’re trying to be all perfect and symmetrical. Turner just... feels. Reminds me a bit of Hockney, actually. That bold use of colour. Hockney, eh? Never 'eard of ‘im. Always been more of a Constable man meself. ‘E painted Norfolk, didn't he? Used to wander round and just paint what ‘e saw. Honest work that. Not all this… faffing about with colours and shapes, like some of these modern things. Arthur, don't be like that. Not everything modern is faffing. Eleanor and David will tell you. They know about art, you know. Well, Mum’s right, Dad. Modern art isn't all bad. Take someone like Yayoi Kusama – her installations are just mesmerising. The repetition, the colour… It explores themes of infinity and self-obliteration. It's deeply psychological. And consider the work of Cornelia Parker. She takes everyday objects – like garden sheds or even bomb fragments – and transforms them into these incredible, monumental sculptures. It's all about recontextualizing the familiar, making you see things in a new light. Bomb fragments, you say? Now see ‘ere, that’s just morbid, innit? Building things out of destruction. Give me a nice bit of countryside any day. Constable's 'Hay Wain', that's somethin’ to look at. Proper peaceful. There’s beauty in destruction too, Arthur. It’s a different kind of beauty, perhaps, but it can be just as moving. Remember that exhibition we saw in London, about the Blitz? All those photographs... Exactly, Annie. And considering the current state of the world, looking at art that engages with conflict and trauma can be really illuminating.

Honestly, Chloe, I could scream. This project is actively trying to sabotage itself. Brenda keeps changing the brief, and Mark’s just…not getting it. At all. Brenda, eh? Sounds like a classic. Same as that awful Karen from my ward. Keeps insisting she  doesn’t  need medication, then has a total meltdown when she’s feeling anxious. It’s exhausting. You need more wine. Definitely. Though I’m supposed to be prepping for a presentation on Monday. Which, naturally, I'm spectacularly failing to do. I've spent the last hour scrolling through TikTok looking at videos of cats falling off furniture. Productivity is  not  my strong suit tonight. Don't beat yourself up. Monday's a long way off. And cat videos are vital for the preservation of sanity. Though, speaking of procrastination, I was supposed to be writing up that patient report, but…Instagram happened. You and me both. I swear, social media is a black hole for time. Do you ever think about how ridiculously complex the English language is? "Their," "there," and "they're" are actively trying to trip me up. I used "their" in an email today, and I  knew  it was wrong as soon as I hit send. Oh god, the grammar gremlins! They’re everywhere. It's ridiculous, isn't it? Like, why does "read" have two completely different pronunciations and past tenses? It's designed to confuse us, I'm convinced. It's like the language itself is laughing at us. Exactly! And don’t even get me started on the subjunctive mood. I’m fairly certain nobody actually  uses  it outside of stuffy historical novels. “If I were to go…” Ugh. So pretentious. Speaking of pretentious and actively annoying…did you see Bethany's Instagram post about her "wellness retreat"? Positively dripping with organic green juice and forced smiles. Oh, Bethany. Don't even. She’s always trying so hard. It's a cry for attention disguised as self-care. Remember last year when she tried to convince everyone she was a certified yoga instructor after a weekend course? Oh my god, yes! And the leggings! She bought, like, five pairs of those ridiculously expensive ones. It’s just… exhausting to watch. It's like, just be yourself, Bethany! A slightly-out-of-touch, well-meaning person is perfectly acceptable. Precisely! Although, I’m starting to feel a lot like that myself with this project.

Honestly, another day, another avalanche of emails. Mr. Davies really needs to learn to delegate. It's exhausting, you know? And he wonders why I'm reaching for that Pinot Grigio a little earlier than usual. Delegate? He’s trying to control every comma, aren’t he? Par for the course with Davies. At least you’re getting a decent vintage to soothe your frayed nerves. Don’t go overboard though, love. We've got that dinner with the Millers on Saturday. I’m not planning on becoming a lush, darling. Just a small glass. Although, the thought of spending an evening listening to Fiona Miller lecturing me on organic gardening… well, it does tempt me toward a bottle. Speaking of which, did you manage to lay off the fags today? Nearly. Had a stressful call with the Henderson account. Nearly cracked. Pathetic, I know. This quitting lark is harder than quantum physics. It is, isn’t it? It's willpower, pure and simple. You’ve got this. Remember what the doctor said. And honestly, you already look healthier than you did last year. Less grey around the edges, practically glowing...though maybe that's the Pinot already talking. Flattery will get you everywhere. It’s just… these cravings, they hit like a freight train. It makes you think, doesn’t it? About common sense versus intelligence. I mean, I know it's dreadful for me. Intelligent man knows it’s dreadful. But common sense sometimes just…flies out the window. Absolutely. There's a difference. Intelligence is knowing something, common sense is  doing  what you know is right. Like, I know eating that entire chocolate cake yesterday was a terrible idea, but my brain told me otherwise. Exactly! It's why I sometimes feel like I’m surrounded by clever people doing daft things. Though, I suppose I’m contributing to the illogical pool myself at the moment. Don’t be silly. It's a human thing. Tell you what, I was reading something interesting today. It was a piece about German workplace culture. Apparently, Friday afternoons are practically sacrosanct. No work, just socialising, beer, and snacks. Imagine that! Here, Davies is emailing his workers at 10 pm. Sounds idyllic. Proper 'gezelligheid' as the Dutch would say. It's interesting, isn't it? How different cultures approach things. My mate, Liam, was on a business trip in Japan last year.

Right, well, that was quite the day, wasn’t it? Absolute chaos, but a good kind of chaos. The kids were buzzing all evening. The piggies! The piggies were SO muddy! And they squeaked! Squeak, squeak, squeak! Tractor! I sat on the tractor! It was big! You both did! Honestly, little ones, you were brilliant. Although, Leo, must you try to climb  everything ? Nearly gave me a heart attack when you started scaling that hay bale. It was fun! And I got to the top! I saw a fluffy sheep! And it had a baby sheep! A wobbly lamb! You did! They were adorable, weren’t they? Farmer Giles said they'd just been born a few weeks ago. Did you remember to say thank you to Farmer Giles, darlings? Yes! I said thank you for the carrots! I didn’t get any carrots. I ate a strawberry! Yes, you did! A rather large strawberry, I believe. Right, let’s talk about school tomorrow. Mrs. Davies called me after school today, about both of you, actually. Oh. What did she say? Did I do something bad? No, sweetheart, you didn’t do anything  terrible . It’s just... both of you were a little bit distracted during maths. You were chatting a bit too much, weren't you? We were talking about the piggies! And the tractor! I understand you're still excited about the farm, but we need to remember that school is for learning, okay? Mrs. Davies said it disrupted a few other children, so we need to try and focus when she’s teaching. I’ll try, Mummy. Okay. But can we watch a DVD tonight? A tractor one? A tractor DVD? Honestly, you two. We can watch something, yes. But how about we pick something a little... less tractors? Maybe something with animals that  aren't  on a farm? Can we watch 'Paddington'? No! ‘Toy Story’! Please, Mummy, ‘Toy Story’! Oh, here we go. Another debate. Alright, alright. How about we let Mummy decide tonight? And tomorrow, we’ll have a proper chat about school. And no climbing on the furniture before bedtime! Promise? Promise, Mummy? I promise. Now, who wants some apple slices? I made a crumble earlier, but it’s nearly all gone. Me! Me! Apple slices, please! Me too! With custard! Custard it is. Honestly, you two. You exhaust me. But I wouldn't change it for the world.

Right, then. Earl Grey it is. Standard, no fancy fruit infusions for me today, eh, Liam? Needed a good, strong cuppa after wrestling with those survey results. Honestly, half the responses were gibberish. People just putting anything they can think of! Gibberish, eh? Sounds about right for research. My own attempts at drawing conclusions from literature reviews are feeling pretty similar sometimes. At least your results are  active  gibberish. Mine just sits there on the page, mocking me. Fancy a biscuit with that? I got those ginger ones you like. Aye, ginger ones would be champion! You're a star. So, did you see that documentary last night? About the Olympic athletes? The dedication was absolutely incredible. Made me feel a bit rubbish about spending all evening scrolling through TikTok, to be honest. I did! The swimmer, that young lad Matthew, the one who nearly didn’t make it through trials... wow. Proper inspiring. Though, I have to say, the commentator kept saying "pushing through the pain barrier." It’s a cliché, innit? “Pain barrier.” As if pain is some kind of uniform obstacle everyone hits. Aye, it is a bit cheesy. But you can't deny there's a lot of grit involved, can you? Speaking of grit, I saw Florence Pugh's interview with Vogue. She’s smashing it, isn’t she? Proper Northern lass, like me, taking on Hollywood. Giving it right back to 'em. Florence Pugh is fantastic. The way she talked about her grandmother teaching her to knit – a really lovely story. That reminds me, have you managed to start that scarf yet? The one for your mam? Easter’s not  that  far away. Don't remind me! It's still a sad pile of wool in a corner. I got distracted by…well, everything, really. Between the research, trying to keep up with the Olympics, and just generally existing, knitting has fallen by the wayside. It’s a relaxing hobby, in principle. But I find myself overthinking every stitch. Overthinking? That's very you. Remember when you tried to knit a hat and argued for an hour about the optimal tension? Oh, don't! That was a disaster. I ended up with a hat that looked like a wonky mushroom. It’s a wonder my mam even  accepted  it. She's a good soul, my mam. She’d say, "It’s lovely, pet. You made it yourself."

Right then, Arthur. That was a lovely bit of sunshine, weren’t it? Shame about the crowds, mind. Felt like bein’ trampled underfoot at times. Could’ve nipped to the National Gallery for a proper look, but that queue! Goodness me. Aye, it was alright. A bit… much, though. All those people jostling. Not really my cup of tea, that. The Natural History Museum was decent, though. All those bones. Gave me a proper think, it did. Made me realise just how short our time is, really. Always the philosopher, aren't you, love? Bones and the brevity of existence! You were lookin' at those dinosaurs proper intently, weren't you? Remember you saying somethin' about the size of their teeth? Right you are. Massive, weren't they? Bigger than my head, easy. Makes you wonder how they ever moved. And that IMAX, though. I’m still not entirely convinced about the 3D, you know. Head hurt a bit, to be honest. Felt a bit gimmicky, really. All that shaking and flashing. I know what you mean. Used to love the Imax when I was a kid. Felt grand. Now… it's just a bit much, innit? Gives me a headache too. All them special effects. Back in the day, a good story was enough. And the price! Robbery, it is. Absolutely. And getting there! That blasted tube…utter chaos. Couldn’t hardly move. Why can’t they run more trains on a Sunday? It’s always like this. It’s not as if they don't know to expect the crowds. Tell me about it! I swear, the Southern Rail are takin’ the mick. You’d think they'd sort somethin' out. I spent half the journey squeezed between a woman with a giant shopping bag and some teenager glued to his phone. I felt like I was gonna spontaneously combust! And the smell! Don't even get me started on the smell. Ah, yes. The lovely aroma of… well, let's just say it wasn’t roses. Honestly, it's a disgrace. They need to invest in some proper ventilation, don't they? And train the staff to actually  help  people. Nobody seemed to know where anything was. I asked a bloke where the Victoria line went, and he just looked at me blankly! Just like me! I was tryin' to find the platform for the Northern Line and another fella just pointed vaguely towards a tunnel and said, "Somewhere down there, love."

Right then, Christmas. It's looming, isn’t it? Feels earlier every year. So, tentative plans? I was thinking, we could do the traditional roast turkey thing, but maybe with a bit more… flair this time? I saw a recipe for a cranberry and port reduction that looked rather impressive. Flair, eh? You're turning into your mother, lad. Though I like the sound of that cranberry and port business. My Nan used to make a mean bread sauce. Could add that in, traditional AND fancy. Though, between you and me, I’m more concerned about getting enough sprouts. The little buggers are like gold dust here. Sprouts are non-negotiable, absolutely. I’ve already started scouting out the local markets. They’re… variable, to say the least. I did manage to find some decent parsnips, though. What about timing? Are we sticking with Boxing Day lunch as usual? It feels ages away. Boxing Day suits me fine. Gives me a bit of breathing space after the 25th itself, you know? All that family chaos. Speaking of which, have you heard anything from Sarah and Mark? They were saying they might be able to pop over from Shanghai. I texted Mark yesterday. He said they’re working on it. Apparently, flights are a nightmare. He’ll let me know for sure by next week, he reckons. It would be brilliant if they could make it. It’s been too long. Remember that disastrous Christmas Eve party we had at Mark's flat back in uni? The one where the cat got into the trifle? Oh, don’t remind me! Poor Mittens. Covered head to toe in custard and soaked cherries. Nearly gave his grandmother a heart attack. Good times, though. Absolutely mad. He had to spend three hours bathing the cat. Still laugh about that one. What about films this year? Any festive classics on your list? I’m thinking ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ again. Can’t go wrong with that. Absolutely ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’. A must. I’m also leaning towards ‘The Muppet Christmas Carol’. Always cheers me up, no matter how many times I've seen it. I saw a trailer for some new film, ‘Spirited’, with Ryan Reynolds and Will Ferrell, that looks pretty daft. Might be worth a look. Have you seen anything good recently, beyond the Christmas staples? I just watched 'Everything Everywhere All at Once'.

Right, just saw another one. Honestly, people on Twitter are unbelievable. This bloke's moaning about the font size on a university website. A  font size . Like, what is the world coming to? Oh, the usual keyboard warriors then? Don’t even get me started. Had a woman today, complained her sourdough was “too sourdoughy.” Like, what did she expect? A fluffy white loaf? Tell me about it. I had a guy in the café this afternoon who claimed his latte wasn’t ‘Instagrammable’ enough. Said it needed more foam art. More foam! I nearly lost it. I just pointed to the framed photo of Van Gogh’s Starry Night and said, 'Is  that  Instagrammable enough for you?' You’re a legend, El. Seriously. My thesis deadline is looming, and just reading about people’s petty grievances online is more stressful than the actual research sometimes. Should probably log off… but one more scroll… You do that. Meanwhile, I’m trying to ignore the two-star review someone left on Google. "Bread was hard. Staff were unhelpful. Ambience was depressing." Depressing! It was a Tuesday afternoon, drizzling, and the only ambience was the hum of the oven. Hard bread is a feature, not a bug! Reviews, eh? They’re a necessary evil, aren’t they? I’ve been obsessing over the design of the new seating area in the café. I’m thinking rattan chairs, lots of plants… trying to create a really chill, relaxed vibe. But what if people don’t  get  it? What if they leave reviews saying it’s ‘too minimalist’ or ‘too trendy’? See, that's a good problem to have, isn't it? Better than "too sourdoughy." Design is subjective. Rattan and plants sounds lovely. Are you considering getting one of those hanging macrame plant things? They're everywhere at the moment. I actually saw a really cool one in Margate last weekend! Went down there for a little break, breathed some sea air, and grabbed some fish and chips. Absolutely gorgeous architecture down there, too. You should come sometime. Margate? I’ve always wanted to go! It’s been on my list forever. I was thinking about maybe doing a little pop-up café there for the summer. Just a small one, with pastries and coffee. Test the waters, you know? Seriously? That's amazing, El! You should. It'd be perfect. It’s got that cool, slightly alternative vibe, right?

Right then, nearly ready! Oisin, darling, are you behaving yourself? Don’t you go throwing your dinner again. I’m being good, Mummy! But I want raspberries! Oh, groundbreaking news, Oisin. You want fruit. Truly monumental. Be nice, Liam. There are raspberries on the table, sweetie. Just wait until dinner's properly served. Honestly, you’d think he only lived on raspberries and chocolate ice cream. Speaking of chocolate ice cream, did you get any from that new place in town, Sarah? I keep seeing pictures all over Instagram. It looks  amazing . Not yet, Fiona. Perhaps for Liam after he's finished his vegetables. He's got those exams looming, doesn't he? Need to fuel that brain of his. They're not  looming . They’re next week. And I  like  vegetables. Mostly. Carrots are good. Broccoli is…acceptable. Yucky! See? A tiny critic. Remember what we talked about, darling? Superpowers come from eating your greens! Makes you strong enough to fly! Flying’s a long shot, even with greens, love. Though I did see a robin’s nest in my garden today. Full of eggs. Tiny, blue-green ones. It was rather beautiful. I saw a badger in Bristol last month. Nearly tripped over it on my way home from football practice. Big thing. Smelly, too. A badger! Goodness! You’re lucky you didn’t get a fright. We had a couple of gerbils when I was Oisin's age. Tiny little things, they were. Scuttling around all day. Remember, Liam and Fiona? We had them in that glass tank? Oh, I do! You named them Nibbles and Squeak, didn't you? You were obsessed with them. Cleaning the cage every day. I was! It's funny the things you remember. Anyway... Liam, how was your bike ride this morning? Did you go up to the woods? Yeah, it was good. Bit muddy in places. Actually saw Mrs. Peterson trying to prune her roses. She was really struggling. Needed a hand, but I didn’t want to stop. That's sweet of you to notice, even if you didn’t offer to help. Clearly, you're developing a very keen observational eye, just like your grandad used to have. Speaking of which, I planted some more tomato seedlings today. Hopefully, we'll have a bumper crop this year. Can I have raspberries  now ? Please, Mummy? I'm a good girl!

Honestly, the supermarket was absolute chaos this morning. People were grabbing everything in sight like it was the end of the world. I swear, someone nearly knocked me over reaching for the last jar of pesto. Did you manage to get everything you needed, Carol? Oh, love, you’re telling me! Went to Asda this mornin’, same story. Little nippers runnin’ about, people pushin’ trolleys like they’re racin'. Managed alright though. Got the Hoover bags and the bleach – essential supplies, innit? And some lovely apples. Fancy a slice with your coffee? Apples are good for you, dear. Keeps the doctor away, that’s what my mum always said. Though, I reckon a good cuppa tea and a biscuit is just as good! Used to get lovely apples from Mr. Higgins’ orchard back in the day. Best apples you ever tasted, they were. That's lovely, Nan. Remember when you used to grow your own rhubarb? So tart and delicious! Carol, about Mrs. Davies… I spoke to her yesterday. Her arthritis is really acting up, and she’s struggling to get to the shops. I was thinking, maybe we could take turns doing her shopping for her? That's a good idea, Sarah. Poor Mrs. Davies. I can do a couple of hours next week, no problem. She's a sweet lady, always having a biscuit ready. Got to look after our neighbours, haven't we? Though, I told her last week she really ought to cut down on the biscuits. She chuckled and said, “Cor, Carol, don’t you start!” Used to be a right chatterbox, Mrs. Davies. Remember when she used to come round for a game of bingo? Always had a lucky charm, she did. A little porcelain cat. I remember! Speaking of appearances, I'm dreading my eyebrow appointment next week. Honestly, it’s so fiddly. I always end up looking like Groucho Marx! Oh, you and your eyebrows! Bless you, love. Mine's just a quick pluck with the tweezers. Can't be bothered with all that threading and tinting. Though, I did see Dotty down the pub the other day, and her eyebrows were something else. Looked like caterpillars had taken up residence! Dotty! Always a character, that one. Used to smoke like a chimney, she did. Remember the smell of her fags clinging to your clothes after she'd been round? Oh, please, Nan!

Honestly, this weaning process is proving to be quite the adventure, isn’t it? Little Leo managed to get more sweet potato in his hair than in his mouth this morning. It was a right mess! Tell me about it! Elsie did the same with carrot – bright orange everywhere. It’s like they're specifically trying to make a statement about their dislike of vegetables. Though, he  did  seem to enjoy the apple puree. He actually smiled, a proper, gooey smile. See, that's the breakthrough, isn't it? That one little smile makes all the mess worthwhile. I remember the same with Finn, the pureed pears were the key. Such a fussy baby, he was. How’s Elsie settling in at the school? You seemed a bit tired last week. She is, actually. Really enjoying it. The other children are lovely, and the headteacher is brilliant. I was just a bit run down, I think. A few late nights marking and planning lessons. Nothing a decent night's sleep and Leo's not demanding my attention for a change won't fix! What about you? Still working through those garden plans? Yes, slowly but surely. I’ve ordered some lavender seeds and a climbing rose - 'Gertrude Jekyll' variety, you know. Apparently, the scent is divine. I’m hoping to create a little haven out back. It needs a lot of work, mind. It's looking a bit worse for wear. Speaking of things needing work, have you thought about what we're doing next week? Auntie Carol’s birthday is looming. Oh, yes! Carol’s birthday. I completely forgot! We should definitely do something nice. I was thinking maybe we could take her out for a nice lunch? Somewhere she hasn’t been before? There's that Italian place near Tamworth, 'Bella Notte,' she's been wanting to try. Bella Notte sounds lovely! I’ll book a table. And what about Uncle David? Is he free? It would be nice if we could all go together. I'll give him a ring. He mentioned he had a work engagement on Wednesday, but maybe he's free on Thursday? I’ll find out. It would definitely be better with them both there. So, lavender and roses... and a birthday lunch for Carol. Sounds like a busy, but lovely week. It does. And Leo needs to be weaned onto something other than sweet potato, apparently.

Honestly, it’s just… lovely, isn't it? I’d forgotten how much I missed this. Being away from the university, away from the city… it’s a balm for the soul. You know, you sound like a particularly earnest postcard. "Greetings from Norfolk! Feeling refreshed and contemplating the beauty of nature!" But yes, it is. Absolutely stunning. Especially given how flat we are generally speaking. Flat? Don’t be ridiculous. We’ve got hills. Hills? Those gentle undulations barely qualify as hills. You’re stretching it, darling. London has more pronounced lumps than Norfolk, and that's saying something. Oh, stop being so London-centric. That little rise over there, by the old stone wall? That’s a hill! A small one, admittedly, but a hill nonetheless. It gives a different perspective, doesn't it? You can see further. Perspective from a modest incline. Right. Still, I'll concede you have a point. It’s a nice change from the relentless concrete jungle. Remember that time we tried to hike Primrose Hill and half the park was closed for filming? Don’t remind me! We spent more time dodging camera crews than enjoying the view. This is… peaceful. And the villages! Look at that one - Little Walsingham. It looks completely untouched by modern life. It probably hasn't changed much in centuries. They're remarkably well-preserved, those Norfolk villages. All flint and thatch, winding lanes... I read something the other day about how their preservation is partially due to the local clay being so unsuitable for industrial development. Kept the factories away. See? There's a history here, a proper sense of place. It's not just pretty scenery. It’s interwoven with lives and stories. Think of all the people who have walked these paths before us. Farming families, smugglers... Smugglers, yes. Norfolk’s coastline was prime territory for that sort of thing. I should look into that. Perhaps a topic for a lecture? 'The Economic Impact of Maritime Smuggling in 18th Century Norfolk'... might need a bit more work than that though. You’d spin it into something incredibly academic, I’m sure. Don't forget to mention the local pubs that were essentially smuggling hubs. Naturally. The social impact wouldn't be ignored. Researching in actual pubs, of course, for authenticity. That's important fieldwork. You are incorrigible. But seriously, it's amazing how the landscape shapes a culture.

Honestly, did you  see  'Dune: Part Two'? Absolute spectacle, wasn’t it? Like, visually, just… wow. But I'm still not sure I completely got all the politics. It were a bit much, weren't they? A bit much? That’s putting it mildly! I spent the whole time trying to keep track of the houses and their grudges. But yes, visually stunning. Zimmer’s score was phenomenal, as always. Did you think Zendaya’s character arc was believable? Aye, I did, actually. I think Florence Pugh's in 'Oppenheimer’ were better though. I reckon she's going to be huge. Proper star quality. Anyway, speaking of grand schemes and complicated stuff… did you hear back about Liam’s application to 'GreenTech Solutions'? Just spoke to him actually. He got it! Senior Analyst, apparently. Quite a jump from what he was doing at the university. He sounds thrilled. A lot more money too, which is… good. Brilliant for him! He deserves it, honestly. Always been a clever lad. Though I remember him moaning about all the paperwork at uni. GreenTech’s going to be even worse, I bet, but at least he’ll be helping the planet, eh? It's good he's finally found something he's passionate about. It’s about time he stopped panicking about what his parents wanted him to do! Definitely. He seemed much more relaxed when I spoke to him. Less perpetually anxious. And it’s a proper proper company, apparently. Cutting-edge stuff with renewable energy. Maybe I could have a chat with him about some of the structural engineering aspects. It might be mutually beneficial. Ooh, yeah, do that! I’m glad he’s landed on his feet. Sometimes I worry about all me mates, just drifting, ya know? Trying to find their way. Though I'm happy here, I suppose. Corpus admin's not exactly jet-setting, but it’s steady work, and I like the detail of it. It's important work, Anon. Someone has to manage the linguistic data! And you're brilliant at it. Back to something slightly less serious… have you noticed how many cyclists there are these days? Honestly, it’s like they’ve completely taken over the roads. Tell me about it! Driving 'ere in Newcastle is a nightmare! They just weave in and out, no signalling, wearing headphones… It's like they think the rules don't apply to them.

Honestly, this is just balm for the soul, isn’t it? After marking those essays… goodness, some of them were frankly baffling. Did they even  read  the set texts? Sounds like a typical Tuesday. The undergrads engaging in a valiant, but often misguided, attempt at critical analysis. Though, I did have one particularly sparky response to Baudrillard this week. Actually made me rethink a couple of things. Oh really? Do tell! I'm always up for a little Baudrillard-induced existential crisis. But first, look at these poppies! They’re absolutely bursting. You could almost feel the economic impact of a good poppy harvest, couldn't you? The agricultural subsidies, the global trade… it's all connected. You see economics  everywhere , don't you, Elara? Yes, absolutely. Though I suspect this particular lot aren't destined for anything more lucrative than brightening a Norfolk field. Speaking of economics, I was reading a piece about the devaluation of the pound. Quite worrying, actually. Especially for research funding. Dreadful, isn’t it? All this instability. Makes securing that grant for my comparative linguistics project even more stressful. Think about it – I'm trying to compare the evolution of regional dialects in three countries, and the funding is tied to exchange rates! Utter chaos. Precisely. It highlights the fragility of these things, doesn't it? My research on historical trade routes is having similar issues. Trying to account for fluctuating currency values across centuries... a nightmare. Though, I did find a fascinating correlation between the rise of Flemish textile trade and early usage of the word "button." Right, because  that's  what’s important in a crumbling economy. Buttons! Still, it’s fascinating stuff. You know, it always amazes me how language reflects economic power. Think about all the loanwords French has contributed to English - a direct result of Norman dominance. Footing the bill of an invasion, eh? Absolutely. And the reverse, of course. English has left its mark globally, largely due to the British Empire's economic clout. It's no surprise to see English as a lingua franca in so many former colonies. Do you think they'll ever properly sort out the offside rule in football, though? That’s a problem with international ramifications, you know. Arguably as important to global relations as trade. Don’t be ridiculous, David. Football is significantly  less  important than trade. Though, I do agree, the current interpretation is baffling.

Right, so, parking at Wimbledon. You  swear  it's a nightmare? Like, worse than trying to get a space near the Angel on a Sunday? Significantly worse, love. Think Piccadilly Circus at rush hour, but with fewer buses and a lot more people in white. You’ll be circling for ages. I’ve got a reservation at the NCP on Lower Ground, but it’s still a fifteen-minute walk, minimum. And that’s if you don’t get held up by a rogue family pushing a triple buggy. Fifteen minutes! Seriously? I'm already picturing my ankles swelling up. Still, better than the alternative. Is that the one you booked before? The posh one? The one with the valet option. Thought we'd treat ourselves. Saves lugging the tennis bags and my ridiculously large cooler box. You know, essentials. Ridiculously large cooler box? What's in it, a full Sunday roast? You’re mad! Although… that  would  be a good idea. Better than those overpriced sandwiches they sell inside. Almost as good. Mostly just enough Pims to sink a battleship and cucumber sandwiches. It’s a tradition. Speaking of traditions... Are you still backing Newcastle for the Premier League this year? Don’t tell me you’ve lost faith after last season’s…unpleasantness. Never! I wouldn’t abandon the Toon Army for all the cucumber sandwiches in Wimbledon Village. Okay, maybe  most  of the cucumber sandwiches. They’re pretty good. But yeah, I’m sticking with them. We’ve got a decent squad now, and Howe’s got them playing well. It’s our year, I'm telling you. Brave words, love. Very brave. I'm cautiously optimistic about Arsenal, myself. Though, let’s be honest, they choke spectacularly every season. It's a comedic highlight, really. Optimistic, eh? You're a posh lad through and through, aren't you? Always backing the favourites. It’s a wonder you haven't lost your discerning taste for bespoke tailoring by now. Hey, a little ambition never hurt anyone. Although, thinking of ambitions… Have you had any movement on that flat you were looking at in Hackney? The one near Victoria Park? Actually, yeah. They got back to me. Apparently, there's a viewing next week. It's a tiny little place, mind. But it’s got a balcony with a decent view, and it’s ridiculously well-connected. And the parking… they have allocated spaces!

Honestly, it’s all anyone’s talking about, isn’t it? The Depp-Heard trial. Absolutely bonkers. I’ve been following it religiously. I can't believe how much detail has come out. Aye, I've seen bits and bobs on telly. Seems a right mess, doesn’t it? All that shouting and accusations. Never did understand why people get involved in such things. Best to keep yourself to yourself, I always say. Heard about it, dear. Can't say I'm bothered much. All that fuss over…celebrities. Give me a good pair of binoculars any day. Look at those geese! Oh, yes! They’re looking particularly plump today. Are they getting ready to go, do you think? Migration season must be approaching. They'll be off soon, alright. Remember last year? We had a proper flock hanging around, gobbling up all the bread crumbs. Had to shoo 'em away from the bird table, they were getting greedy. Greedy little beggars they are. Used to have a right old gaggle around here when I was a girl. Back in the thirties. Used to scare the wits out of you, those geese. Huge they were! Not like these little fellows. Really? Were they migrating through then too, or did they stay put? They mostly stayed, dear. Used to nest in the fields behind the house. My father, bless his soul, he used to take me out to watch them hatch their eggs. Lovely sight it was, the goslings all tumbling out. Right fluffy things they were. My grandad used to tell stories about geese raiding the vegetable patches. Took half his prize-winning cabbages, he said! Sounded a proper nuisance, but he always had a twinkle in his eye when he told it. They do have a reputation! It's fascinating, isn't it, how their migration patterns change. I read an article the other day about scientists tracking them using GPS. Apparently, they use the stars and Earth's magnetic field to navigate! Stars and magnetic fields, you say? Well, I never! We just knew they'd be heading south when the weather turned cold. Common sense, really. Follow the warm air. My cousin, she saw a flock of geese flying over earlier this week. Heading east, she said. Odd, that. Usually they go south, don’t they? That is strange. Could be a slight shift in prevailing winds affecting their route.

Honestly, Anon, this is lovely! You’ve really outdone yourself. Proper feast. I was starving after that awful commute. Birmingham traffic is just… relentless. Glad you like it! It’s nothing fancy, just a bit of what I had in the fridge. You know how it is. Kids, leftovers… you either eat it or it goes in the bin. Traffic, eh? You’re lucky coming from Hitchin. My journey in today was a nightmare too. Someone had clearly decided to have a full-on breakdown on the M5. Oh, that's just brilliant timing, isn't it? And I had that interview prep running round in my head the whole way. Speaking of which… how was little Leo today? He seemed a bit peaky last time I saw him. He was a bit grumpy, to be honest. Teething, I think. He mostly just wanted to be held and gnaw on things. But he gave me a lovely gummy smile when I managed to distract him with a banana. He’s such a little character. What about Elsie? Still terrorising the cat, I presume? Absolutely. Barnaby hasn’t had a peaceful nap in weeks. She’s decided he’s her personal climbing frame. I’m half-expecting to find her wearing his tail as a scarf one day. But she's amazing, really. So clever. Anyway, about the interview... it was… a mixed bag. Oh dear. Not good? You were so well-prepared, I thought you’d ace it. What happened? Don't be shy, tell me all about it. Pass me some of that quiche, by the way – this smells divine. Well, the panel were pleasant enough, but one of them kept interrupting me! Honestly, it was so frustrating. I'd just get into a proper answer about differentiating instruction and suddenly,  bam , another question. I felt like I didn't get to fully explain my ideas and experience. And they kept pushing me on this one specific behaviour management strategy that I’m not entirely comfortable with. It felt a bit… prescriptive. Ugh, that sounds awful! That’s so rude, interrupting like that. And a restrictive behaviour policy? Honestly, some schools are stuck in the dark ages. It's about building relationships and understanding, isn't it? Not just imposing rules. Did you mention your success with the peer mentoring program at your last school? I did, briefly. But it got cut off again!

Honestly, this whole "future" thing feels utterly overwhelming, doesn’t it? Like, everyone keeps asking, "What's the five-year plan?" and I just want to scream. My five-year plan is to not fall down the stairs. I know exactly what you mean! It’s like there’s this expectation that we should all have it figured out. My mum’s been on at me since Christmas about "settling down" and getting a house. Settle down! I’m twenty-three! I'm barely settled in Cambridge. Tell me about it. My nan keeps dropping hints about grandchildren. Like, I appreciate the sentiment, but I haven't even managed to keep a succulent alive, let alone nurture a tiny human. Production controlling is stressful enough as it is! Right? The pressure is relentless. But, you know, sometimes I do wonder… I mean, I like my job, I really do. It’s decent money, and Sarah's a lovely boss. But…is this  it ? Is this what I’ll be doing in five years? Processing spreadsheets in a beige office? That's exactly the feeling! It’s not that I hate my job. It’s… stable. Solid. And that’s good, right? But I keep thinking about that postgraduate course I nearly did, the one on sustainable design. It felt…more  me . Sustainable design? That sounds amazing! Why didn't you do it? Crikey, money mostly. And a feeling that it was a bit… frivolous, maybe? My dad always stressed the importance of a 'proper' career, you know? Something secure, something with a pension. Production controlling ticks all those boxes. I get that. My parents are the same. But maybe it's not too late? You could do it part-time, couldn't you? Or online? I hadn’t really thought about online. Though, honestly, the thought of staring at another screen after a full day of production schedules… it’s exhausting just  thinking  about it. What about you? Any secret dreams bubbling under the surface of administrative efficiency? Oh, loads. I used to write poetry, actually. Proper, rhyming, pretentious stuff. I even entered a competition when I was sixteen. Got absolutely slaughtered by the judge, but it was still… fun. Now it’s just grocery lists in my head. You should write something again! Seriously. There's a spoken word night at The Portland Arms next month, you should go, see what it’s like.

Honestly, Bethany, he’s just… infuriating. Like, actively trying to wind me up infuriating. Who, Liam? Still going on about that girl from uni? Give it a rest, Maisie, love. You’ve told us this story about six times already this trip. Six times?! It feels like sixty. But he keeps bringing it up! He was going on about how “clever” she is, and how they have “so much in common.” I nearly chucked my latte at him. Common? The only thing you two have in common is a shared appreciation for lukewarm instant coffee! You're catastrophizing, Maisie. It’s classic boyfriend insecurity. He probably just wants to feel secure in your relationship, and this is his incredibly awkward way of doing it. Insecurity? That’s just an excuse for being a right git, Chloe! I’m secure. I’m as solid as Sheffield steel. I don’t need him listing the intellectual merits of every woman he breathes near. Besides, he knows I’m planning on starting that pottery course next term. He knows I'm busy and focused! True, the pottery thing is a good distraction. You'll be covered in clay and swearing by the end of week one. It'll be a right laugh, actually. Speaking of laughter, did you see Sarah’s Instagram story? No! What? Don't keep me in suspense! Is it another one of her attempts at 'effortless chic' with a bin bag and a safety pin? Better! Worse, actually. She's with Josh. Holding hands. In Nice. No way! But… didn’t she just dump him last month for being “emotionally unavailable”? That was a whole drama, involving a blocked number and a strongly worded text about his inability to commit to… ordering pizza toppings. Women. Go figure. Relationships are truly baffling. It’s probably a rebound. Josh brings a certain… stability. Even if that stability is just the ability to remember to buy milk. Stability? He once forgot their anniversary and replaced his own birthday cake with a box of potted plants. Potted plants, Chloe! Seriously. See? Emotionally unavailable. Deeply, deeply emotionally unavailable. It's a miracle they were together for longer than a week. It's annoying, though, isn’t it? Seeing them all happy and coupled up when I’m dealing with Liam’s competitive obsession with random female academics. It's right unfair. Don't let it get to you, Maisie.

Right then, that was a lovely chicken curry, wasn’t it? Mark, you practically inhaled yours! It was excellent, Sarah. Honestly, one of the best you’ve made. Needed after that hockey match, believe me. My legs are screaming. Was it a good match, Dad? Did your team win? It was a nail-biter, Ollie. Tied right up until the last minute. We managed to pull one out though, 3-2. Sore, but worth it. Loads of penalties though, far too much handbags stuff going on. Handbags? What’s that mean? It's just a silly term we use in hockey, Liam. Meaning unnecessary fighting or aggressive play. Just a lot of silly pushing and shoving, really. Nothing serious. It’s a common complaint, isn't it? This season seems particularly…robust. Anyway, Ollie, did you finish your maths homework? Almost. Just need to do the last two questions on quadratic equations. Ugh. Quadratic equations! Remember when I used to struggle with those? I'm glad I don't have to do them anymore. Speaking of struggling, I've been wrestling with this proofreading job for a new client. It’s a technical manual for… I don’t even know what it is, honestly! Something to do with industrial pumps. Industrial pumps! Sounds thrilling. At least it’s paying the bills. It is, thankfully. But I’d rather be proofreading a holiday brochure or something. It’s all contract work, mind, which is fine, keeps things interesting, but... I was thinking, maybe we could actually put some proper plans in place for a holiday this year? A holiday? Where? Yeah, where are we going? I’ve been looking at a few options actually. Remember we talked about going to the Lake District? Or maybe somewhere in Cornwall? I quite like the look of Cornwall. Lots of beaches, proper cream teas... It would be lovely to get away for a week, just properly unwind. We haven't had a decent family holiday in ages. Cornwall sounds alright. Can we do some surfing? Surfing! Definitely surfing! Are there good waves? There are decent waves, Ollie. Not Hawaiian Pipeline, mind you, but perfectly acceptable for beginners. We’d need to rent some boards, of course. Right, well, I'll have a proper look at some websites tonight. See what sort of deals we can find. What dates would work best for everyone? Liam, your school summer holiday – when does that start?

Honestly, this is breathtaking, isn’t it? I’ve seen pictures, of course, but nothing quite prepares you for the sheer scale of these trees. It’s humbling. Yeah, it’s alright. Bit… green, innit? All this green. I’m used to slightly less verdant surroundings back home. Although, to be fair, Enfield isn’t exactly a forest. "Alright?" Seriously, Chloe? We're driving through a national park full of ancient giants! Think about how long these trees have been standing here, witnessing history. My grandma would have adored this. She used to drag us on nature walks in Kent, though those were considerably less impressive, mostly just muddy fields and grumpy sheep. Okay, okay, you’re right. It  is  impressive. Just... a bit overwhelming. Makes you feel rather small, doesn’t it? Speaking of grandparents, how’s Aunt Carol doing? Last I heard from Mum, she was convinced the neighbours were spying on her. Oh, Carol. She’s… Carol. Still convinced the neighbours are plotting something. Apparently, Mr. Henderson’s new security cameras are specifically aimed at her prize-winning roses. She bought a camouflage net for them. A camouflage net, Chloe! Honestly, the woman is a marvel. Mum’s trying to reason with her, but it’s like talking to a brick wall. Did she ever mention the squirrels stealing her birdseed? She’s convinced they're trained operatives, paid off by Mr. Henderson to deplete her reserves. Trained squirrel operatives! Only Carol. Honestly, Mum has her work cut out for her. Remember when she thought the postman was leaving coded messages in her junk mail? It was just pizza flyers, but she swore they used a substitute for 'e' that only she could decipher. Exactly! It’s a constant source of amusement and mild concern. Though, to be fair, she's generally happy. It’s just… her imagination runs a bit wild sometimes. I wonder if it's hereditary. Do you ever feel like you get a little  too  carried away imagining things? Not really. I’m more the practical type, I think. Though, I’ve had my moments. Remember that time I was convinced I saw a UFO over Enfield retail park? Turned out it was just a weather balloon. I felt really silly after that. Silly? You insisted on calling the local paper! They actually sent a reporter. He looked  very  skeptical. He was! And he’s probably still telling that story at parties.

Jaysus, this is grand. Proper Chicken Kiev this is, not that watery stuff you get in some places. Right, so, did you lads see the match yesterday? Absolute thriller, it was. That last-minute penalty… nearly gave me a cardiac arrest. Yeah, it was good! Bit stressful though, Dad. I thought we were gonna lose. Did you shout at the telly? He  always  shouts at the telly, darling. It's a national pastime, isn't it? Honestly, the language sometimes... Still, a good win. Though, I couldn’t really follow it properly, to be fair, I was mostly trying to stop Leo from throwing his puree at the screen. He’s got a remarkable aim, that one. He'll be a natural at hurling then. Leo, is it? Should be called ‘The Missile’. And I wasn’t  shouting , I was… expressing my concern, passionately. It's different. So, about Granny… Are we still on for visiting her next Saturday? Yeah, sounds good. Can I take my new drone? I want to film the garden. Drone? In Granny’s garden? Now hold on a minute, there's a limit to the technology you bring around her. She’d faint! Remember that time you showed her a TikTok? Nearly scared her half to death. Honestly, both of you. Let the boy have a bit of fun. It’s not like he’s going to be buzzing it around her head. And it might be nice for Granny to see the garden from a different angle. She's been complaining about her back again, you know. Can’t bend down as easily these days. Alright, alright. Just promise me you'll keep it away from the prize-winning roses. Last thing we need is a drone incident involving horticultural chaos. Right. Speaking of chaos, you wouldn't believe the day I had in the office. Gary from accounts… Absolute Wallie. Tried to upload the quarterly reports directly to the shared drive. Didn't even bother with Dropbox or Flickr! A Wallie? What's a Wallie? It’s a term of endearment, son. A term of endearment for someone who's… not the sharpest tool in the shed. Essentially, a daft eejit. Happened again last week, you know. Trying to email a ten gig file.
