Honestly, it’s like teaching a cat to do algebra. It’s exhausting. Sounds like you need a holiday, love.

Right, nearly there. Just needs a bit more… something. What do you think, love? A pinch more rosemary? Hmm? Oh, the soup? Yeah, rosemary sounds good. It’s smelling rather lovely, actually. Better than that… that attempt at buckwheat bread last week. Don't remind me! Honestly, it was like eating cardboard. I followed the recipe exactly, I swear. Buckwheat is clearly not my forte. We’ll stick to shop-bought for now, shall we? Though I did see a woman at the market on Saturday selling the most gorgeous loaves… all sourdough, naturally. The market, yes. I was distracted by that new cheese stall – the smoked cheddar was exceptional. Almost worth battling the crowds for. Did you find anything interesting? Besides evidence of my baking failure? Definitely. You know I've been on the hunt for a proper vintage tea set. And I think I’ve finally scored. Look! Blimey! That's… rather something. Is that Royal Albert? The 'Old Country Roses' pattern? I think so! The listing said it was, and the photos looked genuine. Apparently, it's from the 1960s. Six cups, six saucers, a cake plate… all in remarkably good condition, considering. I snagged it on eBay for a surprisingly reasonable price. You did? Seriously? That's fantastic! You’ve been obsessing over those for ages. Are you sure it’s not a fake? There's a lot of that about. I’ve checked the hallmarks and the back stamps. They seem legitimate. The seller had a high feedback score, too. I’m taking a risk, I know, but I just couldn't resist. It's arriving tomorrow. I'm so excited I could burst. Well, don't burst just yet – we need to eat! And speaking of excitement… have you thought any more about next Friday? Sarah's leaving do. It's at The Red Lion, remember. Yes, Friday. I was thinking about what to get her. She mentioned she’s taking up pottery, so maybe a voucher for a class? Or something pottery-related… clay tools, maybe? That’s a brilliant idea! Something practical. I was just thinking of getting her a bottle of wine, but that feels a bit… impersonal, doesn’t it? I’ll look online tonight. Do you think we should go early? It'll probably be packed. Yes, definitely. Early doors is always the best policy. It's going to be a bit sad seeing her go, though.

Right then, so, you’re sayin’ this… 'structurin’' as you call it… is like, normal practice now? Like, everyone does it with their business? Honestly, it sounds proper dodgy, doesn't it? I mean, Dad always said if it looks like a duck, and quacks like a duck… Look, love, it's not about being dodgy. It’s about efficiency. The French banking system, specifically, they're not fans of large sums moving around. They get nervous. Structuring is about breaking those large sums into smaller deposits, multiple accounts, spreading the risk. It's tax-efficient too, and frankly, perfectly legal  if  done correctly. And believe me, I've got it down to a fine art. It’s just…smart business. But…criminal records, aren't they? I read somethin’ about that online. About how even if it’s  legal , they can still nail you. Finn, Finn, Finn. You and the internet. Let me explain something. There's a difference between structuring and money laundering. Money laundering is dirty money  made  from illegal activities, being disguised as legitimate funds. Structuring is taking  clean  money and strategically moving it. Now, if you get caught because you’re absolutely dithering about with the amounts and attracting attention, well, then you could get a fine. A hefty one. Trust me, I know. Remember that fiasco with the Monaco accounts in ‘08? Lost a fortune in fines over that. Oh, God, don't remind me. You were proper stressed about that. Did Mum know? Your mum knew I was “dealing with some paperwork” that involved a lot of late nights and international calls. She wouldn’t have understood the nuances. And honestly, it’s better she didn't. The less they know, the less burdened they are. It’s a shield, really. Protecting them. So, you’re sayin’ it’s like… a secret you keep, to protect everyone? In a way, yes. It's about insulating the family. Think of it like this – running a successful business, especially one with international transactions, requires…certain strategies. And those strategies aren't always pretty or easily explained. But what about Amelia? And Leo? What if they find out down the line? They're sharp kids, they'll work it out eventually. That's a worry, I won't lie. But by the time they’re old enough to really question things, hopefully, the business will be restructured further, less… complicated.

Honestly, this weather is just bonkers, isn't it? One minute it's sunshine, the next it's threatening to rain sideways. Remember last week when we had that hail? Aye, a proper hailstorm that was. Nearly dented the car. Fundraising events are a nightmare when the weather's like this. People are less inclined to stand around in the wind. Been trying to convince the committee we need a gazebo for the summer fair. It’s a bit chaotic, definitely. But I rather like it. It’s characterful! Things at school are pretty manic, though. Ofsted are looming, you know. All the kids are a bit edgy, and so are the staff. Tell me about it! Retail is the same. Everyone's got that end-of-month spending panic. Plus, we’re getting ready for the summer sale – it’s a frenzy. My team are already exhausted. We’re finally getting a better system for stock rotation, though. It should hopefully make things a bit smoother. That’s good, love. Speaking of things getting smoother, how’s the sign language class going, Elodie? I’ve been thinking about it, and it seems such a brilliant way to broaden your skillset. It’s amazing, actually! Really challenging, but absolutely brilliant. We're learning basic greetings and introductions this week. It's so interesting trying to visualize the language; it’s like a whole new way of communicating. I'm feeling much more confident already. I’d love to incorporate some signing into the classroom. It could be really beneficial for some of the children. That’s fantastic, love. Good on you for giving it a go. Any chance you could teach me a few signs? I need something to impress at the next charity gala. You know, 'thank you' and 'donation accepted' would be a good start. Absolutely, Dad! I’d be happy to. Though, you have to promise to practice between now and then. It's lovely that you're doing that, Elodie. You're always thinking of new ways to help people. So, have you decided on a name for the little one yet? Still playing it close to your chest? We're getting close. We've got a shortlist, that's for sure. We want something that feels…right, you know? Something that suits her. Don't rush it, love. It’s a big decision. Though, I’m starting to picture myself pushing a pram around Lichfield.

Right, so, this sourdough is  actually  decent. Considering it’s from the Press canteen, I was expecting something resembling cardboard. It’s…fine. I’m trying to be healthy, you know? Big deadline next week, need to be firing on all cylinders. It’s the Alistair Finch manuscript; the author’s notoriously difficult. Oh, Finch! Don’t even get me started. I had to proofread a chapter of his last year. Every single comma felt like a personal attack. Honestly, I spent half my time arguing with him about Oxford serial commas. Oxford serial commas? Is that like...a regional thing? I'm still trying to get my head around the whole 'biscuit' versus 'cookie' debate, and now this? It absolutely is, Elodie. A truly passionate battleground. It’s a style choice, really, whether or not to include the serial comma before the 'and' in a list. Some publishers – Cambridge University Press being one of them – are very strict about it. Drives copy editors mad. It’s all about clarity, officially, but it’s more about tradition, innit? Don't remind me. Alistair Finch is a serial comma absolutist. He threatened to pull the entire manuscript if it wasn't precisely to his liking. It’s utterly exhausting. I think my stress levels have aged me ten years. Tell me about it. I actually dreamed in commas for a week after working on Finch’s stuff. I woke up and started alphabetising my cutlery. It was a dark time. So, Elodie, are you enjoying your temporary placement? What are you working on? It's...interesting. Very different from what I’m used to. I’m mostly helping with the marketing materials for a new series on Scandinavian folklore. Lots of pretty pictures of forests and mythical creatures. It’s much less stressful than dealing with demanding authors. Though, I did have a bit of a mishap with a spreadsheet today. Let’s just say, pivot tables and I don’t get along. Pivot tables are the bane of everyone’s existence, aren’t they? I spent a whole afternoon last week wrestling with one during a data analysis project. Pulled out all my hair trying to filter by language group. It’s like they’re deliberately designed to confuse you. What language research are you coordinating, anyway? Sounds fascinating. It is, actually. I’m currently focusing on the impact of AI on language learning.

Right, so, gumtree’s a right waste of time, innit? Posted five ads, not a single peep. Five! Folk just scroll past, like we're sellin' somethin' nobody wants. We’re tryin’ ta raise money for kids, for cryin’ out loud! Honestly, Liam, you can’t expect miracles. Gumtree’s a bit… chaotic. Did you actually put details in the ads? Like, what the rally is? What the charity are? People need somethin’ to grab onto, not just “Charity Rally - Donate!” Aye, aye. Said it all. “Mongolia Rally, Save the Children, donations welcome, prizes for best fancy dress…” The lot. Maybe I need to, like, use more emojis? Does that even work on Gumtree? Probably not. Look, let's back off Gumtree for now. We’re better off focusing on flyers around Warrington and maybe knocking on doors. More personal, y’know? Speaking of which, how’s the visa application comin’ along? You sent off everything they asked for? That’s the thing, isn't it? I'm still wrestling with it. They wanted two passport photos, ‘head and shoulders, plain background, no glasses’. I’ve taken about twenty photos and they all look like I’m trying to escape from a bad hair day. Every single one! I look like a startled ferret. You do look like a startled ferret sometimes, yeah. Have you tried somewhere that does professional prints? Like Timpson’s? They’ll sort you out, guaranteed. It'll cost a few quid, but it’s worth it. A blurry photo will just get rejected and delay everything. Aye, I reckon you're right. I was tryin’ to save a few bob. But stubborn fool that I am, I thought I could conquer the art of passport photography. Failed miserably, haven't I? Right, Timpson’s it is. Tomorrow mornin'. What about the donations? Did your mate at the pub put the collection tin out? He did, yeah. Said he's already had a few quid. Not a fortune, but every little helps. I was thinking, maybe we could run a bake sale? My mum's a whiz at baking. She could make loads of cakes and cookies. We could set it up in the town square. A bake sale! That’s brilliant, that is! Loads of folk will be about on a Saturday. We could even get me grandma to bake. Her Eccles cakes are legendary. Though, gettin’ her to actually  bake … that’s the challenge.

Ugh, I’m proper knackered. Honestly, last night was… a lot. Feels like I've been run over by a bus. Tell me about it. My head’s absolutely pounding. You okay though? Still sore from, you know… the arm thing? Yeah, a bit. It’s throbbing a bit actually. The painkillers are doing their job, I reckon, but I still feel a bit wobbly. Blimey, the hospital was mental, innit? So many people. And that waiting room...felt like I was in there for hours. It was grim, yeah. I kept checking my phone every five minutes, just panicking you weren’t alright. Did they say what caused it? The arm injury, I mean? Nah, not really. They did an X-ray, just to rule out anything serious, and apparently it’s just a bad sprain. They gave me some stronger painkillers and told me to rest it. Easier said than done when you're trying to grab a takeaway pizza at two in the morning! Typical you. So, pizza prompted the arm-hurting incident? Pretty much! I was reaching for the last slice and just… went over. Felt a proper pop. Honestly, I thought I'd broken it. Well, you're back now and that's the main thing. You need to be careful though, honestly. And maybe avoid late-night pizza missions for a while. Right, I’m gonna pop to the kitchen to make some toast. Anyone want anything? Yeah, buttered, please. And a confession... I may have spent a considerable amount of last night thinking about Liam. Liam?  That  Liam? The one with the ridiculously floppy hair? The one and only. He was… charming. We talked for ages after the lecture about Romantic poetry. Apparently, he’s a massive Keats fan. Keats? That’s a good sign. Means he’s got some depth. It does, doesn't it? But he also mentioned he's going to a football match on Saturday. Liverpool vs. Man U. Ooh, tricky. Liverpool, eh? Bold move for a bloke you’ve just met. Exactly! So, now I'm torn. Should I play it cool? Or should I… well, subtly mention I’m also a Liverpool fan? Definitely mention the Liverpool fan thing. Common ground is always good. But don't force it. Just… let it drop casually. Like, "Oh, I'm gutted to miss that match on Saturday!" Yeah, that’s good.

Right then, love. That was quite the do, wasn't it? Twenty-five years! Can you believe it? Seems like just yesterday your dad was chasing me round the garden with a watering can. Yeah, it was alright, Gran. A bit… loud though, innit? Loads of people. Loud? It were a celebration, lad! A proper family knees-up. And your Auntie Carol did a smashing job with the buffet, didn't she? All that little Yorkshire pudding action. The Yorkshire puddings were okay. I mostly had chips. And cake. Loads of cake. But Uncle Barry was telling the same story about catching that carp for, like, the tenth time. It got a bit tiresome. Oh, Barry. He does love a good yarn, doesn't he? Bless 'im. But he were chuffed to bits that you were there, you know. He kept saying how much you’d grown. Nearly burst with pride, he did. Did you speak to your cousin, Emily? She seemed interested in your A-Level choices. Briefly. She asked about Physics, but then she started going on about her horses. It's always horses with Emily. Aye, horses are her passion, aren't they? Good on her for having something she loves. Still, I thought she seemed genuinely interested. You should tell her about that new solar panel project you’re working on. She might find it quite clever, you know. Thinking outside the box, like you do. Nah. She wouldn’t get it. It’s just science-y stuff. Besides, your mum cornered me for half an hour about university applications. Talk about pressure. Your mum does get a bit carried away, I’ll admit. Just wants what’s best for you, though, love. She's proud of you, you know that. And she's worried. It's a big decision. Have you narrowed it down a bit? Still thinking about Leeds? I’ve looked at Leeds, yeah. And Sheffield. But I saw this place in Manchester… it’s got a really good robotics lab. I could do some serious research there. Manchester, eh? Bit far from home, isn't it? Your dad’ll have a fit. He’ll be wanting you down the pub every Friday night, like clockwork. He’ll get over it. And I can still come home for weekends. It’s just… it feels like a better opportunity. Well, you need to follow your own path, lad.

Are we nearly there yet, Dad? My bum’s numb. And I'm parched. Where's me water bottle? Now, now, Elsie. We’ve only been driving for, what, three and a half hours? And your bum’s not numb, you're just being dramatic. Your water bottle's in that bag beside you, love. I put it there myself. You’ll need it for the rest of the journey. Well, it’s hard to see in that black bag. And I need a pen too. I want to write down some of these places we're passin’. Like, what even  is  Shropshire? It sounds like something from Harry Potter. Shropshire’s a county, Elsie. Proper old English county. And you need a pen? Right, let me have a rummage. Found one! Here you go. Think of it as a bit of a history lesson, eh? We're practically touching Wales now, you know. Wales! Can we stop for a pasty? I’m starvin’. What are we having for supper tonight? Hopefully not beans on toast again. We'll see about a pasty, love. Can’t promise anything with that traffic though. Supper… I was thinking we could grab something on the way into Cornwall, maybe fish and chips. Or we could even stop at a Holland and Barrett. Holland and Barrett? Dad! Seriously? I want proper food, not kale and chia seeds. Remember that time you bought all that liquorice root for your IBS? Awful. Absolutely awful. Don't remind me, Elsie. My stomach hasn’t forgiven me for that. It was supposed to help, you know. My gut plays up something fierce these days, put it that way. Brings back memories of moving house, though, doesn't it? All that unpacking… it’s stressful. Sorting through all the old boxes. Yeah, but at least moving from that tiny flat to the new one was a good thing. More space for Basil, definitely. Have you ordered the new cat flap yet? The old one's stuck. Been trying to, but Amazon have been a right mess lately. Delivery times are all over the place. We’ll have to pop to a local shop once we're settled. Speaking of settled, I've been trying to work out the best way to get that antique desk into the new house. It's a beast! Needs to be disassembled, I reckon. Oh, that desk is gorgeous!

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that solicitor's letter. Three years! Three years chasing down that dodgy accountant and for what? A paltry sum, really. It feels like a monumental waste of time and effort. I know, love. I saw the stress etched all over your face these past few months. But you persevered, and you got something back. That’s more than a lot of people would have managed. You’re incredibly tenacious, you know that? Tenacity is a vital quality, David. Particularly in this day and age. The world doesn’t hand you anything on a silver platter. Your sister, Eleanor, has shown remarkable grit. It's a pity young people today don't cultivate it more. They expect everything to be instantly gratifying. Grit? Aye, you need a good bit o’ grit to build a decent sideboard, let me tell you. Dealing with suppliers, getting the right timber delivered... it’s a constant battle sometimes. But Eleanor, you’re right, she’s a powerhouse. I always knew it, even when she was a wee thing, correcting my grammar at every turn. Oh, stop it, Bryn! You were my favourite victim. But seriously, it's exhausting. And what are we even going to  do  with the money? It’s not enough to buy a small island in the Caribbean. We could put it towards that new conservatory you’ve been wanting. It would be lovely to have a proper space for your plants. Remember how you were complaining about the lack of sunlight in the living room? A conservatory is a capital idea. A light, airy space. One could grow orchids, you know. I always had a beautiful collection in my study at the school. Though, maintenance was a beast. Orchids, eh? Too fussy for me. Give me a good, sturdy oak tree any day. Something that'll stand the test of time. A conservatory… it’s all well and good, but will it keep the rain out? That’s the real question. Bryn has a point. We need something practical. And something that won't require a constant stream of maintenance. A sunroom with decent insulation, perhaps? Somewhere we can sit and read during the winter months. A sunroom it is, then. We could look at some designs online tonight. Something modern, but with a bit of character. Not too sterile, you know? Modernity is all well and good, but don't forget the importance of natural light.

Right, Mother’s Day. It's creeping up on us, isn't it? Seems like just yesterday we were wrestling with Christmas decorations. Mummy, what’s Mother’s Day? Is it when we give you flowers? And chocolate! Can I pick the chocolate? I want the one with the caramel swirls! Yes, loves, it's when we celebrate you both being amazing, which you are, every single day! And yes, there will be flowers and chocolate. But it's more than that, isn't it? It’s about appreciating all mums do. You know, like cooking your dinner – which I'm doing now – and chasing away the monsters under the bed? The monsters are scared of your loud voice! They should be! So, what do you think we should do? We could go out for lunch… but I was thinking maybe something a little different this year. Forest School! Can we go to Forest School, Mummy? Please? We can build a den for you! Yeah! And collect pretty leaves! Forest School… That’s actually a brilliant idea! Being outside, getting muddy, building something… it's definitely more 'you' than a stuffy restaurant. But it's a bit unpredictable weather-wise, isn’t it? We don't mind a bit of rain! We’re like ducks! You are like ducks! Right, I’ll check the forecast. But let's say, presuming the weather behaves, Forest School it is. Now, we need to think about what  else  to do for you both. I’m utterly stumped. I'm drawing a blank, really. It's harder than it looks, isn't it? I feel like I’m pulling my hair out trying to think of something special. Tell us a joke! You always tell good jokes! Alright, you’ve twisted my arm. Here's one... Why don't scientists trust atoms? Why? Because they make up everything! That's silly! Silly! Glad you liked it! Okay, jokes aside, I was reading about idioms the other day, and it made me think… We say so many funny things, don’t we? Like, "break a leg" - which is utterly ridiculous! You’re  not  actually wishing someone to injure themselves! Why do people say that, Mummy? Well, nobody's  entirely  sure. But it's thought to come from Shakespeare's time, where a good performance would mean the actors had to “break” the line of the stage with their dancing.

Honestly, Sarah, I don’t know how Mum’s coping. Every phone call is… draining. It’s just a litany of aches and pains, tiredness, and then that look in her voice. You know the one. The one that says, "I'm trying to be brave, but I'm really, really scared." I know exactly the one. It’s heartbreaking, isn’t it? It’s different when it’s a distant relative, or someone you barely know. But Mum… she's  Mum . Seeing her like this, knowing what she's going through… it’s just…unfair. The chemo's clearly taking its toll. Did she mention anything about the new scan results? Not explicitly. She just said, "The doctor wants to see me next week. Something about 'further options'." Further options. That’s code for ‘things aren’t looking good’, isn’t it? I tried to press her, but she just brushed it off, said, "Don't you worry your head, love. I'm being positive." Positive my foot! She’s trying to protect us, as always. It’s a Midlands thing, innit? Always downplaying everything. Absolutely. Burying it all deep down. Remember Dad and that dodgy heart? He practically ignored it for months until he ended up in A&E. I rang him because he’d stopped taking his medication, and he just said, “Oh, I'm fine, just a bit breathless.” It's exhausting, trying to get them to be honest. I told her last week to keep a detailed diary of everything - symptoms, pain levels, what the meds are doing... anything. It'll be helpful for the doctors, and for us to understand what’s going on. I tried suggesting that too! She just said, “Diary? I’m not writing a diary, love! I’ve got more important things to do.” Like watching Bargain Hunt, probably. Look, I feel terrible even saying this, but sometimes I wonder if… if she’s actually internalising it more than she lets on. It’s the quiet moments, you know? When she’s not trying to be strong, you catch a glimpse of… something else. I think you're right. It's not about  not  being strong, is it? It’s about being  too  strong, to the point of denial. Have you spoken to your brother about it? Briefly. He’s… well, he’s David. Head in the sand, pretending everything is normal.

Right, that’s the last of the grammar exercises marked. My brain feels like scrambled eggs. Fancy a coffee? I was thinking of popping to the Sainsbury's later, need some decent coffee beans. Their own brand are surprisingly not bad. Please, yes, coffee sounds divine. I've been wrestling with this Chomsky chapter for ages. It's properly frying my brain. Sainsbury's is good. Are you thinking of getting those cherry tomatoes too? I'm craving a decent salad for lunch. Definitely tomatoes. And some avocado if they’ve got any that aren't rock hard. Speaking of lunch, we really need to plan something slightly more sophisticated than beans on toast every day. My culinary skills are…limited, to say the least. You managed a perfectly acceptable veggie stir-fry last week! We could try that again. Or, I was thinking, since you're looking at South Korean grammar with your students…maybe we could actually  make  some Korean food? Bibimbap is surprisingly easy, I think. Korean food, eh? Tempting. Though I’m slightly terrified of messing up the gochujang ratio and setting off the smoke alarm. My Korean students are fascinated by British food, though. They're always asking about roast dinners and… haggis. Haggis. Right. That's a conversation for another day. Seriously though, Korean food would be fun. I read an article about Chuseok - it's like their version of Thanksgiving, all about harvest and family. They make these rice cakes, songpyeon, shaped like the moon. That sounds lovely. Actually, that links nicely to one of my lectures next week - comparing autumnal harvest festivals across different cultures. China’s Mid-Autumn Festival, Korean Chuseok… It’s fascinating how motifs and symbolism repeat across continents. It is, isn't it? Though, from what I understand, the gender dynamics in South Korea can be a bit…dated. My friend who studied abroad there said the pressure on women to marry young is intense. Yeah, I’ve picked up on that too. It’s a complex societal structure. Similar issues, albeit to a different degree, can be found in some parts of China as well. I read some interesting research on the impact of the one-child policy on gender ratios and social expectations. Speaking of research, have you thought any more about whether to look into sociolinguistics for your dissertation? I'm leaning towards it. The way dialect influences online communication is fascinating.

Ugh, this is exactly what I needed after that disastrous physics tutorial. Honestly, Professor Davies just…lectured at us for an hour about momentum without actually explaining how to  do  any calculations. Sounds about right for Davies. He's a legend, but not in a good way, is he? Still, pizza’s brilliant. Pepperoni’s always the best choice. Did you get the one with the extra cheese, Liv? Yeah, piled high. I deserve it. How was your maths revision, Phoebe? Did you manage to crack that integral? Nearly! I think I’m getting it now, though. It’s a right pain in the backside, that one. I’m absolutely starving. Anyone want another slice? I’m reclaiming this one. Go for it, Chloe! I'm fine. Although, I’m still horrifyingly behind on my module assessment stuff. I swear, I’m going to be living in the library for the next two weeks. Did you guys see anything about the flooding downtown? It's looking pretty grim online. I did! Poor Sarah’s flat’s practically on the riverbank. Fingers crossed it doesn't get too bad. Remember when we tried camping last year and it rained the entire time? Don't remind me! More like ‘surviving’ than camping. It was like the Jurassic period! We were covered in mud and biting insects. I still find the occasional leaf sticking to my waterproofs. Thinking about escaping the weather makes me want to book that trip to Africa. Remember we talked about going to Tanzania? Oh my god, yeah! Safaris and stunning landscapes. That’d be amazing. Though, knowing us, we’d probably get lost and eaten by a lion. Let’s aim for slightly less dangerous travel then, eh? Seriously though, I need a distraction. Anyone fancy a game? We could play Articulate? Or Heads Up? Heads Up sounds good! Although, I'm bringing my A-game tonight. Remember last time when I could barely guess "Edward Cullen" in Twilight? I’ve been practicing. You looked like you’d never seen a sparkly vampire in your life! Oh, speaking of terrible pop culture… did anyone catch Jack Whitehall's new stand-up? Absolutely hilarious. Loved it! Especially the bit about trying to do yoga. I’m the same – a complete disaster. Anyone seen  The Big Fat Quiz  yet? They always have a question about Cloud Atlas, and I never know the answer.

Honestly, Liam, you wouldn’t  believe  the day I’ve had. It’s been pure chaos at the corpus. Absolute mayhem. Mayhem? Sounds interesting. More interesting than bridge supports, anyway. Tell me everything. And try to avoid too much jargon, alright? Last time you explained the tagging system, my eyes glazed over within five minutes. Oh, I’m a terrible explainer, am I? Well, it’s not exactly gripping stuff, is it? But right, well. We had a massive data migration scheduled for this morning, see? Supposed to be straightforward. Standard practice. Turns out, someone - and I’m not naming names, but it  might  have been young Mark from the transcription team – hadn’t backed up the metadata. No backup? Seriously? That’s… that’s horrifying! What happened then? Horrifying is putting it mildly. The whole system nearly crashed. We lost a significant chunk of annotations, and I spent three hours frantically trying to recover anything we could. Three hours! I missed my lunch break. I practically lived in the server room. It were like something out of a disaster movie, pet. Wow. That sounds awful. You must be exhausted. I'm really impressed you managed to salvage anything at all. You're a lifesaver, honestly. So, Mark... Is he going to be getting a right telling-off? Aye, he is. The Head of Department had a proper go at him. He looked like a kicked puppy. To be fair, he’s only been there a few weeks, and he clearly didn’t know what he was doing. But still! Metadata, Liam! It’s the foundation of everything! It’s like… like building a house on sand. A very apt analogy. You're very good at those, you know. It reminds me of that time my uncle… Oh, never mind. Completely different scale of disaster. So, after the great metadata meltdown, did you manage to celebrate surviving? Celebrate? I went home, ordered a massive pizza, and collapsed in front of the telly. Don’t judge me. It were a long day. I'm still buzzing from the stress, to be honest. I kept expecting the phone to ring and for it all to come crashing down again. You deserve a massive pizza and a good long rest. Clearly. I'm glad you got through it. You're incredibly resilient, you know that? Speaking of which, I actually had a pretty interesting day myself, though nothing nearly as dramatic as a data apocalypse.

Cor blimey, this drizzle ain’t letting up, is it? Been like this for a week solid. Damp gets right into yer bones, it does. Makes me rheumatiz act up somethin' awful. Oh, Arthur, don’t go on about your bones. You’ll attract more rain! It's just a bit of a shower, really. Though I do agree, it’s been persistently gloomy. At least it’s not snow. Remember that winter of '78? Couldn’t get out for a week! Honestly, Mum, it’s a standard English autumn. Bit grey, a bit soggy. Nothing to complain about too much. Dad, how’s the knee today? Did the physio exercises help at all? Aye, the exercises. Feel a bit like a rusty hinge, I do. That physio lad, bless 'im, he keeps tellin' me to "engage my core." What's that even  mean ? Me core’s been mostly relaxin' for seventy-odd years, I reckon! Bit late to be engagin' it now, innit? Engage your core, Dad? Sounds horribly clinical. They call it that to confuse you, I think. It just means tighten your stomach muscles. Like when you’re about to lift something heavy. Lifting? The heaviest thing I lift these days is the telly remote. And that gives me a twinge! Speaking o' telly, did you lot see that Norwich game on Saturday? Dreadful! Absolutely dreadful. Should've stayed in bed, I tell ya. Arthur, please. Not football. Let’s talk about something pleasant. Did you manage to get that new smart speaker sorted, dear? Emily said it was a struggle setting it up. That blasted thing… a struggle? It's a conspiracy, I tell you! A right faff. Emily spent hours pokin' and proddin' at it. Tried to get it to play Vera Lynn, it did! Played some racketin’ pop song no one’s ever 'eard of. Dad, you can't expect it to just  know  Vera Lynn! You have to tell it. "Alexa, play Vera Lynn." Simple. Alexa? Sounds like a fancy waitress. Just give me a wireless and a decent tune, that’s all I need. All this technology… it's goin' to yer 'ead, it is. Give me a good paperback any day. Less likely to explode, y'know. It’s not likely to explode, Dad, honestly. It’s just a speaker. You can ask it to tell you the weather, play news... it can even order you shopping.

Honestly, this wedding planning is eating my soul. Invitations, seating charts, caterers...it’s endless! I feel like I’m running a small business, not organizing a celebration of love. Oh relax, Chloe! It's supposed to be stressful, isn't it? But think of the payoff – seeing everyone you love in one place, celebrating with you. Are you having fun, despite the chaos? Fun? Chloe looks like she’s aged five years in the last month. More like organised torment! Speaking of torment, are we actually going to talk about anything besides Chloe’s impending nuptials, or are we doomed to a never-ending slideshow of floral arrangements? Don't be mean, Liv! It  is  a big day. And Chloe, have you sorted the music yet? Remember what happened at Aunt Carol’s wedding with that dodgy DJ?  Never  let a dodgy DJ near a microphone. Oh god, don’t remind me. I’m having a playlist, thank you very much. And yes, I’m still debating between a string quartet or a jazz band for the ceremony. It’s crucial! What about you two? Any exciting developments in the world of Mac Artworking and Sales Management? Things are pretty hectic at work, actually. We're launching a new product line and I'm basically living on coffee and spreadsheets. But it's good, challenging. And… I might have a  slightly  interesting dating update. Ooh, spill! Don’t leave us hanging, Sarah! Is it the charming architect from the gallery opening? Nope, surprise! It's Liam. Remember Liam from uni? The one who always wore those awful Hawaiian shirts? Liam?  That  Liam? Seriously? He always tried to sell me overpriced comic books and claimed to be an expert on obscure 80s movies. I know, right? I’d completely forgotten about him. But he tracked me down on LinkedIn, sent me a really thoughtful message, and we've been chatting. Turns out he's a vet now and actually quite…nice. We went for dinner last week. A vet? Wow, that’s a glow-up! So, is there a second dinner on the horizon? Don't get swept away too much though, remember what happened with Ben! I know, I know! Lesson learned. But he’s genuinely lovely, Chloe. It’s refreshing to talk to someone who isn’t obsessed with climbing the career ladder. Speaking of career ladders, I’m thinking of taking a short course in graphic design focused on animation.

Blimey, this Earl Grey’s a bit strong, isn’t it, Brenda? Mind you, it's better than nothin'. Rain's lashin' down again, like clockwork. Used to be able to predict it, you know. Felt it in me bones, I did. It is a bit strong, Arthur. I'll add a bit more milk. Norfolk weather, eh? Always something unpredictable. Though I do miss the proper sunshine. It’s been dreary for weeks. Did you see little Leo tried to video call his grandma? Nearly had a meltdown when the screen wouldn't cooperate. Kids and technology, aren't they a marvel? I spend half my time at school explaining how to turn a tablet on and the other half stopping them from watching cat videos during a lesson on Shakespeare. Though, you have to admit, YouTube can be a good resource. Used it loads when prepping for the new curriculum. Shakespeare? Never been much of a poet man, me. Give me a bit of Dick Francis any day. Horses, now  that's  somethin’ I understand. Remember old Bess, down at Farmer Giles’ place? A beauty she was. Could practically read her mind, I could. Used to help out muckin' stalls, I did. Good honest work. Oh, horses! My niece, Chloe, is mad about them. She’s saving up for riding lessons, bless her. It's quite expensive, though. It makes you realize how prices have gone up, doesn’t it? Everything's a struggle these days. Absolutely. It's worrying. I’m in a slightly better position, being a teacher, but even with a mortgage and everything, it’s a tight squeeze. Especially with the energy bills. My son's just bought a flat, and he’s terrified of what the next bill will be. Keeps saying he's eating beans on toast every night. Beans on toast! Used to be a luxury, that was! Back in the day, you'd be lucky to get a bit of bacon with it. Things were tough, alright. But there was a… a sense of community, you know? Everyone helped each other out. Not like it is now. Everyone's lookin' inwards. I agree, Arthur. When I used to look after the children, we’d have little gatherings, potlucks, and games in the garden. Simple pleasures. Now, it's all screens and online this and online that. Makes you yearn for a simpler time.

Oh, this is lovely, Arthur. Thank you so much for popping by. It’s been ages! Birmingham’s been good to me, you know, the teaching’s going well. Much less chaotic than London used to be. Birmingham, eh? Always seemed a bit… industrial to me. Though I've not spent much time up North. London was always the place to be, back in my day. Though, truth be told, I’m glad to be back in Essex now. Peace and quiet really does suit a chap in his… well, let’s just say a more seasoned age. Absolutely. Peace is priceless. So, what have you been up to? Still enjoying your gardening, I hope? Last time we spoke you were battling slugs with a vengeance. Ah, the slugs. They're a constant war, you know. Never truly won. But the roses are blooming beautifully this year, I must say. Got a particularly fine 'Gertrude Jekyll' at the moment. Reminds me of your Aunt Margaret, actually. She adored those roses. How's Margaret doing, by the way? Still volunteering at the church fete? She is! Still as energetic as ever. She’s already planning the raffle for this year’s fete – it's a huge event. She sends her love, by the way. Said she misses our chats. I'm teaching mostly French at the moment, a few Spanish classes sprinkled in. It’s fascinating seeing how quickly some people pick it up. One of the cleverest chaps I have, he's 17 and speaks three languages already! Absolutely astounding. Do you remember learning French at school? Dreadful, wasn't it? Dreadful is putting it mildly. Mr. Grimshaw – proper stickler, he was. All grammar drills and conjugations. Never got to actually  speak  the language, did we? It put me right off foreign languages. I always thought it was a bit… frivolous. Managing a company, you see, you needed concrete skills, not the ability to order a croissant in Paris. I can see that. But it's more than just ordering croissants, Arthur. It's understanding different cultures, communicating with people who see the world differently. That's what I find so rewarding. Actually, I’m planning a short trip to France next spring, with a group of my students. A little immersion experience. Maybe I'll see you before then? France, you say? Fancy that. Never been abroad, you know. Never had the inclination.

Honestly, Leah, Valentine's Day. What even  is  the point? Like, a manufactured holiday designed to make single people feel inadequate. It's mental, innit? Alright, alright, calm down, Chloe! Don't start your anti-romance crusade. It's just a bit of fun, yeah? Besides, it was Friday, we had a decent night. Remember that dodgy karaoke upstairs? Dodgy is an understatement. You absolutely butchered Whitney Houston. I’m still having flashbacks. But yeah, the karaoke was a laugh. It just…everyone’s going on about roses and fancy dinners and declarations of eternal love. Meanwhile, I’m here, contemplating the merits of microwave noodles. You always were a romantic cynic. I had a nice enough time, though. Liam took me to that Italian, Bella Notte? Remember, we said we'd try it? Oh yeah, the one you were raving about for ages. Was it as good as you said? I'm starving, by the way. This tea ain’t cutting it. Seriously contemplating a trip to the Spar for a packet of cheesy chips. It was brilliant! Proper authentic. The pasta was handmade, the tiramisu...oh, Chloe, the tiramisu. You need to go. Like, yesterday. Proper lush. You should treat yourself. Forget the cheesy chips, you deserve a decent meal. Lush? You’re proper Midlands, aren't you? Everything’s lush with you. I’d have said “delicious” or “amazing.” Sounds expensive, though. My student loan's weeping at the mere thought. It’s not  that  bad. And look, Liam offered to pay! He's embarrassing, always wanting to treat me. He kept saying things like “My Queen” and “My Princess.” I nearly choked on my spaghetti. Oh, bless him. He’s trying, isn’t he? Sounds like a proper sweetheart. You’re lucky, you know. Having someone who fusses over you like that. I know, I know. It's just...sometimes it's a bit much. He’s constantly sending me little heart emojis. It's cute initially, but after the fifth message in an hour… I have to pretend I'm busy. What about you? Any Valentine’s shenanigans? Anyone brave enough to send  you  a heart emoji? Absolutely not. I spent the evening watching  Parasite  for the third time. Clearly, I am destined to be a lonely film buff. Seriously though, it was brilliant. Have you seen it? Yeah! Brilliant is the word. The twist was incredible.

Honestly, Priya, this is exactly what I needed. Spicy, comforting, and a temporary escape from… everything. Did you see that article about the new developments in Canary Wharf? Another luxury tower block. It's just… relentless. Yeah, I saw it. They’re calling it “The Pinnacle of Living.” Pinnacle of  who’s  living, exactly? People who can afford a mortgage that costs more than my entire year’s income? It’s obscene. And the thing is, they’re touting it as “revitalising the area,” pushing out all the smaller businesses that actually  give  Canary Wharf character. Precisely! It’s all performative revitalization. And the rhetoric around it… “Creating jobs!” Like those jobs will magically trickle down to the people who are being priced out of London. It just feels so deeply… cynical. Cynical is putting it mildly. It’s just the bleeding obvious manifestation of capitalism, isn’t it? Concentrating wealth at the top and squeezing everyone else out. I was talking to a source yesterday, about the rise in racist hate crime coinciding with these economic anxieties. Apparently, there's a definite link. People are feeling desperate, they're looking for someone to blame... and unfortunately, it’s often minorities and immigrants who end up taking the brunt of that anger. That’s… devastating. It’s not surprising, obviously, but hearing it confirmed that way… It’s just so sad. My parents kept saying, when I was growing up, that racism was getting better, that things were changing. But it never really has, has it? It just morphs and hides. It does. And it weaponizes existing inequalities. The housing crisis, for example – it disproportionately affects Black and Brown communities. Look at the areas where affordable housing is actually  available  - often outside of London, hours away from job opportunities and support networks. It creates a two-tiered system. And my office is full of it. Remember Mark from the planning department? The comments he made last month about that social housing project in Hackney? Barely veiled coded language… it’s exhausting having to navigate that kind of microaggression constantly. It makes you question whether you even  want  to do this job sometimes. I mean, I love architecture, but… Don’t let him win. You’re brilliant, and your work genuinely matters. Just… document it. Keep a record of these instances. It’s a pain, but it’s useful leverage. And remember why you’re doing it.

Honestly, love, I’m a bit of a nervous wreck about little Leo starting nursery next week. It feels… momentous, doesn't it? Like a real chunk of my life is changing. I keep picturing him all alone, you know? Surrounded by strangers. I know, Mum. It’s a big thing. But he'll be fine. He’s a little social butterfly, remember? He loves playing with other kids at the park. It’s just a bigger group, really. And you've picked a good nursery, haven’t you? Little Wonders? Everyone says they're brilliant. They  seem  brilliant. The lady, Mrs. Davies, is lovely. But it’s still… I’m going back to work full-time, isn’t it? Properly back. It’s been just part-time for so long, juggling things. I’m dreading the commute, to be honest. This Sutton Coldfield traffic is appalling. Well, you’ll get used to it. And you said that new job is really interesting, right? The project management stuff? It’ll be good for you, Mum. A bit of a change. Besides, a little peace and quiet might do you good! Remember how stressed you were always feeling? Peace and quiet. Don’t remind me! Though, you're right. It  is  a good opportunity. Money’s been a little tight lately, hasn’t it? Speaking of which… have you looked at holidays yet? I was thinking, if we can get ourselves sorted, maybe Spain next summer? Somewhere with a proper beach, that Leo can paddle in. Spain sounds amazing! I’ve been looking a bit, actually. There are some really affordable apartments in Costa Brava. We could get a little villa with a pool... think of it, Mum – sun, sangria, and no Leo throwing mashed sweet potato everywhere! Oh, don’t even tempt me! Speaking of mashed sweet potato… weaning is a nightmare, isn't it? He spat out broccoli  again  last night. Like I’d ever eat broccoli! Honestly, Mum. It's the worst. I remember weaning Finn. He used to smear everything across his face and the highchair. It was like a Jackson Pollock painting, but with pureed carrots. Have you tried those baby-led weaning recipes? Apparently, giving them finger foods is less messy. I’ve looked at them. Seems a bit risky, though, doesn't it? Choking hazards everywhere. I’m sticking with the spoon-feeding, I think.

Right, so, the police were… thorough, weren't they? Honestly, I felt a bit like I was back in court. They wanted every single detail about what I saw that night. Aye, they do. Gotta cover all bases. Important you got everything down, love. Don't want any gaps they can trip you up on later. Did you mention the van? The colour? Yes, definitely. Bright red, quite distinctive. And the partial registration – I relayed that. I'm just… troubled by it all, you know? Seeing that happen, so close to home. It’s unsettling. Did they take a formal statement, Auntie Anon? Like, signed and everything? Yes, they did, Maisie. Signed, witnessed, and initialled. The whole shebang. They said they might need to contact me again, though. That’s standard, Auntie. Don’t worry about it. They're just building a case. You did the right thing going to them. Absolutely. You did good, lass. Proud of you for stepping up. Now, about this phone bill… EE are robbing me blind! Nearly £150 this month! They said it was the data usage. Honestly, I barely use data! Dad, you’ve been streaming boxing matches all week. Don't play innocent. I resent that! I'm appreciating a sport! It's culturally enriching! And besides, 150 quid? It's scandalous! I’m going to complain to Ofcom. Honestly, Barry, you’ll drive yourself mad. Threaten to leave. That always gets a better deal. You should have done it ages ago. I’ve had similar issues with them, Dad. Switched to Virgin. Much better value and faster broadband. You should seriously consider it. I'm with Virgin too! It’s brilliant. Plus, their customer service is actually decent. Virgin, eh? Hmmm. I’ll have a look. But I'm still complaining to Ofcom first! Gotta make a stand against corporate greed! Of course you are. So, plans for the week? Maisie, are you still on for that pottery class on Thursday? Yep! Really looking forward to it. I’m thinking of trying to make a little planter for Mum’s herbs. I'm free Thursday evening. Could give you a lift, Maisie. Don't want you battling the buses. That’d be amazing, Jamie, thanks! I’m going to that classic car show at Stone on Saturday. You lot want to come? They've got a Restomod display this year, apparently... loads of old Minis and Mustangs, all spruced up.

Right then, so you’ve actually done it! Married! Didn’t think you’d ever settle down, Liam. Feels weird seeing you back in Bedford, actually. Last time I saw you, you were already halfway to Cyprus, promising me stories of olive groves and sunshine. Aye, well, life's thrown a few curveballs, hasn't it? It’s good to be back, though. Needed a proper cuppa and a chat with a familiar face. You still obsessed with Roman history? Last time we were dissecting Spartacus, you were convinced he’d have won the Third Servile War if he’d only had a decent siege engineer. Absolutely! The man was a brilliant tactician, hampered by... logistics. And the brutality of the Romans, of course. Speaking of brutality, have you seen “Domina” on Netflix? It's a bit… graphic, but the attention to detail with the gladiatorial aspects is remarkable. Of course, it takes  massive  creative liberties. Real history’s much more fascinating, don't you think? I did catch a glimpse of it. A bit much for me, truth be told. I prefer something a bit less… visceral. I've been listening to a lot of Nick Cave lately, actually. His darker stuff, you know? Fits the mood sometimes, when you're out weeding and thinking about all the empires that have crumbled to dust. Nick Cave! Good choice. Speaking of things that crumble, you wouldn’t believe the state of the mortar on Mrs. Henderson’s garden wall. It’s practically falling apart. I was thinking about getting a proper mortar and pestle, grind my own lime – a bit of a DIY project, you know? Imagine compounding your own render! You’re going full medieval artisan now, are you? Sounds like something you’d find in China, all those ancient building techniques. Mind you, building materials can be pretty brutal on the body – I’ve come across some nasty sea lice out in Cyprus, clinging to nets and causing havoc. Didn't even know those existed! Sea lice! That’s horrific. Makes malarial precautions seem almost quaint. So, Cyprus… tell me everything! What’s the food like? Are you still foraging for wild herbs? I'm trying to get more adventurous with my cooking, beyond the usual pasta and beans. Found some amazing smoked paprika though, really elevates a chickpea stew. The food's incredible. So fresh. Loads of herbs, obviously – oregano, thyme, rosemary, growing wild everywhere.

Honestly, this English test felt like a personal attack. Like, Mrs. Davies  knew  I was having a rough week and still threw that Shakespeare passage at me. Tell me about it! I spent ages trying to decipher what Hamlet was even  saying . It was all "to be or not to be" and then suddenly there were ghosts. My brain just shut down. Did you at least manage to write something vaguely coherent? Vaguely. I think? I wrote about how being indecisive can be a good thing, because you get to weigh up all the options? I'm not sure if that's actually what Shakespeare wanted, but it's what came out. What did you say? I rambled about the pressure of making big decisions. I kept going off on a tangent about choosing which ice cream flavour to get. I think Mrs. Davies will mark me down for that. She hates tangents. She  does ! Right, well, at least we're both suffering. Speaking of suffering, Art lessons are turning into a production of ‘paint splatters and existential dread’. Mr. Peterson keeps telling us to 'express ourselves’ but all I’m expressing is frustration. True! I tried to paint a sunflower. It looked like a mutant broccoli. I think I'm going to stick to sketching for a bit. Are you still doing that portrait of your nan? Yeah, slowly. It's actually going quite well, surprisingly. Nan’s being very patient with me. Although she keeps suggesting I add more "glimmer." She’s obsessed with glitter. Of course she is! My grandma’s the same. Everything needs a bit of sparkle. Right, changing the subject completely – are you going to the wind band rehearsal on Tuesday? Yep! I’m actually looking forward to it, surprisingly. We're finally getting to work on that new piece by Holst. It's really quite beautiful, even if playing the clarinet for two hours does make my fingers ache. Oh, I know! I'm so excited about the Holst piece too. The oboe part is gorgeous. I've been practicing it constantly. I heard Mr. Evans might be letting us try out some of the solo bits. Seriously? That's amazing! You’d smash it. Are you still finding French lessons a total nightmare then? Don’t even get me started! Madame Dubois is determined to torture us with verb conjugations. I can't remember whether something needs an ‘er’ or an ‘es’ or an ‘e’!

Och, look at that rain, love. Proper miserable it is this afternoon. Reminds me of a November day back in '88, freezing fog, couldn't see your hand in front of your face. Remember that, Maureen? Aye, Margaret, I do! Though I think '89 was worse. We were queuing for the bus, trying to get to the market, and the frost was so thick you could practically chew it. Me feet were numb for hours after that. Nowadays, folks complain if it’s a bit chilly. Soft, they are. Soft is right! This lot wouldn’t last five minutes in our childhoods, that’s for sure. Speaking of childhoods, how’s young Liam doing? Still glued to that PlayStation, is he? Nah, not  all  the time. I’m doing a project at school, Mrs. Davies set it – it’s about regional accents. Accents, is it? Well, that's a grand topic for a lad from Newcastle! You’ll be right at home then, pet. Do you know a lot about it? Yeah, a bit. We’ve been listening to recordings, and looking at how dialect changes across the North. Apparently, it's got links to Viking settlements. Fancy that, eh? Vikings! Always the Vikings, aren't they? Though there’s truth in it, mind. You can hear it in some of the older words, especially around the coast. I remember me mam used to say “gan yem,” for “go eat.” Don't hear that much these days. Aye, “gan yem” – lovely. My grandma used to say it. It’s all fading away, isn't it? All these youngsters speaking like they’re in London. It’s a pity, a real pity. How much is your project worth, Liam? It's worth 20% of my English grade. I’m thinking of doing my presentation on the differences between Geordie and Yorkshire accents. It’ll be interesting 'cos loads of me mates are from over the border. Gets right heated sometimes, doesn't it? Oh, does it ever! A Geordie and a Yorkshireman arguing? That's like watching a volcano erupt. Always good for a laugh, though. Have you considered looking at the influence of mining communities on the language, Liam? That’s deep-rooted. Maureen’s right, love. The mines shaped the way people spoke. My dad worked down at Dean and Cover. Didn’t talk much about the work, mind, but you could hear it in the way he used words.

Right, so Dad, you were saying about the new exhaust on Brenda’s Fiesta? It sounded…extensive. Extensive is the word, love. Blimey. The whole system needed replacing. Rusted through, practically. Little tin can was rattling like a box of loose bolts. Cost a pretty penny, I’ll tell you that. Though, I managed to get a good deal on the parts. Always do. Well, at least you’re keeping her going. Brenda relies on that car. Remember when she tried taking the bus to Ipswich? Dreadful journey. I remember. She came back looking like she'd wrestled a badger. Speaking of journeys… did you see that report on the news? About childhood obesity rates in Norfolk? Apparently, they’re higher than the national average. Yes, it’s truly alarming, isn't it? I was just reading an article about the genetic predisposition to weight gain. Apparently, it’s far more complicated than just “eat less, move more.” Genes, eh? Always an excuse, innit? My mother used to say, "A little bit of lard never hurt anyone." But she was a baker, so you’d expect her to say that. Your mother had a sweet tooth the size of a football, Arthur! And everything was buttery. I remember. Still, she was a good woman. Used to make the best apple crumble… It’s not about excuses, Eleanor. It’s about understanding the biological factors at play. There are definite genetic markers that can increase your susceptibility. Then you factor in environment, access to healthy food, and even socioeconomic factors... it's a complex web. Exactly. And it’s not just about genetics either. It's about the marketing of processed foods, the lack of affordable healthy options, the decline of PE in schools… It’s a system problem. All sounds a bit doom and gloom to me. People need to take responsibility. Back in my day, we ran around all day, scraping our knees and eating proper meals. Didn’t have time for all this worrying about genetics. Honestly, Arthur, you’re sounding like a Victorian schoolmaster! Things have changed. They’re different now. Speaking of different, did you hear about Mrs. Henderson down the road? She had that surgery for her allergies - the desensitisation one? Apparently, it was a success. She’s not sneezing constantly anymore. Oh, that’s fantastic news! I wasn’t sure how that would work. Those allergies were really impacting her quality of life.

Honestly, Moodle is trying to actively sabotage me today. I spent a good hour trying to upload these lecture slides for the intro to coding course, and it just... refused. Kept giving me some obscure error message. “Resource too large”, it said. The slides are  perfectly  within the size limit! Moodle, eh? The bane of every lecturer's existence. Resource too large is usually a red herring, isn’t it? Often it’s something else entirely. Did you try zipping the files? That usually works a treat. Yes! Of course I tried zipping them! I’m not entirely clueless, darling. I tried various zip methods, different file formats... I even tried uploading them individually, which is utterly ridiculous when they're clearly a coherent unit. I feel like I'm battling a particularly obtuse robot. Alright, alright, no need to get existential with the robot. It’s just Moodle being Moodle. What specifically were you uploading? Was it videos embedded in the slides? That can sometimes cause issues even if the zip is small. No videos, thankfully. Just a lot of images and code snippets. I’m trying to make them visually engaging, you know? It’s hard to get students interested in Python without a bit of colour and, dare I say, personality. The department head keeps going on about ‘active learning’ and ‘student engagement’… it’s all well and good, but presenting walls of text isn’t exactly captivating. True, true. I completely get it. Visuals are key. I’ve found that incorporating little animated GIFs helps too - keeps them awake at least! Did you try clearing your browser cache? Sometimes that can interfere with uploads. A long shot, I know, but worth a try. I cleared the cache, I tried a different browser… I even restarted the computer! I'm starting to feel slightly unhinged. You wouldn't believe the students' emails I got last night about the online quiz. Apparently, some of them couldn't access it. I’m going to have to email them all again in the morning and apologize. That’s rough. Moodle's responsiveness can be so unpredictable. Especially on Friday afternoons. It's probably running on a single overworked server somewhere. Listen, let me have a quick look. Maybe a fresh pair of eyes will spot something obvious. Pass me the laptop. Be gentle with it, please. I'm already teetering on the edge of despair.

Ugh, I feel like I’ve been rolled through a tumble dryer. This jetlag is  brutal . Did you manage to sleep at all? A bit, yeah. Fitful. The little ones weren’t exactly conducive to a deep, restorative slumber, were they? Leo decided 3 am was the perfect time to practice his roar. Oh, bless him. Matilda was demanding cuddles. I swear, they’ve plotted this exhaustion together. Right, let’s tackle this weekend. I was thinking, we should definitely go see “A Midsummer Night's Dream” at the Wyvern. The reviews are superb. At the Wyvern, yes! Lovely choice. I read something about their set design being particularly inventive this year. It’s a bit pricey, isn't it though? A little bit. But it’s been ages since we’ve just, you know,  done  something. Without small humans attached. We deserve a treat. I’ve already had a look at the times – Saturday evening seems best, 7:30 curtain up? Saturday sounds good. Logistically, though… are we managing childcare? Nanny’s available, right? I called Sarah this morning. She’s free both Saturday and Sunday. I mentioned the theatre, and she said she’d happily do Saturday. She even suggested staying over that night, which would be amazing. We could actually have a proper, uninterrupted dinner. A proper dinner? That  is  something to look forward to. Consider it a major victory. So, Sarah Saturday, confirm tickets, and… then what? Sunday seems rather daunting after a night out. Well, I was thinking a gentle walk in the park on Sunday morning. Let the kids burn off some energy, and we can grab a coffee afterwards. Something low-key. Unless you're feeling ambitious? We could try that new brunch place on the high street. "The Lemon Tree," I think it's called. "The Lemon Tree"... sounds pleasant. But honestly, a gentle walk sounds  extremely  appealing. My brain feels like scrambled eggs at the moment. Did you manage to unpack at all? My suitcase is still... well, it's a monument to chaos on the bedroom floor. Don’t remind me. I threw a load of washing on, but the actual unpacking… it’s on the to-do list somewhere after "restore sanity" and "learn to sleep again." So, tickets? Do you want to book them now? I could do it on my phone. Yes, please do! Let’s get that sorted.

Right then, Omar, tell me more about your niece. You were saying she’s trying to get out, yeah? To…Canada, I think? Yes, Layla. She's… ambitious. And, frankly, a bit worried. Not just about the situation in Kurdistan, which is volatile as ever, but about the wider region. The instability...it’s creeping everywhere. She’s got a good degree, you know. Economics. Useful stuff these days. Her parents are pushing her, of course. My sister, especially. She sees Canada as a fresh start, a safe haven. But the visa process… it’s a nightmare. Tell me about it. I had a student from Eritrea applying last year. Three months, just for a visitor’s visa! Absolutely baffling. They dangle the possibility of education, encourage these young people to pursue it, then make it almost impossible to actually access it. It’s a cynical game, isn’t it? Cynical is… understated. It’s cruel. And it feeds hopelessness. Layla's concerned about the paperwork, the interviews...the whole charade of proving you’re not going to disappear and leech off the system. Which, frankly, after everything my family has put up with... it feels insulting. Absolutely. I understand that frustration. You know, my cousin, Hans-Dieter, he’s still in Germany. He's a civil servant, deals with immigrant applications. He says the level of bureaucracy is astounding, even for Germany. All these hoops to jump through… It's designed to discourage, I think. Designed to discourage... that's a good way of putting it. And it's not just about Canada. People are looking at Australia, New Zealand... anywhere that offers some semblance of stability. You wouldn't believe the price of flights these days. Everyone’s scrambling. It reminds me, actually, of… well, my grandfather, after the Ba'athist repression. He spent years trying to get a visa to Sweden. It took him seventeen years! Seventeen years! Wow. That’s… That’s dedication. Makes the Eritrean student’s visa seem relatively straightforward. It’s the displacement, isn’t it? The feeling of rootlessness. Gets under your skin. It’s the same thing I feel, sometimes, being German-British, never quite fitting completely in either place. Exactly. Speaking of displacement, have you heard anything about the situation in Libya? It's a mess, isn't it? All those factions, each with their own agenda... and oil, of course, always oil.

That was absolutely delicious, David. Honestly, the best roast lamb I’ve had in ages. You really outdid yourself. Glad you think so, love. It's a bit of an art, isn’t it? Getting that crispy crust and keeping the inside juicy. Though, ANON did say she was craving it for weeks, so I had to step up my game. Aye, David, you’ve got a good hand with the roasting. Though, I’m still partial to a good haggis, myself. Now  that's  a challenge! Oh, Granny, you’re incorrigible! Speaking of challenges, I’m still battling with this TV situation. It's just so distracting having it in the dining room. Can’t relax properly when dinner's finished and we’re chatting, knowing it’s there, beckoning. I know what you mean. It’s become a bit too much of a focal point. We could move it back into the living room, but then we’d be without a decent-sized screen in there. It’s a proper conundrum. Honestly, putting a television in the dining room... It was a gentleman’s club and a polite conversation back in my day. Now, it’s all screens and instant gratification. Makes me want to call the headmaster – even if that's me! You and your headmasterly pronouncements, Granny. It  is  a bit modern, I suppose. But it's ANON's house, she likes it. Speaking of liking things, has anyone tried that Scottish tablet ANON got? It’s phenomenal. Better than anything I've had before. Tablet! Now you’re talking. It’s a national treasure, that is. I remember my grandmother making it herself, using only the finest butter and sugar. None of this mass-produced nonsense. I had a bit with my coffee. It's seriously addictive. I’m worried I’ll be eating it for breakfast, lunch and dinner. I’m thinking we need to get some holiday booked. Something... relaxing. I was looking at cruises. Caribbean, maybe? All-inclusive, no cooking, just sunshine and cocktails. A cruise! That does sound lovely. I've always wanted to go. Though, I'm not sure I'd be able to relax completely. I'd probably spend the whole time worrying about whether the Wi-Fi is good enough to keep up with my transcription work. Wi-Fi! You young folks are obsessed with it. A cruise should be about disconnecting, seeing new places, enjoying the company.

Right, so, another day, another… nothin’. Proper state of affairs, innit? Mum’s on at me again. Says I need to ‘get a shift on.’ As if it's that easy, lass. Tell me about it. My Mum’s doing the same. At least you’ve got the benefit of having a roof over your head, though. This student loan ain’t exactly covering the cost of living. How’s the room situation going? Still sharing with… well, everybody? Just a bit! We’re a cozy bunch, aren’t we? I’ve made some tea. Strong stuff, needed after a morning trying to decipher German philosophy. Absolutely baffling. At least it's a change from the stench of your yesterday's chips, Liam. Hey! Those were lovely chips. And cozy? Maisie, we're practically stacked in here like sardines. And you haven’t exactly helped by bringing all your German books. Is there a book in there you aren’t reading? Speak of sardines! Smells like a chippy explosion in here. What's everyone up to? Liam, still mastering the art of… nothing? Very funny, Daniel. I’m contemplating the existential dread of unemployment, thank you very much. And trying to avoid Mum's nagging. He's being dramatic. He mostly just watches telly. So, Daniel, how was your day helping little terrors learn their times tables? Pretty hectic, actually. Little Ethan threw a tantrum because he couldn't spell 'Wednesday.' You wouldn't believe the drama. But it’s alright, keeps me busy. It’s better than… well, you know. Speaking of busy, are you even  thinking  about applying anywhere, Liam? Even a temporary Christmas job? I’ve had a look, yeah. Everything’s either no experience needed, or requires experience. Catch-22, that is. I did try for that warehouse job down at the docks, but they said I was “overqualified.” Overqualified to stack boxes? Seriously? That’s ridiculous! You’ve got a degree. You should be doing something with it. Even if it’s not directly related, it shows you’re intelligent and can learn. Intelligence don't pay the bills, Maisie. And don’t start on the degree again. It's gathering dust, that is. It feels like a waste, doesn’t it? It’s not a waste, Liam. It's something to be proud of. Look, maybe we can help you? We could look at job websites, practice interview questions... anything.

Right, so the sugar’s in, butter’s softened… this Victoria Sponge needs to be perfect for Year 3. They’re learning about fractions, you see, and what better way to understand halves and quarters than through cake? Will I get a slice, Mummy? A big one? Of course, sweetheart! But only after the lesson. We need to save some for the class. Remember, you and Ollie are chief taste-testers. You have to tell me if it’s ‘delicious’ enough for the children to visualise fractions! I’m a  very  good taste-tester! I can taste… chocolate! And… sprinkles! You certainly can, my little man. You always find the sprinkles. Ollie, are you listening to Mummy? This cake is important! What are you going to  do  at the lesson, Mummy? Besides giving us cake? Well, I’ll start by showing them the whole cake. Then I’ll cut it in half, explaining that each piece is one half. Then I’ll cut those halves in half again… quarters! We’ll work through different scenarios. "If I eat one quarter, how much is left?" That sort of thing. They love it. It’s much more engaging than just writing numbers on the board. Can you cut it into tiny pieces? Like,  really  tiny? Maybe not  that  tiny, Ollie! Although, thinking about it, a crumbled cake demonstration would be awfully messy. I’ll stick to halves and quarters. Anyway, did you two have fun at your half birthday party yesterday? It was brilliant! Grandma got me a Tomodachi Life game. Oh, lovely! I saw you playing it earlier. It’s utterly ridiculous, isn't it? Those little pixelated characters. I made my Tomodachi get married! To a penguin! A penguin! That’s very creative, darling. Honestly, I’m glad I don’t have to teach  that  sort of maths. Mummy, did you find that book you were looking for in Morrisons? The one about dragons? I did! Yes! They’d just put a new shipment out. It was hidden behind a mountain of travel guides. "Dragons and Their Hoards," it’s called. I thought it would be good to read aloud to the class - a bit of creative writing inspiration. Can  I  read the dragon book? Please? Eventually, Ollie. Once you’ve mastered your fractions, of course. Speaking of books, have you been reading anything interesting lately, either of you? Anything besides Tomodachi Life, that is?

Honestly, Mark, I still don’t understand the obsession with these… these enormous cars. It’s just… unnecessary. You’ve been going on about this new Range Rover for weeks. Unnecessary? Eleanor, it's not just about unnecessary. It’s about… presence. And frankly, navigating Norfolk lanes in a Fiesta isn't ideal when you’re trying to get to your mum’s. Remember last Christmas? Scraping the bottom of every ditch? I remember being slightly embarrassed, yes. But a Range Rover? Really? It's like saying you need a JCB to mow the lawn. And the environmental impact… don’t even get me started. Alright, alright, I concede the point about the environment. It’s not perfect, I know. But they're working on electric ones, you know. And the safety features are incredible. Plus, think about the practicality! We could actually fit all your books in the boot for a weekend away! No more Tetris-ing them in. That  is  tempting, I admit. But still… it feels… ostentatious. I just don’t see the appeal. It's all a bit performative, isn’t it? Like some of the stuff you see on Facebook. People showing off their new cars, their holidays… it’s all so curated. See, I think that's a cynical view. Some people genuinely enjoy sharing their lives. And showing off a Range Rover is hardly the biggest societal ill, is it? It's just… a bit of harmless fun. Though, I do agree Facebook can be a bit of a rabbit hole of manufactured happiness. I was looking at old school photos the other day – everyone looked so unbelievably happy. It’s impossible! Exactly! You’re basically comparing your real life to everyone’s highlight reel. And then you feel inadequate. I've started limiting my time on it. It’s surprisingly liberating. Do you ever feel that pressure? To project some ideal version of yourself online? Occasionally. I think we all do, a little. It’s hard not to. It's ingrained, you know? But I try not to get too caught up in it. Though, I must admit, sharing photos of the dog gets a surprising amount of engagement. People love dogs. Of course they do. Barnaby is universally adored. He's far more photogenic than either of us. Speaking of the internet, have you seen this article about how AI is going to replace all lecturers?

Right, finally. My feet are killing me. That shift at Sports Direct was… a lot. Absolute chaos today. People just grabbing everything, Black Friday levels of madness even though it's a Tuesday. Did you sell loads, then? Did you have to shout at anyone? Loads of protein shakers, surprisingly. And yes, I had to politely tell a bloke that no, he couldn’t return a pair of football boots he’d clearly worn for a five-a-side match. He was having a right go, though. Said it was the shop's fault the studs were falling off. Silly man! Look, it's raining meatballs! Proper giant ones! Yeah, it is. "Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs," right? Remember watching this as a kid. It’s surprisingly clever, actually. You know, the whole consumerism angle. All this food production ending up in the sky… a bit of a commentary on waste, innit? It’s just funny! Sam’s really good at making the food. He looks proper sad when it all goes wrong, though. He does. And Flint… he's the classic impulsive character. Always chasing something, even if it's not the best thing for him or anyone else. It's a bit like… well, having to deal with some of the customers at Sports Direct sometimes! Always wanting the last size ten trainers, even if they clearly don’t fit. Can I have some more juice? I’m hungry. Absolutely. You wolfed down that pizza earlier. Got a bigger appetite than me, you do. Speaking of appetite, I'm starving. Think I'll rustle up some chips when this is done. Can you pass me the remote? I can't reach it. It’s a silly remote. Loads of buttons and I don’t know what half of them do. It’s not like the one at home. Tell me about it! Typical. Always the most complicated remote. Right, let's see... There we go. So, you’re thinking about that art project for your sixth form, yeah? The one about… representation? Yeah. It’s hard, though. Like, everyone says we should have equal representation of women in art, but then what even  is  that? Do we just copy the men? Or do we do something totally different? That's a brilliant question, actually. It's not about just  being  there, is it? It's about  how  you're there, and what message that sends.

Right then, Barry, good to see you. Didn't expect to see a Liverpool cabbie all the way up here in Joensuu! Blimey, what brings you so far north? Must be a good fare, eh? Aye, Karl, good to see you too! It's a long story, this. Got a mate, used to work down the docks with me, he’s got a Finnish wife. They're sending him over for a specialist piece of… well, I don't rightly know what it is, but it’s important. And they needed a driver reliable enough to get him from Helsinki to Joensuu without any bother. Pays alright, it does. Beats the road back home at the moment, that’s for sure. You lookin' a bit peakish, Karl. Everything alright with you? Just the usual, Barry. University stuff, you know. Endless committees and students who seem to think Shakespeare wrote TikTok scripts. But it's politics that's got me properly riled these days. This government... it's a right mess, isn't it? Tell me about it! They're bleedin' the country dry, they are. Remember New Labour? Tony Blair, back in the day? Thought he was alright, he did. Promised change, promised things would get better. Invested in the NHS, proper did. Now look at things. Privatisation creeping in everywhere, NHS on its knees… it's a disgrace. It's the relentless austerity, Barry. The dismantling of public services brick by brick. And the sheer  arrogance  of these politicians! You'd think they'd have learned something from the last few decades. My students argue about it endlessly – the legacy of Thatcher, the impact of neoliberalism... it’s a constant hum of discontent. Thatcher… Now  there’s  a name that winds people up. My mum used to say she’d filled the graveyards with her policies. And she weren’t far wrong, were she? Things were hard then, Karl. Really hard. Back then, football was the only escape for a lot of us. Remember the ’80s? Massive unemployment, riots… but we had Shankly’s spirit, didn’t we? Proper team. Oh, absolutely! The passion, the community… it felt like more than just a football club. A symbol of hope, almost. And then came the Hillsborough disaster… that completely broke my heart. The injustice of it all, the way the police tried to blame the fans... it was sickening. It makes you question everything, doesn’t it?

Right, so I’ve been going through some of these BNC recordings… Honestly, it's fascinating, but also a bit bonkers. There's one from 1988 where a bloke's ranting about the price of petrol, and it's basically the same complaints people have now! Just… different numbers. Proper timeless, innit? It’s funny how some things never change. You ever get that feeling, like you're just recycling history? I’m editing a piece on sustainable tourism, and it’s full of anxieties about overcrowding and environmental impact that people were voicing like, decades ago. Makes you feel a bit bleak. Bleak is a strong word. Evolution. Fair point, actually. But still! Moving on from existential dread... Did you see Elara posted about getting a new job on LinkedIn? Head of Marketing for that online travel agency. Serious hustle. No! Blimey, that's brilliant for her. She was moaning about being stuck in that admin role for ages. Good on her! I need to congratulate her. Think I'll send her a little something… maybe a care package with some Welsh cakes? Ooh, good shout. I’ll drop her a message too. Though, I’m trying to be a bit more disciplined on social media, you know? Less scrolling, more doing. Trying to be productive like Elara. Easier said than done, love. It's a vortex. Remember when we tried that social media detox? Lasted about three hours. Don't remind me! My hand was twitching for my phone. I miss seeing you though, especially now you're in Spain. When are you coming back to visit? We’re planning a trip for… October, hopefully. End of October, just as the weather starts to turn. We've got friends coming over too from back home, so it'll be a bit of a reunion. It’s just… booking flights still terrifies me. Oh, the flying thing! Still?
