You'd think after all these years… Don’t even. It’s irrational, I know. I have a whole system of affirmations and deep breathing techniques, and even then, I'm basically a shaking mess. I'd much rather take a boat. Spend weeks at sea. Boats are unreliable. Says the one who lives in relative mystery! We barely know anything about you, do we? Where are you originally from, anyway? Doesn't matter now. Right then, let’s deflect from that slightly unsettling topic.

Right, so, I’m thinking, proper big one on my forearm. Like, shoulder-width. What do you reckon, Sal? Too much? Too much commitment, maybe, Leo. You’re only just turning twenty-two, innit? Remember when you dyed your hair bright orange and swore you’d never regret it? Don't remind me. That was a  phase . This is different. It’s… meaningful. It’s a tribute to my nan. Sparrows, you know? She loved sparrows. Always feeding them in the garden. Sparrows are lovely. But a shoulder-width tribute? Are you sure a smaller, more subtle design wouldn't work just as well? You don't want it to look like you’re trying too hard. I’m not! I just… I want it to be  noticeable . Something I can look at and just… remember her. Plus, they’re really cool, sparrows. Like little winged dynamos. And I’ve got a guy, Liam, he does proper realistic ones. Showed me his portfolio online. Blimey. Online portfolios can be deceiving. I’ve seen some dodgy tattoos in my time. Remember Aunt Maureen's ‘dreamcatcher’ that looked like a spider had exploded on her arm? Yeah, fair point. But Liam’s different. He’s proper talented. Anyway, less about inking, more about grub, yeah? This Bolognese smells incredible. You've outdone yourself. It’s my secret ingredient. A tiny splash of balsamic vinegar. Changes everything. Oh, here's the doorbell. That must be Chloe. Right on cue! She's always punctual, that one. Chloe, darling! Come in, come in! You’re just in time. Smells good, doesn't it? It smells  amazing ! Honestly, I’m starving. Big day at the office, you wouldn't believe. You two already started, I see. Yeah, Sal’s a Bolognese wizard. We were just debating the merits of large-scale sparrow tattoos. Only you, Leo. Seriously though, what’s the big day at the office? So, the Christmas campaign launch. Absolute madness, it’s been. And then  then , Mr. Henderson, the senior editor, decided the entire ad needed a rewrite. Last minute. At four o’clock this afternoon! I spent the last three hours basically battling for the Oxford comma. You know how he is. Sounds rough. Oxford commas are serious business. The tyranny of style guides. It’s what I deal with every day, dear. But you're handling it well, I’m sure. So, Christmas plans shaping up?

Right then, nearly ready. Just needs another five minutes to thicken up. Honestly, this lentil shepherd’s pie is a lifesaver on a chilly evening like this. You’ve got to try it, Chloe. It's surprisingly good, even if I do say so myself. Mmm, smells divine, Anna. Lentils, eh? Bit healthier than my usual Friday night takeaway, that’s for sure. I’m trying to be… you know… a responsible adult. London’s really taken its toll, I think. I need more greens in my life. London does that to you! All those late nights, too much coffee, not enough sleep. I’m glad you made the trip up. Birmingham's nice and quiet, a good breather. You look a bit knackered, actually. How's that deadline you were facing? Don’t even  ask . It was brutal. Three days straight of subs and fact-checking. My eyes are still twitching. I think I aged about five years. The editor was breathing down my neck about a piece on sustainable fashion – apparently, everyone’s obsessed with ‘conscious consumption’ now. Oh, really? Sustainable fashion... I’ve been dipping my toe in. I bought a really lovely scarf from a fair-trade shop in St Albans last month. Such beautiful colours. Though ironically, getting it back to Birmingham involved a whole lot of travel. Speaking of which, are you thinking of finally booking that trip to Morocco we talked about? I am! I've been looking at flights. Marrakech looks absolutely incredible. I’m slightly terrified of the food though, to be honest. All those spices… My stomach isn’t exactly the most adventurous. You'll be fine! Just take some imodium. Seriously, it’s delicious. They use spices so brilliantly. It’s all about balance, you know? I found a fantastic tagine recipe online - I'll send it to you. Anyway, about exercise – have you joined that new Pilates class I mentioned? Not yet. I haven't had the time, you know how it is. Though I'm feeling the lack of it. My back's been playing up something fierce. I actually saw a physio last week – he was saying I need to strengthen my core. Easier said than done when you're hunched over a computer all day. Absolutely! Pilates is brilliant for that. It’s surprisingly challenging, though. So much more than just stretching. It really works those muscles.

Honestly, this air is still such a novelty. Crisp, but…clean. Not like London smog. It's lovely to walk home like this, isn’t it? No rush hour crushing. It absolutely is. Though I do miss a proper pub after a long day. This place just isn't quite ready for a decent pint of bitter, is it? Still, the dumplings were excellent tonight. Though, did you notice Mrs. Chen staring again? Oh, she always stares! I think she’s fascinated by our… footwear. Honestly, my toes are screaming. These hiking boots were a mistake. Utterly. They looked so sensible in the shop. Sensible is your middle name, darling. Especially when choosing shoes. You'll be battling ingrown toenails by the end of the semester at this rate. You really need to get some proper walking sandals. These are clearly designed for mountainous terrain, not a ten-minute stroll through a Chinese city. You’re probably right. It's just… feels more appropriate for exploring. Bit less touristy, you know? Anyway, more pressing than my aching toes! Did you hear back from Liam about the conference? Not yet. I texted him this afternoon. He's probably still wrestling with that tenure application. Poor bloke, he's a nervous wreck about it. I keep telling him it’s practically guaranteed, but… you know Liam. Absolutely. Always second-guessing himself. Reminds me a bit of my dad, actually. It’s just so frustrating to watch someone so brilliant beating themselves up. I feel for him. Maybe we should suggest a weekend getaway? Something completely unrelated to academia. Like where? A donkey sanctuary in rural Guangdong? He’d spend the entire time researching donkey husbandry techniques. Alright, fair point. Perhaps not. How about we just invite him over for dinner next weekend? Roast chicken, good wine, distracting conversation. Force him to relax. That’s actually a really good idea. We could rope in Chloe and Ben too. It’s been far too long since we all got together properly. Chloe’s been completely swallowed up by her new project, hasn't she? She keeps muttering about ‘data integrity’ and ‘statistical significance.’ Sounds utterly draining. It does! I tried to call her last week, but she just sent me a string of emojis – the stressed-out face, the spinning globe, the sweary monkey. Classic Chloe. She'll burn out if she doesn’t take a break.

Honestly, this place is always packed, isn't it? Good to see you, Liam! It feels like ages. How's everything going? Chloe! It  has  been a while. You look great, really. Everything's… well, busy, as always. The business is demanding, but generally good. How about you? Still wrangling teenagers with Shakespeare? You have no idea. This year's lot are particularly enthusiastic about emojis in their sonnets. It's… a challenge. Though, I did get one to genuinely appreciate Macbeth’s ambition, which felt like a little victory. Have you seen anything decent on telly lately? I’ve been meaning to catch up on something other than subtitles and adolescent angst. Not much to write home about, to be honest. I did binge-watch that new conspiracy docuseries, “The Silent Architects.” You know, about the… well, just the general idea that powerful, hidden forces are manipulating everything. Oh, really? You and your conspiracy theories, Liam! Do tell. I'm always up for a bit of a rabbit hole. Is it pyramids and lizard people? Nothing that extreme, thankfully. It’s more about economic control and subtle shifts in policy. It’s surprisingly well-researched, though it’s certainly got its detractors. It makes you wonder, doesn’t it? About who  really  pulls the strings. It does. Though, I find sometimes those theories are just a rather dramatic way of processing feeling powerless. I’d rather focus on something a bit lighter. I was thinking of seeing that new Margot Robbie film, “Barbie.” Ridiculous premise, I know, but the trailers look genuinely funny. Margot Robbie? She used to date that cricketer, didn't she? What was his name... Broad? He seemed like a decent chap. Anyway, Barbie… I'm not sure. My wife, Sarah, is convinced it's some kind of feminist manifesto disguised as a plastic doll. That’s exactly why I want to see it! It’s probably no deeper than a paddling pool, but the satire could be brilliant. Speaking of wives, how are things with Sarah? Still chasing marathon times? She is, relentlessly. Just signed up for one in Amsterdam in the spring. She’s become almost frighteningly dedicated. Me, I’m trying to keep up with the HIIT classes here. It’s a losing battle, frankly. Work’s been intense too. We're trying to expand into the European market, which is… a whole new level of paperwork and bureaucracy.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? It's taking ages. And this road is just…grey. So much grey. Now, Elsie, you know Cornwall isn't just around the corner. It's a good few hours still. And it's not  all  grey, lass. Look, there’s a patch o’ buttercups just bursting up there on that verge. See 'em? Bright yellow, cheering the place up. Besides, grey’s a good colour, steady and strong, like the roads we’re travelling on. Buttercups are yellow though, Dad. Yellow like the Yellow Brick Road in  The Wizard of Oz . Remember when we watched that last year? I wish we were going somewhere with witches and flying monkeys, instead of caravans and seagulls. Flying monkeys would be a bit much for a holiday, wouldn’t they? Though your mum would probably like the witches. She’s always been partial to a bit o’ magic. Still, Cornwall’s got its own magic, Elsie. Old stories, smugglers, legends… like Jamaica Inn. Do you know about Jamaica Inn? A bit. It’s a place where smugglers used to hide, right? Like in  Sherlock Holmes , when he’s tracking down criminals? Aye, that’s it. A bit like that. It’s said that Daphne du Maurier, the writer, used to visit that Inn and get all her inspiration from the wild Cornish weather and the isolation. Did you know du Maurier was quite clever wi' languages? Used to speak French fluently. Makes you think about things, doesn’t it. Communication, back then... before texts and emails. What did people do? Send telegrams? Like in that old movie? Aye, telegrams! And telegraphs, o’ course. It was all Morse code then. Click, click, dash… I remember trying to learn it when I was a lad. Never got the hang of it, mind. My Gran, she could read it a bit. She said it was like a secret code to unlock… it reminded her of Lewis Carroll and his nonsense poems. All those hidden meanings. Morse code… Braille too! My school had a little display about it. How do you read with your fingers? Well, you use raised dots to represent letters and numbers. Clever system, really. Just like books themselves, innit? Holding all sorts of stories and knowledge. Fancy that, Elsie – a whole world inside a few pages. Speaking of books, are you sure we're going the right way?

Right then, Grandad, you were sayin’ about petrol stations? I cannae quite believe how much they charge nowadays, can you? It’s bleedin’ daylight robbery, honestly. Used to be you could fill your tank for a fiver, couldn't you? A fiver! A veritable feast, lass! I remember when fourpence a gallon was considered dear. Fourpence! And we'd queue up, you know, well into the road. Wartime rationing, you see. Not like now, pulling up and swiping your card like you’re buying a packet of crisps. Those little forecourt places used to be proper community hubs. You’d catch up on the local gossip, get a bag of broken biscuits… simpler times, lass, simpler times. Well, the cost is largely driven by global oil prices, isn’t it? Geopolitics, supply and demand… quite complex when you dig into it. Although, I will agree, the margin at the pump seems excessive. I was just reading about a report suggesting… Oh, aye, I’m sure it’s complex, love. But me mam’s always said, ‘Don’t let ‘em baffle ye with jargon, pet.’ She was a wise woman, me mam. Always. Anyway, this Channel swimming thing… you’re actually going to  attempt  that, Liam? Are you bonkers? Trying to be sensible about it, actually. Training schedule's rather intense. And it's for charity, of course. Supporting the RNLI. What did you think, Chloe? Reckon I'll make it? Make it? You’ll freeze off your knackers, that’s what you’ll do! But good on you for the charity, genuinely. Still, freezing. Sounds grim. Remember when we used to play those board games down at your nan’s, Grandad and I? You  always  cheated at Monopoly. Cheated? I simply employed…  strategic adjustments ! You were far too keen on Park Lane, girl. A dreadful investment, you know. Far better to focus on the orange set. Much more reliable. Strategic adjustments, indeed! I seem to recall you secretly moving your hotels when no one was looking. Classic Grandad. It's like a family tradition. It is! And you’re taking after him, Liam! Sneaky little practices in the pool, I bet. You were quite the cardsharp at Go Fish when you were a kid. It’s in the blood, I reckon. Speaking of kids… Penelope Rhodes. Remember her from primary school? Timperley Primary, that was. Dizzy brunette, always getting into mischief.

Right then, Mum. Jet lag is  really  hitting me now. That flight from Seoul was a beast. Worth it to see you, though. Smells amazing in here, what is it? Oh, love, you’re looking a bit peaky! It’s just a simple shepherd's pie. Comfort food for a weary traveller. Sit down, sit down. I’ve got a cuppa brewing too. You must be famished. Had anything to eat on the plane? A tiny sandwich and some questionable airline crisps. Definitely not enough. Shepherd’s pie sounds perfect. Seriously, you always knew how to make me feel better. So, about the house… I’ve started a list. It's embarrassingly long. A list is good, darling. A very good thing. Don’t you worry about it being long. Moving is  always  a nightmare. Did you remember to pack the photo albums? Those are precious. They’re in the big box marked ‘Memories’. I was thinking we could sort through them while we’re here? Might be a good way to kill some time before the removals van arrives next week. It’s just… so much stuff. I'm downsizing considerably, you know, from a three-bedroom flat to a one-bedroom apartment. Oh, bless you. A smaller place is lovely though, isn’t it? Less to clean! Remember when your grandad was obsessed with collecting porcelain figurines? The sheer volume of them! We had entire shelves dedicated to little dogs and cats. Oh god, yes! The dust! Mom, honestly, I don't want to end up like Grandad. I’m trying to be minimalist. But there are things… like your old sewing box. I promised I'd take that. You absolutely should. That’s full of bits and pieces from your childhood. Ribbons, buttons, scraps of fabric… I even put a little woven bracelet in there you made when you were about six. Do you remember it? Bright pink and covered in… well, who knows what! I… faintly. Mostly I remember spending hours watching you sew. You were such a whiz with a needle and thread. Remember that ridiculous dress you made me for the school play? The one with the giant sunflower on the front? Oh, that! That was a masterpiece, darling. Truly. The other mums were horrified, but you looked so pleased! You were playing a bumblebee, you see. It was entirely appropriate. Your father nearly choked he was laughing so much.

Dead reet, isn’t it? Look at that orchid. Just… thriving. We could do with a bit o’ that thriving in our own lives, ay? Especially wi' everything going on. Thriving, yes. Though orchids are notoriously picky. A lot of fuss for a few flowers, really. Reminds me of trying to get funding for this research, actually. Constant vigilance, specific conditions... Aye, well, we’re not talking about funding, are we? We're talking about plants that look happy. Unlike my hair, which is currently defying all attempts at happiness. Been thinking about chopping it a bit shorter, maybe? Something like yours, a bit neater? My hair is the product of hours of product and a silent pact with my barber. It's not a natural gift, love. Though I do think a shorter style would suit you. What were you thinking? A bob? Nah, not a bob. Something a bit more… choppy, maybe. Like a really good pixie cut. But I’m scared of looking like a right state if it doesn’t go right. It’s a risk, innit? Like trusting the NHS these days. Don’t go starting on the NHS now. I know you’re worried, but it's still the best system we’ve got. Admittedly, it's creaking under the pressure. My mum’s been waiting months for a specialist appointment. It's a disgrace, honestly. It is! Absolutely is. And it’s getting worse. Me mam’s still moaning about the wait times, an’ she’s not even got anything serious. It’s just… the whole system feels like it’s on the brink. Speaking of things on the brink, did you see what they’re planning with the A-Levels? The reforms? Yes, I did. It’s madness. Further streamlining, even more assessment. It's just going to pile the pressure on the students even higher. They want to churn out graduates to fill quotas, not nurture independent thinkers. Exactly! My little cousin’s just finished his GCSEs, and he’s already stressed to buggery about A-Levels. He wants to study history, but they’re cutting back on humanities subjects, aren't they? Says it’s about employability. Like young people are just cogs in a machine. It’s a short-sighted view, isn't it? And it’s driven by these constant political shifts. Every government has their own agenda. It's exhausting keeping up.

Honestly, I'm proper knackered. Another shift at the chippy, another mountain of greasy chips. I swear, me feet are gonna fall off. You're still smoking? Seriously, Chloe? We talked about this. You've got that coughing thing going on too. Cambridge air is fresh, Leeds air… well, it’s Leeds air. Aye, well, fresh air doesn't pay the rent, does it, Eliza? Gotta fund this fancy law degree somehow. Besides, it calms me nerves. Legal jargon ain't exactly soothing. Law? You? Chloe, you yell at checkout staff for being out of your favourite flavour crisps. How are you gonna be a barrister? Charm, Marnie! Raw, Yorkshire charm. It's a deadly weapon. Plus, I'm good at arguing. You lot know that. Aye, she’ll be a terror, she will. Remember that time she tried to convince Mrs. Henderson that pigeons were secretly government spies? That was one time! And pigeons  do  look suspicious, don't they? Anyway, what about you two? How's uni going, Gemma and Marnie? Still swanning about Newcastle and Durham, I presume? Durham’s alright, although it's ridiculously historic. Like, cobblestone streets and portraits of dead blokes everywhere. Trying to get me head round medieval history is giving me a right headache. It's all kings and plagues and whatnot. Honestly, Marnie, medieval history is fascinating! Think about the Black Death. Imagine wiping out half of Europe’s population? It’s… compelling. Eliza started a whole debate about pandemic preparedness for her sociology module. See? Eliza’s always been a bit extreme. Though, admittedly, the world could do with being a bit more prepared. Though, honestly, worrying about the Black Plague when my bank account's looking emptier than a politician’s promises? Priorities! Tell me about it. Working at the call centre in Sunderland is draining the life out of me. Dealing with angry customers all day... I'm considering applying for a job at Greggs, just for the smell of sausage rolls. You should come to Durham, Gemma! We're having a feminist society meeting next week about the impact of historical patriarchy on modern wage gaps. It’ll be right up your street. That actually sounds brilliant, Marnie. I've been meaning to get more involved in the feminism society here. We’re planning a campaign to get more women studying STEM subjects. It’s abysmal how few there are.

It’s…odd, isn’t it? How friendships just…fade. Not with a dramatic blow-up, just…a gentle lessening. I’ve been thinking a lot about it lately. Yeah, it is. I've definitely experienced that. It’s much more common than people admit, I think. Everyone's all about ‘friendship goals’ and forever friends, but realistically, life changes, people change. You drift. Exactly! And the tricky part isn’t the drifting, it’s the acknowledging that you  want  the drifting to accelerate. I find myself less and less inclined to make an effort with a few people we’ve known for years. And that feels…wrong. Like you're abandoning them. I get that. There’s a massive guilt factor. Especially when you've got shared history. But is it really abandoning them, or is it acknowledging that the relationship isn’t serving you anymore? My mum always used to say, "You're not obligated to keep watering plants that don't want to grow." Bit blunt, but there's truth in it. Your mum sounds wonderfully pragmatic. And you’re right. I’m just... I don’t want to ghost them. That feels cowardly. And potentially hurtful. I'd rather gently steer the ship towards a quieter port, you know? But how  do  you do that? Without causing a scene? It’s a slow burn, isn’t it? It's not a conversation you just blurt out – "Right, I'm phasing you out!" – unless you're deliberately trying to cause drama. I think it’s about subtly scaling back. Less availability. Shorter calls. Less enthusiasm for their invites. I  have  been doing that, subconsciously, I think. Making excuses. Getting busy. But it feels…a bit manipulative. A little bit, maybe. But also, a little bit necessary. It's about protecting your energy, right? You’re allowed to prioritize your own wellbeing. I’ve found that mirroring their level of effort can be surprisingly effective. If they're not reaching out much, you don't either. That's... clever. I hadn't thought of it like that. I’ve been so preoccupied with  their  perspective, I haven't considered that they might be feeling the same way. Maybe this is mutual. Probably is. Look at Sarah, remember her? From university? We were inseparable for like, three years. Then, after graduation, she just…drifted away. I felt awful for ages, convinced I’d done something wrong.

Right, so Professor Davies really laid it on thick this morning. Said my dissertation proposal was ‘intriguing, but lacked demonstrable rigor.’ Rigor! Like I haven’t been pulling all-nighters fuelled by instant noodles and existential dread for the last six months. Oh, academic pronouncements. A veritable art form in themselves, aren't they? Don’t you let him deflate you, darling. Intriguing is good. It means you’re thinking outside the box. What’s the topic again? Something to do with post-war urban planning, wasn’t it? Yeah, it's about the impact of speculative housing on community cohesion in post-war London. Sounds a lot more glamorous when you read it on paper. Professor Davies wants more… numbers. More statistics. Apparently, gut feeling and historical context aren't enough these days. Numbers can be misleading, love. They tell you  what  happened, but not  why . Remember what I always say about art? It’s about the why. The feeling. The unspoken connection. Your dissertation sounds fascinating, really. London’s changed so much. I remember… well, I remember a very different London. You do. You’ve told me stories. Always wanted to hear more. Like, what was it  really  like after the war? Not the history books version, but what did  you  see? Oh, it was… raw. Still. The rubble, the rationing, the determination to rebuild. It was chaotic, but simultaneously full of hope. People were rebuilding their lives as much as they were rebuilding the city. There were artists then too, you know. Struggling, vibrant, creating beauty in the wreckage. It’s what drew me here. I was just a young woman then, newly arrived from Vienna, utterly overwhelmed and yet… strangely at home. Vienna! You never really talk about that much. What was it like leaving? Was it difficult? Difficult doesn't even begin to cover it. Leaving family, leaving a life… It was necessary, though. The political climate… it was becoming unbearable. My family had always been involved in the arts, and Austria was… changing. Becoming less tolerant of difference. So, I packed a suitcase and a few canvases, and I ran. It’s a story for another time, perhaps. Tell me more about your uni friends. Are you still seeing Liam? Nah, Liam and I… we drifted. It was amicable, but you know how it is. He's focusing on his rugby scholarship, I’m buried in Victorian housing estates.

Honestly, I’m starving. We really should've stopped for something a bit more substantial than those pastries in Nowy Sącz. My stomach’s starting to rumble. Do you think we could grab a bite before we hit the gym in Tarnów? Aye, yeah, definitely. You're right, those were just a tease. I'm feeling it too, now you mention it. Though, honestly, I’m not massively keen on having a big meal right before a workout. Might make me feel sluggish. Think something light-ish? Maybe a sandwich or a salad? Light-ish suits me well. I don't want to be waddling around the gym feeling like a stuffed sausage. Though, a proper Polish pierogi wouldn't go amiss… but no, you're right, restraint is key. How much further do you reckon? This road's… well, it's a road, isn't it? According to the map, about another hour and a half, I'd say. Traffic's looking pretty good though. You doing alright on the driving front? You haven’t seemed completely focused, love. Just checking. Perfectly fine, dear. Just letting my thoughts wander. It’s terribly dull, isn’t it, driving for such a long stretch? But then, that’s the joy of campervanning, isn't it? The vast, empty spaces. It's a bit… liberating, in a way. After all these years of being cooped up… I know what you mean. It is good to get out and about. And you're a surprisingly good driver, by the way. Better than my dad, certainly. He’d have us in a ditch within the first five minutes. Seriously, he thinks roundabouts are optional. Your dad sounds like a character. Well, I did have lessons, you know. Years ago. Although, I wouldn’t put myself up against a professional. And we  are  getting close to the gym. Are you still set on a full leg day? It’s a bit… intense, isn’t it? Yeah, still planning on it. I want to really work on my squats. Plus, it's good to challenge myself. You joining in? I might. Perhaps just a gentle cycle on the stationary bike. Honestly, my knees aren’t what they used to be. And I’m not sure I fancy pulling a muscle. Plus, I've not really  exercised  properly in… well, a very long time. No pressure at all, then.

Right then, Nana, fancy a top-up? This brew’s proper good this morning. Feels good to sit out here after all that rain yesterday. Did you see how fierce it was? Absolutely lashed down. Aye, love, a right downpour it were. Glad I got me washing in before it started. Though I'm thinking, having no heating on all day, it’s made the damp extra bad. Feels like the walls are breathin’ on me. That's a worry, isn’t it? We need to get that damp sorted properly. I keep meaning to call the damp proofing people, but you know how it is, life gets in the way. Speaking of which, I’ve been trying to pot on those geraniums I showed you. They’re lookin’ a bit rootbound already. Geraniums, eh? Always liked a bit of colour. Reminds me of Mrs. Featherstone's garden, over on Lumb Lane. She had the best geraniums in Bradford, she did. Big, red, showy things. Proper beauty. So, about these mugs… you’re still makin' ‘em? They're lovely, you know. Really are. Aye, still at it. Just finished a batch, actually. Trying a slightly darker clay this time. Makes the colours pop a bit more, don't you think? I've got a few with tiny little bluebells painted on. Reckon they'd be a smashing present. Fancy having a proper look? Got a tray of 'em in the kitchen. I was thinkin' about selling some at the Little Horton festival, that’s coming up next month. Little Horton festival! Oh, I always enjoyed that. Though last year, it were a bit too crowded for me, to be honest. All that pushin’ and shovin’. Still, the cakes were grand. And the brass band, of course. Used to love a bit o' brass. You gettin' a proper stall, then? I am, yes. Got a friend of mine, Sarah – you remember Sarah from the Women's Institute? - she's helping me out with the display. She's no bother, Sarah. Always cheerful. Listen, speaking of people we remember… I saw Maureen Hargreaves the other day. She's doing alright, considering. Still lives on Cemetery Road. Maureen Hargreaves! Goodness me, that's a long time. She always had a sweet tooth, Maureen did. Remember that time she tried to sneak an extra jam tart at the school fete? Nearly got caught! You know, I saw a spider in the bathroom this mornin’.

Ugh, another influencer doing a perfect beach photoshoot. It's just not fair when we're stuck packing for Cornwall. Stuck? Honestly, Elsie, you sound like you're being punished. Cornwall is lovely! Think of the pasties, the cream teas, the coastal walks… and no influencers invading  our  little coves. I know, I know. It’s just… Liam and Chloe are going to Majorca. Majorca! All-inclusive, cocktails by the pool, the whole shebang. I felt like I had to at least  pretend  to be excited about windy cliffs and seagulls. Windy cliffs and seagulls are character-building, lass. Keeps you grounded. Majorca's just… well, it’s Majorca. Overdone. And probably full of people desperate for a tan. See! Dad gets it. But I'll miss them, you know? Liam specifically. It's just going to be awkward when we're back and they're posting all their sun-kissed pictures. Sweetheart, a little perspective. They'll be complaining about the heat and the crowds in a week. And honestly, you'll be back here, practically running up the cliffs, breathing the fresh sea air. Remember last time, how much you loved rock pooling at Caderly? Yeah, but that was with Maya and Jess. They’re not coming this year. Maya’s got that summer internship in London, and Jess is… I don't even know what Jess is doing. Lost contact, I think. Lost contact? Happens, Elsie. People drift. Doesn’t mean you won’t make new friends. Cornwall’s a good place for that. Loads of proper folk. Not those Insta-types. Your dad’s right. And you’ll see lots of other kids on the beach. You can always make a couple of new pals. Remember that boy, what was his name… Tom? You met him when we went to St Ives a few years ago. Tom! Yeah, he was cool. He built a massive sandcastle. But he lived there full-time. It wouldn't be the same. Well, you might find someone as good at sandcastle building. They’re a rare breed, those. Building a proper castle is an art form, you know. Requires planning, structural integrity... Right, Dad. You’re going to give me a sandcastle engineering lesson on holiday. Brilliant. Don’t wind him up, Elsie. He’s just trying to be encouraging. Speaking of which, have you finished packing your waterproofs? The weather forecast isn’t exactly brilliant.

Ugh, that film was  amazing  though, wasn't it? Like, seriously, Heath Ledger? Iconic. I’m proper having a crush. Yeah, it was good. Kat Stratford is my spirit animal, though. All that, "I hate almost everything" vibe. Me too, honestly, especially on Mondays. Which, coincidentally, is tomorrow. Don't remind me! History’s got a whole lesson on the Tudors. Mr. Davies is going on about Henry VIII's wives  again . I swear he’s obsessed. Like, get over it, it was centuries ago! Tell me about it! Mrs. Peterson’s English test is looming too. Remember she said it was going to be 'challenging'? That’s just code for 'impossible'. I'm dreading it. Think she'll ask about Shakespeare? Possibly. She loves Shakespeare. Probably a Romeo and Juliet essay, yeah? I need to revamp my ideas. My first attempt was…rubbish, to be honest. I spent like, half an hour just staring at the question. Total blank. I did the same with the poetry analysis last week. Just…nothing. My brain just emptied. I was worried I’d have to ask for an extension. Mum would've killed me. Yeah, no good. Remember last year when Emily tried to get an extension on her maths coursework? Nearly had a meltdown in front of Mr. Finch. Oh god, yes! That was a spectacle. She said she had a family emergency, and then it turned out her cat had knocked over her water glass. Seriously? Right drama queen. Anyway, back to the misery of school. Are you actually doing anything about that Geography project? The one on sustainable cities? Vaguely. I’ve done a bit of research, but actually  writing  it feels like climbing Everest. I keep putting it off. Maybe if I started with the introduction... Do it! Do it now! We could maybe brainstorm a bit? Two brains are better than one, right? I’m actually quite good at structure. I might be able to help you with the planning bit. That would be amazing, actually. Seriously. I'm completely lost on how to structure the whole thing. I have loads of ideas, just can't seem to make them flow. Okay, cool. Let's have a look later tonight? After dinner, maybe? We could order pizzas. Yes! Pizza sounds  perfect . Okay, geography plan of attack after pizza. Sounds much better. Speaking of plans...are you all excited about London next month?

Cor, this is a lovely brew, Annie. Proper builder's tea, just how I like it. Mind you, Facebook's gone and gone all topsy-turvy again. Keep seein' things I don't 'alf understand. Proper baffling, it is. Oh, don’t even start, Arthur. It’s a complete minefield, isn’t it? All these algorithms. I saw a post the other day about… well, I can’t even remember  what  it was about, but it was full of flashing lights and people yelling. Gave me quite a fright. At my age, I just want to see pictures of my grandkids! Not… whatever that was. It's definitely designed to be a bit overwhelming, Mum. It's all about maximising engagement, you know? Keeping you scrolling. It's a bit like, deliberately creating a feeling of… slight anxiety, so you come back for more. A bit cynical, Elodie, aren’t we? Though, there's definitely something to what you're saying. I was looking at an article the other day about how platforms intentionally trigger reward pathways in the brain. It's practically addictive. Reward pathways? Sounds like a right mess, that does. Back in my day, the only reward was a good packet of biscuits. And maybe a bit of sunshine. Exactly, Arthur! Simpler times. Though, goodness, I do worry about Jamie these days, glued to that phone. Remember when he had chicken pox? He just sat playing games, didn’t even complain about the itching. He was a remarkably stoic child, actually. I think he just saw it as a temporary inconvenience. Though, it was pretty miserable for you, Mum, having to bathe him three times a day. Don’t remind me. Calamine lotion everywhere! And the constant worry. You never knew what would trigger the next outbreak of spots. It does make you think, doesn't it? About how vulnerable children are. It’s a weird kind of resilience, finding ways to entertain yourself even when you’re feeling terrible. I think that's something people are losing a bit of. Speaking of worry… I was readin’ somethin’ online - don't you go thinkin’ I’m spendin’ all day on that Facebook thing, mind - but it was about… obsessive somethin’ or other. Called it OCD, didn’t it? Yes, Arthur. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. It's a mental health condition. Have you been noticing something that worries you? Well, it weren’t for me, love.

Right, nearly there then. Dinner's shaping up nicely, wouldn't you say? Mark, are you getting on with the sprouts alright? They need a bit of salt, love. Yeah, yeah, almost done, Sarah. Don't worry, I haven't burnt 'em this time. Remember last Christmas? That was a disaster. Oh, don't remind me! They were practically charcoal. Dad ended up ordering a pizza! Don't be disrespectful, Lucy! I told you, that pizza was the best thing that happened that day. At least we ate  something . And the kids loved it. Speaking of the kids, have you heard from Emily? She hasn't texted me back about the flight details. I’m starting to get a bit anxious about the Germany trip. She's probably just busy, love. These young 'uns are always glued to their phones. Germany, though… Fancy going back. Remember when your Grandad took us all there, Chloe? Oh, yes. 1985, wasn’t it? With that dreadful Ford Sierra. Honestly, Sarah, that car was the bane of my existence. The suspension was awful on those German roads. Oh, stop moaning, Roger! It got us there, didn't it? And it was an adventure. Remember trying to order food in German? My German was appalling, bless me. "Ein Bier, bitte…und…um…Kartoffeln?" I sounded like a right fool. And Dad tried to haggle for a cuckoo clock! He seriously thought he could get it cheaper. I remember that! The shopkeeper just looked at him like he was mad. Proper stared him down. Well, a man's got to try! It's the British spirit, isn't it? Besides, I nearly got it down a few Deutschmark. Not quite, but nearly. It's the trying that counts. Though Sarah did burst out laughing, didn’t she? I couldn’t help it! You were going red in the face. It was priceless. Your German was even worse than mine! You guys are hilarious. So, Grandad and his haggling skills… He really did try to speak every language, didn’t he? Even pigeon German. I remember him trying to teach us bits and pieces. He always did fancy himself a linguist. Though his French was even worse than his German. I used to tease him relentlessly. 'Bonjour, Monsieur…uh…voiture?' He’d get all flustered. He had a lovely accent though, didn’t he? Always a bit of a drawl, even when he was trying to speak properly.

So, you're  still  slinging pans then, eh? Last time we spoke, you were contemplating a career change to…competitive ferret grooming? Don't remind me! That was a brief, dark period fueled by watching too much Animal Planet. Cooking’s still the thing, yeah. Got a pretty sweet internship lined up at The Salty Siren down in Torquay, actually. Really proper seafood place. No way! The Salty Siren? That’s… impressive. I thought they only took in experienced chefs. How'd you manage that? Bit of luck, mostly. Sent off a load of applications, and their head chef, Liam, had apparently worked with my old mentor, Dave. Small world, innit? Anyway, Dave put in a good word. It's just for the summer, but it's a serious opportunity. Proper intense environment, apparently. Intense is good, though, right? Builds character. Speaking of intense… have you had a listen to 'Chromatic Cascade' by Nova Bloom yet? Their new album dropped last week. Absolutely gutted the live show in Bristol last month. The drummer, Finn, was on fire. Nova Bloom? Vaguely rings a bell… what genre are they? Another one of your indie-electronic things, I bet. I’m still stuck on Rival Sons, you know. Raw, gritty, that's what I like. Proper rock and roll. Heard their latest live album – recorded in Berlin – it’s phenomenal. The energy's just insane. They’re a bit more atmospheric. Think Portishead meets Tycho, but with a bit more…oomph. Finn, the drummer, is incredible. Seriously, you should check them out. He’s got this crazy polyrhythmic thing going on. You’d appreciate it, I reckon. Remember when we tried to form a band in sixth form? You on bass, me flailing around on the drums… Oh god, don’t remind me. The "Atomic Squirrels," wasn't it? We were terrible! My mum still has a recording somewhere, I swear. It’s a sonic crime against humanity. Though, that bass I had… I wish I’d kept it. It was a total monstrosity, all sparkly pink and chipped. Anyway, Nova Bloom's drumming is on another level. Actually, talking about people we know… how’s Chloe doing? Last I heard she was trying to get into that graphic design studio in London. Chloe’s alright, I think. She’s been quiet on social media, which usually means she’s been buried in work.

Right then, Thomas. This is nice, isn’t it? A bit of peace and quiet. Though this place  is  busy, isn't it? Can hardly hear myself think over the clatter. Aye, it’s a bit loud, Mam. But the coffee's decent, I reckon. Better than that instant stuff you make sometimes. Just kidding! Oh, you cheeky monkey! Don't you start. So, we’ve got the Durham trip booked for Saturday. Did you pack your comfy shoes? It'll be a lot of walking around the Cathedral. Yeah, I’ve got me trainers. Is Dad coming? He’s working, love. That new contract’s keeping him chained to his desk. He’s hoping to get a decent chunk of it wrapped up by Friday though. It's a right faff, this business structure he’s trying to build. All that talk of liability and limited companies...My head spins! Still, good for him, becoming an entrepreneur like that. Yeah, it’s alright. Does he ever talk about what he actually  does ? Sounds a bit boring. Well, he’s trying to be vague about it. Something about logistics and supply chains. He keeps saying the ‘Drive-through’ crews are getting mighty clever with their delivery routes and he’s helping them optimise it. Right… like those lads we saw the other day, zooming past in those fancy vans? They were proper speeding, mind. Hope they were insured. They probably were. Anyway, speaking of optimising things, I need to make a list. We’re running low on everything. Milk, bread, washing-up liquid… Tomatoes! We desperately need tomatoes. And don't even get me started on the state of the cupboards – total chaos! I can pop down to the shops after school, if you want. Would you, love? That would be brilliant. Just remember, loyalty promotions on the coffee at Tesco. Get the extra points, eh? We're saving up for that summer holiday, remember? Spain, hopefully. Spain sounds good. Do we need to get those new sleeping bags then? I think mine's getting a bit small. And beds, maybe? Those pop-up ones are a nightmare to fold. We'll look at it. Let's see how much we've got left after Spain. I've been reading in the news about obesity and the rising costs of healthcare. It's worrying, especially with how much fast food some kids are eating these days.

Right, so, welcome! Sorry it’s a bit…mid-unpacking still. Found a decent spot for you, though. Fancy a cuppa? I’ve got Earl Grey, builders, that sort of thing. Cheers, mate. Earl Grey's good. Place looks brilliant, actually. Sussex, eh? Bit of a change from Bronsgrove! Feels...leafier. Proper nice. And bigger than I pictured. You've done well. Cheers. It’s been a mission, getting it sorted. Hence the current state, as you can see. Listen, I was hoping we could record a bit tonight, if you’re up for it? Just a quick thing for my linguistics blog. Nothing serious. A linguistics blog? You're teaching English and blogging about linguistics? Proper clever clogs, you are. What’s the angle? Well, I'm doing a series on regional dialects. Thought you'd be perfect, given your accent - that lovely West Midlands twang. We could just chat about colloquialisms, how language changes, that sort of thing. Right, alright. Press gang me into your linguistics experiment! But don’t expect Shakespeare. I’m more of a “t’ell” and “our” kind of speaker, innit? Perfect! That's exactly what I’m after. So, how's life been treating you, anyway? Last time we properly spoke, you were agonizing over spreadsheets at that assurance firm. Still the spreadsheets, sadly. Although I did get a decent pay rise, actually. Not complaining, mind. Living in London wasn’t cheap. Getting married has changed things, though. Sarah’s doing brilliantly, she's about six months pregnant now. Wow! Congratulations! Seriously! That’s amazing news. You’ll be a brilliant dad. Have you started thinking about names yet? Trying to! It’s harder than the spreadsheets, I swear. We've got a list, but nothing’s stuck. And the cost of everything…it's mental. We're seriously looking at joint accounts now, actually. Shared bills, pregnancy stuff… it all adds up. What about you? Still enjoying the teaching? Loving it. The students are great, mostly. Though marking essays can be…a trial. This year's cohort have a fondness for using "like" as a substitute for every other word. It's a linguistic train wreck. And I'm finally getting to grips with budgeting. This move has been a real wake-up call about money. Sussex is deceptively expensive. Tell me about it! London was eye-watering, but the South Coast... it’s got a charm all its own, and a price tag to match.

Honestly, Sarah, I don’t know how she’s coping. Seeing Mum like this… it’s just… awful. The chemo's really taken it out of her. Yesterday she couldn't even remember where she put her glasses. And she  always  has them perched on her head. I know, love. It’s heartbreaking. I saw her last week, at the hospice coffee morning. She looked… smaller. And she kept drifting off, you know? Like her brain was just… elsewhere. Did she mention anything about the new consultant? Briefly. She said he seems nice, very clinical, of course. All about the percentages and options. She didn’t seem to latch onto any of it, though. Just… mumbled something about wanting to go home. Which, I suppose, is understandable. I tried to talk to her about Liam and Emily, but she just kept looking at the roses in the vase. It was so sad, watching her detach like that. It is. It's the worst part, isn't it? The loss of self, even before… you know. Remember when we were kids, and Mum used to take us blackberry picking? She knew absolutely every patch within a five-mile radius. She could identify every variety of rose, too! Now… Now, she struggles to remember what she had for breakfast. It's like pieces of her are just… slipping away. I feel guilty, you know? Guilty that I’m not there every single day, but the business… it's keeping my head above water, and someone has to do it. And Dad... he’s relying on me too. Don't you dare feel guilty. You're doing brilliantly, juggling everything. And Dad's a tough one; he puts on a brave face, but I’ve noticed he’s lost weight. He's not been sleeping well, I bet. Have you talked to him about getting some proper support? Not just the practical things, but… counseling, maybe? I've tried, but he clams up. “I’m fine, love,” he says. “Just a bit tired.” It’s the classic Dad response. You know, with Emily's A-levels looming, and Liam's applying for university… the stress is just piling up on everybody. Tell me about it. Chloe's having a wobble with her UCAS application. They want her to do a personal statement on ‘resilience,’ can you believe it? As if a teenager voluntarily applying for university is showing remarkable resilience already!

Right then, that was a lovely roast. Honestly, Dave, you’ve outdone yourself again. Just following a recipe, love. Nothing special. So, lads, how was school today? Liam, you look like you've seen a ghost. It was alright. Geography test. Didn't go brilliantly. I smashed mine! Got a B+ on the Tudor history essay! Mr. Davies was really impressed. I even quoted Shakespeare. Shakespeare, eh? That's impressive, Ethan. Fancy that from a young man! Liam, don't look so glum. One test doesn't define you. How’s the tennis coaching going? You were looking forward to that. It’s…okay. Mrs. Henderson is really strict. She keeps going on about grip and footwork. It’s boring. I just want to hit the ball really hard. That's often how it is when you're learning a skill, son. The fundamentals are key. Remember when I was first learning this business? All about process and systems, not just about getting the job done quickly. Oh, don’t start regaling us with tales of your early, disastrous management techniques, Dave. We’ll be here all night! Seriously though, Liam, you enjoy it. It's good exercise, and you might actually enjoy learning the proper technique. It'll improve your game later on. Speaking of games, did you see the football match yesterday? Liverpool got hammered! Yeah, awful! Dad, why do you even bother watching them? You’re always miserable afterwards. Because I  support  them, Liam! It's about loyalty! And besides, this referendum nonsense has put everyone in a bad mood. All that arguing… it’s exhausting. It is, isn't it? The whole country seems to be divided. It’s hard to even have a conversation about it without someone getting upset. Although, I do think it's important to be informed and have an opinion, even if it's a differing one. My mum was talking about apprenticeships the other day. Apparently, they’re really good now, with good pay and training. Might be better than Uni, actually. Really? Like what sort of apprenticeships? I don't know, loads of stuff. Engineering, IT, even finance. Apparently, you get paid while you learn. That's a very sensible thought, Ethan. An apprenticeship can be a brilliant route to a career. It’s practical and gives you experience. Liam, have you given any thought to what you might want to do after school?

Right, so Lancaster. It's proper countryside stuff, isn't it? Nothing like Aylesbury. All rolling hills and…well, I’m guessing it’ll be rather different from Lincoln too. Definitely! Lincoln's got its cathedral, which is amazing, obviously, but Lancaster is more…historic feeling, you know? All those old castles and whatnot. My aunt lives just outside Lancaster, that’s why we’re going. It’s been ages since I’ve seen her. Oh, lovely. A family visit! Much needed, I reckon. My mum's been on at me to see Gran more often. It's just, research deadlines, you know? Everything's been a bit manic lately. Tell me about it. This admin stuff can be relentless. Though, at least it's steady. I worry a lot about job security, to be honest. Did you hear about those redundancies at the local council? Yeah, I saw something about that. Terrible, isn't it? So many talented people. Makes you think, doesn’t it? All this hard work and qualifications…and still, it’s not a guarantee. It's made me seriously consider dipping my toe into academia properly, eventually. Maybe a masters? A masters! That’s brilliant! What would you do? You'd smash it, honestly. I'm thinking about it too, but the dissertation… the thought just fills me with dread. It's a mountain of work, isn't it? It is. But think of the possibilities! And it would look decent on the CV, wouldn’t it? I was looking at some linguistics ones at UCL, but Lancaster Uni’s got a decent department too, apparently. We should poke around their websites when we get some signal. Maybe we should both investigate? Yeah, we definitely should. What area are you thinking of specialising in? Something with computational linguistics, I imagine? Probably. Or maybe sociolinguistics – exploring how regional dialects are evolving. It's fascinating. What about you? Still leaning toward something in TEFL? I think so. Though I've been looking at some language policy roles too. It's all a bit overwhelming, to be honest. Sometimes I just want to grab a massive portion of fish and chips and forget about it all. Speaking of which, are we going to try the Lancaster fish and chips? Apparently, they're legendary. Absolutely! It's a requirement, isn’t it? A proper seaside holiday isn't complete without it.

Alright, alright, settle down, Mr. Moody. What's got your knickers in a twist tonight? You've been staring at that pint like it owes you money for the last half hour. Nah, nothin' really. Just thinkin', that’s all. About… well, about Friday night. The gig. Friday night? The 'Static Bloom' gig? What about it? They're supposed to be cracking, aren’t they? Liam’s been goin’ on about ‘em for weeks. They are. They are proper good. But… I just felt a bit weird last night. At Ben's house, rehearsing with them. He's got that new amp, remember? The one he saved up for ages? And it just… sounded a bit… much, you know? Overpowered. Overpowered? Ben’s always been a bit of a show-off with his equipment. Always needs the biggest, loudest thing. He’ll be slingin' speakers at ya next! Seriously though, what’s the problem? You’re the sensible one, you usually have a good ear. Exactly! That’s it! I should have said somethin'. I kept thinkin', ‘Nah, he’s put his heart and soul into this, don’t be a killjoy.’ But it drowned out the subtlety, the little bits that made their sound unique. It wasn't about the volume, it was about muddiness. I see. Right. So, it was losing its… finesse, was it? Like a good Yorkshire pudding with too much flour. Still edible, but not quite right. Spot on, lass! That's exactly it! I need to say somethin', I think. Otherwise, they’ll just keep piling more on and… well, they’ll lose what makes 'em good. You definitely should. But tread carefully. Ben’s sensitive about his gear. Maybe start by complimentin’ the guitar sound first, then gently suggesting he turn it down a tad to let the bass breathe. You know, with that nice, subtle Yorkshire diplomacy. Subtle diplomacy. Right. That’s me. I’ll try that. What about you? Found any good gigs lately? Anything exciting to report on the student arts scene? Actually, yeah! I went to see ‘The Crimson Echoes’ down at the Trades Hall on Tuesday. You remember ‘em, from school? Sam’s still fronting them. Sam! Blimey, I’d completely forgotten about them! They were brilliant even back then, weren't they? All moody and dark. Did they sound alright? They were phenomenal. Restyled a bit though, you know?

Right, okay. I've managed to build this in Atlanta – hopefully crucial for containing the purple outbreak. Rhys, are you  sure  you didn't want to take the Medic? You've been complaining you're bored. Boredom is a luxury, Seren! We’re facing global annihilation here! And honestly, I’m better with the Operations Expert. Moving those city cards is vital. Besides, Dai was eyeing the Medic. He  needs  to be healing everyone. Dai 'needs' to be healing everyone? Last time he played, he cured the black plague in Jakarta and then promptly forgot he needed to treat the red fever in Lyon. Bless him, he tries. Leave him alone, Mark. He's doing his best. And anyway,  I  think Dai’s doing alright. It's you, Matthew, who keeps forgetting to build research stations. We’re running out of places to put them! Now, now, let's not bicker! A little friendly competition never hurt anyone. Though, I must say, I’m finding this game surprisingly stressful. Reminds me a bit too much of the outbreaks we used to deal with at the community centre. Only with…slightly fewer coughs. Arthur’s right, darlings. Let’s try to keep the stress levels down. It  is  a holiday, after all. And Dai, dear, are you  certain  you’re using the right coloured cubes? Last time, you swore you’d cured the yellow fever with blue ones. That’s a memory for the ages, Bronwen. Right, focus everyone! I’m moving to Bangkok. I need to trade some cards and hopefully put another research station down. Glyn, what's your hand looking like? Need any help? Actually, yeah. I’ve got a ridiculous number of red city cards. And I’m stuck. I was hoping to get to Moscow to build something… Moscow's a bad look right now. Massive outbreak potential if you don't stabilize it. Mark, you’re closest. Can you swing by and chuck a research station down? Give me a minute. I’m currently fending off the blue plague outbreak on the Pacific Rim. Trying to stop it from spiralling out of control. It's tricky with only a few cards to play. Although, I did manage to steal one of Bronwen's event cards earlier. Sorry, Bronwen. Oh, you cheeky thing! Stealing my one-use event card, were you? Just wait 'til I need to airlift someone.

Right, operation birthday plans is officially underway. Poppy, Leo, tell me, how excited are you both for Grandma’s birthday next month? On a scale of one to a very, very sparkly unicorn? A sparkly,  rainbow  unicorn, Mummy! Grandma’s going to be so old! Old like...a dinosaur? Can dinosaurs have birthdays? Well, dinosaurs probably had… celebrations of some sort, darling. But Grandma’s not quite dinosaur-old. She’s just… experienced! And we need to make it a really special day for her. I was thinking a picnic, weather permitting? We could go to Grantchester meadows. Yay! Can we have cake with sprinkles? And balloons! Lots and lots of balloons! And sandwiches! With crusts cut off! Of course, my loves. Crusts off for the little man. Now, speaking of special days, did you both enjoy the CBeebies pantomime yesterday? The one with the princess and the grumpy badger? I liked the princess! She had a sparkly crown and sang a very good song. The badger was silly! He kept falling over! He said, "Oh dear, oh dear, I've dropped my pear!" He did, didn't he? That's a classic badger saying! "Oh dear, oh dear, I’ve dropped my pear." Remember when I told you that nursery rhyme about the farmer and the bear? It's similar, isn’t it? Yes! Like, “Oh dear, oh dear, I’ve lost my bear!” Did bears really get lost? In stories, darling. It’s just a way of telling a silly tale. It’s a bit like those stories on CBeebies, sometimes. They make things up! Like, a badger could probably find a pear no problem. They’re very good diggers! I like the stories where the little bear gets rescued! The one with the sparkly stream? That’s a good one. Right, moving on to more pressing matters! World Book Day is next week. Have you thought about what you want to dress up as? A pirate! With a sword! A fairy! With a wand and glitter! Fantastic choices! I’ll get the fairy wings sorted, then. And a slightly less pointy pirate sword for you, darling. We don’t want any accidental pokes. And Mother’s Day isn’t far off either. Any ideas on how we can spoil Mummy? I'll draw you a picture, Mummy! A really, really good one! With lots of colours and… and a rainbow!

Right, so, moving. Still feels a bit… bonkers, doesn’t it? Selling up, leaving London… it's a big shift. I keep running through lists in my head – vital things to pack, forms to fill, people to tell. Tell me about it! I'm mostly wrestling with the journalism angle. My editor’s being surprisingly chill about it, given I’m basically relocating to the middle of nowhere. He hinted at remote working, but said I’d need to demonstrate I could still cover regional stories. Which, fair enough. Middle of nowhere is a bit harsh, isn’t it, Liv? There are lovely villages around there. And Mark, you’ll be closer to proper countryside for your cycling. That's a massive plus. Think fresh air, not smog! I appreciate the optimism, Chloe. The cycling is definitely a draw. But I'm used to being able to order practically anything at 2 am. What happens when I fancy a specific kind of obscure cheese at 2 am? I'm genuinely worried. You're concerned about cheese availability? Seriously? You’re an engineer, you can probably build a cheese-dispensing machine by then. Don't tempt me! Though, seriously, the practicalities are stressing me out. And leaving behind… well, everyone. I’ll miss you two, naturally. And the pub quizzes. We'll come and visit! It won't be the same without your epic knowledge of obscure 80s trivia, but we’ll make it work. And I’m sure there’ll be pubs with quizzes in your new area. Maybe you’ll become a local legend! It’s not just about pubs, though, is it, Mark? You’re leaving a good chunk of your social circle. Dating scene’s going to be a challenge, too, I imagine. Don't even get me started. The dating apps are… not inspiring. Endless parade of hiking enthusiasts and people who think "ambitious" means posting inspirational quotes. I’ve started considering adopting a cat just for companionship. Now, that's not so bad. I actually met a really lovely guy through a language exchange app, you know. It’s a bit different, focusing on shared interests rather than just… swiping. You could try something like that. Learn some Norwegian, maybe? Norwegian? I'd need a significant amount of convincing to dedicate myself to learning Norwegian for dating purposes. Is it particularly good for attracting a partner?

Honestly, this book was a bit of a slog, wasn't it? All that descriptive prose about the wildflowers - lovely, I suppose, but I just wanted  something  to happen! Still, at least the biscuits are good. Did you manage to snag any of those lavender ones, Chloe? They  are  rather lovely, aren't they? Fiona outdid herself. And yes, I got two! Though, battling Margaret for them was a bit of a sport in itself. She’s got a surprisingly aggressive streak when it comes to lavender shortbread. Margaret’s always been like that! Remember when she tried to claim all the bouncy balls at Sarah’s fifth birthday party? Ruined the whole thing, basically. She just hoarded them all in her arms, wouldn't let anyone else near! Oh my goodness, yes! I’d completely forgotten about the bouncy ball incident. That’s just… classic Margaret. We were all trying to get a turn and she had this look on her face like she’d won the lottery. It's amazing how fiercely children can defend a plastic sphere. Speaking of childhoods, does anyone else remember those Spirograph sets? Those were  the  thing, weren't they? Absolutely! I had one with the little plastic gears. Spent hours making those repetitive, hypnotic patterns. My mum used to get so cross because I'd leave them all over the carpet. Did you have one, Fiona? I did, love! And I was terrible at it. I never got the patterns to look right. Always ended up with these messy, wobbly things. My sister, Emily, she was brilliant. She could create these intricate designs. Always showing off, she was! Always had to be the best at everything. Sisters, eh? It’s a universal tale. I was always battling my brother, Tom, for the remote control. It was a constant power struggle. Although, I have to say, Tom's gone to learn Italian now. Apparently, he’s quite fluent. It’s rather impressive, really. Italian! That  is  impressive. I wish I had the time. I tried to learn Spanish at university, but I just couldn’t stick with it. All those conjugations! It's just… daunting. You know, I've always been fascinated by regional dialects. I've noticed you both have very distinct ways of speaking. Fiona, you have that very clipped, almost formal tone - very London, isn't it? Well, I grew up in Peterborough, love.

Right then, where were we? Ah yes, the Lake District. Honestly, it was just… glorious. Absolutely glorious. Sheila kept saying how much she loved it, bless her, but I think even she was a bit taken aback by the scenery. You were both gone for a full week, weren’t you? A proper break. Did you manage to do any walking? Dad, you always say you'll hike up Scafell Pike… Well, the Pike was a bit ambitious this time, love. My knees weren’t having any of it. Sheila kept nudging me, though. “Come on, Derek, just a little peak!” she'd say. But no, I stuck to the easier trails around Keswick. Did see a fantastic view, though, of Derwentwater. Just breathtaking. Sheila got some lovely photos. Aye, I did! Loads of ‘em. And you shouldn’t be discounting those peaks entirely, Derek. A gentle stroll, that’s all you need. Remind you of the old days, doesn’t it? When we used to tackle them! Sounds amazing. Keswick, you say? I’ve heard good things. Sheila, did you try any of the local Grasmere gingerbread? I’ve heard it's legendary. Legendary it is! I’m practically powered by gingerbread now. Bought a whole bag to bring back, you know. . Here, have a piece. Fresh, still. Mmm, delicious! Thanks, Sheila. So, what else did you get up to? Just walking and gingerbread? No, no. We went on a boat trip on the lake. Quite relaxing, that was. Though a couple of the tourists were a bit… enthusiastic about waving at everything. Gave me a headache, to be honest. And we visited that Beatrix Potter museum. Sheila’s a big fan, you know. Oh, right! Peter Rabbit and all that. Did you buy any of the little figurines? Don’t be daft! Derek would have had a fit. No, I just had a good look around. It's surprisingly interesting, actually. They've got loads of her original illustrations. And we had a lovely pub lunch on the last day. Proper Yorkshire pudding. You always find the best pubs! What about the weather? The Lake District is notoriously unpredictable. Surprisingly good, actually. We had a couple of drizzly mornings, but mostly it was sunny with just a few fluffy clouds. Perfect for those scenic photos Sheila was taking. Couldn’t have asked for better, really. Just wish my knees hadn’t been creaking quite so much.

Right, that’s a decent brew. Needed it. Woke up feeling like I’d wrestled a badger all night. That overtime on the Davies project is killing me. Sounds rough, Liam. You know, you really do need to prioritize sleep. You're turning a rather alarming shade of grey. And badger wrestling isn't a listed skill on your CV, is it? Morning, you two! Grey badger wrestler. That's going in my next article, I’m calling it "The Trials of the Midlands Engineer." Catchy, right? Very funny, Chloe. It’s not exactly glamorous, is it? It's mostly spreadsheets and structural calculations, trying to convince Mr. Henderson that reinforced concrete  is  a good idea. He still thinks wood is the future, you know. Henderson? He still wears a tweed jacket in July. Honestly. Are you thinking about taking some holiday soon, Liam? You’ve been burning the candle at both ends. I'd love to, honestly. Just… the budget's a bit tight at the moment. That new phone is already draining me. Had to get the latest one, you know, for site visits and stuff. The camera's surprisingly good. Speaking of new phones, did you see that Selena Gomez is apparently using some AI filter that makes her look twenty years younger? The internet is losing it. It's creating a whole new level of unrealistic beauty standards. Ugh, don't even get me started. It's ridiculous. I’m trying to teach my Year 7s about media literacy, and they’re completely saturated with this stuff. It’s hard to explain that what they see online isn't always reality. It’s the same with everything, isn’t it? Trying to cut through the noise. Speaking of noise, did you catch the news about the potential rail strikes? Dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. I need to be in London next month for a conference. Looks like I might be in serious trouble if that happens. I’ll have to look into alternative transport. Trains are a nightmare even  without  strikes. Why don’t you come with me to that pottery class next week? It’s really relaxing, and a good way to de-stress. Actually, Liam, you should come too. You look like you could do with some mindful clay shaping. Pottery? Seriously? I’m more of a ‘building bridges, not miniature pots’ kind of guy. Although... I do need to switch off.

Honestly, it feels so weird saying goodbye already. Like, this is just… a normal Thursday night, isn't it? Except Reg’s heading off to Saudi Arabia. It doesn't feel real. Yeah, it’s a bit of a leap. One minute he's moaning about needing a new shelf for the garage, the next he's swapping Merseyside for desert heat. It’s mental. At least he's getting good money. More than he’d be earning here, that's for sure. Did he tell you about the accommodation? Apparently, it's pretty swanky. Swanky? Sounds like he’s gonna be livin’ like a king. Still, Saudi? That's a long way. Bloke needs to keep his wits about him over there. Different kettle of fish, innit? Aye, that’s right, lad. Different kettle of fish altogether. Don’t be goin' thinkin’ it's all sunshine and roses, though. Bit of culture shock, that. He needs to be respectful, do his research. Read up on it, Reg. Don’t go makin’ a fool of yourself, eh? He's been reading, Dad, don't worry. He’s obsessed with Google Maps, actually. He’s been meticulously plotting every possible journey he might need to take. It’s quite amusing. Keeps saying he needs to be prepared for anything. Seriously? Even in the desert? I thought he'd have relied on the sat nav for that. He did, initially. But then he realized sat navs can be unreliable, especially in places he’s never been before. He went down a rabbit hole of topographical maps and three-dimensional perspectives on Google Earth. He’s analysing terrain, road layouts… It’s a bit intense. You’re havin’ him on, yeah? Like, charting the sand dunes? Pretty much! He’s even labelled potential emergency stopping points in case he gets a flat tyre. It’s ridiculous, but also… impressive? Proper Liverpool thing, that is. Always plannin’ for the worst. Keeps you safe. Reminds me of when I was stationed in Germany. Never left home without a fully charged map reader and a compass. Technology's great, but never trust it completely. Speaking of technology, remember when we tried to navigate to Uncle Barry's last Christmas using  just  Google Maps? Ended up on a farm track surrounded by sheep. Oh my god, I'd completely forgotten! Thought we were gonna be stuck there forever!

Bloody brilliant colour, isn’t it? Makes you wonder how they get this intensity. I’ve been trying to replicate it in my own garden back home, but… well, New Zealand soil isn't exactly Swedish, is it? Everything seems to struggle a bit. How are you both feeling, by the way? I've been battling this persistent tickle in my throat. Feels like something's caught, you know? It's lovely here, isn’t it? Absolutely stunning. And honestly, I’m feeling alright, a bit tired, teaching always drains me. But nothing a good cup of tea and a walk amongst these beauties can't fix. The tickle, though… have you tried honey and lemon? It cleared up a horrible cough I had last autumn. Old wives' tales, mostly, I know, but sometimes they work! And are you still using that organic hand sanitizer you were raving about? I swear my hands were cracking from all the handwashing at school. Honey and lemon’s always a good shout, Claire. And yes, Mark, I’ve noticed you’ve been clearing your throat a lot. Are you getting enough sleep? You’ve been pushing yourself hard with that new venture, haven’t you? I'm feeling okay, although I may have overdone it last night. That networking dinner ran late, and the canapés… well, let’s just say they weren't exactly nourishing. Need to be better about looking after myself, honestly. These orchids are fascinating, though. Did you know some species are mycorrhizal? They have symbiotic relationships with fungi… Symbiotic relationships, eh? Sounds about right for my life these days. One thing relying on another just to stay upright. Sleep? Don’t mention sleep! I'd love to get eight hours, but between the business and trying to keep the house from falling down around my ears... it’s a pipe dream. And yes, I’m still using that hand sanitizer, Willow. It’s a godsend. Turns out, my risk aversion extends to microscopic organisms too! Regarding the orchids, fascinating, but slightly overwhelming. Give me a good old-fashioned fern any day. Something sturdy and dependable. You and your ferns, Mark! You’re such a creature of habit. It's endearing, really. So, Willow, anything exciting happening in your world of communications? You were telling me about a new campaign last week... Oh, it’s coming together nicely, actually. It involves a sustainable clothing brand - very eco-conscious, focused on traceability and ethical sourcing.

Honestly, this voice recognition thing is useless. I was just trying to dictate a quick email to my tutor, and it kept turning "Gillingham" into "willing ham." Willing ham! Where would you even  get  willing ham? Gillingham, eh? Lovely little town. Used to get the train through there on my way to see my aunt in Margate. Strong accent you’ve got, love. Proper Kentish. Don’t let them technology things erase it. It is a strong accent, Daisy. You can hear the estuary in it immediately. Mine's faded a bit, living in Essex all these years. Though my mum, bless her, never changed a bit. Still sounds like she was born and bred in Harlow, even now. It’s funny, isn’t it? How the sound of your voice can just tie you to a place. My mum always said I sounded like a chimney sweep. Rough, apparently. Didn't exactly make me feel brilliant, did it? Oh, stop being so dramatic, Mark. Chimney sweeps didn't even have accents. They were just… dirty. Besides, Dad’s been going on and on about the ‘proper’ London accent. Says mine sounds like I'm trying too hard to be posh. He wouldn’t be entirely wrong, love. There’s a difference between being proud of where you come from and trying to mimic something you’re not. I used to have a bit more of a Cockney twang when I was younger, spent a lot of time down the market, you see. It’s drifted away over the years. Speaking of drifting away, how’s things with you and Liam, Daisy? You seemed a bit quiet at dinner. Not great, to be honest. He's…distant. Says he needs space. Says I’m too clingy. Which is rich coming from a man who spends all day glued to his Minecraft world. Space to do what? Build more digital blocks? Come on! Now, now, Mark. Leave the young lady be. Relationships are tricky things. Takes patience, they do. Don't go rushing into conclusions. Easy for you to say, Dad. You haven't been in a relationship in... well, ever really. And Liam's been drinking more lately, too. Not loads, but a bit too much for my liking. Drinking  more ? Daisy, you need to be careful. You’ve got to protect yourself. I’ve seen it happen too many times. I know, I know.

Right, nearly ready. Just needs a bit more seasoning. Honestly, this béchamel is being a right pain tonight. It keeps splitting! Anyone want more wine while I wrestle with this sauce? Nah, I'm good, Mum. Just finishing this level. It’s proper stressful. "Proper stressful" playing on your phone? Try making hollandaise sauce when you’ve got a room full of hungry teenage boys expecting a decent supper. That’s stressful. You know, I’m attempting Baked Alaska for dessert. Think you and Finn can handle grating the cheese for the base? It’s a ridiculous amount. Baked Alaska? Seriously? That’s… ambitious. And grating cheese? That's boring. Can't we just have pizza? Absolutely not. This is "Supper with the Boys" – a tradition. And traditions demand Baked Alaska. Plus, it’s good practice. You need to learn basic culinary skills, darling. You can’t live on Deliveroo forever. Reminds me of when your Dad tried to make a trifle back in uni... utter chaos. The custard split, the jelly wobbled... Dad’s cooking is legendary for its disasters. He tried to carve a pumpkin for the Halloween party last year and gave himself a paper cut. A rather significant paper cut, I recall. Anyway, Halloween! Are you and Finn sorted for costumes? We're still finalizing the decorations. I’m leaning towards a Victorian séance theme. Creepy but classy, you know? Finn’s going as a zombie. I’m being... undecided. Something low effort, probably. Sarah’s going as a witch, she’s already got the hat sorted. It’s got, like, actual moving parts apparently. Moving parts? Goodness. Right, cheese grating duty then. And while you’re doing that, Finn, could you pop the bread for the croutons in the oven? Speaking of things changing… I’m having a nightmare recruiting for the new project. Everyone seems to think they’re entitled to a six-figure salary straight out of university. Six figures? Wow. That’s… a lot. It is! And the attitude! Honestly, the entitlement... reminds me a bit of the arguments we had when you were younger, insisting you  needed  that particular limited-edition video game. It’s frustrating to deal with. It's not just about experience, it’s about willingness to learn, a good work ethic... things that seem to be disappearing. People just want the easy money now, I guess. Everything's different.

Cor, this is lovely, this is. Proper Welsh breakfast, innit? You’ve outdone yourself, love. Though, a bit much bacon for a Tuesday, wouldn't you say? It's a Tuesday relaxer, Bronwyn! You've been working yourself ragged with those postgraduate dissertations. Besides, you said you weren’t eating enough. Remember? You were practically fading away last time you were down. Aye, well, deadlines do that to a body, don’t they? Still, fades a bit less gracefully Yorkshire folk, I reckon. So, New York… you were saying? You went without me? Feel a bit left out, I do. Don't be daft. It was a whirlwind conference trip. Very academic, very serious. Lots of PowerPoints and very little sightseeing. Though, I did manage to sneak in a Broadway show – “Wicked.” Absolutely brilliant. You would have loved it. "Wicked," eh? Never been much for musicals, myself. Give me a good Brontë novel any day. So, what was the point of the trip then? Some newfangled theory on post-structuralism or somethin'? Something like that, yes. Though, it actually involved a fascinating cross-section of linguistic theory and… well, it’s complicated. Remember how we talked about the nuances of regional dialect drift? It tied into that. Anyway, it was exhausting. I’m glad to be back in Swansea and avoiding transatlantic flights for a while. Speaking of which, have you made any progress with your flying lessons? Oh, the flying lessons. That’s a story in itself, that is. The instructor, Barry, he’s a lovely lad, but he keeps calling me “Captain.” Captain Bronwyn! Like I’m Amelia Earhart or somethin’. And I stall the plane every time we practice a landing. Every. Single. Time. He doesn't seem unduly concerned, mind. Said I've got a "natural knack for disorientation." Charming. Disorientation, eh? Sounds like you could benefit from a bit more mindfulness. Maybe try some meditation? Meditation? While I'm three thousand feet in the air, plummeting towards a field of sheep? I don't think so, love. Right, what’s the plan for today then? You promised to show me that new coastal path you were raving about. Absolutely! We can pack a picnic. And afterwards, I was thinking we could pop down to the post box. I need to send a letter to my cousin Huw. It’s proper old-fashioned, I know. I hate that everything goes online these days.

Right, "Quixotic." Ten points. I'm officially declaring you all hopeless. And frankly, I'm still livid about arriving half an hour late. The train was a nightmare. Oh, relax, Ben. You're always late. It’s practically a signature move. Besides, it gave me time to strategize. Which, by the way, is why I just used "Zloty" and snagged a double word score. Twenty-eight points! Beat that. Twenty-eight? That’s… respectable. But not impressive. I just laid down "Jejune." Fifteen points. And a triple letter score on that J. See? Paying attention in sixth form finally came in handy. Although, I still have no idea what 'jejune' actually  means . It means juvenile, apparently. Or lacking in depth. Like… most of our current Scrabble tactics. Seriously, we're all just throwing letters at the board. Where’s the artistry? Artistry? It’s Scrabble, Dan. It’s about vocab and maximizing points. Speaking of which, I’ve got a “Zenith” here... placement is crucial. You’re taking this far too seriously! It's just a bit of fun. Remember when we were kids, and we’d argue about whether 'ye' was a proper word? Because it's like 'the' but older, right? Oh god, yes! My mum used to spend ages searching for the etymology of everything. Turns out 'ye' was just an archaic form of 'the' – Old English, you know. Always loved that little linguistic rabbit hole.
