My mum was obsessed with children's books. Specifically, those really long, flowery ones by Rosemary Sutcliff. Remember  The Eagle of the Ninth ? I struggled with that at A-levels. It was like reading a history thesis disguised as a story. Rosemary Sutcliff! Yes! Utterly brilliant, but no one reads those properly anymore. Everyone's into Harry Potter and dystopian fiction. I'm doing a module on Victorian Literature this year, so I'm constantly having to brush up on Austen and Dickens. It's fascinating, but sometimes I just want something simple. Victorian Literature sounds intense. What are you specialising in, Ben? English Literature, naturally. I'm leaning towards a dissertation on the evolving portrayal of the working class in 19th-century novels. It’s a bit dry, I admit. How's that culinary course going, Tom? Are you conquering the world of fancy foams and reductions? Conquering might be a strong word. I'm currently trying to perfect a decent hollandaise sauce without it curdling.

Cor blimey, this rain, eh? Proper biblical, it is. Haven't seen it this thick since… well, since I can't rightly remember. Brings back memories, though. Damp mornings, huddled up, waiting for the buses. It  is  something, isn't it? Glad we’re inside, anyway. Though I do feel a little guilty keeping the bird feeders full. They must be soaked through out there. I’ll pop some more seed out in a minute. Fancy a cuppa, Arthur? A cuppa? Don't mind if I do, Marjorie. Strong, mind. Like me blood. And a biscuit, if you've got 'em. Those ginger snaps you made last week were ever so nice. Right then. Ginger snaps aplenty. Though I might have nibbled a few already... Don't tell anyone. So, anything on your mind today? You’ve been unusually quiet, other than commenting on the weather, which, frankly, we all know is dreadful. Just thinkin’, Marjorie. Thinkin’ about young Timmy down the street. Heard his daughter, Sarah, had a bit of a wobbler at school today. Said she’s being bullied. Oh, dear. That's awful. Poor Sarah. What a dreadful thing for a child to go through. Bullying... it never changes, does it? I saw my share of it in Harrow, believe you me. Not necessarily physical, mind. More subtle. Snide remarks, being left out… it cuts just as deep. Aye, cuts deep it does. Remember old Reginald at the school? Always picking on little Derek. Skinny lad, Derek was. Never stood a chance. Always came home with a tear in ‘is eye. Teachers didn't seem to notice, much. They rarely did, did they? Too busy with the 'important' things. Ofsted inspections and test scores. Children's feelings were secondary. That’s why I loved childminding, in a way. I could really  see  them. See when they were happy, when they were sad, when something was bothering them. You were good at it, you were. All the little ones loved you. Always had a smile on your face, even when Mrs. Peterson’s little terror, Rupert, was paintin’ the walls. Rupert  was  a handful! But even he had his moments of sweetness. It’s easy to forget, when you’re dealing with tantrums and sticky fingers. You know, I wonder what Sarah’s parents are doing about it? Have they spoken to the school? That’s what I was thinkin’.

These are absolutely cracking, Annie. Honestly, you’ve outdone yourself. Better than my Doris used to make, and that's saying something. She was a dab hand in the kitchen, my Doris. Oh, Dad, you always say that! And Doris was lovely, but I think Annie's roast potatoes are a pretty strong contender. A little rosemary, you see, makes all the difference. Are you feeling alright, though? You seemed a bit quiet earlier. Just a bit tired, love. This whole holiday's been a whirlwind. So lovely to see you both though, really. It’s been far too long. And that Devon air…does a body good. Though my knees are reminding me I'm not a spring chicken anymore. You're not old, Michael. Just... seasoned. And the exercise walks we've been doing have been good for you. Remember how you were complaining about your walking last year? You're powering along now! Well, a bit of fresh air and some prompting from you both does wonders. Not like back in the day, though. I used to be halfway up Snowdon before breakfast. You’re exaggerating, Dad. Slightly. So, Mum, have you had a chance to properly look at this 'FitTrack' app I told you about? It's really quite clever, tracks everything. Calories, steps, even monitors your sleep. I have, yes. It did seem a bit… intensive, didn’t it? All those reminders and notifications. I'm not sure I need my phone telling me to ‘hydrate’ every hour. I rather like to decide that for myself, thank you very much. That’s what you can adjust, Mum! You can tone down the notifications. It's brilliant for planning meals, though. I used it to work out the macros for this roast, actually. Ensuring a good balance of protein and carbs. Macros? What are we talking about now? Sounds like some sort of government agency. It's just… nutrients, Dad. Protein, carbohydrates, fats. It’s a way of understanding what your body needs. It's not vital, of course, but it's interesting. It’s impressive that you've found something so useful, love. Speaking of interesting, did you see that article in the  Western Times ? About the new train station finally opening? They’re saying it’s going to be next month! Really? About time too! After all those delays! I remember when they first announced it.

Right, so, that seminar this morning… absolute disaster. Professor Davies decided to spend thirty minutes arguing the merits of iambic pentameter in  Richard III  while ignoring the fact half the class hadn't even read it. Seriously, I saw Liam openly yawning. Davies, eh? Typical. He always gets carried away with the Shakespeare stuff. I swear, he thinks we’re all vying to be the next Ian McKellen. You’d almost think  he  wanted to be the next Ian McKellen. Almost! It’s like he’s forgotten we’re learning about literary theory, not auditioning for the RSC. Speaking of theatrical ambitions, did you see that production of  Hamlet  on BBC Two last week? Decent, but a bit heavy on the brooding, wasn't it? Yeah, a bit. I thought the scenery was stunning though. Really captured the atmosphere. But honestly, I'd rather be gaming right now. That new Cyberpunk DLC just dropped. Oh, don't even start. My bank account is weeping. I promise myself I'm cutting back, but then… shiny new things! How's your stag do planning going? Jamie’s already badgering everyone about dares. I’m expecting some truly mortifying stories. Don't remind me. He wants a full-blown escape room scenario involving a cardboard cutout of the groom and strategically placed rubber chickens. It's... ambitious. I'm suggesting we book a brewery tour somewhere in Wales, eh? Something a bit more sophisticated. Less chance of arrest. Sophisticated for Jamie? That's ambitious in itself. A brewery tour sounds sensible though. Less potential for Instagram disasters. You know, I was reading this article the other day about the political fallout from that reshuffle. Absolute chaos. Tell me about it. My mum's been glued to the news all week. She's fuming about X, Y, and Z. Says the whole thing is a distraction from the real issues. Like, you know, the cost of living crisis. Exactly! And it's all swirling around Europe too, isn’t it? Feels like Brexit is still hanging over everything, even though it's been ages. It always will be. A permanent stain, probably. Speaking of things that won't go away, have you been to that new Italian place on Cryws Road yet? Apparently, the pizza is incredible. No, not yet! I saw it the other day. Worth a try? I’m starving. Uni food is doing my head in.

Honestly, this place is buzzing! I didn’t expect Greens to be this busy on a Thursday. It's a good thing you messaged, or we’d never have got a table. Tell me about it! Cambourne's definitely growing. It was practically a ghost town last time I was here. Glad I managed to snag this one though. It feels nice to actually  see  you, face-to-face. It’s been ages since Oxford, hasn't it? Ages! Feels like a lifetime ago, doesn't it? How are things in the marketing world? Still drowning in spreadsheets? You have  no  idea. Pearson is... Pearson. Always a challenge. The new campaign for the textbooks is basically consuming my life. Lots of late nights, lots of PowerPoint presentations. But, you know, the team's good, so it's manageable. How's the project coordination going? Still keeping everything running smoothly? Generally, yes. We’ve finally got the Henderson account wrapped up, which is a massive relief. It was a nightmare of shifting deadlines and conflicting demands. Seriously, the director of Henderson seemed to change his mind every five minutes. Learned a lot, though. And now I'm onto the Davies project, which, fingers crossed, is going to be a bit less chaotic. Fingers crossed indeed. You deserve a bit of calm after Henderson! So, tell me everything that's been happening. Last I heard, you weren't having the best time with… Liam, was it? Liam. Yes. Liam. It's officially over. Done. Kaput. We had the conversation last month. Turns out, “needing space” meant he was seeing someone else. Classic. Oh, no! Seriously? I’m so sorry, love. I knew there was something off about him. He always seemed a bit… bland. Bland is generous. He was beige. And actively avoided any sort of spontaneity. But, you know, I’d invested a lot of time, so… foolishly held on. It’s been a bit rough, but honestly, I feel lighter. It's like a weight’s been lifted. I can imagine. You have to be so careful, don’t you? It’s so easy to get caught up. Speaking of guys… any new contenders on the horizon? Not yet! I'm deliberately avoiding anything serious. Concentrating on work and my pottery classes. It’s actually quite therapeutic. Have you seen my last vase? It’s  almost  presentable. Pottery? That’s brilliant!

Right, that's done its job! Fancy a builder's brew, love? Strong enough to stand a spoon up in, like me mam used to make. Coming! Just finishing up this quick reading. Yeah, builders brew sounds perfect. Needed. This Derrida's a right headache, you know? Abstract as anything. Derrida, eh? Sounds fancy. More fancy than me mam’s tea, that’s for sure. So, how’s the PhD going otherwise? Still drowning in philosophical jargon? Basically. It's…challenging. But I'm making progress, slowly but surely. Found a really interesting connection between his ideas on language and…well, that’s a long story. You wouldn’t be interested. Try me. I manage research projects all day; I can handle a long story. Besides, a good cuppa always helps. Got the biscuits out, haven't I? Alright, alright. It’s about how Derrida’s deconstruction of language – this idea that language can’t ever fully capture meaning – actually has parallels with how we understand plant communication. Plant communication? Now you've got my attention. Honestly, I thought plants were just, well, plant-y. Doing their own thing. It's fascinating! It turns out they communicate chemically, through their roots, and even through airborne signals. These signals are incredibly subtle, context-dependent, and often ambiguous. Like, one signal could mean ‘danger’ to one plant and ‘attract pollinators’ to another, depending on the situation. It’s a constant negotiation of meaning, just like language, but without a fixed system to decode it. Blimey. So, it's all a bit…fluid then? Nothing’s set in stone, like you said about Derrida? Exactly! It challenges the idea of a stable, objective reality. Just like Derrida challenges the idea of a fixed, stable meaning in language. I’m arguing that thinking about plant communication through a Derridean lens can give us new insight into ecological relationships. You're trying to use philosophy to understand...grass? That's brilliant, love! Seriously. It's like me trying to explain the complexities of user behaviour using statistical analysis. Seems a bit mad at first glance, but there's logic somewhere. Precisely! And it’s made me think about our own garden, actually. I’ve been wanting to get a miniature ecosystem going, you know, a little wildlife haven in pots. Oh, that’s a grand idea! Remember that lavender I brought back from Whitby? It’s gone mental!

Well, Gwyn, another Monday looms. Did you manage to salvage a decent weekend? The rain, of course, was relentless. Nearly ruined my attempt at deadheading the roses. Salvaged is a good word for it, Alistair. Salvaged! The rain was biblical, honestly. My allotment looked like the Amazon rainforest by Saturday afternoon. Managed to get some leeks in, though. Solid leeks. Nothing fancy, mind. Just good honest leeks. How were the roses holding up then? You've got a prize-winning collection, don't you? They’re soldiering on, thank you. A bit waterlogged, but resilient, like…well, like a good Welshman, I suppose. I was watching that programme on Sunday about all the footballers’ children. Quite remarkable how many are trying to follow in their fathers’ footsteps, isn't it? Some are showing promise, others… well, let's just say they’re benefiting more from the name than the skill. Aye, it’s a strange one, isn’t it? The pressure must be immense. Remember that lad, Ryan Giggs' son? He’s giving it a go at Manchester United’s academy, isn’t he? Seems a decent talent, although, naturally, he's got a lot to prove. It's not all about genetics, is it? I saw Mark Selby playing snooker on Saturday, too. Brilliant stuff. He's a master of the long game, that one. Selby! An absolute craftsman. I’m rather enjoying watching him. I used to be quite keen on snooker myself, back in my student days. Sadly, the priorities shift as one matures, you know? More marking, less potting. How’s the mountain of student essays progressing for you? Mine are a veritable deluge. The history students seem particularly prone to sweeping generalisations this year. Don't even mention it! I'm wading through a sea of poorly researched arguments on the Welsh Disestablishment. Honestly, some of them haven't even bothered to look at primary sources! It’s disheartening. Although, I did discover one student who’s shown remarkable aptitude for understanding the nuances of Gladstone’s position. A bright spark, that one. It reminds you why you bother, doesn't it? Absolutely. There's always one or two who genuinely surprise you. I was reading about the increased entry requirements for the police and armed forces. Seems they are making it deliberately difficult to get in now. Massive psychological aptitude tests, rigorous physical assessments… That's right.

Right then, let’s have a proper chat. Poppy, love, are you hungry? Fancy a biscuit? Yes, please! Chocolate one! And can we draw after? I wanna draw a princess! Of course, darling. Chocolate biscuit it is. Now, your mum's been on the phone again. Still going on about the Christening. Mum's been on the phone? What’s she rabbiting on about  now ? Probably about the canapés again. Honestly, she’ll have a breakdown if the vol-au-vents aren’t perfectly symmetrical. Don't exaggerate, love. She just wants it to be special for little Willow. And to be fair, she's doing a  lot  of organising. I’m trying to spread the load, but she's got a very specific vision. A  very  specific vision involving ten different shades of cream and a string quartet. I get it, it's a big deal. Have you managed to wrangle Auntie Brenda away from her prize-winning begonias long enough for her to make a speech? Trying. She keeps saying the begonias need deadheading. Apparently, that takes precedence over a celebratory address. I’ve promised her a guided tour of Lichfield Cathedral gardens afterwards. That seemed to appease her somewhat. What's a speech? Is it like a story? It's like a story, sweetie, but grown-up. People say nice things about Willow. Right, but prepare for a long, rambling anecdote about Brenda’s childhood pet hamster. It's practically a family tradition. Speaking of family, what’s the plan for Grandma’s birthday next month? Have we booked a table anywhere? I was thinking The Oak Room. They do a lovely Sunday lunch and she always enjoys it there. I've booked a table for twelve. Should be nice and relaxed. Good choice! Though twelve people is a  lot  to wrangle. You'll need a tactical plan for dessert distribution. Remember Uncle Geoff attempting to steal the trifle last year? Don’t remind me! I had to physically restrain him. Actually, I think I’ll discreetly purchase an extra trifle. Just in case. Can I have some trifle? Please, please, please? We'll see, Poppy. It's for Grandma's birthday. But there  might  be a tiny sneaky spoonful. So, work’s still causing you grief, then? You mentioned it on the phone. It is. Mrs. Hawthorne is being particularly difficult. Honestly, she seems to delight in finding fault.

Honestly, this drizzle is relentless, isn’t it? Feels like it’s been raining non-stop for a week. Though, I suppose it's better than snow. Remember that Christmas a few years back? Being snowed in wasn’t exactly ideal. Oh, don’t remind me! The kids were bouncing off the walls, and we ran out of bread on Boxing Day. That was a classic. How’s work been, though? Still the same old chaos at the shop? Pretty much. We're getting ready for the spring collections, which is always a flurry of activity. The new stock arrives daily, and the display needs constant tweaking. It’s rewarding, but exhausting. Speaking of rewarding, how's little Poppy doing? Last I heard she was attempting to learn the recorder. I can play 'Twinkle, Twinkle'! She can! She's not exactly Mozart, but she's enthusiastic, isn’t she? She's been obsessed with New York lately too. All because of that cartoon about the squirrels. Squirrels in New York? That’s a new one. Speaking of New York… we really need to solidify some dates and start looking at flights, don't we? It feels like we’ve been talking about it forever. I know! I've been looking at some apartments on Airbnb. I found one in Greenwich Village, right near Washington Square Park. It’s got a great balcony, and it’s walkable to loads of places. What do you think? Greenwich Village sounds lovely! Balcony's a must. Imagine, coffee and croissants overlooking the park… perfect. Let’s pull up the listing and have a proper look. What about flights? Have you had a chance to compare prices? I did a quick search yesterday. Direct flights are surprisingly expensive, especially for the dates we were thinking of. But I saw a few options with a layover in Amsterdam that were significantly cheaper. Would you be up for that? Not terribly, I must admit. But if it saves a substantial amount of money... We could use the extra for theatre tickets, couldn't we? Remember our wedding? We didn’t have a penny left after paying for everything! Oh, our wedding! That was such a beautiful day. The flowers, the sunshine... even Uncle Geoff's slightly embarrassing rendition of 'Brown Eyed Girl'. He really did go for it, didn't he? And the cake! That was truly magnificent.

Right, so, this is… this is the current state of affairs. It's a bit of a mess, innit? I've been trying to get my head around this postgraduate funding application, specifically the evidence they want about my previous research. It's like they're deliberately trying to make it difficult, aren't they? Tell me about it. Funding applications are a special kind of torture. Salford’s alright for student life, but the funding process feels like it was designed by someone who's never actually  been  a student. What's tripping you up specifically? Looks like you've got, what, a dissertation chapter, a conference abstract, and... is that a shopping list? Yeah, the shopping list is unrelated. I was just making a note to get more biscuits. Crucial research fuel, you know. But honestly, it’s just the sheer volume of stuff they want. They want evidence of my analytical skills, my engagement with the literature, my ability to conduct research… It’s all in there somewhere, I swear, but connecting it all feels like piecing together a jigsaw with half the pieces missing. This chapter, for example, it was alright when I wrote it for my undergrad, but does it  really  demonstrate postgraduate-level analysis? That’s the question. Lay it on me, what's the chapter about? Maybe an outside perspective will help. I've been drowning in psychoanalytic theory myself, so at least I understand the level of complexity they're expecting. I'm studying film, remember? So, I’m used to sifting through layers and layers of meaning. It's on the impact of the Industrial Revolution on rural communities in Lancashire. Specifically, I looked at how changes in farming practices affected folk tales and traditions. Bit niche, I know, but my supervisor loved it. I argued that the shift from communal farming to more individualised practices led to a gradual erosion of shared narratives and a sense of collective identity. Right, okay. That’s solid. Sounds like it goes beyond just describing what happened; it’s arguing a causal relationship. That’s good. They're looking for that analytical link, yeah? I reckon that's a definitely a postgraduate-level thing. The undergrads I was teaching last year were mostly just recounting events. See, that's what I kept thinking, but writing it down, articulating  why  it's postgraduate level... that’s the hard part.

Right, coffee’s on. Anyone else need a top-up? Still feeling knackered after that presentation today. Prospect Research are really pushing for that Henderson account, you know. It's a big one. Good luck with that. Sounds stressful. I need the caffeine too, thanks. Little ones were a whirlwind today. Poppy kept insisting she was a mermaid and Finn was a pirate battling a giant squid. Squid! Big squid! Arrrgh! The squid has me! Woosh! Sounds like a lively classroom. More interesting than spreadsheets, that's for sure. Speaking of interesting… I had a proper weird dream last night. Oh? Do tell. Last night I dreamt I was giving a lecture to a room full of squirrels wearing tiny graduation hats. It was utterly bizarre. You always have the best dreams! Mine was… I was on a game show. But the prize was… a pet shop. A massive one, filled with every animal you could imagine. And the host was Alan Carr. Alan Carr? That’s wonderfully random. Did you win? No! I bottled it. They asked me what kind of pet I'd get, and my brain just blanked. I said… a pineapple. A pineapple! And lost the entire pet shop. It was mortifying in the dream, honestly. Pineapple pet! Silly! Gimme a dog! See? That’s what you should have said! A dog! Both of them are practically begging for one. Don’t you think we should finally do it? I keep seeing these gorgeous labradoodles… I know, I know. I’ve been thinking about it too. But it’s a big responsibility. Walks, vet bills… the house would be covered in fur. Remember how much work it was when your Auntie Brenda's poodle came to stay? That was different. That was for a week. This would be a permanent member of the family. I think Poppy and Finn have missed having a furry friend around since we moved here. Look at them, they’re practically vibrating with excitement at the thought of a dog. Doggy! Play! Fetch! Walkies! Belly rubs! Alright, alright. You’re wearing me down. It’s just… money’s been a bit tight lately, hasn’t it? With the school trips, and Poppy’s dance classes… We'd manage. We always do. And… I was looking at those lottery numbers last night. Honestly, just a whim, but… what if we won a decent amount?

Och, I’m tellin’ ya, it were rank. Absolutely rank. The wait, the smell… like disinfectant and despair, mixed wi' a whiff o' microwaved lasagne. Honestly. Right, well, you’re here now. Safe and sound. And I've managed to find somewhere to park. Less disinfectant, hopefully. How’s the ankle feeling? Still throbbing? Throbbing’s an understatement, lad. It’s like a wee volcano’s erupted in me foot. I can barely put weight on it. Honestly, I thought I’d broken it. Trippin' over that ridiculous gnome in the garden – who puts a gnome  there  anyway? – and the pain just shot right up. A gnome? Seriously? You went to A&E for a gnome-related injury? Don’t you start! It weren’t  just  a gnome, alright? It were a poorly placed, ceramic, smiling gnome. And I were carryin' a bag full o' groceries. Dominate gravity, ye ken? Plus, Mum were panicking. She insisted. "Get it checked, lass! Better safe than sorry!" And here I am, lookin’ like a prize idiot. Well, Mum's got a point, though. It’s better to be safe. Did they X-ray it? Aye, they did. Sat me there for ages, starin’ at the blank wall, surrounded by people coughin' and cryin'. And then the nurse came in and said, “Right, no break, just a bad sprain. Ice and elevat-.” Honestly, the monotonous repetition of “ice and elevate” nearly drove me mad. Like they were programmed. Well, at least it’s not broken. We can get you some decent ice packs, put your foot up. I brought your favourite ginger biscuits. Foot and biscuits – the perfect recovery combo. You’re a good lad, you are. But honestly, the whole A&E experience… it's just awful, isn't it? All those people in pain, distress... and the telly was on some craic show. Really? A game show when folks are properly hurt? I know, it's bizarre. It feels almost… dismissive, doesn't it? Like they’re trying to create some kind of background noise to avoid confronting the seriousness of the situation. It's a system under pressure, I suppose. Overworked and understaffed, everyone saying the same thing. Aye, the nurses were workin’ their socks off, though. You could tell. Just… completely exhausted. I felt awful takin' up their time wi’ a sprained ankle. There was this poor fella wi’ a nasty gash on his arm, lookin’ proper distraught.

Honestly, Bernard, did you see that piece in the Telegraph this morning about the escalating tensions in the South China Sea? Absolute madness, isn’t it? Feels like we're edging closer to something… unpleasant. Aye, saw it. Dreadful, dreadful. Always brewing, isn't it? Never a moment’s peace. Though, to be honest, Harold, my mind’s been preoccupied with something else entirely this week. Something a bit closer to home. Oh? Let me guess, more trouble with that blasted boiler again? You really need to get that sorted, Bernard. It’s bound to explode one of these days. No, no, not the boiler. Though you’re right to worry about that. It’s... well, it's about a business idea, actually. Something I've been mulling over. A business? You? Bernard, you’ve always said you were perfectly content sticking to your antique furniture restoration. What's changed? Well, times change, Harold. And frankly, the restoration business is... slowing down. People aren't as interested in old mahogany these days as they used to be. I've been thinking... seaside experiences, Harold. Remember how popular those quirky little ‘experience’ businesses got a few years back? Escape rooms, axe throwing… Axe throwing? Good heavens, Bernard. What’s seaside got to do with axe throwing? Not axe throwing, silly man! Though, never say never! I was thinking… immersive historical tours. Based on the history of Hove and Brighton. Think costumed guides, interactive displays, maybe even a small-scale recreation of a Victorian pier scene. Something genuinely engaging for tourists. That’s actually… not a bad idea, Bernard. Brighton and Hove have such rich history. The Regency era, the Victorian boom… it's ripe for exploitation, so to speak. Though, “immersive” sounds rather expensive. I’ve done the initial research. It’s manageable. I've found a small property by the seafront, ideally located. It wouldn't require a massive upfront investment. And think of the appeal! Gets people out and about, learning something while they’re having a bit of fun. Plus, I've spoken to old Elsie down at the library, she's offered to help with historical accuracy. She's a fountain of knowledge, that one. Elsie's a gem, yes. Heard she remembers the Blitz like it was yesterday. So, you’re serious about this then? Properly serious? Absolutely. I’ve put together a rough business plan. Found a decent accountant, too.

Honestly, this pub is… interesting, isn't it? It's got a lot of character, I'll give it that. Bit much with the nautical theme though, don't you think? All the anchors and ropes... feels a bit staged. It does, doesn’t it? But I rather like it. It’s got a proper, old-fashioned feel. Much better than those sterile, modern bars popping up everywhere. Reminds me a bit of pubs back in Edinburgh, actually. Not quite the same, of course. What do you reckon we should eat when we’re ready? Fish and chips is obviously the classic choice. Fish and chips sounds lovely, actually. Or maybe a pie? They do a decent steak and ale pie, according to the menu. I'm starving. This transcription work has been relentless today. Six hours straight just listening to legal depositions. Makes you want to curl up with a good blanket and a cup of tea, not a pint of ale. Six hours? Blimey, that's brutal. You deserve a huge pie then. So, pie it is? By the way, did you catch the latest episode of Happy Valley? Oh my God, yes! Absolutely gripping. I’m completely hooked. Catherine Cawood is incredible. Such a complex, flawed character. Honestly, I'm dreading the finale. It’s bound to be devastating. Did you enjoy that scene with the farmer and the chickens? Rather darkly comic, wasn't it? It was! Perfectly pitched black humour. Sarah Lancashire is just phenomenal, as always. Reminds me a bit of that gritty realism they used to strive for at Edinburgh University, you know, in the drama department. Very serious, very intense. Remember Fiona Guthrie? She went on to do some really interesting things in theatre. Fiona Guthrie! Good heavens, I haven’t thought about her in years! We were inseparable at university. Remember those all-nighters in the library fuelled by instant noodles and sheer desperation? The smell of old paper and despair. Absolutely! Those were the days. I’m glad I brought my coat, actually. It’s getting a bit chilly outside. You should have brought yours too. Are you alright? You seem a little cold. I'm fine. Just a slight shiver. I’m usually warmer than this. It’s likely the combination of the cider and being out of the house. Being cooped up transcribing all day makes you feel quite detached.

Ach, this is the ticket, eh, Calum? Proper pint after a dreich day. Feels like November already, doesn’t it? Aye, Ryan. It’s daft, isn’t it? August and you'd think the rain would ease off. Remember that summer of '03? Scorcher it was. Went camping up in the Cairngorms. '03... that was before I got the warehouse job. You were still lecturing then, weren’t you? I vaguely recall you going on about some Shakespeare module. Ha! That’s right. Still stuck in those dusty old texts, trying to make sense of it all. Though, I did manage to drag myself away for a bit last year. Did that photography tour in Iceland. Iceland? Gadzooks! Always wanted to go, I did. Saw some incredible pictures online. What was it like? Was it as bleak as they make out? Bleak in its beauty, I'd say. Vast, stark landscapes. Black sand beaches, glaciers… it’s something else. Seriously. The light, though – that’s what hooked me. The way it shifts and changes. I’ve been trying to capture that since I got back. Aye, I can imagine. Photography's always been a wee ambition o’ mine. Got a decent camera, just never seem to have the time or the skill to properly use it. Mostly end up taking blurry pictures o’ the dog. We all start somewhere, Ryan. It's about seeing things differently, you know? Not just  looking  at a scene, but  seeing  it. The textures, the colours, the composition… You should try getting out early, during the golden hour. That’s when the light’s at its best. Golden hour, eh? Sounds posher than anything I’ve ever heard. Like something you'd hear lecturers sayin'! I usually just get up when the warehouse siren goes off. Not much time for golden hours then. Fair enough. But even a quick walk round Arthur's Seat at sunrise… you’d be surprised. And there's plenty of good stuff to photograph right here in Edinburgh. The buildings, the Old Town, the Castle... It’s a photographer’s dream, really. True enough. Though I'm no sure I'd have the patience. Takes a certain eye, doesn't it? I’m more of a ‘snap and hope for the best’ kind of guy. I did try taking some photos during a wee trip to the Highlands last year, but they mostly just ended up lookin' like grey.

Right then, Lizzie, let’s get this sorted. Week ahead. Feels like a right mountain of things already, doesn't it? Honestly, I'm knackered just thinking about it. It doesn't  have  to be a mountain, Mum! We can chip away at it. What’s top of the list? Still the garden? The garden is a constant, isn't it? It’s like a needy toddler, forever wanting attention. But yes, the borders really do need a weed. And I need to get those dahlias planted. Then there's that blasted leak under the kitchen sink... the plumber's booked for Thursday, thank goodness. I was starting to worry he’d forgotten. Thursday's good. Gives me a bit of breathing room. I'm mostly just focused on the little ones at school. We’ve got that phonics screening coming up at the end of the week, which is always a bit stressful. Poor little darlings get so worked up. Oh, I know. It’s relentless, isn’t it? Wanting them to perform perfectly. Is little Leo settling in alright? I remember he seemed a little shy last time I was at the school play. He is, actually! He's come on so much. He’s making friends, and he even volunteered to be a narrator for our new class story! Can you believe it? It's just... the nursery situation is still niggling me. Have you looked at any more of those options I sent you? I have, love. Briefly. Honestly, it's all so overwhelming. Those places are like gold dust these days, aren't they? The one near the library seemed alright, but the waiting list… massive. And the fees... well, let’s just say they’d make your eyes water. I know. I'm starting to think I should put him on every single waiting list within a ten-mile radius and just hope something falls into place. It's just… I’m worried about him being with someone I don’t completely trust. It’s the hardest decision. I get it, sweetheart. It is. You want the best for him. You're a good mum, you know that. Remember how frantic  I  was when you started school? I’d practically stake out the classroom! You did! I remember. Mrs. Peterson had to ask you to leave. Well, she did need to! Anyway... what about that new show on telly?

This is reet good, this bread. Proper crusty. You get good bread up 'ere, don't ya, Finn? Back home, it’s all fluffy nonsense. Could bounce a ball off it. It's alright. Bit fancy for me, mind. Mum always buys the cheap stuff. Still, beats beans on toast, eh? So, how was the conference today, Liv? You sounded stressed on the phone. Stress is my middle name these days, Finn. Honestly. This financial firm… they’re a nightmare. Spent all morning wrangling with their IT department because the projector wouldn’t connect. A projector! It’s 2024, for crying out loud! Eventually, some bloke comes out, mumbles something about ‘legacy systems,’ and fixes it with a paperclip. A paperclip! Makes you want to scream, it does. Legacy systems… a classic. You’d think these fancy firms would have their tech sorted. My company’s been talking about migrating to the cloud for, like, five years. Still haven't happened. Tell me about it! And the speakers... good grief. One of 'em spent twenty minutes talking about his golf handicap. Twenty minutes! I nearly walked out. Sounds rough. But hey, at least you're getting paid. I spent the whole day moving bricks. Back-breaking work, it is. My shoulders are screaming. You wouldn't happen to be working on that new housing development near the river, would you, Finn? I saw a crane there the other day. Yeah, that’s the one. Proper slog. They’re building some posh flats, all glass and steel. Not a brick in sight for the actual residents, just for show. Fancy! Any chance you could sneak me a brick? I could use it as a paperweight. My desk’s a right mess. Speaking of which… Chloe, you look amazing! That dress is stunning. Where’d you get it? Thanks, Liv! It’s from a vintage shop in Shoreditch. Found it on a market stall, actually. It was a steal. It's silk, can you believe it? I was thinking of wearing it to that gallery opening next week... Gallery opening? Sounds a bit posh for me. I'd probably spill something on it within five minutes. That's why you can't come, Finn. Just kidding! It’s on Thursday, the 17th. Anyone fancy going? There's a new exhibition by that photographer, Anya Volkov, you know, the one who does those incredible black and white portraits?

Cor, this is a bit weak, isn’t it? Like dishwater, it is. I asked for a good, strong cuppa - you know, something to put a bit of pep in your step. Not this… this pale imitation. Oh, come on, Arthur. Don't be such a fusspot. I thought I'd made it a bit milder this time, remembering you saying last week you felt it was a bit strong. And it's perfectly good tea, honestly. PG Tips, you know. Not some of that fancy stuff. Mild tea? Arthur expecting mild tea? That's rich, Brenda! Remember the time he sent back a pot at the Bowls Club because it wasn't steeped long enough? Nearly started a riot, he did. Well, a man needs his tea properly brewed, doesn’t he, Geoffrey? It’s a fundamental right! And the Bowls Club tea was practically cold! They were using lukewarm water too. Honestly, the standards these days… Now, now, Arthur. Let's not get into a debate about the merits of Bowls Club refreshments. Brenda, dear, is it Ceylon? It has a rather… delicate aroma. It’s… it's PG Tips, Margaret. I’m using the new floral blend. I thought it might be a little different. Floral blend, eh? Fancy! Back in my day, we just had the standard red box. Yorkshire Tea, of course. Now  that’s  a proper brew. Strong enough to stand a spoon in. Yorkshire Tea, Geoffrey, you're talking sense. That’s the ticket. PG Tips, blooming nonsense. Tastes like hay. Arthur! You’re being deliberately difficult. I’ve been trying to cater to everyone’s tastes. Geoffrey likes his strong, you said last week you wanted it milder… Perhaps Brenda should try a dual infusion. Steep the teabag for three minutes, remove it, then add a fresh bag and steep for another two. That can often enhance the flavour without making it excessively bitter. It’s a technique I learned during my time teaching Home Economics. Dual infusion? Sounds like a lot of bother for a cuppa. Just give me a strong one, Margaret. Plain and simple. None of this faffing about. Margaret's got a point, though Brenda. It’s all about the timing. You’ve got to get it right. Too long, it's bitter. Too short, it's weak. It's an art, really. Like teaching Shakespeare. You have to find the precise moment to get the message across.

Right, everyone piled up? I think this chicken's coming along beautifully. Honestly, this rosemary and garlic rub is a game changer. You wouldn't believe how many students claim to 'know' about roasting a chicken, but… well, let's just say the results aren’t always edible. Don’t be too harsh, Elodie. They’re just trying. At least they’re engaging with the curriculum. And this smells amazing, by the way. Much better than that dodgy Thai place we tried last week. Remember? The one that charged extra for noodles? Extra for noodles? Blimey! That's a new level of audacity. This pudding looks proper, though. Proper Yorkshire. Beating my nan's, probably. She’d be furious, the old girl. Speaking of furious, did anyone see that protest in London the other day? The anti-circumcision lot? Bit… passionate, weren't they? Passionate is one word for it, Rhys. I was down there for a bit. It was… intense. Quite a lot of shouting. And police presence. Honestly, the whole thing felt needlessly theatrical. Seems a terribly divisive topic. I’ve been reading a bit about the history, actually. Fascinating, in a morbid sort of way. Morbid, Ben? Bit strong, isn’t it? It's a medical procedure, ultimately. Though, I suppose the cultural and religious implications are huge, depending on your perspective. Anyway, before we get completely bogged down in contentious debates over ancient traditions, let’s enjoy this food. Sarah, are you alright? You’re awfully quiet. Just thinking about needing a proper break. Work’s been relentless. We're rolling out a new training program on safeguarding and suddenly everyone needs a CRB check. It’s a nightmare coordinating it all. And then they want extra training on… well, everything. Apparently, you can't be too careful. It's stressing me out. We should book a weekend away. Somewhere nice. A weekend away sounds cracking! We could head to Cardiff, check out some of the galleries there. Or even a little trip down to Cornwall. Remember that hotel we stayed in near St Ives? The one with the ridiculous sea views? St Ives is always a good shout. Though, remember the drive back? Torrential rain, visibility was down to zero. I was practically white-knuckled the entire way. I really shouldn't drink so much Merlot before attempting to drive back. You were a sight, Ben!

Right, I’m home! Honestly, that was the most chaotic, glorious week. Sunburnt, exhausted, and smelling vaguely of sunscreen, but I’m here! How was everything while I was gone? Did the cat eat all the plants again? Welcome back! You look like you’ve actually  seen  the sun. No plant casualties this time, thankfully. Mittens was mostly obsessed with the new bird feeder I put up. Seriously, it’s like a tiny nature documentary in the garden now. How was Spain? Spill! Spain was...intense. In the best possible way. The heat, the siestas, the tapas… Honestly, I think I gained about five pounds just inhaling paella. We went to Valencia, Barcelona, a little village in the Pyrenees…it was a whirlwind. There was this one, absolutely ridiculous bullfighting museum… A bullfighting museum? You and your penchant for weird history. You’ll fit right in with the post-op debriefs at work, then. So, Barcelona was good? I remember you saying you really wanted to see the Sagrada Familia. Oh my God, the Sagrada Familia. Pictures don't do it justice, honestly. Stood there for ages, just staring up. It's… spiritual, even for someone as cynical as me. We had this amazing little tapas bar tucked away near Las Ramblas, the best patatas bravas I’ve ever had. You  have  to go. Listen, I brought you back a little something. Oh, Liv, that’s lovely! You shouldn’t have. It’s gorgeous. Thanks! So, work's been… well, work. The usual. We're short-staffed as always, so the pressure is on. But I finally managed to get Mrs. Davies sorted out and her anxiety is much better. That feels like a win, you know? Absolutely! Those little victories are everything. It must be rewarding, even with the stress. Did you catch any of the women's football? England were amazing against Denmark! I saw bits! Millie Bright was a beast! Honestly, their midfield was incredible. You should have seen it with me. We were both shouting at the TV like loons. I'm going to try to make it to the next match at Old Trafford. Fancy coming? I got a discount on tickets through the hospital. Oh, YES! Definitely. That would be brilliant. Do you think Dad would want to come? It would be a proper family outing. I’ll ask. He’s been moaning about the cricket lately, says they’re not playing well enough.

Right, so I spoke to Sarah again this morning. It wasn't good, love. Really not good. Oh no. What did she say? Don't keep me in suspense. Is it the chemo? Are they adjusting it? It's… more than that, I think. She said the scans showed it's spread further than they initially thought. To her liver. She sounded… resigned, you know? Not angry, not even particularly upset, just… resigned. It broke my heart. Oh, darling. That’s… devastating. I’m so sorry. Has she told Mark? Yes, he's with her now. He's being the stalwart he always is, trying to be upbeat, but I could hear the wobble in his voice when she told me. They're both just… exhausted. I offered to go round, but she said she just wanted to be left to it for a bit. That’s probably sensible. Sometimes being there physically isn’t what’s needed. Offering support remotely is best, I think. What about the Macmillan nurse? Is she still seeing her regularly? Yes, the Macmillan nurse is a godsend, honestly. Sarah says she’s been incredible. They’re managing the pain, thankfully, but… it’s the uncertainty. That’s what’s getting to her. Absolutely. Uncertainty’s the worst. We need to do something practical, don't we? Beyond sending flowers and offering vague platitudes. I was thinking about that. Mark mentioned they’re struggling with getting Sarah food prepared. I could start a roster with some of the others, get people to drop off meals a few times a week? It’d be one less thing for them to worry about. That’s brilliant, love. Absolutely brilliant. I can help you coordinate that. Let's get a group email going. And maybe offer to help with some cleaning or errands too, if they need it. They’re both so busy just focusing on Sarah. Definitely. Right, well, that’s the heavy stuff. Let's try and distract ourselves a bit. Did you see that new listing in Little Puddleton? The one on the High Street? The one with the overgrown garden and the wonky porch? Yes, I did. It's got potential, certainly, but it needs  serious  work. And the planning permission... Exactly! I went online and looked at the planning applications. Apparently, the current owners applied to build an extension last year. It was rejected.

Right, I'm tellin' ya, this job… don't get me wrong, it's steady, pays the bills. But there's just  things . Things that get right under yer skin, y'know? Tell me about it, Liam. Honestly, I feel like 90% of my job is just dealing with things I don’t like. What's got you wound up today? It's the music, Sarah. The  constant  music. Some lad, room 312, he’s got this… this dubstep, is it? Sounds like a swarm of angry wasps trapped in a washing machine. Blasting it at all hours. I've had to go up there three times this week just to ask him to turn it down a bit. And he just gives me this blank stare and mumbles something 'bout "vibes.” Vibes! I’m tryin’ to keep the peace 'ere, not facilitate a rave. Oh god, the noise complaints. Don't even get me started. We had a group last month playing Fortnite at 4 am. 4 am! They didn’t even apologise, just started arguing about who had the best kill-death ratio. It's exhausting. My least favourite thing, by far, is the complete lack of consideration some of these students have. Like, basic courtesy seems to have vanished. Aye, it’s a right palaver. And it’s not just the noise, is it? It's the mess, too. Found a pizza box, still with remnants, abandoned in the communal kitchen yesterday. Just… left there. Like they expected it to magically disappear. I spent fifteen minutes scraping it off the floor. Ugh, the kitchen. Don’t even. It's a biohazard zone half the time. I’ve seen things in that kitchen, Liam. Things I can’t unsee. Honestly, I wish we had a cleaner come in daily. Or even just someone to enforce the ‘clean up after yourself’ rule. It’s like talking to a brick wall. I've left passive aggressive notes - the little smiley faces ironically - and they just get ignored. Smiley faces? You're braver than me. I just try to look stern and hope they get the message. Doesn't always work, mind. They’re a different breed now, these students. Don't seem to have the respect for authority that we had when we were young'uns. I think it's more a case of entitlement, to be honest. They expect everything to be done  for  them.

Honestly, it’s just so mad, isn't it? Running into people from back home here in Brighton. We saw Mrs. Higgins from Gillingham just the other day, queuing for the pier! She said her daughter's dragged her down for a "cheeky weekend break.” Cheeky, she calls lugging a suitcase and a windbreaker cheeky. Brighton draws ‘em in, doesn’t it? Always has. Reminds me of those package tours they used to run. Remember those, Maureen? Slough to Skegness, all on a coach… organized chaos. Oh, definitely, Arthur. My auntie went on a few of those. Came back looking like she’d wrestled a seagull and lost. Speaking of trips, has anyone been to a Christmas market recently? Thinking of popping over somewhere in Europe. I was thinking the same! Antwerp, maybe? I’ve heard good things. Though getting there would involve navigating London traffic… the thought alone sends shivers down me spine. Antwerp’s lovely, but expensive. Not exactly ideal on a pension, is it? Remember that time we tried to go caravanning in Dorset? Absolute nightmare. Ended up with a flooded tent and a swarm of midges. Still, got a good story out of it. Oh, Arthur, you always do! I remember that. We barely slept a wink. It's funny, isn't it? Thinking back, some of the worst holidays make the best memories. It's a bit like raising boys, really. A constant source of stress and joy. Little terrors, bless ‘em. Totally! My little brother’s turning eight next month. We’re trying to decide if we should do a bouncy castle or a petting zoo. It's surprisingly stressful, choosing between a bouncy castle and a collection of slightly dubious-looking sheep. My uni cohort are all struggling with similar dilemmas – birthdays, school plays… feels like we’ve gone from students to parents overnight. Seems like only yesterday you were all fresh-faced and arguing about Hegel. Time flies, doesn’t it? Makes you think about retirement, in a way. Although no amount of time will make Brighton traffic less of a trial. Retirement's something I think about, but not in a wistful way. Still enjoying my work, you know? Keeps me busy. And the patients are lovely, most of them. Though some days… well, some days it's hard. Losing Mrs. Peterson last month was particularly rough. She was like a grandma to me.

Ugh, this equality vote thing is proper confusing, Mum. Everyone at school's going on about it, but nobody actually explains what it  means . Like, they just say ‘it’s important!’ Seriously? Important for  who ? Right, well, sit down properly, love. It  is  a bit complicated, isn't it? It’s basically a vote on whether to change the Irish Constitution to recognise relationships beyond just marriage. So, you know, same-sex couples, civil partnerships… giving them the same rights and protections as married couples. So… it’s about gay people? Not that there's anything wrong with that, obviously. It’s just… grown-ups always make everything sound so serious. It  is  serious, but it doesn't have to be scary. Look, currently, the Constitution defines marriage as between a man and a woman. This vote is asking if that definition should be removed, to make it more inclusive. It's about equality, like you said, important for  who ? Important for everyone, really. Because it shows we value fairness and acceptance. Okay, that makes a bit more sense. But why did it need to be defined in the first place, like, between a man and a woman? Why was it ever like that? That’s a long story, involving history and… well, let's just say a lot of people used to think differently. It reflects the views of a different time, you know? People's ideas about what's "normal" change, hopefully for the better. Remember when I used to make you wear those awful beige trousers to school? Times change, right? Don’t remind me! I still have nightmares about those trousers. But seriously, so it's like… taking something old and outdated away? Exactly. It's about updating the rules to reflect the way society is now. It’s about recognizing that love is love, regardless of who’s doing the loving. Right. So, if it passes, does that mean gay people can get married no matter what? Like, even if they don't want to? No, no. It doesn't  force  anyone to marry anyone. It just removes that specific definition from the Constitution. People can still choose to get married, or not, regardless of their sexuality. It's about giving them the  option  without it being seen as… unusual or wrong. So, what do you think we should do? You know, vote. It's a personal choice, love.

Right then, Marjorie, this chilli's a bit fierce, innit? A bit more kick than I'm used to. Though, I do like a bit o' spice. Reminds me of that trip we took to… well, never you mind where. Long time ago. It’s fine, Arthur. Just needs a bit more rice. Honestly, you’re always moaning about the heat. Remember Brenda’s curry night?  That  was spicy. You were practically breathing fire. Brenda’s curry nights were legendary. And Arthur, you were indeed a sight to behold. Redder than a beetroot, you were. Though, speaking of tools that require skill… I was looking at some new turning tools the other day, actually. For the lathe. Found a set of carbide inserts – really sharp, apparently. Thinking about trying them out on some elm. Elm, you say? Lovely wood, elm. Used to make the best chair legs. Remember old Mr. Pring back in Costessey? Used to carve the most beautiful things from elm. Had a proper workshop, he did. Full of shavings and the smell of fresh cut wood. He used to let me watch when I was a boy… Arthur, darling, go on. Let’s hear about Mr. Pring. But first, more rice? Honestly, you’ll give yourself indigestion. Derek, are you alright? You’ve been awfully quiet. Sorry, Marjorie. Just…thinking. It's just bizarre, really. I was reading this article online…about hamsters, of all things. And it described this absolutely dreadful incident. Hamsters? What sort of incident? Don’t tell me they’ve bred ‘em bigger now, have they? They’re already right cheeky little blighters. No, nothing like that. Apparently, some young… they put a hamster in a microwave. Derek! How can you even  say  such a thing? That's appalling! Disgusting! I can't believe someone would do that. Poor little thing. Blimey. Nowt explains the cruelty of some people, does it? Absolutely shocking. A hamster! In a microwave! What possessed ‘em? The article didn’t go into the motivation, just the…the aftermath. It was awful. It just struck me as so incredibly senseless. I mean, these tools I was looking at, they are used to  create  things. Beautiful, functional things. This...this is the complete opposite. It’s just… inhuman. Unforgivable. Rest in peace, little hamster. Honestly, the world is going mad. Aye, Marjorie's right. Mad as a box of frogs. You read about these things and you just can't make sense of it.

Honestly, David, this article about a cat rescuing its owner from a house fire – ridiculous, isn’t it? They're making the poor thing out to be a hero. Cats are just opportunists, you know. Looking for a warm spot and a full bowl. Opportunistic, perhaps, but often surprisingly perceptive. I read something about mirror-writing the other day, actually. Similar principle, isn't it? People claiming incredible abilities when it’s just a knack for reversing things. Remember that chap who claimed it was a sign from beyond? Oh, nonsense, David. Animals are far more intelligent than we give them credit for. And as for mirror-writing, there’s a genuine neurological condition, you know. Not everyone is faking it. I had a student years ago who wrote exclusively like that. Quite a bright girl, too. Though, entirely impractical for taking notes in a lecture! Well, I’m sticking with the opportunistic cat view. It probably just panicked and happened to nudge the owner awake. Speaking of panic, have you seen what house prices are doing again? Absolutely outrageous. I was looking at a little flat in Tooting the other day, and it’s asking for nearly £400,000! Tell me about it. I’m still trying to untangle myself from the mess with the bank. They’re insisting on those ridiculous fees for the overdraft. Honestly, it feels like they deliberately design the system to keep people in debt. Speaking of which, your sister's wedding... are you sticking with your original outfit? The outfit is hanging sadly in the wardrobe. I’m thinking of just buying something new. That dress was a disaster at Aunt Mildred's birthday. I felt like a sack of potatoes. And the wedding... it's stressing me out. I’m worried about Uncle George. He gets so easily overwhelmed in large groups. George is a dear, but he needs to learn to focus. A good crossword puzzle always helped me when I was feeling flustered. Keeps the mind sharp. Anyone fancy a go at one later? I’ve got a particularly fiendish one here. I’d be up for that, Margaret. Anything to distract me from thinking about loan applications. Do you ever worry about all this technology, Margaret? This new AI stuff… it’s rather unsettling. Seems like jobs are going to disappear faster than we realise. I'm a transcriber, David!

Honestly, you two. Look at this kitchen. It’s a disaster! Lego scattered everywhere, controllers abandoned on the table… and not a book in sight. But Mummy, Kai’s building a new Ninjago temple! It’s got a secret passage! And I’m almost finished terraforming the desert area in my Minecraft world. I need to get enough sand for the pyramid. That's lovely, really it is. But you've been on those screens for hours. Remember we talked about balancing things? Reading is important too, you know. Remember the new Harry Potter book came out? Harry Potter's boring! Ninjago is way cooler. There's a new villain, Morbus! He can control shadows! Minecraft is  always  cooler. You can build  anything . Magic is just...limited. Limited? Try creating a whole ecosystem, David. Building intricate redstone circuits. That's pretty impressive magic in itself! Seriously though, I’m not saying you can’t play. It’s fun! But you promised you'd read for at least an hour today. But the new Ninjago series just dropped, Mummy! Episode five is on! It has a massive battle! I know, sweetheart. And I bet it’s really exciting. But think of it like this – those Ninjago characters, they  have  stories. Stories were written down somewhere, before they were animated. Someone had to imagine them first, just like J.K. Rowling imagined Harry Potter. So, you’re saying someone  wrote  the Ninjago story? Who? Well, a whole team of writers and designers, actually. But the underlying idea, the whole world… it started with words. And reading helps you create your own worlds too, David. Imagine you're building your Minecraft world, and you want to write a story about why that pyramid is there. You need words for that! Hmmm… So, if I read about knights, I can build a castle in Minecraft? Absolutely! Reading about things – about history, about science, about other people’s experiences – it all feeds your imagination. It gives you ideas. It gives you tools to build, to create. Both in Minecraft and in the real world. Can I read a book about redstone engineering? Maybe that will help with my automatic farm. Now  that’s  a brilliant idea! I think I might actually have something perfect. Come on, let’s look. You can tackle that farm design  after  an hour of reading. And maybe, just maybe, while you're reading, you’ll get a spark of inspiration that’ll make your farm even more amazing.

Right then, girls. Lovely to have you both here. That holiday… honestly, it was a bit of a whirlwind, wasn’t it? I’m still unpacking memories, let alone clothes! Absolutely, Mum. Whirlwind is the perfect word. The sun, the sea… it was exactly what I needed. Though, I am slightly sunburnt on my shoulders. Should’ve put more factor 50 on, really. You always say that, Chloe! And you never learn. I felt like I was constantly reapplying it, but then I was too busy trying to build ridiculous sandcastles. Remember that one, Mum? The one that kept collapsing? Oh, I do remember! You were determined to build a castle fit for a queen, weren’t you, Bethany? It was a valiant effort, even if the tide had other plans. Honestly, seeing you two as adults, still playing in the sand like that… it just warmed my heart. It was brilliant. It’s good for the soul, isn’t it? Just… letting go and being a bit silly. Work’s been a bit manic lately, so it was nice to switch off completely. We sold out of everything in the garden centre, practically! Trying to keep up with the demand for hanging baskets was exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, my lectures are ramping up. Midterms are looming, and Professor Davies is being particularly brutal this year. I swear, he’s trying to make us all fail. Although, his lectures on post-structuralism  are  fascinating, once you get your head around them. Post-structuralism? Sounds rather intense. Well, you’re a clever girl, Bethany. You’ll conquer it. Chloe, anything new happening at the garden centre? Besides selling out of hanging baskets, of course. They’re talking about expanding the outdoor furniture section. Apparently, there’s a big demand. It would mean more responsibility for me, managing a bigger team and dealing with suppliers, but it could be a good opportunity. I’m just a bit… apprehensive, to be honest. It’s a lot. Go for it! You’re a fantastic manager, Chloe. Everyone always says how good you are. You always know how to motivate people, and you’re so organised. Don’t doubt yourself. Your sister's right, darling. You’ve got a real talent for it. Don't be afraid to take the leap. It'll be challenging, yes, but you'll thrive. Do you want me to have a look at your business plan?

Right, Uno then? I’m calling dibs on being dealer. Gotta strategize, you know. Last time, Liam nearly had a meltdown when I drew a Draw Four. Liam always has a meltdown about something. Remember when Mrs. Davies made him present his history project on the suffragettes? He swore she was deliberately trying to make him embarrass himself. Honestly, the drama. He  does  overreact. But I feel for him sometimes. He’s got it tough with his dad, hasn’t he? Always on him about his grades. My mum would never… well, she’s definitely got opinions, but she'd never belittle me like that. Yeah, it's rough. Anyway, Uno! You two taking cards or what? I’m feeling lucky today. I watched 'SAS: Rogue Heroes' last night – proper intense. Makes you think, doesn’t it? All that stuff, the army, the wars… It was pretty good, yeah. My grandad was in the army, you know. He wouldn’t talk about it much, but he had this… look in his eyes sometimes. A faraway look. Mum says it was from seeing too much. That's awful. My cousin’s boy is thinking of joining the Air Force. Honestly, I'm terrified for him. There’s so much going on in the world right now – Ukraine, that mess with Israel… It’s scary. Totally. It makes you think about stuff, doesn't it? Like, what are we even fighting over these days? Seems like it’s always something. Anyway, back to Uno. Red reverse, eh? Excellent. Your turn, Chloe. Ugh, fine. Green skip. Seriously? I was hoping for a wild card. You're hogging all the good ones. By the way, did you hear Mr. Harrison's announced the new prefects? No way! Who got it? Apparently, Emily Carter and… wait for it… James Peterson. James Peterson? Seriously? He spends half his lessons staring out the window and the other half arguing with Mr. Davies about the correct pronunciation of "verisimilitude.” He’s hopeless! I know! Emily’s alright, I suppose, but James? He’ll be asleep during all the meetings. Honestly, the school's gone mad. I applied, you know. You did? I didn't realise. You would have been brilliant, Chloe. You're actually organised and responsible. He’s just… James. And totally obsessed with that manga, ‘Attack on Titan’. He’s trying to convince everyone it’s a deep philosophical commentary on the nature of… something.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is  killing  me this year. Physics is already hard enough without him deciding to make every lesson a cryptic riddle. Tell me about it. He asked us to explain, like, the entire concept of momentum using only interpretive dance yesterday. Interpretive dance! Who even  does  that? I nearly choked on my own laughter. Chloe tried, bless her, but it just ended up looking like she was desperately trying to swat away invisible bees. Mr. Davies actually gave her a participation mark! The man’s lost it. Seriously. And remember last week when he told us the answer to a calculation was ‘approximately the feeling of immense pressure'? What even  is  that as an answer? I wrote down "a very unpleasant sensation" just to be contrary. He didn’t mark me down, though. I think he was too busy staring blankly into space. So, how’s Mrs. Peterson’s English class going? At least she doesn't try to be a performance artist. Actually, it’s surprisingly good. We’re reading ‘Pride and Prejudice’ at the moment. I know, I know, sounds horribly dull, doesn’t it? But she makes it so interesting. She does these amazing close readings, picking up on all the subtle irony and social commentary. Ooh, I like that. I'm terrible at close reading. I just read for the plot, you know? Is it actually good, though? I’ve never seen the appeal. Honestly? It’s brilliant. Elizabeth Bennet is so clever and independent. And Darcy… okay, Darcy is a bit of a snob at first, but he's got layers. Have you seen that film, "17 Again"? Vaguely. Isn’t it about a guy who magically turns back into a teenager? Yeah! And he goes back to high school. It's a bit cheesy, but it’s actually really funny, especially when he's trying to be cool again. It makes you think, wouldn't it be amazing to go back and do everything differently? Definitely. Especially those disastrous maths tests last term. I'd totally ace them if I could go back! Speaking of school stories… did you hear about Liam Anderson and the science experiment? No! Do tell. Apparently, he was trying to build a miniature volcano for the science fair. But he used way too much baking soda and vinegar, and it exploded all over Mrs. Grimshaw’s new cardigan.

Right, so, Transylvania, eh? You’re actually going? Seriously? Sounds mental. Like, proper Dracula vibes. Are you sure you’ve checked for… you know… garlic supplies? Don't be ridiculous, Ben! It's not like I'm expecting to be chased by vampires. It’s a history tour, mostly. Old castles, medieval towns, the works. I've been reading up on it. Apparently, the Dracula legend is totally based on a real Romanian prince, Vlad the Impaler. It's fascinating! And the pastries there are supposed to be  amazing.  That's a big draw for me, obviously. Pastries are  always  a draw for you, Liv. Can’t blame you! Transylvania though… that’s a bit of a leap from Brixton Market, isn’t it? I’m just saying. These are ginger biscuits, by the way. Still warming up after a busy Sunday at the café. Honestly, Sundays are manic. Ginger biscuits? Fair dinkum! Those are grouse. Makes a change from flat whites and lattes, eh? Transylvania, Liv? Struth, you're a brave one. Reminds me of the time I tried to hike through the Blue Mountains and ended up hopelessly lost and covered in eucalyptus oil. Eucalyptus oil? Why? Did you fall in a bush? Pretty much! Tried to use it as insect repellent. Didn't work. Learned a lesson that day: Australian bush is not to be trifled with. And don’t underestimate the power of a mozzie. Right, so what's happening with you lot this weekend? Anyone fancy a beer garden crawl on Saturday? I'm in! Need to de-stress before my ridiculously early flight on Monday. It’s 6 am! Ugh. I’m proper dreading it. I even thought about laser eye surgery, you know? Just to avoid needing glasses for navigating airport security at that ungodly hour. Laser eye surgery?! Liv, are you serious? That's a big decision! My cousin had it done, and she said the recovery was a nightmare. Swears she saw spots for weeks. I know, I know. Just thinking about it. The convenience would be incredible, though. No more squinting at boarding passes. Plus, think of the money I'd save on glasses! Reckon you should have a good chat with a few different surgeons first. Don't just jump into it, yeah? Although, no more glasses… that does sound tempting. Remember when Chloe chipped hers at that dodgy student house party?

Right, nearly dinner time. Who’s hungry? You two bouncing around like that, I’d have thought you'd be famished. Me! Me! Hungry, Mummy! Can we have chips? Please, please, please? Chips! Chips! And ketchup! Lots of ketchup! Chips it is then, my loves. But first, can we have a little quiet please? I’m trying to think. I’ve been looking at these photos… remember that photoshoot we did last weekend? The one with the hats? I liked the pointy one! I wanted the pirate hat! It was much better! You both did. It was lovely, wasn’t it? I was thinking of getting a proper canvas print made of the one of us all together, grinning like loons. It would look lovely in the hallway. Can we hang it near the aerial hoop? So I can look at it when I'm training! Absolutely. Want to talk about the aerial hoop for a minute? Your Grandma mentioned she’s coming to watch you next Saturday. Wow! Grandma's coming?! Will she bring biscuits? She might! But she also said she wants to see you do that tricky drop you've been practicing. It's hard! I wobbled a bit yesterday. You’ll get it, sweetie. Practice makes perfect. Remember what we said about persistence? Like learning that tricky bit of that song you were listening to earlier? The one with the… the  word ? Yes, the one with the slightly naughty word. We talked about not using it, didn’t we? Even when you're excited. It’s best to keep it to yourself. But Leo used it on the obstacle course! When he fell in the mud! Did he now? Well, even when you’re covered in mud and having a brilliant time, we still need to be mindful of our language. It's a good thing you reminded me about the obstacle course though. It was brilliant, wasn't it? All that mud! MUD! And slides! And that rope swing! It was. It was absolute chaos! Speaking of chaos... remember Sarah's party next weekend? I need to sort out a present for her. Any ideas? A sparkly unicorn! Like the one in Alice in Wonderland! A robot! A robot that makes funny noises! Alright, alright! Sparkly unicorns and robots are duly noted. Perhaps something a little more…practical? Like a nice bottle of wine? Though I doubt Sarah would appreciate a robot unicorn.

Cor blimey, look at this spread! Margherita and that… that chocolatey thing you’ve made, Brenda? Smells right lovely, it does. Proper treat. It’s a roulade, Arthur. And yes, it is! Thought we deserved something special after all the stress of exam results. How’s your tummy feeling today? Didn't want to give you too much, knowing you. Tummy's grand, Brenda. Grand. Just a bit…jittery, you know? All this talk of exams and driving lessons… young Elsie and Maisie are puttin’ a fair bit of pressure on an old man. Pressure points, eh, Arthur? Happens to the best of us. It's just natural, isn't it? Young people want to confirm independence. Maisie's results were excellent, though. Really excellent. Did you see her reaction when she got that A in Physics? Dad’s going on again. Physics wasn't  that  amazing. I'm just glad it's over! I'm going to tweet a picture of this pizza. #PizzaNight #ExamResults #SoRelieved No you’re not! Put that away. Let me post it! My followers need to see this epic roulade! #ChocolateHeaven #FamilyTime Give it! You always steal my posts! Cor! Look at you two! Like little kittens, you are. Fighting over a bit of tech. Reminds me of me and my brother, Barry, when we were youngsters. Used to wrestle over a football down Costessey way. Good times, good times... though Barry always cheated. Honestly, Arthur, you tell that story every time we have pizza. Do you remember Mrs. Higgins’ parents’ evening last week? A right palaver, that was. She was convinced they were plotting against her because her son didn't get the grade he wanted. Parents' evenings… a necessary evil. You get every stereotype represented there. The overly-invested, the perpetually absent, the ones who think their child is destined for Oxford regardless of the evidence… Mrs. Higgins' son drives me mad in Maths. He always shows off. He’s got a serious attitude problem. But his dad just claps him on the back and tells him he's ‘a natural’. Fancy that. All this fuss about grades. My dad never pushed me to do much at school. Said, "Just don't get into trouble, Arthur." And I mostly managed that. Though I did have a bit of a scrape with Mr. Davies and a rotten apple… that’s another story. Oh, here we go… another long story.

Honestly, these old cassettes… they’re a treasure trove, aren’t they? Your father recorded everything. Christmases, birthdays, even just rambling conversations. I found one from 1998 where he was trying to explain the rules of Chinese chess to poor Aunt Mildred. She was utterly bewildered. Morning! Smells like bacon frying. That’s a welcome change from instant coffee. So, Chinese chess again today? My brain still aches from yesterday. You were being ruthless. Ruthless is putting it mildly! I kept getting distracted trying to remember if I left the sprinkler on in the garden. The rain we had yesterday was a tease, only a sprinkle. Everything’s still parched. Gardening's a nightmare this year. And the slugs… don't even get me started. The weather is dreadful, really, isn't it? Unpredictable. You’d think after all these years we'd understand it. Remember that storm in 2007? Blew half the fence down. Anyway, speaking of unpredictable, did you see that article about South Korea considering mandatory English lessons starting in primary school? I did! Wild, right? Seems like a massive undertaking. I wonder if it’ll actually make a difference, or just create a generation of people who can recite phrases but can’t actually  use  the language. My current students… some struggle so much even with the basics. It’s the tuition fees, isn’t it? It's a disgrace what they charge these days. When I was thinking about university, it was a much smaller burden. Now it’s crippling debt for young people. Makes you wonder if it's worth it sometimes, or if they're just setting themselves up for a lifetime of financial strain. Absolutely. And the housing market! Don't even get me started. It’s no wonder so many are worried. I was reading about that debate around Scottish independence again. Do you think it'll come to anything this time? It’s a constant cycle, isn't it? I think it’s more about frustration with Westminster than a genuine desire for independence. It's complicated by Brexit, of course. It’s fascinating from a linguistics perspective, though. The potential divergence of dialects… if Scotland became independent, you’d probably see a resurgence in distinct Scottish English features. Fascinating, yes, but all I'm thinking about is the potential disruption. I've got family in Scotland. It's a mess.

Honestly, darling, this place is quite charming, isn’t it? Tarnow… who’d have thought I’d be having a latte in Poland? It’s a far cry from Cambridge, that’s for sure. Though, equally, a far cry from, well, anything I’ve done in ages, really. It is lovely! I wasn’t expecting so much history. And the pastries look incredible. Anyway, you were saying about your students? Are they proving a handful? I've got a particularly challenging group of Japanese businessmen at the moment. They’re incredibly polite, which is nice, but the grammar… it’s a battlefield. A handful is putting it mildly. One young Korean chap, bless him, seems to think ‘have’ and ‘has’ are interchangeable. And the conversational English... it's a bit like trying to build a house out of marshmallows. It just doesn't  stick . It’s rewarding, of course, when you see a glimmer of understanding, but some days… I just want to curl up with a box set. Speaking of which, have you seen that new Netflix documentary about… well, it’s hard to explain. Consent. And relationships. It's rather thought-provoking. Oh, yeah! I started watching that. It's really uncomfortable in parts, isn’t it? Makes you think, definitely. But good that it’s being discussed. Anyway, back to the battlefield… my students are struggling with the conditional tense. It's a nightmare. At least they're paying their tuition fees, unlike… well, unlike me, when I was their age and drowning in student loans. Remember how awful that felt? Drowning is the correct word. Still paying them off, actually. Though, with the way pensions are going... I shudder to think. I’m basically relying on the kindness of strangers and the occasional TEFL payment to keep me afloat. It's… a unique situation. Speaking of which, I need to get the car MOT'd when I get back. It’s been threatening to fall apart for months now. Oh, right! Your little Fiat. Honestly, that thing’s a miracle it’s still running. Have you found a garage yet? I know a decent one near Preston if you need a recommendation. So, you thinking of staying here in Poland long-term? You seem to be enjoying it. Long-term? Heavens, no. Just a little break. A change of scenery. It’s significantly cheaper than living in England, I have to admit.

Right, so… this place is mental, isn’t it? Never realised how busy it got on a Saturday. Glad we escaped the house though. Mum was on about dusting the bookshelves again. Tell me about it. My nan was breathing down my neck about cleaning the patio. This is much better. Cheers! So, Human Sciences, yeah? Still pretty set on that? It sounds… intense. Yeah, well, intense in a good way, I think. It’s just… so broad. Philosophy, psychology, sociology, economics... all mashed together. It's like trying to understand the whole human race, basically. I’m a bit nervous actually, about the workload. What about you? Still sticking with Maths? Pretty much. Though, I’m starting to think about specializing. Maybe Statistics? Everyone says it's got loads of job prospects. My dad keeps telling me to think about the money, obviously. You know how he is. Human Sciences sounds brilliant though, seriously. Do you think you could actually, like,  do  anything with it? That’s what I’ve been asking myself! Some of the alumni profiles are insane. People working in policy, international development... I’ve even seen one who works in behavioural economics, advising advertising companies. It's less about a specific job and more about the skills, I guess. Problem-solving, critical thinking... that kind of thing. Right, makes sense. I mean, with Maths, it's pretty clear. Banking, finance, data analysis... it's all very… concrete. Less chance of being completely baffled by what I’m doing. Though, I also quite like the idea of building something, you know? Creating equations, solving complex problems... it’s a bit of a buzz. I get that. It’s the same with Human Sciences, in a way. Taking a massive, complicated societal issue and trying to break it down and understand it. Speaking of complicated… are you even allowed to be drinking this stuff? Technically, no. But it's… diluted. It's a dark lemonade, apparently. My cousin Alex works here. He’s got a system. Don't tell my mum. Besides, we need to have some energy for rugby tomorrow! True! I’m actually feeling pretty nervous about that game. Old Man Hemmings has his nephews playing, and they're total beasts. Have you practiced your tackling this week? A bit. Mostly just avoided my little brother. He’s been trying to teach me this new move he saw on YouTube.

Right then, love. Where were we? You were poking at that thing about the inheritance tax, weren’t you? Seemed a bit flustered by it all. I am, Dad. It's just... complicated. I’ve read a few articles online, and they all seem to contradict each other. Basically, if I were to inherit something substantial from… well, let’s say from Aunt Margaret – you know she’s got that lovely little cottage in Cornwall? - how much tax would I actually pay?
