Proper one, with loads of veg. And I made gravy from scratch. It's for celebrating. Celebrating what? Did I miss something? Your birthday’s coming up, love. Just a little pre-celebration. We've still got the big bash on Saturday, remember? Oh! Right. I completely forgot we were doing this. How lovely. Thank you both. But… what present did you get me? Please don’t say something practical like a new toothbrush. Now, now, we’re not telling. It’s a surprise. But I will say it involves something you’ve been wanting for ages. No way! You didn't… is it a vintage typewriter? Oh my goodness! Let’s not spoil the surprise completely, shall we? But you're not far off. It's perfect for a copywriter, wouldn't you say? It is! Absolutely brilliant! You two are the best. Although, I do need to tell you about this freelance project I landed. It’s for a rather quirky tea company, and they want me to write copy for their new range of, get this, floral-infused teas. Lavender Earl Grey, Rosehip Rooibos… it's delightfully mad.

Cor blimey, this draught's fierce. Didn’t think it’d be this nippy, even for November. Used to be, the heating was on full blast by now. Feels like living in a cupboard, it does. You’re shivering, dear. I told you to put on another jumper. Honestly, you’re like a child. The electricity bill used to be a fright, wasn’t it? But well, we're managing, aren't we? A bit of extra layering. It’s not so bad once you get used to it. Did you see Brenda at the shops yesterday? Managing? That's a generous term, Margaret. More like scraping by. Though the biscuits are rather good, Arthur. Shortbread, I presume? Always a winner. Brenda, you say? What was she up to, gossiping, I imagine? Brenda’s still complaining about Jeremy’s new girlfriend, apparently. Says she’s far too young for him. Shocking choice of company for a man his age. Honestly, the way some people carry on. Speaking of shocking...did you all see last night's Big Brother? Absolutely dreadful. Honestly, the behaviour… Big Brother? Bah! All those young 'uns shouting and vying for attention. Give me a quiet evening with a cup o' tea and the telly any day. Though, even  that's  a luxury now, with the electricity. Remember when we had proper viewers, not these flickering things. Don’t be like that, Arthur. Big Brother has its moments. And poor Jeremy. Brenda’s got a point, though. A mistress at his age! It’s simply not cricket. Though, I always suspected something wasn’t quite right with him and Penelope…a bit too much hand-holding for a married man, if you ask me. Penelope was always a drama queen. Designed to stir things up. Jeremy, poor chap, probably just got swept along. Regardless, it’s a messy situation. Speaking of messy, have you sorted out the seating plan for the party next Saturday? I need to confirm numbers with the caterer. We’re still working on it. Trying to avoid any uncomfortable conversations, you know. Aunt Millie still hasn’t forgiven Cousin Charles for…well, you know. And Jeremy’s ex-wife won't be pleased if she sees him and the…new companion. It's a minefield! A party? Splendid! Need a bit of cheering up, we do. Though I’m not sure my legs are up to much dancing these days.

Right, this smells proper good, doesn't it? I reckon it'll be a good 'un. Though, I’m still having nightmares about that time I tried to make risotto. Absolute disaster, that was. Like glue, it was. Oh god, you and risotto. My mum never lets you live it down! It was on the family WhatsApp group for weeks. Seriously, you looked mortified. But yeah, this pasta smells amazing, honestly. So much better than anything I could've whipped up tonight. I'm officially declaring myself 'moral support and wine drinker'. Fair enough! You're a star, lass. So, what did you think of 'Everything Everywhere All at Once'? We're watching it after we eat, right? Absolutely! I just... wow. Right? I mean, it was utterly bonkers, but also so profoundly moving. I still feel a bit like my brain’s been scrambled, to be honest. The bagel, the rocks… I need to process it all. Did you get all the interdimensional stuff? Most of it, yeah. I had to rewind a couple of times, mind. It were a bit much, innit? Trying to keep up with the different universes and the googly eyes… But Michelle Yeoh, eh? She absolutely smashed it. Proper powerful performance. And Jamie Lee Curtis… a revelation! Seriously! Jamie Lee Curtis as a tax auditor? Genius casting. I loved how they handled the generational trauma thing, too. It felt… real, even amidst all the crazy multiverse madness. My mum would hate it, though. She’s a very straightforward woman. Wouldn't grasp the bagel existentialism at all. My grandma’s the same. She’d be like, "What's all this bother about? Just get on with making a cup o' tea!” Speaking of family… how’s your Auntie Sheila doing? I haven’t heard from her in ages. She’s good, actually! She finally booked that pottery class she’s been talking about for years. Apparently, she’s making little gnomes. Really kitsch ones, she says. She's sent me a picture - they have little beards and wonky hats. Very her. She’s also being surprisingly tech-savvy, ordering all her clay and tools online. That's brilliant! Good for her. Makes a change from moaning about the price of biscuits at the shops. My mum's been going on about my cousin Liam again. He's still trying to become a TikTok star. Still?

Right then, Liam. Your Grandad’s been goin’ on somethin’ fierce about this Scottish referendum, hasn’t he? Keeps mutterin’ about the Union and breakin' it up. Reckon you've been listenin' to him too? A bit, yeah. He gets really worked up about it. Says it'll ruin everything. But I'm not sure I really understand  why  it's such a big deal. Like, why do they  want  to leave? Well, love, it’s been a long, complicated history, hasn’t it? Scotland and England have been joined for centuries, but there's always been a strong Scottish identity, a desire to govern themselves. Remember what I told you about the Jacobite rebellions? That was all about wanting a Scottish King, rather than a King from London. Vaguely. Something about kilts and bagpipes and fighting? Aye, kilts and bagpipes aplenty! And a lot of bloodshed, I'll tell thee. But the feeling’s never really gone away, has it? They've got their own Parliament now, been havin' it since '99. But it doesn’t have as much power as the UK Parliament. Some folks in Scotland feel they’re being ignored by Westminster, that the ‘London bubble’ doesn't understand their needs. Things like oil revenue, for instance - they feel Scotland doesn’t get a fair share. Oil? So, if they leave, they keep all the oil money? That's part of it, aye. But it's more complicated than that. Oil’s a dwindling resource, remember. There’s talk of renewables, wind farms and all that. And think about things like the NHS - Scotland's got its own version, but it's funded through the UK government. If they leave, they'd have to figure out how to pay for it all themselves. It's a tricky business, balancing independence with the practicalities. That makes sense. So, there’s good reasons  and  bad reasons to leave? Exactly. And it's not just about money, mind. It's about national pride, about feeling you can make your own decisions, shape your own future. My Auntie Maureen, she's a right firebrand for Scottish independence. She’s got Scottish grandparents on her Mam’s side, you see. She used to tell me stories about visiting her Gran in Glasgow as a little girl. She says it felt like a different country, a place with its own spirit. My mum’s got a friend who lives in Edinburgh, she loves it.

Honestly, tha’s reet mingin', innit? Look at ‘em! Arguein’ over a DNA test like its the be-all and end-all. Proper drama. Aye, it is a bit much, isn’t it? But you gotta admit, Jeremy Kyle's face…it's just priceless. Like he’s permanently having to deal with the most ridiculous people on the planet. Which, let's face it, he probably is. I just don't understand why people go on that show. You know you're going to get shouted at, humiliated, and probably told you're a terrible person. What’s the appeal? Well, tha’s got to have a bit of a masochistic streak, don't tha? And look at 'er, talkin' about "he's me li'l angel." Angel, my foot! He’s clear as day cheatin'! Don’t be so harsh, love. Maybe she's just desperate. Everyone’s got their reasons for doin’ daft things. Listen to that though, she’s just elided ‘is. She said "’e's me li’l angel". Proper Yorkshire, that is. Elided? Is that what you’re calling it? I call it proper lazy talkin’. We all do it, though, don't we? I say "gonna" instead of "going to" all the time. Mum’s always on at me about it. Says I sound uneducated. Your mum says everything’s uneducated, doesn’t she? Mine’s the same. She's always correcting my Scouse. Like saying "I’m gonna go" is a crime against the English language. It’s just quicker! It’s just…efficient. That's what I tell my mum. Least, that’s what I say when she's griping about my dropping the 'g' in "going." I mean, why say "going" when "goin'" says the same thing? It saves time! True! Gets the point across quicker. Like when they’re talkin’ about bein’ “proper bothered”. Don't need to drag it out, do ya? “Proper bothered.” Just gets right to the punch. It’s the rhythm of it, isn't it? All these accents - Yorkshire, Scouse, Midlands…they all have their own rhythms. And elision just fits right in. Makes the words flow. Listen to Jeremy, even  he  does it sometimes. See! He just said “'avin’ a laugh!” He’s fallin’ prey to it too! Even a professional...well, a professional something. He's a professional arguer, love. That's his job.

Right, right. Honestly, this ref is having a right mare, innit? Giving nothing to Newcastle! Absolutely nothing. He is a bit questionable, I’ll admit. Though, to be fair, it's a fast-paced game. Hard to catch everything. Still, that tackle on Isak was dodgy. Dodgy? Aye, dodgy doesn’t even cover it! That was a clear foul! My mam would have had a heart attack if she’d seen that. She’s proper passionate about the Toon, she is. Remember that time she painted the whole house black and white after we won the FA Cup in '99? Vaguely. I was a teenager then, wasn’t I? I seem to recall a lot of black and white bunting, and your dad looking incredibly stressed. Stressed? He was mental! Spent the whole week scrubbing the black paint off the patio. Worth it though, didn't it? Anyway, back to the ref. Honestly, he's favouring Man U big time. Let's try to maintain some objectivity here. It’s only 1-0. Plenty of time for Newcastle to equalize. Besides, look, they're building something up down the left wing now… Aye, that's Miggy. He's a canny player, that one. You know, I was thinking, the Olympics are coming up. Remember how excited we were in 2012? The whole country was buzzing. Absolutely. It was amazing. The atmosphere in London was electric. I spent a week volunteering at the rowing venue - a truly memorable experience. Though, I think I’m more used to being on the sidelines now, researching rather than actively participating. My knees aren’t what they used to be. Researchers’ knees are the worst. All that sitting! I've been trying to take up knitting to get my hands moving a bit more. Keeps me busy when I'm drowning in data. It's surprisingly relaxing. What do you think of this scarf? It's fantastic! Really striking colours. You’re getting quite good, you know. My mum tried knitting once, ended up with a shapeless blob she claimed was a hat. Well, that’s a hurdle we'll need to overcome. I'm thinking of doing a blanket for the baby when… well, you know. Yes, when. Have you given any more thought to names? Penelope and Arthur are still top of my list. Aye, still considering. Penelope’s lovely, but feels a bit… posh?

Honestly, you two. You’ve watched  The Bee Movie  three times this week! Three! And every single time, you ask me the same question. But, Mummy, does Barry actually  own  the flowers? Like, legally? No! He makes a deal! It’s just like King Arthur! Except with bees. Right, a bee-themed King Arthur. That’s… a new one. And no, darling, Barry doesn't  own  the flowers. It was all a complicated, slightly ridiculous, legal argument in a film. It's not real life. But what if it  was  real life? What if bees  did  own the flowers and charged us to pick them? Then I’d be King! I’d make the bees pay  me  to protect the flowers! And I’d have a round table! With bee-shaped seats! You're a very ambitious king, aren't you? You know, it’s a bit like going to Buckingham Palace. You have to pay to go in, don't you? But why? It’s the Queen’s house! Shouldn’t it be free? That's what a lot of people think, love. Some people believe we should be a republic, like France or America. No King or Queen, no palaces paid for by taxpayers. But then who would wear the sparkly crowns? And have the corgis? Excellent point. Though, I imagine a president could get a dog too. Perhaps a very grumpy bulldog. Look, the thing is, being royalty is a bit like being a politician, isn’t it? A lot of responsibility, a lot of attention, and you have to try and do things that are good for the country and the people. I want to be a politician! I’ll make everyone have to eat fruit! Royal fruit! Like… like the Queen’s plums! Are those special? Well, posh people sometimes think fruit grown on royal estates has a certain something. Though, I suspect it's mostly the  idea  of it being royal. We’ve got some lovely blueberries in the fridge, though. Much more important for you two – full of vitamins! Vitamins are boring. Can we go see the diving at the stadium? Remember? We talked about it. Of course! That'll be brilliant. But we have to be  very  quiet. Remember what I said? Like watching royalty. You have to be respectful and silent. Quiet? That’s hard! Especially when I want to shout "Go, diver!"

Oh, my word. That was a beastly clear-out, wasn't it, Arthur? Honestly, you wouldn't believe the amount of clutter one accumulates over a lifetime. Felt a bit like clearing out a museum of forgotten regrets, I did. A museum of forgotten regrets? That's a rather poetic way of describing it, Mum. Though I can’t entirely disagree. Found your collection of ceramic thimbles, didn’t I? Mountains of 'em. They were my grandmother’s, Arthur! Each one a little treasure! And now they’re off to some charity auction, no doubt ending up in someone’s novelty Christmas stocking. Such a waste. Wasteful or not, Doreen, at least it's one step closer to you moving. Honestly, your house is bursting at the seams. And you'll love that little cottage in Thirsk, you really will. Much easier to manage. Thirsk…yes, well. It’s a big change, Brenda. A very big change. I’m dreading it, to be honest. Leaving all my memories here… It’s not just bricks and mortar, you know. It’s…well, it's everything. Speaking of big changes, did you hear about Liam’s stag do? Apparently, they're going white-water rafting! Aye, mad, innit? Reckon he'll be alright? They've got proper wetsuits, have they? Last thing he needs is hypothermia on his stag. Don’t worry, lad. They've got all the gear. It should be a laugh, although his mum’s already put a bet on how many times he'll fall in. Really, Arthur! Betting on your son's near-drowning experience? Manners, man! Though… …I suppose a small wager wouldn’t hurt. Honestly, Doreen! You’re terrible. Liam’s getting married! This should be a happy occasion. Although, have you seen that new series on the telly, 'The Chronicles of...' what’s it called? Something with a Scottish clan? Absolutely dreadful acting. I nearly switched it off after five minutes. You mean 'Highland Legacy'? It’s on BBC Scotland, Brenda. Not exactly BBC One quality, is it? Though, the scenery is lovely. Reminded me a bit of my grandfather’s stories about the Jacobites. He used to spin a right yarn about Bonnie Prince Charlie. My gran told me stories about the Romans! Built roads everywhere, she said. Proper clever they were. Easier than trying to get a decent mobile signal out in the countryside now.

Oy, Beth! I’m knackered. That school run was a right palaver today. Absolute chaos trying to find parking near the blasted museum. You again, battling the museum parking gods? Seriously, Liam, you need to find an alternative. It’s going to give you an ulcer. How was the exhibition, though? The Ancient Egyptian one, right? Yeah, Ancient Egypt. It were alright, mind. Loads o’ mummies and stuff. Little Billy was proper chuffed, though, kept shouting "Pharaoh!" at everything. Nearly deafened me, he did. But the parking... honestly, Beth. I circled for twenty minutes. Ended up leaving him halfway down the street, practically running across the road. It wasn't ideal, not ideal at all. Right, classic. We  need  to brainstorm your parking situation. Maybe the train one stop over? It’s a bit of a walk, but saving your sanity is worth it. Speaking of brainstorming… how did the interview for the Masters go? You sounded a bit stressed about it last night. Went alright, I think. The fella seemed alright, proper chatty even. Asked loads about classroom management and different learning styles. I just tried to sound confident and knowledgeable. Did alright on the bit about applying Chomsky’s theories, I reckon. Fingers crossed, eh? Need the scholarship though, that's the kicker. You will! You’re brilliant, Liam. Seriously, you have such a knack with those kids. And you know your stuff. Scholarship or not, they’d be lucky to have you. So, what are you thinking for Christmas this year? We need to start thinking about pressies for your mum and dad - Auntie Carol's already started hinting about a new scarf for your mum. Aye, Christmas. Feels a million miles away still, doesn’t it? I was thinking… maybe a new record player for me dad? He's been moaning about his old one for ages. And for your mum... hmm... maybe something from that little shop on Bold Street? You know, the one with all the fancy candles. Ooh, that’s a good idea for my mum. I like it. Though, remember last Christmas, Dad spent the entire day fiddling with the new Bluetooth speaker, and never actually listened to any music on it! We need to be more strategic. Actually, talking about money… have you looked at the quotes for the removal company yet? Just had a look this afternoon. Bloody daylight robbery, the lot of ‘em!

Honestly, this Wi-Fi is  atrocious  today. I’ve been trying to upload a picture to Insta for like, fifteen minutes. It’s just spinning. You’d think a uni could manage a decent connection, wouldn’t you? Tell me about it! I tried to stream that new episode of ‘The Bear’ during my break earlier and it kept buffering. It’s infuriating. Proper ruins the vibe, innit? You uploading something glam? Nah, not really. Just a flatlay of my notes from the lecture. Thought it would be ‘aesthetic’ or something. You know, gotta keep the followers happy, right? What about you? What’s keeping you busy on Insta these days? Mostly just watching Reels, to be fair. There’s this proper funny one going around of a dog trying to steal a pizza... makes me laugh every time. You seen it? Anyway, I was just scrolling and saw Liam posted a picture from that football match yesterday. Proper dodgy ref, wasn’t he? Oh my god, yes! So unfair! They should've given us that penalty! Liam looks fit in that picture though... he always does. Bit of a cliché footballer look, ya know? Dark hair, strong jaw... You’re proper obsessed with him! Remember when you were convinced he liked you after he smiled at you in the library? Don’t remind me! That was mortifying. I thought I was being all smooth and subtle, and he was probably just smiling because he saw a spilled coffee on my lap. Anyway, what are you doing this weekend? Fancy going to that new cafe, "Brew & Bloom"? I’ve heard they do amazing matcha lattes. Ooh, proper sounds good! I was thinking of heading back to see my nan, though. She’s been feeling a bit poorly, so I promised I'd pop over. Maybe next weekend? We could even watch some Disney. I'm in the mood for nostalgia. 'The Little Mermaid' perhaps? Yeah, definitely! I’ve been craving a Disney marathon. Remember when we were kids and we’d watch 'Beauty and the Beast' on repeat? My mum used to make us popcorn with extra butter. Simpler times, eh? They were! Before essays and stress and dodgy Wi-Fi. Speaking of stress, have you even started thinking about your dissertation yet? I'm dreading it. Don't even mention it! I'm planning on pretending it doesn't exist until, like, November.

This is taking ages. Can we Skyping Grandad after dinner? I wanted to show him my new Charizard card. It's holographic! Of course, love. Just finish your dinner first. Oisin's making a right mess, isn’t he? Look at him, he’s got green all over his face! Baa! He’s a little…enthusiastic, isn’t he? Anyway, Grandad was saying he finally downloaded Pokémon Go. Can you imagine? He's going to be all over Bristol catching Pikachus. That's brilliant! He sounds like he's having a laugh. You should tell him about the new expansion pack – the one with the mythical Pokémon, remember? Yeah! I’ve been saving up for it ages. I’m just short a few quid. Maybe I can do some extra chores… Don't you worry about that, sweetie. We can sort something out. Speaking of saving up, do you remember we talked about going to that Ramen place in town? Yeah! The one with the huge bowls of noodles? Can we go this weekend? Please? We can definitely look into it. Oisin's pretty much a walking hurricane at the moment, so we’ll need to plan carefully. Maybe Saturday afternoon? After you’ve had a proper practice on the guitar? Yeah! I'm trying to learn that new riff. It’s tricky. Mom keeps saying I need to practice more, but it's hard when all I want to do is play Pokémon. Well, a bit of both is good, isn't it? A balanced life. Though, honestly, I wouldn’t mind a little peace and quiet sometimes. Oisin's been experimenting with the volume on the telly. It's been rather…loud. Tee! Tee! He's got good taste, then. What's he watching? Just some cartoon with singing animals. It's surprisingly catchy. By the way, have you seen your slippers? I can’t find them anywhere. Nope. Maybe Oisin's taken them. He likes chewing on things he shouldn’t. Oh, don't even mention it! Last week he was trying to eat a corner of the rug! Speaking of things little ones shouldn’t do, I saw a picture online of a kid wearing skinny jeans. They looked so uncomfortable! Yeah, they are a bit tight, aren't they? I was thinking about getting some, but then I thought, nah, I’d rather be able to breathe.

Honestly, this cupboard is a disaster zone, isn't it, Doris? I don't know how I've let it get so cluttered. It's like a time capsule of forgotten… things. Tell me about it, Margaret! I'm surprised you’ve even found room for the robin. It  is  rather a monument to dust, though. Right, let's tackle this systematically. What shall we start with? Oh! What's this lurking at the back? Good heavens! Is that… the gardening set? The little plastic trowels and watering can? Remember those? We were convinced we were award-winning horticulturalists, digging for buried treasure in Mum's flowerbeds. Oh, Margaret, bless you! I'd almost forgotten. Tiny gardening gloves, too. They were horrifyingly itchy, weren't they? We always ended up abandoning the gardening and just making mud pies instead. I remember Mum saying, "Honestly, you two are more trouble than they’re worth!" With a smile, of course. She didn’t really mean it. She liked our chaos. She did, didn't she? Always said we brought the sunshine in. Honestly, those flowerbeds were probably ruined forever. We’d transplant dandelions like they were prize-winning roses. It's funny what survives, isn’t it? All this… stuff. It’s like a little window into being eight again. Speaking of surviving… look! The Bako set! Goodness, this takes me right back. Remember how we’d design elaborate castles and space stations? Oh, Bako! Absolutely! Those oddly shaped wooden blocks. We’d spend hours,  hours , building these impossible structures, and then inevitably knock them down with a dramatic flourish. I think we were practicing our demolition skills, really. We were so serious about it. Each block had its purpose, didn’t it? The long ones were always the supports, and the triangle-shaped ones were… well, I can’t quite remember what the triangles  were  supposed to be, actually. Flags, maybe? Flags, yes! Or battlements! We were clearly aspiring to be medieval architects. Though, demi-architects really, considering the propensity for collapse. It is a bit melancholy, isn't it? All this stuff reminding you of… simpler times. It is. But a lovely melancholy. It’s nice to remember. You know, the weather’s been dreadful lately, hasn’t it? Proper dreary. I was thinking of planting some lavender on the little patio, if it ever stops raining. Oh, that’s a lovely idea, Doris.

Honestly, darling, I’m starting to think we've imported a whole ecosystem of mosquitoes with little Leo. He's been absolutely  covered  in bites this week. I put repellent on him before we left, but… you know how they are. Little vampires. You’re not wrong. I’ve been bitten senseless myself. It's ridiculous. Are you sure you used the deet-based one? That’s the only stuff that  really  works on them. I’ll grab another bottle later. Did you remember to check the mosquito net for the crib? Yes, definitely. It was a nightmare last night. He was waking up all the time, scratching. I felt terrible for him. I keep thinking we should invest in one of those citronella burners for the garden, but then I worry about him being near the smoke. Good shout about the net. Citronella is a possibility, but let's keep him well away from it, yeah? It's probably just a particularly bad year for them. Remember that summer when we were at university and there were literally swarms of them? Oh god, yes! That was awful. We couldn’t even sit outside. Speaking of awful... I’m still fuming about the traffic on the way here. It was completely gridlocked. Why do they always decide to close the A11 on a Saturday morning? Tell me about it. I checked the traffic reports before we left and it looked alright, but then... chaos. Probably some roadworks. Everything seems to be under construction these days. It added at least twenty minutes to the journey. Twenty minutes! I was genuinely worried we wouldn't make it to the park before he woke up. And I was craving that cafe latte from the little place near the bandstand. We'll get there. Patience, my love. It’s Saturday. Let's try and enjoy it. Speaking of enjoyment… did you manage to get tickets for that Fontaines D.C. gig next month? I know how keen you were. I did! I snagged two just last night. They were selling out fast. I was refreshing the page constantly. I almost had a heart attack! I'll have to book a babysitter now, though. Finding someone reliable at short notice is proving tricky. Fantastic! That's brilliant news. I'm so glad you got them. We should celebrate properly. Maybe after Leo's in bed, we could order a take-away and have a little dance party in the living room.

Blimey, that was a day. Honestly, Mrs. Higgins nearly gave me a heart attack on the 12th. Kept shouting "Fore!" like I'd sprouted wings and was about to land on her picnic. Fore? Seriously? You’d think she'd seen a proper ghost at that point. How was the rest of the round? Did you at least manage to avoid the water hazard on the 7th? Managed to, yeah. It felt like a battle out there. The wind kept shifting, and the green was playing a right trick on me. Finished two over, which isn't terrible considering, but not brilliant either. I’m knackered though, absolutely shattered. Fancy a cuppa? Please. And something to eat? I haven't moved from this chair all afternoon, trawling through recruitment websites. It’s mind-numbing. Have you seen that new advert for the marketing assistant role at Sterling & Croft? Sounds… vaguely interesting. Sterling & Croft? Sounds fancy. So, still no luck then? This job hunt’s got to be wearing you down. You’ve sent out so many applications already. I know! And I'm barely getting any replies. It's the ‘experience’ thing again, isn't it? How am I supposed to get experience when nobody will  give  me experience? It's a proper catch-22. At least you've got golf tournaments and sponsorships to pad out your CV. True, true. Listen, about that. I got a letter today. Well, it was actually shoved through the door with all the bills, so I nearly missed it. It’s from the University of Manchester. Manchester? What about it? Are they finally offering you an honorary doctorate for being the best golfer in the South East? Not quite. It’s an offer for a place on their Sports Management course. They said they were impressed with my application and my… dedication to the sport. Apparently, they're running a specific scholarship for rising golfing talents. Seriously? That's… incredible, Liam! You're joking! You’re thinking about doing it? Well, that’s what I'm trying to decide. It would mean moving to Manchester, though. That's a pretty big commitment. And I'd have to take a break from the tournaments, at least for a while. But it could open up so many doors, you know? Coaching, management, the whole shebang. Oh my god. Don't even try to pretend you’re not tempted.

Jaysus, will ye look at that racket, Aisling? Little Finn's gone and decided to audition for 'The Voice' tonight, hasn't he? He’s actually quite good, you know. Bit off-key with the high notes, but the enthusiasm's there. It’s “Twinkle Twinkle Little Star,” by the way, not some cutting-edge audition piece. He’s adorable. Absolutely adorable. Reminds me of when my Leo used to belt out nursery rhymes at the top of his lungs. Utter chaos, but lovely. And the dinner smells amazing, Liam, honestly. What is it? It’s shepherd's pie, love. Proper comfort food. Needed something hearty after a day wrestling with the cloud servers – they’ve been giving me the absolute divil. Think I'm gonna need a strong cup of tea after this. Twinkle, twinkle, little star… How I wonder what you are! He's really committed to this, isn’t he? I told him he needed an audience. He said he wanted to perform for someone important. He certainly got his wish. He’s performing for the most important people in the world right now. Right, love? For your Da and your… For me too! And for Auntie Chloe. It's lovely to see him so happy. Though, honestly, having a toddler perform opera sessions at 7 pm is a lot. My ears are ringing already. Speaking of arrangements, how's your mum doing? You were saying she needed a lift to the doctor’s tomorrow? Yeah, still needs it. I can do that, no bother. Around half past ten, is it? Need to check my meetings first, but I can shuffle things. This cloud migration is eating into my personal time something fierce. Thank you, Liam. You're a lifesaver. It’s just… it’s all a bit much at the moment, you know? Trying to juggle everything, Leo’s speech therapy appointments, the groceries… You’re doing brilliantly, Aisling. You really are. Don't beat yourself up about it. And tell your mum I said hello. I was thinking, if you're free on Saturday, we could go see that new superhero film? The one with the ridiculously long title? Finn’s been obsessed. Ah, superheroes. Always been partial to a bit of caped crusader myself. Sure, why not? That’d be good. Gives Finn something to talk about besides cloud computing. Honestly, the thought of leaving the house on Saturday… it’s overwhelming.

Honestly, love, you wouldn’t believe it. Little Anon was fast asleep on the sofa earlier, covered in a blanket... and just his pants. Just the bloody pants! I didn’t know whether to wake him or just… leave him. Oh, bless him! He’s been non-stop all day, hasn't he? Probably just exhausted himself with all the investigating. Are you sure it wasn't a tactical move? Maybe he was trying to assert dominance over the sofa. Dominance? With a pair of dinosaur print boxers? I think not. It was pure, unadulterated toddler exhaustion. I managed to get him tucked into bed without a peep, though. He's out cold. Dinosaurs are strong! Roar! See? He  does  appreciate the dinosaur boxers! Go back to sleep, sweetheart. Daddy's just having a chat with Mummy. Speaking of chats... I was looking at those estate agent websites earlier. Just dreaming, obviously. But… remember how we were saying we needed more space? Vaguely. Trying not to dwell on the financial improbability of it all. What were you looking at? Well, there's a place just outside Stowmarket, a bit bigger than this one, with a decent garden. But the real kicker is the planning permission they have for a single-story extension at the back. An extension! Right. Let’s reel back the excitement a little. That’s a  massive  undertaking, isn’t it? And Suffolk planning… let’s just say they’re not exactly known for their speedy approvals. I know, I know. But imagine it, love! A proper playroom for the kids. A dedicated office for you, away from the chaos. And I was thinking, maybe a little conservatory attached? Somewhere to sit and read in the winter. Playroom! With a slide! And bouncy castle! A bouncy castle, is it? You're certainly setting the bar high. We’d need a mortgage the size of the Isle of Wight. Don't be so dramatic. We'd budget. We’d cut back on takeaways. We’d… sell my extensive collection of Star Wars figurines. Now you're talking. But seriously, let’s not get carried away just yet. Let's just look at the plans, see what’s involved. It’s nice to dream, though. I quite like the idea of a conservatory. Somewhere to propagate my succulents. See? You’re warming to the idea! Imagine, all those succulents, basking in the sunlight, while the kids are bouncing around in their brand new playroom.

Honestly, Alun, this instant stuff is getting on my nerves. It tastes like burnt toast and despair. Did you manage to get the proper beans in today? Now, now, Charles, don't be so dramatic. It's coffee, not ambrosia. And yes, I did. Got a bag of Ethiopian Yirgacheffe from that new place down the High Street. It's a bit pricier, admittedly, but worth every penny, I reckon. You'll find it a definite improvement. Good man. I’ll need something to fortify me. This funding application for the Mesopotamian excavation is proving… difficult. They want a breakdown of every last trowel and sieve, and insist on a detailed risk assessment for encountering angry beetles. Angry beetles, Alun! Tell me about it. Trying to justify the cost of the new laser scanning equipment for the Celtic history project? It’s a nightmare. They treat you like you’re asking for a private jet, not tools to understand the past. Did you hear back about that grant from the Wellcome Trust? Not a peep. Radio silence. Which is invariably a bad sign. I’m starting to think we need to rethink the entire methodology. Perhaps a more… interdisciplinary approach? Something involving, I don’t know, invertebrate behavioural studies. Angry beetles, indeed! Look, Charles, you’re brilliant at what you do, you know that. Don't start questioning your methods entirely. They're just being tight-fisted. I had similar issues when I was applying for that Heritage Lottery Funding. Ended up having to bake a cake for the review panel. A Victoria sponge, no less. A Victoria sponge? Good heavens! You, a lauded academic, bribing officials with baked goods? Desperate times, Charles, desperate times. It did get them to look at the project a little more favourably. Speaking of desperate, have you seen the latest bill from Thames Water? They're robbing us blind! Don't even get me started. It’s obscene. They’re charging me for water I'm almost certain I'm not using. I'm seriously contemplating moving to a self-sufficient eco-village in Devon. Grow my own vegetables, capture rainwater... You and your utopian visions. Though, I understand the sentiment. I've been thinking about a holiday myself. Italy, perhaps. Always wanted to see the Amalfi Coast. Imagine, lemons, sunshine, good pasta... Italy. Yes,  that  sounds like a plan. We could pop over to CERN while we're at it.

Right, Operation Lego Sort is officially underway. Honestly, you two are brilliant at building, absolutely terrible at tidying. Look at this mess! It's like a dragon exploded. But Mummy, the dragon  did  explode! He exploded and left all these sparkly bits! See? This is definitely a tower piece, Mummy. Not a bridge. Towers are strong. Bridges wobble. You’re both right, in your own way. And you're very observant, darling. Yes, it  was  a sparkly dragon. And yes, towers are strong. Right, let's try and group them. Blues with blues, reds with reds... any preference? Can we make a castle, Mummy? A  really  big one! Like in Harry Potter! With lots of turrets and a secret passage! And a house elf! I want a spaceship! Like the Ninja Turtles have! A super-fast one that can go to other planets! With laser cannons! Okay, okay. We can absolutely have a castle  and  a spaceship. But first, we need to sort these bricks. Otherwise, how will we  build  anything? It's a bit like trying to bake a cake without any flour, isn’t it? But sorting is boring. Can we watch The Simpsons while we sort? Bart is funny! Yeah! And then we can talk about which Ninja Turtle is the best. I still think it’s Leonardo. He’s the leader. The Simpsons is tempting, I’ll admit. But let's try and focus for, say, fifteen minutes? Then we can have a break and watch some TV. Deal? And we can debate the merits of each Ninja Turtle afterwards. It's a very important debate. Deal! But I get to pick the episode! And I get to pick the Ninja Turtle! Fine, fine. You've both got it. Right, let’s get cracking. This mountain of Lego won't sort itself. And speaking of cracks… Granny’s house is still such a state after the leak. We really need to get down there and help her sort through all those boxes. She's been trying to do it all herself. Granny’s house is dusty! And she has funny old pictures. Yeah, and she keeps wanting us to dust her porcelain cats. They creep me out! They  are  a bit weird, aren't they? But Granny loves them. She’s just a bit… overwhelmed, bless her. We’ll tackle that soon. Right now, Lego is the priority.

Oh my god, it’s  good  to be back. This place feels like a haven after battling Gatwick. Seriously, that airport is a nightmare. Welcome home! You look exhausted. Holiday was…intense? You’re a bit flushed. How was Greece? Spill! I’ve been dying to hear all about it. Intense is an understatement. Sun, sea, sand…and a lot of very persistent wasps. Honestly, I spent more time swatting them than relaxing. But yeah, it was gorgeous. Santorini was breathtaking, obviously. All those white houses clinging to the cliffs. We did a boat trip to a black sand beach, which was amazing, and the food…oh, the food. I think I’ve put on about five pounds. Typical. You always come back with an extra kilo or two. Worth it, though, right? Did you take loads of pictures? I expect a full slideshow when you're feeling up to it. Anything exciting happen? Meet any cute locals? There was  one  local…Let's just say he was very charming and had a ridiculously sculpted jawline. His name was Dimitri. He worked at the taverna we ate at most nights. We had a few chats, mostly about the best way to cook octopus – apparently, there's a  very  specific technique. Octopus expertise, huh? Sounds promising. Did 'a few chats' involve anything more than octopus advice? Don't leave me hanging! And don’t tell Mum, she’ll have a fit. Okay, okay! We went for a couple of drinks one night. Just drinks, though! Strictly platonic – I’m still reeling from the Mark debacle, remember? I need a period of enforced solitude and Netflix, not another complicated situation. Besides, he was married. Sort of. Apparently, the paperwork wasn’t quite sorted. It was all very Greek, you know? Oh, you are a magnet for drama. Honestly, Mark was a disaster. Good riddance to him. Solitude and Netflix sounds about right. Though, I'm happy to provide some company when you need it. So, speaking of drama, how was Mum and Dad’s birthday bash? Did Sarah bring that awful boyfriend again? Ugh, yes. Barry. He's still wearing those awful Hawaiian shirts. And he still makes those incredibly inappropriate jokes. Dad just silently changes the subject, but Mum tries to engage with him, bless her heart. It's excruciating to watch. I mostly just stuck to the buffet and pretended to be fascinated by the floral arrangements.

Right then, that’s the kettle on. Arthur, love, could you pop the biscuits out? They’re in the tin, top shelf. And Liam, put your feet up, boy, you're lookin' all scrunched up like a bit of crumpled paper. I’m fine, Mum. Just thinking about this physics assignment. It's a nightmare. Are Gran and Grandpa here yet? We’re here, pet! We're here! Just parked the car, Arthur got a bit flustered trying to find a space, bless him. All these fancy modern cars, so big! Remember when a Mini was a big car? Fancy modern cars, aye. Need a degree in navigation to park 'em. And a lot of patience, which I’m runnin' short on. Oh, Arthur, you’re always complaining about the parking. Now, come and sit down, both of you. You look like you’ve walked a marathon. Liam, offer your great-grandparents a biscuit, will you? Here you go, Gran, Grandpa. Chocolate digestives, your favourite, right? Lovely, love! Thank you, dear. You're a good lad, Liam. Always polite. Not like some of these youngsters I see these days… glued to their phones. Aye, eh, phones are the devil's work, I tell you. Distractin’ folk, that’s what they are. Back in my day, conversation was conversation. Face to face. Right, let’s not get started on the state of the youth, Arthur. We'll all be here 'til closing time. Now, I was thinking, Liam, could you pop down to the shops tomorrow? We’re runnin' low on milk and bread. And maybe some of them frozen chips you like. Yeah, alright Mum. What time? Sometime after you've finished your physics, mind. Don't be dawdlin’ about. It's not a holiday, you know. Though, Arthur keeps tellin' me it feels like one since he retired! Don't you listen to her, boy! It's the best thing that's ever happened to me! No more foreman shoutin' in my ear. Now I can sit and watch the telly all day. Though Doreen does keep me busy. Don't you start, Arthur! I keep you busy with the gardening, and the grandbabies coming to visit, and remindin' you where your slippers are. You'd be lost without me! Oh, you two... alright, alright. Speaking of grandbabies, I booked that caravan in Robin Hood’s Bay for August. Thought we could all go.

Right, so, little ones, are you two excited for tonight? We’re having a proper movie night! Pan, Peter Pan, Tinkerbell… the whole shebang. Yes, yes! Tinkerbell! Can we have popcorn? Lots and lots of popcorn! Peter Pan’s got a sword! Is he going to fight Captain Hook? He absolutely is, sweetheart! There’ll be plenty of clashing swords and daring escapes. It’s a brilliant film, isn’t it? Although, the original 1953 one… that’s a classic, too. Do you know why they made so many versions, darlings? Because they’re good? Tinkerbell's the best! Because people like pirates! You’re both right! But there’s a bigger reason, actually. Peter Pan is based on a play, written a very long time ago, by a man called J.M. Barrie. He wrote the play, and then it was turned into a book, and then into films. People have loved the story for over a hundred years. It’s about believing in magic and never growing up, really. Never growing up? But I want to be a grown-up! I want to teach, like you! You certainly can, my love. But Peter Pan shows us that there's a bit of magic in being a child. Remembering how to have fun, to imagine. And, you know, sometimes adulting is  hard . It's nice to remember a world where you can fly to Neverland. Can we  really  fly? Like Peter Pan? Not literally, sadly. But we can use our imaginations! That’s the real magic. Think about it – Peter Pan uses happy thoughts and fairy dust. That’s like using your imagination. Fairy dust! I need fairy dust! Where’s Tinkerbell’s fairy dust? Well, Tinkerbell keeps it very safe! It’s a secret. Though, maybe if you’re very, very good, you can find a little bit of magic in your own heart. Have you seen the new versions of the films? The ones with the fairies more prominently featured? They're surprisingly lovely. I found myself surprisingly engrossed. The one with the sparkly Tinkerbell? She talks to Peter Pan! Exactly! She  does , doesn't she? It’s interesting how they’ve evolved the characters over the years. Originally, in the play and the first film, Tinkerbell couldn't talk. She could only communicate through tinkling sounds. It was all down to the actors’ imagination to bring her character across.

Right then. Nearly there. Bit of a beast of a journey this morning, wasn't it? Feels like we've been on the road since before dawn. Tell me about it, Dad. I’m practically vibrating with exhaustion. I swear, I haven't slept properly all week. The kids are just… boundless energy, aren't they? Especially Leo at the moment. Jumping off walls. They’ve got you well and truly worn out, love. Remember when we lived in that little cottage near Bovey Tracey? The children were quieter then, somehow. More time to explore the woods, less time to bounce off the furniture. Bovey Tracey... good times. Shame we had to move. Too remote for your liking, wasn’t it, love? All those winding lanes. Gave me palpitations just thinking about driving in rush hour. It was lovely, though, wasn't it? Quiet, peaceful. Just a bit  too  quiet sometimes. And the school run… endless. I remember you complaining about the potholes, Dad, constantly. They were atrocious! Nearly lost a wheel once. And remember the damp? We had to put dehumidifiers everywhere. It was a charming cottage, no doubt, but the condensation was relentless. That's why we ended up in Exeter, wasn’t it? Easier commute for both of us. Exeter was… expensive. Honestly, the prices! And everything so spread out. It felt like a proper city, which wasn't what we were after. I much preferred Little Compton, back when the children were smaller. Remember that old farmhouse? With the orchard? Oh, Little Compton! The apples! We made the most incredible crumble. And those summer evenings… sitting outside, listening to the sheep. But it was tiny, wasn’t it? Felt cramped as soon as Leo started growing. It was cosy, certainly. But the kitchen… absolutely hopeless! I was practically cooking in the corridor. And the garden… overgrown beyond belief. I spent half my life weeding. We’ve certainly moved around a bit, haven't we? Even that place further west, near Taunton. The one with the sea views? Lovely spot, but the wind… you could barely stand up! Honestly, Dad, you made it sound like living near the coast was an ordeal. I loved it. The fresh air, the walks on the beach… It did have a certain charm. But remember the storms? The power outages? We were without electricity for three days once. Candles everywhere! Three days!

Blimey, this track work is a right bother, isn’t it? Makes a body ache something fierce. Needed a good massage after lugging those stones about, I reckon. A proper Swedish, you know. Not one of those fluffy, aromatherapy relaxations. Give me a good knead and a crack, I say. Aye, it’s a beast, this lot. Been at it since dawn. A Swedish massage, eh? Fancy. I’ve never had one meself. Always thought it a bit… frivolous, really. Though my Elsie, God rest her soul, she'd have gone for it in a flash. She were always after the latest therapies. Frivolous? Not at all! When you’re nearing seventy, dear, your bones start protesting something terrible. It's a necessity, like a cup of tea and a sit-down. You wouldn't understand, working with your hands all those years. What did you do, then, you said? Accommodation manager? Nationwide Building Society, yes. Looked after the flats they used for staff while they were away on training. Bit of this, bit of that, you know. Not exactly back-breaking, but kept you on your toes. Elsie, she volunteered at the hospice for years. Said it kept her young. Kept her perspective, she used to say. A hospice, that's…a noble thing to do. My niece, bless her, she’s a nursery teacher. It's remarkable, the progress they make these days, the things they teach ‘em. Little darlings, all learning about fractions and equality. Equality, now there's a subject. Elsie always said women were considerably smarter than men, if you know what I mean. Never let me forget it, either! Though I did the washing-up most evenings. Took the sting out of it, a bit. Oh, I know the feeling! Men think doing the washing-up is some grand gesture. It’s just…port duty! Honestly, I’ve spent a lifetime battling the presumption that because I dealt in antiques, no one thought I was a serious dealer. “Oh, just a nice hobby, isn’t it, dear?” They’d scoff at my appraisals! It’s the terminology, isn’t it? People don’t understand the nuances. True enough. They lump everything together. Just like with the doctors. Elsie had a touch of…well, she never properly defined it. Something to do with nerves, they said. Specialists used all sorts of jargon. Made my head spin, it did.

Right then, Mum, have a look at this. I’ve been poking around at flights to Crete. EasyJet seem to have some decent prices if we book now. What do you reckon? Crete, lovely! Always wanted to go, you know. Let me see… Oh, those are reasonable, aren’t they? Much better than those ludicrous prices I saw last year. Whereabouts in Crete are we looking at? Well, I was thinking near Chania. I’ve seen some beautiful pictures. There’s this little apartment complex just outside the town, with a pool, and it gets amazing reviews. Close enough to explore, but quiet enough to relax. It’s called… "Olive Grove Retreat," I think. Cor blimey, that's a mouthful. "Olive Grove Retreat," sounds idyllic. Chania is a good choice. Less frantic than Heraklion, wouldn’t you say? Remember that time we went to Malia? Nearly lost you in the crush! Don't remind me! I was about seven, and I was convinced a seagull had stolen my ice cream. You practically had to wrestle through a crowd to find me. I'm definitely steering clear of anywhere like that this time around. Relaxation is the key objective, remember? No adrenaline pumping activities. Just sunshine and maybe a bit of pottery. Pottery sounds delightful. I've always been a bit rubbish at it, but it's a lovely, calming thing to do. Have you looked at car hire? It's essential for getting around properly, wouldn’t you say? I have, yeah. That’s the tricky bit. Everything seems to be going up. I've compared a few companies – Zest and Rentalcars – but it's still looking like a good £300 for a week, including insurance. It’s a bit more than I was hoping for. Hmm, that  is  a bit steep. Maybe we could look at public transport? I'm not sure how good it is in that area, though. Perhaps a combination of buses and taxis? We don’t need to go everywhere, do we? We could base ourselves and take day trips. I was thinking that too. A car would give us more freedom, obviously, but it's a significant chunk of the budget. Buses and taxis could work, especially if we stick to the coastal towns. Plus, I'd much rather  you  drove, Mum! My eyesight hasn’t been the best lately. Oh, you cheeky thing!

Right, that’s the last of the essay reading for this week. My brain feels like mush, honestly. Did you catch any of the cricket yesterday? Proper nail-biter, wasn't it? Just bits and pieces, love. Was wrestling with these accounts. Always seems to be a drama with them, doesn't it? England were looking shaky there for a minute, though. Had my heart in my mouth. Tell me about it! Root really needed that innings, didn’t he? Thought we were done for when Bairstow went out. But Stokes… Stokes just has that knack, doesn't he? Comes in and just  does  things. He does. Man's a legend. You know, it reminds me a bit of Sir Garry. That resilience, that fighting spirit... They have that in common. Makes you proud to see it, y'know? Definitely. Speaking of proud moments, did you see Auntie Marlene's photos from her trip to Jamaica? She looked absolutely radiant. So happy! Bit jealous, if I'm honest. I need a proper holiday. Marlene always did look good. Proper sunshine soul, that one. Jamaica suits her. Speaking of travel, I got those flight confirmations for Barbados sorted. Everything’s booked. Really? That's brilliant! When are we going? I’ve been looking at some proper rum punches online… for research purposes, naturally. Research is vital. We’re flying out the 15th of next month. Should be a lovely escape. Just need to finalize the villa booking - Auntie Shirley's cousin recommended one near Crane Beach. Apparently, it's spectacular. Crane Beach, eh? Sounds posher than where we stayed last time. Remember that little guesthouse with the slightly dodgy plumbing and the rooster that woke us up every morning? Don't remind me! That rooster was relentless. But it was… characterful, wasn’t it? This one’s supposed to have a pool and a chef. Though I'm not sure I trust a chef to make a decent Bajan macaroni pie. That's a family skill, you know. You think you're the macaroni pie master, do you? I reckon I can give you a run for your money. I've been watching your mum's YouTube tutorials. You’ve been watching my mum!? Blasphemy! Don't you dare try and steal her secrets. That recipe’s been passed down through generations, lad. It’s sacred. Just saying, I'm prepared to learn.

Lovely cuppa, Brenda. Just what I needed. This Skype thing’s knackering, mind you. Keeps givin' me the willies, it does. Keeps cuttin' out. It's a bit patchy, isn't it, Arthur? But it's lovely to see you both, even if it’s just on a screen. How's the leg today? Still givin’ you gyp? Aye, still. Swollen somethin' awful. Doc says it's the arthritis, of course. Just gotta put up with it. At least the garden's dryin' out a bit. Managed a bit of weeding this mornin’, but it took it out of me, it did. Morning all! Sorry I’m late, the traffic was dreadful. Birmingham's a right nightmare, especially around rush hour. You wouldn’t believe the state of the M6! Brenda, lovely to see you, you look well. Arthur, how's the ancient leg holding up? 'Ello Clive. Traffic, eh? Always is, innit? And the leg’s… it’s a leg. It’s doin’ what it does. Fancy a biscuit? Brenda’s got those ginger ones I like. Of course, Arthur. There’s plenty. Clive, have you had anything to eat? I've made a Victoria sponge. That sounds amazing, Brenda! I think I’ll have a slice later. I was just looking at something on the internet. Remember those big globes we used to have in schools? Oh aye! Jolly big things they were. Spin 'em round and point at where you wanted to go. Used to dream of goin' to Australia, I did. Never got round to it, though. You always wanted to go to Australia, Arthur. You and your fascination with kangaroos. You even tried to build a miniature one out of pipe cleaners once for a school project, didn't you? Did I? Blimey, did I? Got a right telling off from Mrs. Higgins, I did. Said it wasn't educational. It's funny, isn’t it? All those school projects, geographical dreams… I was obsessed with Yorkshire when I was a kid. Spent ages researching it for a class presentation. Wished I'd actually  gone  to Yorkshire! Always wanted to stay in a youth hostel there. Yorkshire’s lovely! I went once with my parents when I was a teenager. We stayed in a little bed and breakfast near York. The Moors are beautiful. Remember that documentary about the underground system in London Clive? Fascinating stuff.

Right, so, EasyJet’s being proper cheeky with prices, innit? Like, £80 just to get from Leeds-Bradford to Gatwick? For a Saturday? You'd think they were flying us to Mars, not London. Tell me about it! I’ve been checking Ryanair too, and they’re not much better. Honestly, it’s ridiculous. The price of flights these days… Remember when we could get return tickets for like, thirty quid? Thirty quid! That’s a dream now, isn’t it? I'm looking at the 24th of October. It's for your cousin's wedding, yeah? Yeah, Leo’s wedding. It’s at that place outside Surrey. Bit fancy, apparently. Apparently, they’ve got a string quartet. My Aunt Carol is absolutely  thrilled . She’s been practicing her clumsy dancing already, I’m sure. Bless her. Right, back to flights. Do you want me to keep looking? Maybe Tuesday or Wednesday would be cheaper? I can check. I’m pretty good at this sort of thing, you know, for work, I'm always finding deals. Could you? Honestly, I'd be eternally grateful. I’ve been staring at these screens for an hour now, my brain’s starting to melt. I'm a production controller, not a flight booking expert! There's a reason the clever people at airlines do it rather than me. No worries, love. What about baggage? Are you taking a suitcase or just a carry-on? That can affect the price too, can’t it? Everything’s a sneaky extra these days. Just a carry-on, definitely. I’m trying to embrace minimalism. It’s cheaper, and I'll avoid paying for luggage. Although, Aunt Carol is sending me a fascinator. That'll be a nightmare to pack. It’s all feathers and sparkly things. Probably needs it’s own oxygen tank. Oh, aye, fascinators are evil! Right, I've found something… Leeds-Bradford to Gatwick, Saturday the 24th, with EasyJet, around £65. Carry-on baggage is extra, but it's still a bit better. And there’s a return on the 26th for… £58. That’s a total of £123. £123? That’s  actually  decent! Seriously, that’s a win. Can we book it? Before they put the price up again, like they always do. Hold on, just confirming times… It’s a bit early, 6:30 AM. But it gets you into Gatwick by 8:00 AM.

Right then, that’s a decent cuppa, Annie. Thanks. Reminds me of my mum’s, actually. Used to make a lovely brew, she did. Though she’d likely have had a biscuit or two alongside it, wouldn’t she? Where’s Sarah? Sorry, just finishing up these shortbreads. They’re a bit crumbly, but decent. Sarah’s just popped to the loo, Dad. So, you were saying about your mum's tea? It's lovely to hear those memories. Shortbread, lovely! Thank you, love. My knees are playing up again today. Damp weather, you see. Always sets them off. Oh, and Sarah's been on the phone to me a dozen times about this blooming mobile phone bill. Vodafone are ripping her off! Vodafone! Don't get me started on them. Absolute cowboys. I switched to Three a couple of years back, best thing I ever did. Much cheaper, and the signal's perfectly adequate where I live. Although, you do have to fight to get any decent customer service. It’s all automated these days, isn’t it? Utterly infuriating. It is, isn't it? Sarah’s been trying to get them to honour a special offer she was promised, but they’re playing silly buggers. It's unbelievable the way companies get away with it. It's almost like a deliberate tactic to frustrate people into giving up. I think we should all have a consumer rights advisor on speed dial. A consumer rights advisor! Good idea, Sarah. My nephew, Darren, is a solicitor, isn't he? Maybe he could have a look. It’s not just the money, you know, it’s the principle of the thing. They're preying on people who don’t know their rights. Speaking of money, did you see the price of butter at Sainsbury's yesterday? Absolutely scandalous! Nearly five pounds! Five pounds? For butter? Blimey! I’ve been buying it from Aldi. Much more reasonable. You just have to be a bit clever about where you shop. It's the only way to keep on top of things these days. Retirement's not quite the goldmine I thought it would be, you know. Savings are dwindling faster than I’d like. I know, Dad. It's tough for everyone. Student loans, mortgages... it's a constant battle. I’m thinking of looking into ethically-sourced investments, something to balance out the doom and gloom of the news.

Right, so we're doing favourites, yeah? Absolute belter of an idea, honestly. Let's start easy. Favourite food? 'Cause I could talk about food all day. Definitely biltong. Can’t get enough of it. Bit of a craving, really. Though, I am partial to a good sticky toffee pudding too. Properly drown it in custard, mind. Biltong? Fancy! I've never even tried it. My favourite food… it’s gotta be my mam’s Sunday roast. Proper meaty gravy, crispy roast potatoes, Yorkshire puddings that are actually like little clouds… the whole shebang. Makes me homesick just thinkin’ about it. And a proper plate of chips with vinegar and salt afterwards, of course. Not those skinny chips, mind, the proper thick-cut ones. Sunday roast does sound good, love. But, for me, it’s gotta be a good Irish stew. My granny used to make the best. Lamb, potatoes, carrots, onions, all simmered for hours until it’s practically melting. Seriously hearty stuff. Keeps ya warm on a dreich day. And a wee bit of soda bread on the side to mop up all the juices. Perfection. What about you, Nia? Oh, Irish stew sounds comforting! My favourite food… it’s a bit more unusual, probably. Laverbread and cockles. It's like, seaweed bread, and then salty cockles. Sounds weird, I know. It’s a Welsh delicacy! My great-grandmother used to harvest the laverbread herself. It's got this earthy, umami flavour, and the cockles… well, they’re just brilliant. Not everyone likes it though, obviously! But it’s home for me. Laverbread and cockles? Blimey. That  is  unusual. Right, well, I’m sticking with something more straightforward then. A good curry. Like, a really good, proper fiery vindaloo. Makes your eyes water and your ears ring, that's how you know it's good. And naan bread, obviously. Loads of it. Sopping up the sauce. Can’t beat it. What’s everyone’s favourite animal, then? Don't say a dog or cat, that's boring. Alright, alright, no dogs or cats then. For me, it's probably a penguin. They’re just ridiculously clumsy and endearing. Watching them waddle around in Antarctica… It just makes me smile. They seem so chilled out, despite living in freezing conditions. Penguins are brilliant! Okay, I’ll go with a hedgehog. They’re just so prickly and shy. We get loads of them in our garden back home.

Blimey, this essay's a right pain, innit? Feels like I'm just staring at words rearranged. What's your take on the Hockney exhibition, though? Proper brilliant, wasn't it? Hockney was…fine. Bit predictable, though, yeah? All those bright colours, landscapes. Safe. I mean, it was pleasant, don’t get me wrong, but it didn’t exactly set my soul on fire. Did you see that little Yorkshire sculpture thing, though? The one that looked like a giant crumpled sweet wrapper? That was proper clever. The shiny thing? Yeah, that was alright. Bit naff, maybe. I preferred the portraits, actually. There was somethin’ in 'em, you know? Like, you could see straight into their thoughts. Makes you wonder what everyone's thinkin' now, doesn’t it? What we'll all be like in, like, sixty years. Don't start with that. I’m trying to finish this blasted analysis of Victorian social realism and now you’re throwing existential dread into the mix? Sixty years... I’ll be ancient! Probably living in a pod, eating nutrient paste and playing virtual bingo. Nutrient paste! That sounds horrific. But, you know, maybe it'll be amazing. Flying cars, robot butlers... and we'll all be connected to the internet directly through our brains. Think of the art then! Imagine painting with your  thoughts ! Okay, that  is  a pretty appealing thought. Imagine crafting entire worlds, just by thinking them into existence. No more messy paints and canvases. Though, would that even  be  art anymore? Would there be any skill involved, or would it just be…randomness? I reckon there'd still be skill. The skill would be in  thinking  the right things, shaping the thoughts into somethin' beautiful. It'd be like composing music, but with visuals. What about you, though? What kind of art would you create if you could just… conjure it? I don’t know. Probably something… glitchy. Like, a constantly evolving landscape built from corrupted data. All sharp angles and shifting perspectives. Kinda unsettling, but also beautiful in its own way. Something to reflect on the fragility of things, you know? Less Hockney, more… digital decay. Right, proper gloomy then! I'd probably make loads of bright, sunny beaches. Loads of paddling pools and ice cream vans. Proper cheerful, to counteract all the nutrient paste. You’d be the eternal optimist. Back to the essay though, you actually gonna do it?

Honestly, I’m knackered. This project is eating my life. Every email, every meeting… it’s just relentless. Tell me about it. Nursing's not exactly a walk in the park either, you know. Had a particularly rough shift today. A new patient, really struggling, needed constant monitoring. It’s draining. What are you making? Smells good. Trying to conjure up some sort of pasta bake. It’s comfort food, innit? Need something hearty to de-stress. Found a recipe online, supposedly super easy. Though, knowing my luck, I’ll probably set off the smoke alarm. You and smoke alarms have a complicated relationship. Remember that time you tried to make popcorn? Anyway, what's the project actually about this time? Still the sustainable packaging one for that biscuit company? Yep, still that. And it’s a nightmare. The client keeps changing their mind, and the suppliers are being utterly useless. I swear, I’m going to lose the plot. I had Brenda from accounts send me a passive-aggressive email today about “efficient use of company stationery”. Efficient! I’m coordinating a multi-million pound project! Brenda, the queen of petty. Honestly, some people… You need to just ignore her. Easier said than done, I know. Did you hear back from Liam about Friday? Are we still on for drinks? Not yet. I sent him a text earlier, just a quick “Hey, still up for it?” No response. I'm trying not to get my hopes up, you know? Last time he said he was free, he bailed because his mate had a last-minute FIFA tournament. That’s not fair to you. He needs to be more considerate. You deserve someone who actually follows through. Honestly, I don't know why you waste your energy. I know, I know. Part of me just thinks I’m being ridiculously optimistic. But you know, a girl can dream, can't she? Although, I'm seriously contemplating just staying in on Friday, ordering a takeaway, and watching terrible reality TV. That sounds… wonderfully therapeutic. And much less emotionally taxing than dealing with Liam. But you should still try to go out. Even if it’s just to grab a coffee with me and rant about Brenda. That's tempting. Okay, maybe. What about Sarah and Ben? Are they coming round on Saturday? They said they probably would. Ben’s got a rugby match in the morning, so they might be a bit tired, but they’re keen to see us.

Right then, let's tackle this consent form first. It's a beast, innit? All these legal clauses… Makes yer head spin. I’ve highlighted a few bits I’m not so sure about, particularly the indemnity section. Seems a bit heavy-handed, don't you think? Asking participants to, essentially, absolve the university of any liability if they… well, if something goes wrong. Yes, I noticed that too, Margaret. It’s standard practice, I suppose, but it does feel…extensive. I’m particularly concerned about the clause regarding recording the sessions. We’re intending to record the seminar for our own review and potentially, with permission, to upload snippets to the university’s online learning platform. Do you think we need to clarify that point more explicitly in the form? Avoid any ambiguity about how the recording will be used? Aye, definitely, Sarah. That needs a right good look at. Folks won’t be happy if they’re thinkin' they're just doin' a wee workshop and then suddenly they’re all over Blackboard! I've re-read it and it’s worded in a way that could be interpreted as them being filmed and distributed willy-nilly. We need to add a line saying specifically the recording will be used solely for internal university purposes and with the participant’s explicit, informed consent for any wider dissemination. And specify  how  we'll seek that consent – a verbal confirmation at the start, maybe? Spot on, Gillian. And maybe a section about data protection too, just to be completely covered. GDPR's a minefield these days, isn't it? Alright, let’s make a note to amend the indemnity and recording clauses. Right, moving on – the seminar itself. I was thinkin' we could structure it around three case studies. One focusing on intercultural misunderstandings in negotiations, one highlighting the challenges of non-verbal communication across cultures, and then one looking at the role of technology in facilitating - or hindering - global business communication. What do you reckon? I like the case study approach, Margaret. Very practical. The intercultural misunderstandings one is particularly relevant, I think. Perhaps we could use the classic example of the Japanese business delegation and the American CEO's handshake? Gets the point across quickly and memorably. As for the technology aspect, perhaps we could focus on the nuances of email etiquette in different cultures? What's considered perfectly polite in one country can be incredibly rude in another.

Honestly, Mark, I'm starting to think this whole "revolutionary pedagogical approach" is just going to be a colossal waste of time. The students just stared blankly at me during the group discussion on post-structuralism. Blankly! You know, the ones who  didn't  spend the entire time scrolling through WeChat, anyway. Come on, love. One slightly glazed-over tutorial doesn't invalidate months of planning. Remember Dr. Chen's workshop? It's designed to shake things up, to get them thinking outside the traditional lecture format. It takes time for students to adjust. Besides, you were brilliant explaining Foucault's concept of power – the bit about the panopticon relating to social media… that was gold. It felt like shouting into a void. They just weren't engaging. And the feedback forms… well, let’s just say 'confusing' and 'unclear objectives' were recurring themes. I’m worried I’m just making things  more  difficult for them, not more enlightening. You always worry, don’t you? You’re a brilliant teacher, Eleanor. You’re dedicated and passionate. And you're pushing them to think critically, which is the entire point. Honestly, most of our colleagues are still clinging to PowerPoint presentations and rote learning. You're trying something different. It’s bound to be a bumpy ride. Easy for you to say. Your Victorian literature seminars are always packed and lauded. People actually  want  to hear about Dickens and Bronte. It’s not like I’m delving into the obscure works of Baudrillard and trying to make them relevant to 21st-century Chinese undergraduates. Baudrillard  is  relevant, darling. It's about simulation and hyperreality - think about their experience growing up immersed in digital culture. You just need to find the right hook. Maybe a case study of a popular influencer? Perhaps. Although, I'm more preoccupied with the fact that the estate agent called again today about the apartment. They’ve had another viewing. Really? Already? That’s good news, isn't it? Lowering the price seemed to have an effect. Were they serious buyers? Apparently. A young couple, both working in tech. They seemed… keen. Which is unsettling, to be honest. I keep thinking we’re rushing into this. Selling our flat in Norwich, moving halfway across the world… it’s a massive upheaval. I know it is. But remember why we’re doing this? The career opportunities here are incredible, Eleanor.

Honestly, this is lovely, Liam, but I feel guilty. We bought so much pesto, and realistically, we won’t use it all before it goes off. It’s just… frustrating, you know? All that food waste. Grandma Elsie would have had a fit. Remember her tiny, beautifully organised fridge? Nothing ever went to waste in her house. Mmm, this is good. Yeah, Elsie was epic at that. She'd use vegetable peelings for stock, bread crusts for breadcrumbs… it’s a lost art, isn't it? We live in a world of instant gratification and massive portions. I saw a statistic the other day – something like a third of all food produced globally is wasted. It's insane. Exactly! And it's not just the food itself, it’s the resources that went into producing it. Water, land, transportation… it’s a huge environmental impact. Do you remember how Grandma would always reuse the plastic bags? Even  after  the charge came in. She’d hoard them, apologize for every single one… Of course. She'd be horrified by how readily we use them now. Though, to be fair, it’s more down to supermarkets pushing pre-packaged everything. Less people are properly cooking from scratch these days. What do you think they teach about that in school now? About reducing food waste, I mean. It’s… patchy, to be honest. We do a little bit in Food Tech, focusing on portion sizes and avoiding food spoilage, but it's not a systemic thing. I wish there was more emphasis on practical cooking skills, rather than just theoretical nutrition. I feel like we’re failing some kids – particularly those from lower-income backgrounds who might not have access to home-cooked meals. And careers advice... it’s abysmal. Tell me about it. When I was doing my work experience at that engineering consultancy, they stressed the importance of internships. Like,  essential . But the schools barely prepare anyone for even  that . They just rattle off a list of universities and expected A-Levels. Closed industries, aren't they? It’s all about who you know, isn't it? Absolutely. That’s what I try to tell my Year 10s. Networking, getting involved, looking beyond the obvious. Though, getting them excited about engineering when they’re obsessed with TikTok is a challenge! But seriously, that feels so unfair. Some kids are brilliant but disadvantaged, and they get shut out.

Right, so the initial results from the mindfulness intervention study are in. And… it’s a bit of a mess, to be honest. A mess how? Like, catastrophically, or just… needs a bit of tweaking? Because I've had one of those days at work, so I’m not exactly brimming with optimism for complicated messes. More of a… nuanced mess. There wasn't a statistically significant improvement in anxiety scores overall. Which is, frankly, infuriating, after all that effort. The control group actually showed a slight decrease, which is baffling. I’m starting to think there was some regression to the mean happening – people inflated their anxiety scores initially, hoping for some kind of research windfall. People trying to game the system? Even in mental health research? Honestly, wouldn't surprise me. People are odd. So, you’re thinking about the initial assessment methodology? Partly. And I’m questioning whether the mindfulness technique we chose was appropriate. It was a very structured, eight-week programme, quite rigid. Perhaps something more adaptive, tailored to individual needs, would have been more effective. The literature is so divided on the best approach. Right, because “one size fits all” rarely does, does it? Like those parenting books. Everyone telling you how to raise a perfect child. Madness. Did you speak to Professor Davies about it? He's usually got a good perspective on methodological hiccups. I did. He suggested looking at the qualitative data more closely. He thinks there might be some common themes emerging in the interviews that explain the lack of quantitative improvement. Apparently one participant mentioned finding the rigid structure quite stressful, ironically. Right! Like, the cure causing the problem. Sounds about right. Any luck with Leo's school thing? Did you hear back from them about the support plan meeting? He seemed so down about it yesterday. No, nothing yet. I chased them up this morning. Apparently, the SENCO is swamped and “prioritising” other cases. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m fighting a bureaucratic war. It's all action points and waiting lists and promises that don’t materialise. It's incredibly frustrating when it comes to something so important for him. I know, it’s awful. Don’t let them gaslight you into thinking you’re being unreasonable. You're just trying to advocate for your son. Maybe I'll give them a ring too, on Monday. Two mums are louder than one, as they say up north.

Cor, it’s a miserable day innit? Reminds me of that trip we took to Skegness back in '78. Rain lashed down somethin’ fierce. Didn't see the sun once. Least we had the arcades, though. Kept the kids quiet, they did. Though, I reckon, it cost us a fair few bob. Oh, Skegness! I remember that. You and Margaret were determined to get little Timmy a giant teddy bear. He dragged it around the entire pier, poor love. And the sand…everywhere. It took weeks to get it out of the car. But yes, a miserable day does bring back memories, doesn’t it? Though, not always pleasant ones. I can imagine. Those family holidays… they’re supposed to be idyllic, aren’t they? Like something from a brochure? But reality rarely aligns. You alright, Arthur? You seem a bit…down. Just feelin’ a bit low, Clive. Always do this time of year, you know. The dark days. It’s like...like the sun forgets about Costessey. Makes things harder. Harder to get out, harder to… well, harder to do most things, really. Oh, Arthur, love. We know. It’s been a tough few years. Remember what the doctor said? Fresh air, a bit of gentle exercise... Even just a short walk. And talking about it, like you’re doing now. That’s good. That’s really good. Exactly. And you do have the volunteering at the community centre, don't you? Helping out with the over-60s group? I always thought that suited you. Getting involved, a bit of purpose… It’s alright. Nice folk, they are. But…it's not the same, is it? Doesn't fill the hole, somehow. Reminds me of all the jobs I never had, y'know? All the things I should’ve done. Feels a bit late now. Now, now, Arthur. Don't go doing that to yourself. You had a good life. You raised a family, you kept a roof over your heads… That's more than some can say. And you’re a good man. A kind man. Absolutely. And look, about the money… Have you had another look at those letters from the council? Maybe there's some assistance you’re entitled to that you haven't realised. I could have a look, if you like? I understand the forms can be a bit daunting. They’re pokin’ around, they are. Sayin’ I’ve got too much saved up.

Honestly, I’m obsessed. Completely obsessed. You  have  to try this, Maisie. It's honestly changed my life, or at least my evenings. Oh? What is it now, Chloe? Don't tell me you've gone and found some thirty-pound face cream promising eternal youth. My bank balance is still recovering from that serum you convinced me to buy last month. No, nothing like that! Although, maybe I  should  look into it... But really, it’s this little nail oil. It’s called 'Beneath The Surface' – sounds a bit granola, I know, but the results are phenomenal. Nail oil? Seriously? I mean, I occasionally slap on some hand cream if my hands are dry, but oil? What’s so special about it? My nails are always a disaster, brittle and peeling. I usually just scrub 'em with a nail brush and call it a day. Maisie! You're depriving yourself! This isn't just any oil. It’s got these amazing ingredients – jojoba, argan, pomegranate seed oil… apparently they all work together to strengthen the nails and hydrate the cuticles. And it  works .
