I've been using it religiously every night for about two weeks, and they're noticeably stronger. No more snapping! And the cuticle hangnails… mostly gone! Pomegranate seed oil? Sounds fancy. Where did you even find it? Not in the Tesco nail aisle, I presume. No, I got it online. From a small, independent brand. I’ll send you the link later. It was a bit pricier than your average nail oil, I'll admit, around £18. But honestly, it's worth every penny. My nails used to be so embarrassing, always breaking when I was doing the weeding. Now, I could probably wrestle a badger with them. Probably. You're being ridiculous. Wrestling a badger? But honestly, I’m intrigued. My nails  are  awful. Remember last week when I was trying to open that jar of pickles and my entire nail split? It was mortifying. Exactly! You need this! And it smells gorgeous too. It's got this subtle, earthy scent. Like… sandalwood and something citrusy, I think. Not at all chemically like some of the cheaper ones. Right. Okay, you've almost convinced me. Almost. Anything else you've been raving about lately? I’m trying to decide if I should treat myself to something new. Sarah was saying she found a  fantastic  eyebrow pencil...

Right, so, parking was a nightmare, weren't it? Absolutely mental. I swear, half the city was circling around here tryin' to find a space. Nearly drove me 'round the bend. Shoulda just walked, eh? But me legs were killin' me after lugging all them textbooks. Tell me about it! I spent twenty minutes just creeping along, lookin' for somethin'. And you know what? Ended up parkin' three streets over, payin' a fortune. This city, man. It’s bleedin' ya dry. Seriously! And for what? To look at some dusty Roman mosaics? Don't get me wrong, the Williamson was brilliant, proper brilliant. That Pompeii exhibition was spot on, yeah? But worth the stress and the cost? Debatable. It was good, aye. Though, to be fair, I was thinkin' about potential funding applications for the community project the whole time. Keepin’ one ear on the conversation, one eye on the grant opportunities. That's social work life, innit? Proper. You always got one foot in the work world, don’t ya? Me, I was already daydreaming about Christmas. I’ve been eyeing up a few bits and bobs online for Nan. She’s gettin' sentimental this year, apparently. Wants a proper old-fashioned snow globe. Snow globe, eh? Classic. My mum’s been dropping hints about a new slow cooker. Says mine's on its last legs. Speaking of last legs, how's the Masters interview goin'? You sounded a bit stressed about it last week. Yeah, still a bit nervy, to be honest. Got it scheduled for next Tuesday. Just dreading the ‘tell me about yourself’ bit. Feels like I'm back in school, bein' judged on my entire life. I've been practicin' in front o' the mirror, sounds ridiculous, doesn't it? Not at all! Smart move, actually. Confidence is key. You’ll smash it, Liam. You’re brilliant at what you do teachin', and your dissertation was cracking. They’d be daft not to take you. And think of the money you'll earn afterwards! That’s the long game, innit? It's a lot of debt to take on, though. Makes you think, doesn't it? Maybe I should just stick where I am. At least I’m savin' a bit now. We need to start thinkin' about moving, don’t we? This flat’s gettin’ smaller by the day. Yeah, definitely. We’re bursting at the seams.

Right then, that was a lovely roast. Honestly, feeling quite full now. How's little Leo been today? Did he manage to avoid throwing mashed potatoes everywhere, for once? Surprisingly, yes! He actually used his spoon, mostly. There was a rogue potato that ended up in his hair, naturally, but overall, a monumental success. He’s asleep now, thank goodness. It's been a pretty hectic day. Bless him. It's wearing you out, isn’t it? You must miss having some time to yourself. Are you still thinking about maybe going back to work at some point? I don’t know. It's a complicated thought. Part of me desperately wants to, you know,  be  someone again, not just "Leo's Mum." But the other part… the thought of handing him over to someone else all day just pulls at me. And honestly, the job market's a scary place at the moment. Plus, the childcare costs would practically swallow any wage. Absolutely. It's a genuine catch-22. You're not alone in feeling that, believe me. Remember what Sarah was saying about her struggle re-entering the workforce after having twins? She felt exactly the same. And childcare providers are charging a fortune now. Sarah’s been through a lot, hasn't she? It's good to know I’m not the only one wrestling with this. Speaking of Sarah, how’s Mark treating her? Still showering her with roses and grand gestures? He is, actually. Overdoing it, if I’m honest. She says she’s starting to feel a bit suffocated. The constant declarations of undying love… the surprise weekend trips… it’s a lot. She's hinted to me she'd appreciate a bit more quiet time, you know? Just an evening in, watching a film, without him filming their every move for Instagram. Oh, dear. That does sound intense. It’s like he's trying to  prove  his love, rather than just  showing  it. It's… performative, isn’t it? Exactly! It's not natural. And you know Sarah. She's a pretty independent woman. She values her space. I think he's just a bit insecure, probably from his past, you know? Keeps trying to buy her affection. It's a common problem, isn't it? Men confusing lavish gifts with genuine connection. My ex, David, used to do the same thing. Flowers, dinners, trips… but never really listened when I actually tried to tell him how  I  was feeling.

Honestly, Mark, you wouldn’t believe the deep dive I’ve been on with Pinterest. It’s terrifying. I started looking for ideas for Liam's birthday – he’s turning ten next month, can you believe it? – and now I'm pinning rustic Scandinavian cabins and artisanal vegan cheese boards. Where did  that  come from? Sounds about right. Pinterest has a way of dragging you down rabbit holes. My sister got sucked into competitive bread-baking for a good six months last year. Turns out Yorkshire puddings are serious business. Liam’s turning ten, eh? Time flies. Remember when he used to chase pigeons in Newcastle? Aye, I do! He was convinced they were plotting against him. Little terror. I’m trying to organise something decent for his birthday. Not a huge party, but… something. He's got proper strong opinions now, that lad. Last year, he declared bouncy castles 'uncool'. Ten-year-olds. The ultimate source of arbitrary trends. So, what's the plan? Theme? Lego extravaganza? I was thinking maybe a woodland adventure theme. Building dens, scavenger hunt… it’s a bit more “me” than a bouncy castle, you know? Though I’m having trouble visualizing it without looking like a toddler’s birthday party. All those streamers... shudder. That's where Pinterest comes in, but it's a dangerous game. I saw one that involved building a miniature fairy village out of moss and twigs. I nearly committed. Moss and twigs! Right. Stick with the den-building, I reckon. Keeps them active. Speaking of activity, did you see that new nature documentary on Channel 4? “Wild Isles”? Sir David Attenborough's voice is just… magic, isn't it? Oh my god, yes! It’s stunning. Absolutely breathtaking. I watched the badger one last night. I literally cried. I'm not even a massive badger fan, ordinarily! I told my mam about it – she's obsessed with wildlife now. She’s sending me links to badger sanctuaries and demanding I knit them hats. Your mam sounds delightful. She's definitely embracing retirement. My nan’s been taking up speed-cubing. It’s completely baffling. Says it’s good for her brain. Speed-cubing? Right. Well, at least she’s doing  something . So, have you heard from Chloe and Ben? They were supposed to be arriving here tonight. Just a text earlier. Said they’re stuck in traffic. Apparently, there’s been an accident on the M1.

Right, let’s have a look at these light fittings. Honestly, the sheer volume on eBay is overwhelming. Do you think that brushed nickel one would go with the dining room? It’s a bit…modern, isn't it? Brushed nickel? Hmm. I’m not entirely sold on it either. It might clash with the wood panelling. Remember what happened with the kitchen tiles? We don't want a repeat of that fiasco. Let’s stick to something a bit more classic. See that one? The brass one with the frosted glass shades. That’s more our style, isn't it? Oh, that  is  rather nice. It’s a bit pricey though, isn't it? £75! For a light fitting? Seriously? Well, it looks sturdy. And the reviews are good. Remember that cheap chandelier we bought last time? It fell apart after three months! Better to invest a little more, I think. Anyway, forget the light fittings for a moment. I’ve been having another look at Rightmove. Oh, here we go again. More houses that are either falling apart or cost the earth? Not entirely. I found a couple that are…interesting. One’s in Little Chalfont. It’s a bit smaller than we’d ideally like, but it has a lovely garden and it’s surprisingly affordable. Little Chalfont? That’s quite a trek, isn’t it? I was hoping for somewhere closer to the station, so I can still commute easily. The thought of a longer journey is…draining. I know, but the price is a factor. It’s £480,000. We’ve been saying we need to be realistic. And the garden  is  genuinely beautiful. Mature trees, a patio… imagine summer evenings out there. Alright, let me see… Oh, it  is  quite pretty. And… it’s got a conservatory? That’s a bonus. But the kitchen looks tiny. And the bathroom… good heavens, that’s a disaster zone! Avocado green? Who fits an avocado green bathroom these days? That’s what I was thinking. We'd definitely need to renovate. But think of the potential! We could put our own stamp on it. And the location  is  good, good schools nearby. Schools aren't a concern for us, are they? Unless we're planning on having children, which... we’re not. Okay, okay. It's definitely worth a look. Let’s add it to the list.

Honestly, Doreen, this rain is relentless. Feels like it’s been drizzling for weeks. Makes you want to just wrap up in a blanket and never leave the house. Tell me about it, love. I was walking Percy this morning, and I swear I was battling a small river down Willow Way. That poor dog looked utterly miserable. Did you see Mrs. Higgins’ hydrangea bush? Absolutely flattened. Percy’s looking really fluffy though, isn’t he? I saw him in the garden yesterday, practically a woolly mammoth! Did he get into the compost again, Doreen? Don't remind me! He’s got a nose for that compost like you and I have for a cream cake. I swear, I spent half an hour yesterday picking bits of vegetable peel out of his fur. He looked very pleased with himself though. You’ll never win with them, will you? My cat, Winston, he's the same. He just stares at you with these big, innocent eyes after he’s knocked over a plant pot. It’s a masterclass in manipulation, really. He looks so guilty after, doesn't he? Like, "It wasn't me, Mum! A rogue gust of wind, perhaps?" Exactly! Speaking of work, that Brenda from Willowbrook… she's a right drama queen, isn’t she? Apparently, Mr. Peterson complained about his toast being 'too brown' this morning. Too brown! I nearly choked on my tea. Honestly, some people. You deal with life or death situations, and then you get a complaint about toast. It’s enough to make you lose the plot. How are you getting on with the job hunting, Sarah? Any luck? Not really, no. I applied for that position at Meadow View, the one you mentioned, Nurse Fiona? Didn’t hear back. Keeps feeling like I’m banging my head against a brick wall. I mean, I’ve got my qualifications, experience… Don't you worry, love. It just takes time. There are so many lovely people looking for care positions. Have you tried putting something on Facebook, in those local groups? Sometimes that works wonders. Doreen’s right. Networking. Absolutely crucial. I remember when I was trying to get into the nursing home on Park Lane… it was my neighbour's sister-in-law who put in a good word for me. Small world, isn’t it? I've had a look, but nothing seemed to stick.

Right, this is good. Really good. You've outdone yourself with this sourdough, love. Did you see that article I sent you about sleep? Absolutely fascinating. Apparently, consistent exposure to blue light for even an hour before bed completely throws off your melatonin production. I did, yes. Quite alarming, wasn’t it? My students are glued to their phones until the last possible moment. It’s a wonder any of them function at all. Though, I suppose they’re fuelled by sheer adrenaline. You know, it’s really made me question our camping trip next month. All those torches, the glow-in-the-dark tent...it's a neon extravaganza! Don’t be silly. A bit of LED light isn't going to negate the whole experience. Think of the stars! We won’t see proper stars like that in London. And the fresh air, the peace… It'll be good for us. Remember how stressed you were just before Christmas? I do. Still, I’m trying to be mindful. Maybe we can invest in those amber-tinted headlamps? Apparently, they emit much less blue light. Although, then we'll look like something out of a sci-fi film. We'll look practical! Speaking of getting lost… do you remember that time in Barcelona? We wandered around those Gothic Quarter streets for hours. Truly, utterly lost. How could I forget? I was convinced we’d have to sleep in a doorway. You, of course, were insisting on your ‘sense of direction,’ which led us directly into a dead end that smelled strongly of paella. That paella did smell divine, though! And it wasn't my fault; the maps were terrible. It's always the same with big European cities, isn't it? You need a really, really good route planned. I've been looking at those Citymapper things. Pretty clever, actually. It suggests the best way in, even taking into account potential delays. I’ve used them. They’re a lifesaver. Much better than relying on my internal compass, which, as you know, points vaguely towards the nearest bakery. Actually, on the topic of navigation… I was reading about that pilot, Captain Davies. Remember him? The one who made that emergency landing at Luton last year? Vaguely. Wasn't it something about a bird strike? Yes, but what’s remarkable is how he managed to land safely, despite the damage. Apparently, his instrument readings were completely skewed, and he had to rely purely on his instincts and years of experience to bring it down.

Right, listen to this! I’ve finally got a little ginger hamster! His name’s Rusty, 'cos, well, he's bright orange, isn't he? He’s absolutely tiny, like a little fuzzy football. Proper cute, he is. You wouldn't believe the time I spent at the pet shop. There were loads, but Rusty just kept staring at me, ya know? It was fate! A ginger hamster? That’s… specific. But well done, honestly. You always did have a thing for the unusual. I saw a black and white one at the shop the other day; looked like a little bandit. What breed is Rusty? A ginger hamster, eh? Sounds like you've got yourself a right comedian, lass. I had a hamster once, years ago. Called him Nibbles. He chewed through everything. Everything, I tell you! My mum nearly went spare. Did he come with a little house? Aye, Nibbles! Good memory, Chloe. Chewing's practically their national sport, isn't it? My gran had a hamster years back. A proper scruffy thing. Spent its days burrowing in its bedding. Is Rusty a proper chewer then, Becka? Expect the furniture to be looking a bit gnawed soon! He hasn't chewed anything  yet , but I'm keeping a close eye! He’s a Syrian, apparently. The bloke at the shop said they're the friendliest. And he's got a snazzy little habitat. Three levels, a little wheel, a hidey-hole...the works! It cost a fortune, mind, but he's worth it. Don't get me started on gingers though... I used to have a ginger cat called Marmalade. Absolute menace to all the birds in Doncaster. Syrians are sweet. My cousin had one. Turns out they're surprisingly good at hiding treats. You’ll find sunflower seeds in the most unlikely places. So, gingers… you’re a big fan, then? Aside from Rusty and Marmalade, obviously. I always thought red hair was proper striking. Me dad's got a bit of a ginger tint, you know – fading now, mind, age catches up with us all. It used to be really bright when he was younger. Makes him look like a Viking! Do you think it’s a genetic thing then, Becka? Like, why are some hamsters ginger and others aren't? Right proper mystery, that is. My best pal’s got reddish hair. Claims she’s part Irish, but nobody's quite sure.

Right, so, Genghis Khan has just conquered Europe. Again. Honestly, Dad, you're relentless. Relentless is what wins wars, lad! You’re too soft, Jamie. Need to be ruthless. Like, you know, those parties ANON throws. Ruthless on the Prosecco front. Remember that one last year? The one where Ms. Davies ended up doing the Macarena on the coffee table? Don't remind me, Barry. The smell of spilled Chardonnay lingered for days. It was dreadful. And Jamie, darling, are you using the updated rule book? Version 4.2? The last one was utterly confusing about reinforcement from Australia. Yes, Mum, I’m using 4.2. Though I still think Australia should be worth more territories. It's a massive continent! Speaking of confusing, I keep forgetting how to pronounce Kamchatka. It’s just… kac… hat… kah? Sounds like a cat with a bad cough, doesn't it? Just say it however you like, son. Nobody cares about proper pronunciation when they're trying to take over the world. Speaking of taking over, I'm feeling lucky. I’m going for South America. You always go for South America, Barry! It's strategically useless. You’re just setting yourself up for defeat. This game is taking hours! I’m craving chocolate. Anyone fancy a biscuit? Yes please! Actually, I was thinking about something. Remember when we were kids, and Grandma used to record all our family gatherings? Oh, aye. VCR tape heaven. Good times. Always ending with some awkward family argument. She said she was documenting our childhoods. Said it was important. I wonder if she ever… you know… recorded the Christmas when… well, you know. The pregnancy test incident? Mum, you don't have to bring that up. I’m trying to focus on strategically outmaneuvering my father's Tibetan army. Oh, here we go. Bringing up old history. Remember how your nan always said having children was the most important thing in life? Well, she was a woman of faith, Barry. She believed it was God's will. But things are different now. The ethics surrounding… well, all aspects of reproduction are so complex. Abortion, sterilization… it’s not as simple as ‘have babies.’ Exactly. And the child policy in China... it's a horrifying overreach. Imagine being told how many children you’re allowed to have. Back in my day, they barely did any pregnancy tests, let alone talked about it openly.

Right, I’m officially stressed. Uni feels… overwhelming, doesn't it? Like, everyone else seems to have it all figured out. Nah, don’t be daft, Liv. Nobody’s got it all figured out. Not really. Especially not at nineteen. I mean, look at me - trying to write this essay on Victorian poetry and all I'm getting is a headache. Victorian poetry! You’re brave. I’m studying marine biology and half the time I'm just staring blankly at diagrams of plankton. Plankton! Is that even a real word? It's proper real, love. Tiny little things that hold the whole ocean together. Bit like lecturers, innit? Small, but you can’t escape 'em. So, what's  really  stressing you out? Besides the plankton. I don't know... just, what am I  doing ? Like, marine biology… is it actually a viable career? My dad keeps going on about needing “something stable." He’d love it if I became an accountant. Can you imagine? Me? An accountant? Oh, God, no! You'd last five minutes. You’d be rescuing stranded seagulls in the break room. Seriously though, don't listen to him. He just wants you to have a mortgage and a cat, like the rest of them. Marine biology is brilliant! Think of all the travel, the diving… True. I do like the idea of working somewhere tropical. But what if I’m terrible at it? What if I end up working in a sewage treatment plant analysing…well, sewage? Right, let’s not go there. Look, everyone has doubts. I was convinced I'd be a professional footballer until I was twelve. Turns out, I'm not  that  good. But even if things don't go to plan, you’ll figure it out. Besides, have you seen Harry Styles lately? He’s got a baby!  Harry Styles has a baby?!  Seriously? Where did you hear that? It's all over TikTok, Liv! Apparently, it’s a girl, and he’s being super private about it, but…Harry Styles! A dad! It's completely mental. Makes all our career worries seem a bit silly, doesn’t it? Massive global superstar, and now changing nappies. He’s probably excellent at it. He’s clearly got some very gentle hands. I reckon he’ll be immaculate at swaddling. Speaking of babies, my cousin’s just announced she’s having twins! Twins!

Right, so Mr. Davies  still  hasn’t marked our history project. It’s been three weeks! I swear, the man lives in a different dimension. Teachers, man. They’re all like that. Remember Mrs. Patel and the biology practical? We practically had to beg for feedback. It’s massively unfair. Especially when it’s worth thirty percent of our final grade. Tell me about it! And it's not just Mr. Davies. It’s everything. Like, the whole thing about the local council wanting to build those luxury flats on the old community garden. Seriously? Who needs another glass tower when there’s kids who can barely afford lunch? Exactly! It's always the same story, isn’t it? Rich people getting richer, and everyone else…well, everyone else struggles. My mum was saying just the other day that even the cost of, like, basic groceries has gone up again. It’s mental. My nan keeps going on about it too. She says it's like going back to the seventies, but with iPhones. She insists we’re all being manipulated by advertising, too. Buying things we don't actually need just because some celebrity says it’s cool. She’s got a point. Remember when everyone was obsessed with those fidget spinners? Complete waste of money. My little sister drained my pocket money on those things. Vaguely. I was more into comics then. Still am, really. Trying to track down a first edition of 'Sandman' is proving to be… challenging. And expensive. Proper collector's item stuff. Costs a fortune. You and your comics. Honestly. But hey, at least it's something you’re passionate about. Speaking of passionate, did you see that article about the new research on dark matter? Pretty mind-blowing, right? Yeah, I saw something about it. Apparently, they’re using these super-sensitive detectors in Italy. It’s insane. Makes you wonder if there’s, like, another universe coexisting with ours or something. Right? It's wild. Kind of makes all this… council stuff and posh flats seem pretty insignificant, doesn't it? Like, there are bigger things to worry about. It does, a bit. But you can’t just ignore what’s happening here, can you? Someone's got to speak up. My mate Liam's trying to start a petition about the community garden. Said we should all sign it. That's good of him.

Honestly, darling, it’s just been  one thing  after another this week. My knees are absolutely screaming at me. I swear, I’m starting to resemble an elderly oak tree – all creaks and groans. The physiotherapist was suggesting I try Pilates again, but honestly, the thought of contorting myself into a pretzel fills me with dread. Pilates? Mum, you hated it last time. Remember? You kept getting stuck in that one pose and you were practically purple. I do recall that rather vividly. And then Mrs. Higgins next door popped her head over the fence to ask if I was alright, thinking I was having a fit! The woman's a busybody, you know that. Always peering over. She asked about the recording, by the way. Said she heard some strange noises coming from the house the other day. What recording? You didn't tell me you were recording anything. Oh, just a little project I'm tinkering with. Remember when I was talking about wanting to record some of Shakespeare's sonnets? I've finally got a decent microphone and a quiet space in the spare room. It’s terribly absorbing, actually. Though it does mean I’m practically glued to the chair, which isn’t helping my joints, naturally. Shakespeare? Really? That's…actually pretty cool, Mum. So, are you doing all the voices? Like, different characters and stuff? Well, I'm just focusing on the sonnets for now. It's more about the intonation and the rhythm. Capturing the feeling, you see. But I could certainly give it a go with a play sometime. Although, I do realize I’m perhaps a bit old to be playing Juliet. Maybe not Juliet, but you could do a fantastic Lady Macbeth! You've got the dramatic flair for it. Anyway, speaking of feeling, I feel absolutely awful. Bloated, sluggish… Oh, darling, not this again! What have you been eating? It’s not what I’ve been  eating , it’s what I  haven’t  been eating. I tried that new juice cleanse everyone's raving about. Three days of disgusting green sludge. It didn’t work. I just ended up feeling even weaker. Honestly, those things are nonsense. They're just a way for companies to make a fortune off people’s insecurities. You need proper food, dear. Sustaining food. Remember how much better you felt when you were helping me with the garden last summer?

Right, I reckon this'll do. Smells proper good, doesn't it? Loads of garlic, just how I like it. Remember that time me Nan tried to make garlic bread and nearly set the kitchen on fire? The smoke alarm went mental! Oh my god, no! I can just imagine. My mum makes a decent garlic bread, but it's nothing compared to the drama of a Yorkshire Nan. Is that passata or something you’ve made from scratch? Looks really rich. Nah, passata. Don’t get me started on making sauce from scratch – far too much faff! I’m all about efficiency, you see. Conference planning has taught me that. Everything needs to be streamlined. Though, I did try making pesto once. That was... a learning experience. Ended up looking like swamp sludge. Streamlined, that's you! I’m a production controller; efficiency is practically my religion. We’re currently battling a massive backlog of component parts for this new modular staircase system. Supplier issues, as always. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m just firefighting all day. Sounds stressful. A staircase system, eh? Fancy. So, are you getting any joy from Cambridge so far then? Settled in alright? You seemed a bit hesitant when you were moving. It’s...different. It's beautiful, obviously. The architecture is incredible and the colleges are stunning. But everything’s so… quiet. Lewisham, even at its busiest, had a certain  energy . Here feels a bit… curated, you know? Like everyone’s performing. Aye, I can see that. Doncaster’s got its own issues, granted, but it's got a proper buzz about it. People talk, people laugh, people moan about the weather. Cambridge feels like everyone’s waiting for a cue. Have you met any people you get on with? Besides me, of course! You're the best! I’ve joined a pottery class, which is surprisingly good. Met a few people there. One’s a history student, loads of interesting stuff to chat about. And there’s a girl who works at the Fitzwilliam Museum, she’s showing me around. It's just... taking time. Still miss the energy, though. Honestly, sometimes I just want a proper greasy kebab and to argue with someone about football. I know exactly what you mean! Right, pasta's ready. Come and get it. Film’s about to start too. Fancy ‘Pride and Prejudice’ again? We always watch it when I come down.

Right, so, Netflix is suggesting “Anyone But You” to me again. Honestly, it's relentless. Have any of you actually  watched  it? It looks… predictable? Predictable is an understatement, Livvy! My mum dragged me to see it. It was, as she put it, “proper cheesy.” But, I have to admit, the scenery was gorgeous. Like, the Australian beaches? Dreamy. Cheesy, eh? Sounds a bit… vanilla for me. I’ve been rewatching “The Banshees of Inisherin” again. Still gets me right in the feels. Martin McDonagh’s a genius. The bleakness of it all... proper brilliant. “Banshees” is amazing! Such a clever film. Though, I get why you’d prefer something a bit lighter after that, Niall. I saw "Poor Things" last week. Absolutely bonkers, but in the best way possible. Emma Stone is phenomenal. "Poor Things"? Is that the one everyone's talking about with the weird lady? My nan saw it and said it was “downright scandalous.” Scandalous, eh, Maisie? Well, it’s certainly… unconventional. But brilliant! I’ve been on a Wes Anderson kick lately. Just finished “Grand Budapest Hotel” for the tenth time, probably. The symmetry! The colour palettes! It's pure joy. Wes Anderson? That’s a bit niche, isn’t it? I mean, I appreciate the aesthetic, but sometimes I just want something I can switch off to. Like, a good rom-com. Even if it's predictable. See, Livvy’s got a point. Sometimes you just  need  something fluffy. I did enjoy "Ticket to Paradise" surprisingly. Julia Roberts and George Clooney, you can't really go wrong. It's like cinematic comfort food. Comfort food films... I'm more of a gritty drama sort of guy. Did anyone see "The Holdovers" yet? Apparently that's the one everyone's raving about. "The Holdovers" is beautiful, Niall. Really touching. Paul Giamatti gives a fantastic performance. It's got that quiet, observational humor that I love. It's surprisingly uplifting, despite being set in a boarding school on Christmas break. Ooh, Paul Giamatti! He's in "Sideways" isn't he? I like "Sideways"! Is it anything like that? It's got a similar vibe, Maisie, yeah. A bit more heartwarming, though. Less wine-induced angst, more... finding connection in unexpected places. Speaking of wine, has anyone seen "Somm"? It's a documentary about sommeliers training, and it’s surprisingly intense! The pressure they’re under… incredible. A documentary about wine?

Oh my god, I need a cup of tea. Paris was… a lot. My feet are killing me. Seriously, I think I’ve developed permanent plantar fasciitis. Blimey, love, you look knackered! Paris, eh? Sounds lovely, but I can imagine all that walking. Sit yourself down, I’ll put the kettle on. How was it, really? Beyond the foot pain, of course. Paris! You’re back! Spill! Photos? Did you see the Mona Lisa? You look like you’ve wrestled a croissant and lost. Right, where to begin? The Mona Lisa was… smaller than I expected. And swarming with people. Like, a human tidal wave. We spent more time fighting for a view than actually  seeing  it. And the food was amazing, obviously, but everything is so expensive! I blew my budget on macarons. Don’t judge. Macarons are a treat! Well deserved after all that battling. Did you at least get to do some sightseeing aside from the Louvre? Norwich isn't exactly known for its artistry, you know. We did! We went up the Eiffel Tower, which was dazzling, obviously, though the queues were horrendous. And we wandered along the Seine, which was really romantic even with the drizzle. But seriously, Mum, my ankle is throbbing. I think I twisted it somewhere between Notre Dame and a patisserie. Twisted your ankle?! Why didn’t you say so? Did you get it checked out? Seriously, you need to be careful. I've seen what stress does to the body, and you’re just asking for trouble. I didn’t  think  it was anything serious. I just hobbled along, fuelled by pain au chocolat. It’s better now, I think, just really stiff. Probably just need some ibuprofen and a good rest. Ibuprofen and a good sit down sounds like a plan. Now, this stew will do you good. Got some lovely root vegetables in. Your Auntie Brenda sent me some parsnips from her allotment – proper Norfolk parsnips, mind you. Not those pale things you get in the supermarkets. Honestly, Mum, root vegetables? Don't you ever deviate from your classics? I'm trying to be healthy, you know. Where are the lentils? The quinoa? The ethically sourced kale? You and your healthy food, love. There’s nothing like a good, hearty stew to warm you up after a chilly weekend. And you, being a mental health nurse, should know a lot of people find comfort in the familiar, eh?

"Hey, Chloe! Fancy seeing you here. About to brave another Monday morning, huh?" "Liam! Hey! Yeah, definitely. Monday mornings hit different, don’t they? Just grabbing a caffeine kickstart before I head to my supervisor meeting. You teaching your intro class today?" "Yep. Level 1 grammar. It's...an experience. Actually, I was just thinking about the British National Corpus. Remember how we used to pore over that stuff for our linguistics undergrads? It’s incredible the insights you can get, even just from analysing word frequency." "Oh god, the BNC. Don't remind me! So many passives. I still have nightmares about identifying passive constructions. Croydon University wasn't exactly known for its fireworks display of enthusiasm for linguistics, though. More…dutiful application of grammar rules. How's Bedford treating you these days?" “Bedford’s good. Mum still insists I’m not eating enough vegetables. Though, I did go to Chichester last weekend. It's such a charming little city, isn't it? Saw a production of ‘Wicked’ at the Festival Theatre. Absolutely brilliant." "Chichester! I love it there. It’s so picturesque. ‘Wicked’ is a classic! I saw ‘The Lion King’ there a few years ago. Being a supervisor, I get a little more time off - barely, but still – and I try to sneak away for theatre whenever I can." "That’s nice. It sounds like a challenging position, being a supervisor. A lot more responsibility, right?" "Massively. Managing twenty-odd people, dealing with complaints... it's not all sunshine and discounts, let me tell you. Speaking of money, pay day's tomorrow. Thank goodness. Student loans and tuition fees from uni are still haunting me, y’know?" "Tell me about it! I’m paying off my Master’s degree for the foreseeable future. I was showing some students some photos of my hometown the other day. They were asking about the accent, naturally. Trying to explain the intricacies of regional dialects is... difficult." "Oh, no doubt. My mum can spot a London accent a mile off! She’s always going on about how people are 'dropping their aitches' these days. She’s quite the character. We’re pretty close. My brother just got engaged, actually. Proper whirlwind romance – knew her for six months and he just dropped to one knee. My sister’s… well, she’s going through a divorce. Messy business." "Wow, that's a lot all at once.

Right, so, you’re  sure  this thing works? It looks a bit…retro. Like something Nan used to have. It's a lifesaver, honestly. My mum gave it to me. Don’t knock it 'til you’ve tried it. It’s much better than trying to get it right on the hob, innit? Less scrubbing up too. Just shove the rice and water in, press a button, and  bam  – perfect rice. Now, have you got the water ratio right? It needs to be slightly more water than rice. About a finger’s width above, yeah? Yeah, I think so. I read online… but online’s always wrong, isn’t it? I reckon it needs more salt. Everything needs more salt. You and salt. You'd salt a chocolate biscuit, wouldn't you? Alright, a tiny pinch then. Don't go overboard. Remember what happened with that spicy chilli oil I got? You nearly set your mouth on fire! That was  one  time! And it was a really good jalapeno oil, though. Proper fiery. I was just… testing it. Testing it nearly landed you in A&E. Listen, speaking of fiery, did you see that voucher I got for that new Indian place, "Spice Paradise"? Fancy going on Saturday? I saw they have a proper vindaloo. Ooh, yeah! That sounds good. Way better than cooking at home. Mum's been saying we need to eat out more, get some fresh air… and escape the smell of curry that’s currently permeating the entire house. Honestly, this curry smells… intense. What  is  in it anyway? It looks like something a jellyfish would build a reef out of. Don't be daft. It's chicken and potatoes, mostly. Loads of spices, obviously. Got a bit carried away with the turmeric today, I think. I found a massive bag at that discount shop, you know, the one down by the river? Everything was practically free! You got a  massive  bag of turmeric? What are you planning on doing, turning the whole house yellow? It’s good for you! Gets rid of inflammation, apparently. Mum says everything’s good for you these days, as long as it's got enough antioxidants. Remember when she was going on about those spirulina smoothies? Bleugh. Still, gotta look after ourselves, yeah? Speaking of looking after ourselves… have you checked the mince in the fridge? It smells a bit… suspect.

Right then. Another week closer to… well, nothing much really, is it? Still no luck with that warehouse job, mind. They said I was "overqualified." Overqualified to stack boxes! Mad, innit? Seriously, Liam? That's ridiculous. What’s massively wrong with stacking boxes? A job’s a job. Did you at least ask if there were other roles? Maybe in dispatch or something? Aye, I did. Said they were “filled.” Honestly, it feels like they're just looking for an excuse not to hire me. Ten years of education, a degree in history, and now I'm competing with lads who left school at fifteen for a job shovelling gravel. You’re being dramatic, Liam. It's frustrating, I get it, but "competing with lads who left school at fifteen" is a bit much, don't you think? Look, I’ve seen you struggle with structure. Maybe something less…rigid would be better for now? Exactly! And you’re always reading, Liam. Why don’t you volunteer at the library? You could organize books, help people find what they need. It’s something, right? Plus, it’s quiet. You’d like that. Quiet’s what I’m gettin’ plenty of, Siobhan. Quiet and unemployment benefit forms. The library? Sounds a bit…boring, doesn’t it? I need something that feels like it’s  going  somewhere. You haven't felt like you're going anywhere for ages, Liam! Anything’s better than this. Mum’s proper worried, you know. She is, and so am I. Look, I’ve got a few connections at the care home where I work. There’s a chance – just a small one – they're looking for a support assistant. It’s not glamorous, it’s messy sometimes, but it’s a foot in the door. Something stable. Support assistant? What would I be doing exactly? Assisting residents with daily living; helping them get dressed, eating, that sort of thing. It's mostly about companionship, really. Listening, chatting. You're pretty good at talking, Liam. And you’re patient. You'd be good with the older folks, Liam. You always were good at chatting to Gran. Remember when you used to read her the newspaper every Sunday? Aye, I do. She loved that, she did. Still… caring for people… it’s not really my… Don't knock it 'til you've tried it, Liam. Seriously. I'm applying for that photography course at the University of Cumbria.

This is reet good, Anon! Proper tasty lasagna. Thanks for havin’ us round. It's been a good change from the conference centre, that's for sure. All that beige carpet and lukewarm coffee… makes a lass miss a proper dinner. Glad you like it, love. It's not exactly Michelin star, but it’s honest food. You’ve been working hard, haven’t you? All those events. Must be a right juggling act. It is, honestly. This last one was a nightmare. Corporate team-building, you know? Trying to get a load of suits to pretend they're explorers in a mock jungle. The sheer awkwardness! One bloke insisted on wearing a pith helmet the whole time. A  pith helmet ! Oh, bless him. People can be odd, can’t they? Reminds me a bit of old Mr. Finch down the road. He wore a deerstalker everywhere. Even to the post office. You're right! Some folks are just built different. So, you’re keeping busy then, are ya? Still playing chess in the park? Most days. Keeps the mind sharp. And I’ve gotten quite good, I’ll have you know. Beat young Tom yesterday. He thinks he’s so clever, always showing off with his fancy apps on his phone. Nothing beats a bit of good old-fashioned strategy, eh? Have you been doing any exercise, love? You mentioned feeling a bit knackered at the conference. I’ve been trying, honestly. I signed up for a yoga class, but it’s a load of nonsense, really. Everyone’s just bending themselves into knots trying to look spiritual, and I’m just there thinkin’ about spreadsheets. It's not exactly my thing. I need somethin' a bit more... energetic. Maybe somethin' where I can actually sweat a bit. You should try walking. Simple, doesn't cost anything. I walk miles every day. Used to be a lot more, mind, before my knees started protestin'. Helps clear the head, it does. Cambridge is a lovely place for a stroll. True, true. I do enjoy a good walk. Maybe I’ll give it a proper go. Just need to motivate myself, I s'pose. It’s hard when you’re constantly chasing deadlines. Speaking of which, Anon, have you heard anythin' about the Christmas party for the company? I’m on the organising committee again. Christmas parties… always a minefield, aren't they?

Right then, operation clear-up commence! Boys, give your dad a hand, will you? Honestly, you lot eat like you haven't seen food in a week. Mum, I’m still digesting! My stomach’s doing flips. That's the protein talking, lad. All that chicken. Come on, a quick tidy and then you can go do whatever it is you teenage boys do. I was thinking about going on Instagram. Liam just posted a really funny Reel. Instagram, is it? Everything’s Instagram these days, isn't it? Be careful what you’re looking at, love. And Liam – is he still trying to grow a proper moustache? He is, Mum! It's… a work in progress. More like a poorly attached caterpillar at the moment. He’s convinced it’ll be like Tom Selleck. Tom Selleck  had  a good moustache. Seriously. Classic. Although, this obsession with facial hair… it’s a bit odd, isn’t it? Especially at your age. I think it’s cool. My history teacher was saying how Hitler had a moustache. It’s kind of… striking. Right. Hold on. Let’s just reel that back a bit, shall we? Comparing a teenage boy's patchy attempt at a moustache to  Hitler’s ? That’s not a comparison to make. It’s… insensitive. And honestly, a bit odd, like your dad said. Sorry, Mum. I just… the teacher said it was a symbol of power back then. It was a symbol of evil, son. There's absolutely no need to link that to trying to grow facial hair. It’s got nothing to do with it. History's fascinating, but you need to be careful how you bring these things up. Context matters. See, this is why I don’t do history. It’s all dates and… Hitler. It's also about understanding how things have changed, and how things  should  be. It’s about learning from the past, not repeating it. Anyway, enough of that. Back to Instagram. What were you looking at, love? Liam's Reel. He was doing a silly dance. Dancing's alright. Just make sure you're not getting sucked into those filter things, are you? The ones that completely distort your face? They're a bit worrying. They’re hilarious, Dad! I made one of you the other day, you looked like a potato. A potato?! I most certainly do not!

Right then, nearly home. Just a few more minutes, love. You alright, pet? You’ve been quiet. Yeah, just thinking. This new sofa… are you  sure  the grey will work with the curtains? I keep picturing it looking a bit… dull. Grey's a good, sensible colour, lass. Always been a sensible colour. Don't go getting yourself something too flash, you’ll regret it. Remember that lime green armchair your grandad bought? Nightmare. Nobody wanted to sit on it. Oh, that  was  a disaster. He thought it would “brighten up the room.” It just clashed with everything. We ended up giving it to Mrs. Davies next door, bless her. She never said if she liked it or not. Honestly, the thought of people judging our furniture choices is stressful. Should we have gone for something with a bit more… pizzazz? Nowt wrong with a bit of pizzazz, but sensible is good, aye? We need something comfortable and that’ll last. Plus, we’ve got all that mountain of stuff to get rid of first. Are we taking it to the tip this weekend? The tip? Good heavens. It’s a right palaver, isn't it? Last time I went, there was a queue round the block. Honestly, people just dump anything and everything. Remember that creepy doll someone left? Giving me nightmares for weeks that was. It's amazing what people throw away! Speaking of which, have you heard back from Anya about her friend’s family? The one who were selling that antique dresser? Not yet. She was going to pop round, weren’t she? Poor Anya’s a bit worried about her mate’s partner, isn’t he? Sounds poorly. Dementia, wasn't it? Dreadful. My old neighbour, Mr. Finch, went through that. It’s heartbreaking to watch. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About how quickly things can change. Absolutely. It’s awful. Makes you appreciate what you’ve got. I’m just trying to sort through my clothes before university starts again. Someone keeps volunteering to wash them for me! My Auntie Maureen keeps offering. Honestly, it’s a bit much. Maureen! She’s always been a bit…overbearing. Don’t argue with her, just say thank you politely and hide your laundry. She’s got the best intentions, bless her. It’s like the time Uncle Barry sent me a ceramic badger for Christmas. An actual badger.

Right, Mum, I’m officially pulling my hair out. This project at work... it’s a disaster waiting to happen. The client keeps changing their minds, the budget’s been slashed, and half the team are calling in sick. Seriously, I'm working sixty-hour weeks just to keep it afloat. Oh, love, that sounds dreadful. Sixty hours! You’re burning the candle at both ends. You need to look after yourself. Remember what your Grandad used to say? "A watched pot never boils, and a stressed girl makes for a terrible project coordinator.” He always had a way with words, didn’t he? He did, didn't he? Bit of a rambling old man though. Anyway, it's spiralling. And the worst part is, there's a rumour swirling around the office... about redundancies. Redundancies? Oh, darling! That's awful. Are they saying who might be affected? You’re a good worker, love, you're brilliant at your job. Don't you worry. They’re not saying anything officially. But Clive from marketing – he’s been here forever – he overheard something from HR. It’s making me proper anxious. I’ve been thinking, maybe it’s a sign I should start looking around. Looking around? Now, now, don't jump at shadows. Let's see what happens first. You’re too clever to be let go. But a bit of discreet looking, I suppose, can't hurt. What about that gym you were saying you wanted to join? Maybe distract yourself. I’ve been going to that Zumba class at the community centre, it’s ever so good for a giggle. Actually, I did sign up! Just started last week. It’s exhausting, but in a good way. Better than lying on the sofa stuffing my face with crisps, that's for sure. Which, by the way, I did a lot of last weekend. Felt absolutely disgusting afterwards. Need to get back on the veggie smoothies. Good girl! Zumba, that’s the ticket. And smoothies are the way forward. Listen, how about we plan something nice for the weekend? Just you and me. Need to take your mind off things. I was thinking we could pop into Cambridge. There's that lovely little antique shop you like, and we could grab a bite at that little cafe, ‘The Willow Tree.' Cambridge sounds lovely, Mum. Just what I need. Although… I was also thinking about finally getting around to properly looking at quotes for the extension.

This is a bit boring, isn’t it, Mum? Just peas and chicken. Well, you ate all the roast beef yesterday, didn’t you? And it’s good for you, love. You need your greens. Little Fiadh loves her peas, doesn't she? Yeah, but Fiadh’ll eat anything. She’d probably eat my socks if you let her. Speaking of things to do… the summer holidays are practically here! What are we doing? It can’t just be peas and chicken, can it? No, of course not, darling. I’ve been thinking. Remember I mentioned Liam and Chloe from down the road? Their mum said they’re free most days. We could get the three of you to play together? Liam and Chloe? They're a bit…loud. And they mostly just want to play  Mick . Honestly, I've had enough of Mick for one lifetime. Oh, don't be like that! Fiadh loves Mick. She shouts "Stick with Mick!" all the time. And it’s good for you to get some social time, isn’t it? Sometimes mum’s a bit…occupied, looking after a little one. I know, I know. It's just...but wouldn't it be good to actually  do  something? Like go swimming? I haven't been to the pool in ages. Swimming’s a brilliant idea! We could try and fit that in. What about some days out? We could go to the park or…I saw something online about a Japanese festival in Cork? It looked quite interesting. Japanese? Like, sushi and samurai? Something like that, I imagine. It might be a bit more exciting than…well, than what we usually do. I was trying to understand what they were saying on the website, some of it was in Japanese, it was a bit tricky. I could try to translate some of it. Remember that online program I downloaded? I can use Google Translate. It's not perfect, but it might give us a rough idea. That would be wonderful, love! You’re so clever. And speaking of practising, have you been playing your guitar? You haven't touched it in a week. I've been busy thinking about the holidays! And...well, I'm trying to learn that new chord, the Fmaj7, and it's really difficult. It just won’t stick. Keep practicing! Things take time to learn. Even Fiadh is learning new words every day.

Right, hold on. This scene's a bit dodgy, innit? Like, the physics just don’t  work . They’re clearly just relying on the spectacle. Dodgy? Nah, it’s proper cinematic, Liam. You’re being massively cynical. It's  Transformers , not a documentary about gravity. Just enjoy the robots smashing things! Easy for you to say, you've never had a postgrad in Creative Writing telling you everything has to be meticulously plausible. It’s drilled into you, see? Like, I’m trying to write a scene, and the principles of light refraction suddenly become paramount. It's a nightmare. You and your principles. Proper posh writer, aren't ya? I had a student the other day trying to explain the subjunctive mood. Gave me a right headache. I just said, "Speak normally, love, nobody cares about the subjunctive." See, that's the beauty of teaching. You get to bypass all the intellectual fuss. Want a biscuit? Got some digestive ones. Aye, go on then. And speaking of bypassing things, I’ve got a dentist appointment next week. Proper worried, I am. Always have been. Oh, dentists. The bane of everyone’s existence. I went last month. They said I need a filling. Said it was “minor.” Minor! It felt major! They always say that. "Minor." Like it's just a little tickle. They'll have you strapped to a chair with a drill in your face, and they’re saying, "Just a minor appointment." Right drama queens, dentists are. You should hear my mum. She's convinced she's allergic to anaesthetic. Always kicking and screaming. It's a whole production. Makes my teeth ache just thinking about it. Your mum's legendary. Speaking of productions, did you ever get around to booking those Citibikes for that trip to the Lake District next month? Almost forgot! I’ll do it now, yeah. Fancy a proper cycle round those lakes, eh? Proper scenic. Thinking about getting a proper waterproof jacket, actually. The Midlands weather’s nothing compared to that wind. You definitely need a good jacket. Actually, talking about holidays… my auntie Brenda’s trying to convince me to go to Benidorm with her. Benidorm? Oh, blimey. No offence, but that sounds… intense. Intense is an understatement. Think bronzed statues, karaoke at 3 am, and enough paella to feed a small army. But, you know, she insists. Says I need some sun.

Right then, love. Tell me everything. You seem…brighter than usual. Has this new job at St. Michael's settled in alright? You were a bit anxious about it, weren’t you? It has! It's honestly brilliant, Mum. Absolutely brilliant. The kids are lovely, really enthusiastic, and Mrs. Davies, the head, is just so supportive. It's a proper team, you know? Not like that awful placement I had last year. Remember how stressed I was then? I do, darling. Heartbreaking to see you so down. And that awful supply teacher seemingly determined to make you fail. Glad you’ve found somewhere decent. So, are you teaching Year Two? Year One! Can you believe it? Little four and five-year-olds. They're just... bundles of energy and questions. One little boy, Leo, spent the entire morning trying to convince me that dinosaurs still exist. Honestly, you have to suspend disbelief sometimes. Oh, bless him. They haven’t lost that magic yet, have they? It's lovely. So, is it a lot of marking? That’s usually the killer, isn't it? It is, but manageable. And the parents are really engaged. We had a meeting last week about Easter activities – and they’re all so keen to help. I even volunteered to bake some Easter cakes for the children’s lunch! Easter cakes, are you? Suddenly feeling rather competitive, are we? Because I've got a rather award-winning Simnel cake recipe, you know. Generations of perfecting it! Oh, Mum, don’t start! I'm not trying to beat you. I was thinking something a bit more…rustic. Carrot cake, maybe? Or lemon drizzle. Nothing too fancy. Lemon drizzle is a good shout. Easy to make and always popular. Though, speaking of popular, have you heard anything more about Emily and Tom’s christening? They're bringing it forward, aren't they? Yes! That’s what I wanted to talk to you about. They're having it on the 15th of April. At St. Giles’. They want you to do a reading. Would you? Oh, darling, of course. Absolutely. What passage were they thinking? I'm not terribly familiar with the readings, you know. Not since…well, a long time ago. They were thinking something about family and love. I'll send you the specifics later. They said they'd be so happy to have you. It means a lot to them.

Honestly, Anon, your house is lovely. So much calmer than my flat! It's perpetually chaotic, you know? Little Leo’s got the energy of ten toddlers. Glad you think so, love. It's my sanctuary, really. After dealing with a bunch of teenagers all day, I need a place to decompress. How’s Leo doing? Still running rings around you? Absolutely! He’s learnt to climb the curtains, which is…entertaining. And noisy. I’m teaching him 'down' is a good thing, but it’s a slow process. Work's been a bit manic too, the new cohort of Year 7s are… a challenge. Such short attention spans. I'm trying to incorporate more interactive games, but even that only holds them for so long. You still at the same school, Brenda? Still plugging away, dear. Though I’m seriously considering early retirement. The marking! It’s a never-ending cycle. And the pressure to meet these new targets… honestly, sometimes I think they’re making it up as they go along. They've got a new initiative about 'personalised learning pathways' this term. Sounds lovely in theory, but practically it's just more paperwork. Oh, I know the feeling! They introduce something new every year, don’t they? It's like they're deliberately trying to drive us mad. Though, I did discover this amazing new skincare product - it's called 'Bloom & Glow,' all natural stuff. It’s made a real difference to my skin, especially after long days of teaching. Really? My skin hasn’t been the same since the menopause, honestly. I’ve tried everything. Anything that doesn’t cost the earth, I’m willing to give a go. Anything with retinol scares me though, I used something once and ended up looking like a lizard. Oh, goodness! No, this isn't retinol based. It's got rosehip oil and chamomile. I can send you a link, if you like. Anyway, how’s Martin? Still obsessed with restoring that old Morris Minor? He is indeed! It’s taken over half the garage now, poor thing. He's convinced he's going to have it show-ready by next summer. I think he just enjoys tinkering with it, truth be told. Sarah's doing well, she got that promotion at the law firm she was after. She's interviewing for senior partner now, which is incredible. That’s fantastic news for her!

Blimey, these are proper good, Chloe. Seriously. Better than my Nan's, and she was a legend. Did you add extra egg whites this year? They’re so fluffy. Thanks, Finn! Yeah, I experimented a bit. Extra whites, a pinch of seltzer – I read it in a retro Jewish cookbook. Trying to channel my inner Bubbe. Did you like the charoset? I used Manischewitz wine this time. It’s excellent, Chloe, truly. Though, I do think a touch more dried apricots would have enhanced the texture. It leaned a little…dense, wouldn’t you say? Still, a very commendable effort, dear. And Finn, you're being far too complimentary to your baker friend. You'll give her a swelled head! Don't listen to her, Chloe. It's brilliant. Seriously, best charoset I’ve had in ages. Reminds me of that little deli we found in Florence last summer. Remember that, guys? The one with the ridiculous amount of cured meats? Florence! Oh yeah, that was mental. Proper feast. We need to go back. Though I'm itching to get to New York next. Thinking around October? Broadway, pizza, the whole shebang. New York sounds amazing! I’d love to come. Although… I’ve been dreaming of Paris, actually. Just wandering the Marais, eating pastries… Paris is always a good choice, darling. The light, the architecture... And the food, of course! Though, you know, the Ortolan is off the menu these days - thank goodness. A rather unsavory practice, even if the Victorians adored it. Ort-what-now? Sounds grim. A songbird, Harry. Cooked whole. Extinct now, thankfully. Though, it's a fascinating footnote in culinary history, wouldn't you say? I was just reading about it for a piece I’m editing. Extremely palatable to the aristocracy, apparently. Disgusting. Right, fascinating… Anyway, have you managed to translate any of the Haggadah passages into Hebrew, Chloe? Your Grandma always used to do it beautifully. I’ve been trying! It's slow going. My Hebrew's a bit rusty. I’m using that app, Memrise. Keeps sending me quizzes on verbs. It's not exactly festive learning, is it? "The verb 'to eat' is conjugated thus…" I could give you a hand with that, actually. My degree wasn’t  just  engineering, you know. A bit of Hebrew thrown in. Never thought it'd come in handy at a Seder, though. Harry, the engineer?

Honestly, this is lovely, Chloe. Thank you for having us. Much nicer than battling the traffic into town, wouldn’t you say, Sarah? Wouldn't it! Glad you could both make it. It's a bit chaotic here, I'm still trying to wrangle the cats, but settle in! Biscuits? I made those shortbread ones you like, Eleanor. And Sarah, you brought that lovely bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, didn’t you? Absolutely lovely, Chloe. And yes, that Sauvignon Blanc smells divine. Traffic was a nightmare, as usual. Though the new series of "The Crown" kept me going. Have either of you started it? Oh, "The Crown"! Eleanor, darling, you  must ! It's absolutely gripping. Though, I do find historical dramas occasionally become a bit…po-faced. They need a bit of humour! Still, the production values are astonishing. I was just telling Mark yesterday about the detail in the costumes. Po-faced is the word, Ele. It is a bit heavy sometimes. But the acting is superb. I’m about three episodes in. Still processing Charles and Diana, you know? Always a tricky one. Speaking of processing… I'm trying to process this knitting project I’ve started - a blanket for little Leo. It’s… ambitious. Ambitious is putting it mildly, Chloe! I remember when you tried to crochet a hat for your nephew last Christmas. It ended up looking like a misshapen space helmet. Don’t remind me! I’m considerably better now, I assure you. Though my tension is still a little… unpredictable. I used to think knitting was so simple, honestly. It's all in the practice, darling. Patience is key. I'm working on a shawl at the moment. A very simple pattern, deliberately. Just a lovely, calming grey. Much better for my nerves than attempting anything too intricate. It’s the perfect antidote to a day of chasing sales figures. I can imagine! My day is filled with spreadsheets and tax returns. I need a proper escape. That’s why I’ve been devouring books. I’ve just finished “Lessons in Chemistry” - have either of you read that? Yes! Absolutely brilliant. I loved the protagonist. Such a strong, independent woman. I did prefer the physical book though. I'm really trying to get away from eBooks. They just don't feel the same, do they? It’s the smell of the paper, the weight in your hands… Eleanor, you’re preaching to the choir!

Right then, let’s have a look at these things, shall we? Feels a bit daft, doesn't it? Unpacking phones in a pub in Joensuu. Still, beats fiddling with them on the train. You alright, love? You look a bit overwhelmed. Just… this SIM tray is a nightmare! I can't get it open. Seriously, they make these things deliberately difficult, don’t they? I’m used to my old one, you know? Simple push and pop. This is like a tiny engineering challenge. There you go, lass. Little trick. It’s got a tiny pinhole. Needed the little Nokia tool I nicked from the hotel room. Always good to have, eh? Reminds me of the good old days. Remember those Nokias we had? Indestructible, they were. Dropped ‘em down stairs and they'd still ring. Yeah, but they looked like enormous bricks! And the ringtones… remember the polyphonic ringtones? So awful. My Nan had "Barney the Dinosaur" on hers. Pierced your ears, it did. This new one's sleek, though. A bit  too  sleek, maybe. Makes me nervous already thinking about dropping it. That's the modern world for ya. All about the slimline design. Still, the technology inside is somethin' else, innit? From brick phones in my childhood, to this. Mad. Are you getting a Finnish SIM card? I’ve already sorted mine. Figured we’d need data for navigating this Eastern Bloc - I mean, beautiful - country. Yeah, got one ordered. Should arrive tomorrow. Hopefully. Everything feels a bit slow here, even getting a SIM. Managed to transfer all my photos and contacts, thankfully. But setting up the email… that's proving a bit tricky. This new security stuff is a right faff. Two-factor authentication… it’s just another layer of hassle, isn't it? Tell me about it! I spent a good half hour yesterday trying to get my NHS account connected. They’re makin’ it as difficult as possible, it seems. Right, let me have a look at your email. Show me what you've done so far. Maybe I can lend a hand. Remember what I told you about setting strong passwords? Don't be using "password123" again, eh? Alright, alright! I know, I know. It's just… the sheer  number  of passwords I have to remember now! I’m starting to feel like a spy in a film. Do you think these phones are… you know… actually listening to us?

Right, so, Liam’s birthday is two weeks away. We  have  to sort this out, Mum. He’s turning seven! He’s expecting something massive, you know? Massive? Liam's seven, love, not seventeen. What did you have in mind? Honestly, he's lucky to have a party at all. We’re a bit tight this month. Yeah, I know, I know. But he’s been obsessed with red pandas lately. Like,  completely  obsessed. I was thinking, maybe we could get him a big stuffed one? Or maybe... a Malamute puppy? Liam and a Malamute puppy? Are you mad? Those things are huge! And they shed  everywhere ! Think of the hoovering. And we're in a rental, remember? Mrs. O’Malley wouldn't be too pleased with a giant dog wrecking the place. “Doggy! Woof woof!” See? Even Finn likes the idea of a dog. He just calls everything ‘doggy’ anyway. But a red panda is cute. Really cute. And less… slobbery. Red pandas are lovely, but expensive. A proper stuffed one will likely set you back a fair bit. What about a trip to the zoo? They have red pandas there, don’t they? It’d be a treat for Liam, and we could pack a picnic. Much cheaper than a furry friend. That’s a good shout, actually. But… it’s been raining for days. Will it even be nice? And he’ll just want to spend all day looking at the pandas, and then be disappointed we can’t take one home. He’s like that. Remember when he wanted to bring a snail home from school? Oh, yes. Poor Mr. Peterson, the teacher. He was not impressed. Still, bringing a snail home is better than a Malamute puppy, in my opinion. Right then, zoo it is. We’ll check the weather forecast. Okay. And... can we still have the party? Like, at least a little one? I was thinking we could have some friends over, do some board games… maybe have a little gymnastics demonstration. Liam's been practicing his cartwheel. Of course, we'll have a party. Don't you worry. We'll make it fun, even if it’s not a  massive  affair. I can bake a cake. Remember the one I made with that Japanese manga design? Liam loved that one. Yeah! The one with the cute little robot? That was brilliant. Maybe we could do a Japanese film night after the party?

Right then, Christmas memories! I’m gonna kick us off with the most chaotic one, ever. Must've been about ten years ago. Auntie Sheila decided to cook the entire Christmas dinner…in a caravan. Like, the full works. Turkey, sprouts, everything. The smell was absolutely mental, clung to your clothes for days. And the condensation! Dripping everywhere. Mum kept saying it was ‘character building’ for us kids. A caravan? Seriously? That’s wild. My Christmases were… less adventurous, I suppose. We'd always have my grandma fly over from Manila. And the whole thing would turn into a massive Filipino fiesta. Lechon, pancit, lots of rice. Christmas Eve was always the biggest – Noche Buena. We’d eat a ridiculous amount, then open presents later. It was beautiful, a real mix of cultures. Noche Buena? That sounds delightful. My Christmases were rather more… traditional, I’m afraid. Bath is always lovely at Christmas, very Dickensian. We’d decorate the house with real greenery – mistletoe, holly, the lot. My husband, Edward, always insisted on a roaring fire and carols. He used to sing terribly, bless him, but with such enthusiasm. He used to make a truly dreadful plum pudding, too, rock hard. Plum pudding, eh? Mine was never  that  bad. Though my wife, Margaret, always complained it was too much brandy. Speaking of traditions, we always used to have a Boxing Day walk along Bognor Regis seafront. Freezing cold, of course, but bracing. And we’d stop at a little cafe for tea and scones. Simple pleasures. Though, I recall one year... a rogue wave almost took my hat! A rogue wave! That’s brilliant. See, that’s what I love about Christmas, everyone's got their own little quirks. My gran always put tinsel on the cat. Honestly, it looked perpetually shell-shocked. And the arguing over who got the drumstick… could cut the tension with a knife. My grandma always said Christmas was a time for family and forgiveness. But the competition for the Lechon skin was fierce! It was like a sport. You had to be quick! There was this one year, my cousin Marco practically wrestled my uncle for a piece. It ended with a lot of laughter, though. It’s fascinating how different cultures celebrate. My daughter, Amelia, she spent a Christmas in Japan, with her husband. Apparently, it’s all about eating KFC. Can you imagine?

Honestly, this is lovely, Anon. It's so…you. All these bookshelves, the comfortable chairs, the scent of old paper and something baking. Did you make that apple crumble I smell? Guilty as charged. Figured everyone needs a bit of comfort food after a long week. How was transcription going for you, Eleanor? Anything particularly bizarre to type up this time? Oh, you know. The usual. Mostly legal documents. Nothing  too  strange, thankfully. Though I did have a rather lengthy deposition about a dispute over a prize-winning marrow. Apparently, competitive vegetable growing is a  serious  business. A marrow! You’re joking! Honestly, the things people get worked up about. It reminds me of the village fete I went to last summer. Someone accused another of unfairly positioning their gooseberry bush to get more sunlight. It was quite dramatic. Exactly! It's fascinating, isn't it? The lengths people will go to. Reminds me a bit of "The Chelsea Detective." Have you been watching that, David? Absolutely! I'm hooked. That Inspector Towsey is brilliant. Such an understated sort of genius. The way he pieces everything together…it's perfectly paced. Better than "Sherlock," frankly. Too much shouting for my taste. I’m slowly getting into it. I did find the first episode a bit slow, but I appreciate the lower key approach. I'm more of a classic Agatha Christie girl myself, you know. Cozy mysteries are my indulgence. What are you reading at the moment, Eleanor? Anything good on your Kindle? Just finished a rather enjoyable historical romance set in Regency England. A bit fluffy, I admit, but perfect for a rainy afternoon. Now I’m starting a biography of Virginia Woolf. Much heavier lifting. What about you, Beatrice? Still working on that novel? Slowly but surely. The second draft is proving to be a beast. I'm battling with the resolution, actually. It feels a bit…predictable. I want something unexpected, but not jarring. It’s a fine line. That’s the writer's conundrum, isn't it? Finding that balance. Perhaps you’re overthinking it? Sometimes, the simplest solution is the best. Perhaps you’re right. I'll try to step back from it for a bit. David, are you still planning on going to that Burns Night supper next month? Yes, absolutely. Booked the tickets ages ago. I’m already practicing my “Address to a Haggis," though I suspect I’ll butcher it horribly.

Cor, another one bites the dust, eh, Brenda? Another bank closin’ a branch. Used to be you could walk down the street and pop into one every few yards. Now? Nothin' but empty shops and takeaways. It's a bleedin' disgrace, innit? Honestly, Arthur, don’t start with the doom and gloom first thing. It’s a beautiful morning. And it’s not  every  bank. Just… well, quite a few, I suppose. Did you remember to put the bins out? Bins are out, Brenda. Always am. Don't you go tryin' to catch me out. And it’s more than “quite a few”! It's the whole bleedin' world gone pear-shaped, I tell you. Makes you wonder what's comin' next. Likely be robots takin' our jobs and then they’ll shut down the tea factories, mark my words. Morning, you two. Sounds like a lively start to the day. Robots taking over tea production? Really, Arthur? That’s a bit far-fetched, even for you. Well, someone’s gotta be pessimistic around here, Richard. Someone’s gotta see the writing on the wall. You’re always so… optimistic. Like the world’s a garden party and everything's roses. Optimism isn't a crime, Arthur. And it’s not entirely unfounded. Look, about that bank closing – it's disruptive, undoubtedly. But it's largely due to the shift to online banking. People simply aren't using physical branches as much anymore. It's an evolution, not an apocalypse. He’s got a point, Arthur. I hardly go in anymore myself. Just withdraw cash for the market, really. And most things I do online now. It's much easier. Easier for  you , maybe, Brenda. I’m not one for all that computer nonsense. Always some virus or another lurkin' around, tryin' to steal your identity. No, thank you. I like a nice chat with a friendly face. And a bit of human interaction, you know? This modern world… it’s bleedin’ cold. That's a valid concern, Arthur. Loneliness  is  a growing issue. But there are things you can do to combat it. Have you considered joining any local groups? The community centre has some interesting activities, I believe. Bowls, even. Bowls? Me? I'd look a right fool with a bowl. And the community centre? Full of… well, never mind what it's full of. It’s not my cup of tea.

Right, so caterers are confirmed for the leaving do. Three different vegan options, thankfully. Chloe was getting quite stressed about that, bless her. Are we still on for doing the playlist, Liv? We need to solidify it. I was thinking a bit of 80s, some classic Britpop... Aye, sorted! Got a cracking playlist goin'. Got The Smiths, definitely Oasis, bit of Stone Roses. Gotta have some Madonna, innit? Can’t have a party without Madonna. I'll send it over to you later, just need to finish the order. You know I’m a stickler for a good song order. Oh, brilliant! That sounds perfect. Can I add some Abba? It’s always a winner, even if it's a little cheesy. Abba’s essential, honestly! Don’t even argue, Lincoln. It’s a cultural necessity. Right, I've just been dealing with the venue confirmation, everything’s booked. Want to pop over and do a quick recce tomorrow after lunch? Just to make sure they haven’t moved the furniture around or anything. Sorry to interrupt the party planning frenzy, but… has anyone seen a Painted Lady butterfly fluttering around here? I swear one just flew past my window. It seems to have gotten trapped inside. A butterfly? Oh, poor thing. Whereabouts did you last see it, Sarah? It was by the pot plants near reception. It’s frantically bumping into the windows. I feel awful; I think it’s disoriented. Right, let's wrangle this little fella. I’m pretty good with insects, surprisingly. My nan used to keep bees. Just needs a bit of gentle guidance. Don't panic, Sarah, we'll get it out. . Should we open a window? Maybe just leave it to its own devices? No, no, leaving it is asking for trouble. It'll exhaust itself and injure itself against the glass. Liv’s on the case. I’ll grab a large sheet of paper, that should help direct it. Anyone got a soft towel? I'll stop dealing with dietary requirements for a sec. Hold on... got a tea towel here. . Right, Liv, be careful! We don't want anyone getting stung, even by a butterfly. Right, got him! Managed to guide him towards the open window with the tea towel. He’s gone! Flew off towards the park. Feel much better knowing he’s free. Oh, thank goodness! You’re a lifesaver, Liv!

Honestly, I am  so  over history. Like, seriously. Why do we need to know about the Tudors? They’re just…old. And boring. Don't be ridiculous, Chloe. Henry VIII was hardly boring. Six wives! That’s pretty dramatic, innit? Besides, Mrs. Davies makes it almost bearable. Ms. Peterson in geography, though…  that's  a nightmare. Mrs. Davies is just... really monotone. It’s like she’s reading from a tomb. And the dates! So many dates! I’m starting to dream in dates, honestly. 1536, 1547, 1558… it’s all blurring into one big, historical mess. Did you finish that essay on the Spanish Armada? I'm stuck. Nearly. I got a good chunk done last night. It's actually quite interesting, once you get into it. It's not just about ships, you know. It's about religion and politics and power. So, what's tripping you up? Was it the different versions of what actually happened? Because that's what I found tricky. Yeah, exactly! Every source says something slightly different. One says the Spanish ships were wrecked by a storm, another says the English ships were brilliant strategists… it's impossible to know what  actually  happened! And then Peterson gave us that worksheet with a million questions. I swear, she lives to torture us. Tell me about it. Remember last week when she asked, “Explain the implications of longitude on 18th-century trade routes?" Who even  thinks  about that stuff? It’s not like it’s relevant to our lives. Absolutely not! I just stared blankly at her. She gave me this look, like I’d personally attacked the French Revolution. Anyway, what about maths? Did you understand anything Mr. Davies was on about today? That whole thing with the quadratic equations… my brain just shut down. Ugh, don’t even go there. I think I grasped the  basic  concept, but the examples he gave were, like, calculating the trajectory of a rocket or something. Where would we even need to do that? It's completely removed from reality. Plus, he keeps saying "therefore" in this really smug voice. It's infuriating. Actually, I think I'll see if Liam can explain it again tomorrow; he got it straight away. Liam's a maths whiz. He probably dreams in equations too. Maybe he should teach  us . I tried to ask him for help after class, but he was busy talking to Sophie about... something.

Honestly, this report is going to be the death of me. Mr. Henderson keeps changing his mind about what he wants included! It’s like pulling teeth. Sounds like classic Henderson. You know, dealing with clients is half the battle in my job. You just have to learn to roll with it. Though, my project's facing a slight delay too - the supplier messed up the order for the materials. Typical. Aye, well, that’s life, isn’t it? Always somethin’ to keep you on your toes. More tea, love? You two look like you’ve wrestled a bear and lost. Those biscuits are homemade, mind you, not like the shop-bought rubbish. Thanks, Mum. Biscuits definitely needed. And yes, a top-up of tea would be marvelous. Henderson's asking for a complete overhaul of the executive summary, just an hour before the deadline. Honestly, I'm starting to think he's deliberately trying to sabotage me. Don’t even say that, Elara. He’s probably just stressed. Maybe try explaining to him gently that each change takes a significant amount of time? A little diplomacy goes a long way. He’s just a man, love. Don’t give him so much power over yer mood. Now, tell me about this supplier problem, lad. What’s gone wrong? Did they send you the wrong colour, or something? Worse, Mum. They sent the  wrong  materials altogether. We needed specialist cabling, and they’ve sent us… garden hoses. Honestly, I had to fight back laughter. The client isn't going to be impressed. I've had to call them repeatedly - customer service is a nightmare. Garden hoses? Seriously? That’s brilliant! You could start a landscaping business on the side. Hilarious, yes. Helpful, no. I'm trying to negotiate a fast delivery on the correct materials, but it's looking like we'll be at least a week behind schedule. That impacts  my  deadline. It's dominoes, really. A week, eh? That's a bit of a worry. Have you spoken to your manager about it? Best to keep them in the loop. No use hiding things until the last minute. I learned that the hard way years ago when I messed up an order for a particularly prickly customer at the shop. Cost me a right telling-off. You always have the best advice, Mum. I should just be upfront with Henderson.

Oh, Sarah, it’s so lovely to see you! Honestly, this week has been… a lot. Just a lot. Aye, you look it, love. You're paler than usual. Tea’s good, isn’t it? You want another? I made a fresh pot. How’s everything really? Beyond the "a lot," I mean. Thanks, but I’m alright for now. It’s just… everything’s piling up. Work’s been manic, obviously, end of quarter and all that. But the kids…oh, the kids. Liam had detention this week. Detention? Liam? What on earth for? That boy’s usually glued to his gaming console. Apparently, he was “disrupting the class” during history. Apparently, he was debating the merits of different Roman emperors with Matthew, and it got a bit… heated. The teacher said they were arguing and distracting the others.
