That's… painfully boring, Tom. I want to branch out! I mean, we  always  get sweet and sour chicken. It’s basically become our default. I want Kung Pao Chicken! Or maybe Mapo Tofu… but then I worry it'll be too spicy. Ooh, excitement! Chinese is a brilliant choice. I was just looking at Red Dragon’s menu too. They’ve got a new dish – Salt and Pepper Squid. Apparently, it's amazing. Salt and pepper squid? Sounds… risky. Is it rubbery? Apparently not! Reviews say it's crispy and really well-seasoned. Fiona at work raved about it. She's a picky eater, you know. See, Tom? Adventure! We need adventure in our culinary lives! Salt and Pepper Squid it is then. But what about a main? I'm still indecisive. Okay, okay, adventure. Fine. But if I have to pick something that tastes like old boots, I'm blaming you both. I’m sticking with the General Tso's Chicken. Reliable. Delicious. No surprises. You are the most predictable person I know. Alright, I'm thinking the Kung Pao Chicken. It's got peanuts, right? I like peanuts. And that slightly sweet, slightly spicy thing going on... Good choice! That’s a winner. I'm going to go for the Beef with Black Bean Sauce. It’s proper comfort food. And we definitely need some egg fried rice. Loads of it. Egg fried rice is non-negotiable. What about starters? Spring rolls? Chicken balls? Spring rolls! Definitely. And those little vegetable spring rolls, the crispy ones with the sweet chilli dip? Yes! And maybe some seaweed? It's surprisingly good. It's not greasy like some starters can be. I hate seaweed. It tastes like the ocean. Raw. You’re so dramatic, Tom! It’s just seaweed. It’s salty and… tasty! Fine, no seaweed. Just spring rolls then. And do they do those little pork buns? The steamed ones? Ooh, yes! Red Dragon does fantastic pork buns. Definitely get those! We can share. Right, so recap: Salt and Pepper Squid, General Tso's Chicken, Kung Pao Chicken, Beef with Black Bean Sauce, egg fried rice, spring rolls, and pork buns. Are we done now, or are we going to spend the entire evening debating the merits of different types of noodles?

Right then, Annie. You're on the front line, aren’t you? Proper frontline, I mean. It must be… something else at the moment. Honestly, I read the papers, of course, but reading about it and  living  it... that must be a different kettle of fish entirely. You’ve no idea, Stefan. It’s relentless. Honestly, the sheer volume of people needing care... and the morale. That’s the really tough bit. People are burnt out, you know? Absolutely knackered. We’re trying to keep spirits up, but… the waiting lists are insane. And the funding… don't even get me started. I can imagine. I've got a student, Liam – bright lad, but his mum’s been battling something for a while now. He's desperate for support for her, proper social care. But it's like pulling teeth, innit? They’re just overwhelmed, the whole system. You’d think in a wealthy country like this… Wealthy for who, Stefan? The shareholders, maybe. They're squeezing every penny out of it. He’s even been saying lately about the government’s plans. It’s practically criminal, the way they are treating the NHS. Honestly, I'd go on strike, but... who’d look after the patients? It’s a right bind. Aye, a bind indeed. It’s infuriating, isn't it? Reminds me a bit of the bureaucracy I wrestled with last year when applying for that research grant. Mountains of paperwork, shifting goalposts… Makes you wonder if anyone actually  wants  you to succeed, sometimes. Although, considerably more important than a research grant, naturally. You're telling me! I had a patient last week, lovely woman, needed a hip replacement. Been on the list for eighteen months. Eighteen months! Walking with sticks and everything. She was practically in tears. I try to be positive, you know, reassure them... but it's hard when you know it’s just… a waiting game. That’s awful, Annie. Absolutely awful. Reminds me of that time we went to Finland, remember? The healthcare system was practically flawless. Preventative measures, readily available appointments… They’ve clearly learned from other countries. Oh, Finland! Remember that cabin we stayed in? Absolutely freezing but gorgeous. And the saunas! Proper scrub down every day. Wish we could bottle that feeling. But aye, their healthcare is something else. They prioritise preventative stuff, a wee bit different from  this , eh? Definitely.

Alright, Arthur? Bit of a nip in the air today, eh? Remember summers like this back in Germany? Blistering, they were. Not a cloud in the sky for weeks. Aye, alright, Jurgen. A nip alright. Though not as bad as some. Remember '63? Snow piled up to the rooftops, it did. Shut the whole city down. Nowadays, a bit of frost and everyone’s in a panic. Modern life, eh? Tell you what, modern life's got a lot to answer for. Saw something on the telly last night - another article about welfare claims going through the roof. It's getting ridiculous, innit? Ridiculous is putting it mild, Jurgen. Absolute bleedin' scandal, it is. People expect everything handed to 'em on a plate, they do. Back in my day… well, back in my day, you worked for what you got. Didn't have a lot, mind you, but you  earned  it. Never claimed a thing in my life. Never needed to. I hear you, Arthur. It’s a different mindset now, isn't it? Though, I do feel for the younger generation. Stiff competition for jobs, and the cost of living… it’s no wonder some feel they have no choice. Speaking of which, did you hear about that raid they did down on Smith Street last week? The police? Aye, I did. Nasty business. Heard they were after some fellas from, what was it... Albania? Stirring up a bit of trouble, apparently. Should’ve kicked 'em out years ago if you ask me. Now, Arthur, easy on that. You can't just blanket-judge everyone. Immigration's a complex issue, you know. Brings benefits too. Diversity, new skills... Diversity? Just means more trouble, Jurgen. More competition for what little work there is. And I’m not just talking about the jobs, I'm talking about the whole way of life. Used to be, you knew everyone on your street. Now? Foreign faces everywhere. Can't even understand half the conversations. It’s changing, definitely. But is that necessarily a bad thing? My niece's married to a Polish fella, lovely lad. Makes a cracking pierogi, he does! Pierogi, eh? Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. My sister, Doreen, she tried making some of them once. Ended up looking like something the cat dragged in. She’s a butcher, you know. Never could cook, bless her. Though, she does make a mean sausage roll.

Aye, this is alright, but nothin' like me mam's packed lunches, is it? Always had a lovely pot o' stottie cake and somethin' proper in there. This feels…engineered. Engineered is a rather harsh word, Chloe. It’s perfectly acceptable salad. A little… refined, perhaps. Reminds me of the lunches Ms. Thornton used to bring into the office. All quinoa and goji berries. Honestly, you'd think she was feeding us royalty. Don't get me started on Ms. Thornton! The sheer theatricality of her lunchtime rituals…it was quite something. I once saw her meticulously separate the pomegranate seeds by colour. Pomegranate seeds! Pomegranate seed colour sorting! That  is  a level of dedication. You ladies are giving me flashbacks to a conference in Boston. This woman brought her own artisanal kombucha and lectured everyone on its probiotic properties. It was intense. Right, well, I think we can all agree that  this  is far more appealing than vegan artistry. I’m starving. This project with Grafica Publishing has been absolutely brutal. Deadlines, deadlines, deadlines. I swear, the printers are breathing down my neck. Tell me about it. This new corpus annotation protocol we’re hashing out is drivin' me mad. The consultants keep addin' layers of complexity. It'll be simpler to teach a badger to speak French. A badger? That’s a rather dramatic comparison, Chloe. You're getting stressed. Don't forget, we're here for a break. Talking about linguistic challenges at lunchtime? That’s just asking for a headache. What about something lighter? Did anyone catch that documentary about dialects on Channel 4 the other night? I did! The one about the resurgence of Cornish? It was fascinating. All that work they're doing to revive the language…and the political battles involved. It really highlights how language is so much more than just words. Agreed. Language is inherently tied to identity, culture, and power. Which, as ELT researchers, we should be acutely aware of. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm juggling ethical considerations along with linguistic data all day. Particularly when we're looking at developing resources for…developing countries, you know? It's a minefield. You’re tellin’ me! I was just fighting with marketing about using a certain phrase in an ad campaign. They thought it was "catchy," I thought it was potentially offensive and perilously close to cultural appropriation. Took hours to explain.

Right then, where were we? Oh yes, you were saying your research into online dialects is… challenging? More so than you anticipated? Massively. I thought people would be fairly consistent online, you know, a Yorkshire accent online would still  sound  like a Yorkshire accent. Turns out, it’s a real mishmash. People adopt personas, obfuscate their origins, or just outright abandon regional markers. It's fascinating, but finding any solid data is proving a nightmare. It's like chasing smoke. Sounds a bit like modern education, doesn't it? Trying to pin down any consistent principles. I mean, I’m struggling to get a decent grasp of Chomsky’s Universal Grammar, let alone convince a room full of undergraduates it’s relevant to their Netflix binging. Netflix binging, precisely! That's part of the problem. Everyone's bombarded with global media. Accents and language are being flattened, homogenised. My niece, bless her, is practically speaking a transatlantic dialect. She says “awesome” and “like” constantly. It’s heartbreaking from a Yorkshire perspective. My nephew’s the same. He picked up a dreadful American inflection from a YouTube gaming streamer. Claims he sounds "cool." I tried explaining to him the beauty of a properly drawn-out West Country "oo-ah," but… youth. You know? What are you teaching these days, by the way? Still focusing on linguistics? Still doing the linguistics, yeah. I've got a couple of undergrads assisting me with the data collection for the online dialect project. It's good experience for them, though I spend half my time correcting their citation styles. It’s surprisingly difficult to explain the nuances of APA to people who've grown up with Wikipedia. Don’t I know it! My own students seem to think footnotes are optional extras. Do you ever find yourself considering teaching abroad? I’m half tempted to chuck it all in and become a language teacher in, I don’t know, Patagonia. Imagine… teaching English to gauchos! Patagonia, eh? Bold move. I’d be tempted, but I do worry about the isolation. I enjoy having easy access to a decent curry. Though, actually, the curry house near my flat has gone down hill. Terribly downhill. Used to be reliable, now it's just… tragic. A culinary tragedy indeed! That’s a real blow. So, you’re thinking about teaching abroad purely for the… change of scenery then? Partly that, partly the opportunity to immerse myself in a different culture.

Right then, that’s the kettle on. Arthur, love, could you pop the biscuits out? They're in the tin, top shelf. And Liam, put your feet up, boy, you're lookin' all scrunched up like a bit of crumpled paper. I’m just tired, Gran. A-Levels are killing me. So much revision. A-Levels, eh? When I were a lass, it were just called ‘leaving cert’… and we didn’t have no fancy materials. Just a slate and a piece of chalk. An' the teacher screamin' if you were late! Oh, leave it, Elsie! You always were the one who got in trouble. Remember that time you tried to steal Mr. Henderson's rhubarb? He were growin' it proper big, Arthur! A girl's gotta eat, doesn't she? Besides, he had plenty. Oh, you two! Always dredging up the past. Liam, this is your Grandad Arthur and your Great-Grandma Elsie. They’ve come down from Hull for a few days. They were wanting to see you before you get completely buried in those books. It's good to see you both. I haven’t seen you in ages. You're growin' into a fine young man, Liam. Strong as an ox, you are. You playing any football lately? Yeah, still with the school team. Got a match on Saturday. Wonderful! We'll have to try and get down to watch you, won’t we? Now, Elsie, how’s your arthritis today? Ach, it's the same as always. Creakin' and groanin' like an old gate. But a cup of tea'll sort me out. Are you using that new brand o' tea, Margaret? The one you said was a bit stronger? Aye, I am. It's a bit posh, but Arthur bought it on offer! I thought I'd give it a whirl. She likes a strong cuppa, this one. Gets her through marking all those blighters’ maths papers! I'll have you know, Arthur, those ‘blighters’ are teenagers trying their best! It's a vital skill, you know. Number skills are essential! It is, actually. I’m finding quadratic equations a nightmare. See? Essential! Now, Liam, want a little help with those equations later? I’m quite good, y’know. Back in my day, we’d just divide it by two and be done with it! Elsie, honestly! They don’t teach maths like that anymore. Right, let's settle down.

Oh, look at this! Remember Sarah’s disastrous attempt at recreating that Parisian cafe? The macarons were…well, let's just say they resembled hockey pucks more than delightful pastries. Hockey pucks is putting it mildly, love. They could have been used as building materials! Poor Sarah, she tried so hard. Still, the wine was decent, wasn’t it? At least she managed  that  part. Absolutely! And the laughter. We were all in stitches. It’s funny looking back, really. It feels like…a lifetime ago, doesn’t it? Since we all properly got together. It does. The kids are practically grown now since then. Speaking of which, have you seen those photos Liam’s mum sent over? He’s got a proper beard going on. A  beard . I barely recognise him. No! I haven't! Send them over. Honestly, boys and their beards. It’s a rite of passage, isn't it? I remember when you were trying to cultivate one in uni. That was a  spectacle . Don't remind me! It looked like a squirrel had died on my chin. I gave up pretty quickly, thankfully. Liam, though… he seems to be embracing the lumberjack look. Is he still talking about going to Nepal? He is. He’s absolutely obsessed with that trek. He’s been poring over maps and gear lists. Honestly, I’m a bit nervous about it. It’s a long way to go, and quite remote. I’ll be a wreck until he’s safely back. He'll be fine. He's a sensible lad. And he'll have a satellite phone. Look, remember our trip to Vietnam? We worried ourselves sick about absolutely nothing. The food poisoning was far more likely to get us than any tiger. Don't even  mention  the food poisoning. That was…an experience. Though, I must say, the scenery was breathtaking. Those rice paddies… absolutely stunning. It makes me want to plan another big trip, doesn’t it? It really does. I was thinking, we've done Southeast Asia quite a lot... maybe somewhere completely different? We’ve talked about South America before, haven’t we? Peru? Patagonia? Oh, Patagonia! The glaciers… the mountains… it sounds incredible. But it’s so… vast. And cold. I’m not sure I’m quite ready for that level of ruggedness. Perhaps somewhere a little more… relaxed? Italy, maybe? We could hire a little scooter and just explore the Tuscan countryside.

Ugh, mornings. Honestly, I feel like I’ve been trampled by a herd of elephants. Last night was…a lot. Tell me about it! I’m pretty sure my liver staged a full-blown protest this morning. That VK was  strong , innit? Serious! I’m not even sure how I got home. I vaguely remember Leo trying to explain quantum physics to a potted plant. Leo's always been a bit…out there, hasn’t he? My mate Chloe ended up wearing a traffic cone. A  traffic cone , Liv! No way! Seriously? She’d lose her mind if she knew. She's so precious about her image. You know, always posting those perfectly filtered selfies. Exactly! Imagine the Insta story meltdown. Though, honestly, sometimes you just gotta let loose, yeah? My mum would absolutely kill me if she saw me like that. She’s perpetually stressed about my reputation. Reminds me of when I was little and she wouldn't let me even  look  at boys. Haha! My nan's the same. Thinks every bloke’s after my bank account. Which, fair enough, some probably are. Proper old-school, she is. Did you see that picture of Harry Styles on TikTok wearing the football shirt? Oh my god, you too?! It’s everywhere! I showed my little brother, and he nearly exploded with excitement. He’s proper obsessed with football, you know? Always kicking a ball around in the garden. It's mental. He’s so cute! I wish I was more into sports. I tried football once in primary school, got proper trampled. Never again. Stick to Pilates for me, thanks. Trying to tone up for summer, ya know? Pilates? You’re a machine! I can barely manage a walk around the block without feeling like I need a nap. I was promising myself I'd start going to the gym with my cousin, but... Netflix is just so comfy. I get it. Although, I  did  see this really cute guy at the library the other day. Proper fit. Big, brown eyes. Kept catching him looking at me. Ooh, spill! What’s he like? What’s he studying? Don't tell me he's another quantum physicist. Actually… he is. Apparently, he’s doing a Masters. Bit nerdy, maybe, but…charmingly nerdy, you know? So, Leo's competition then? You’re going for the brainy types, are ya? You’ve always had a thing for logical minds.

Right then, so Nan’s coming next Tuesday, is it? Tuesday it is. Heavens above, I haven't seen her properly since… well, since Christmas, hasn't she? And Christmas was a whirlwind. I feel I barely had a conversation with her. Yep, Tuesday. Booked the taxi for her. It's a bit of a trek from Lancaster, you know. And the driver’s a nice fella, knows Nan from the bingo, apparently. Should make the journey easier. Bingo, eh? Your Nan’s still at it then. Remember that time she accused old Mr. Henderson of cheating at the last game, the one with the prize of a hamper? Oh, God, yes! She was absolutely convinced he was palming the dabbers. Poor Mr. Henderson looked mortified. Honestly, she can be a firecracker when she’s got a competitive spirit. Did he deny it? Said he hadn’t a clue what she was on about. Nan just muttered something about needing stronger glasses and carried on. Anyway, Tuesday – we need to sort the guest room out. I was thinking fresh flowers? She loves those lilies. Lilies are good. Though, remembering Nan’s reaction to your cat, perhaps something less...flowery. She said Whiskers looked “suspiciously fluffy” and kept eyeing her biscuit tin. Oh, that’s rich! Suspiciously fluffy! He barely knows she’s there! He prefers to nap on the sofa. Speaking of suspicious, I’ve been thinking about that debacle with Liam and his FIFA scores last week. Absolute nonsense, the way he was banned for a day. Tell me about it! Online gaming, honestly. It brings out the worst in people. But he was apparently using some kind of exploit, wasn’t he? Getting ridiculous scores. Exploits… bah! Always an exploit. Back in my day, if you wanted to win, you practised. Spent hours on it. No shortcuts. Though, I must say, even I’m a bit baffled by the level of skill in these modern games. It's practically a sport now. Exactly! And banning him for a day? It's a child! He’ll forget about it by tomorrow. They’re so quick to jump to conclusions on those platforms. I had his father on the phone, fuming. Honestly, you’d think the world was ending. Well, it’s frustrating for the other players, isn't it? It's not fair when someone’s using cheats to gain an advantage.

Right, well, that was lovely. Thanks for coming down, everyone. It's been a bit chaotic, hasn't it? Especially with… the laptop incident. Oh, don't even remind me! I still can't believe I managed to knock it off the table. Luckily, it seems to be alright, though. Just a few scratches. Honestly, I'm such a klutz. Happens to the best of us, love. Remember when I tried to fix that leaky tap and flooded the kitchen? That was a disaster! At least you didn’t cause a flood. You two are always getting into scrapes. Back in my day, a broken teacup was a crisis! Now, this water… is it tap water? Seems a bit bland. Yeah, it's tap, but filtered. We’ve got a Brita. I've been reading up on different water companies – apparently, the mineral content varies loads. Some people swear by bottled, but it just feels so wasteful, doesn't it? Totally. I’m trying to be more conscious about that. Remember that DIY project you were talking about, Liam? The shelves in the living room? Oh, yeah! Still haven’t got around to it, I'm afraid. I ordered the wood, but the screws are the wrong size. I need to pop to B&Q tomorrow. Planning a walk around Brighton tomorrow too, if the weather holds up. It’s been surprisingly decent, hasn't it, for Sussex? It has! Lovely weather for a stroll. I saw some gorgeous hydrangeas in the park the other day. Blooms like crazy down here. Sarah, are you still thinking of visiting next weekend? Definitely! I’ll give you a ring on Monday and we can arrange something proper. I'm keen to show you more of the city. We could even try and find that little didgeridoo shop down by the pier. A didgeridoo? Blimey. Never thought I'd hear that in Brighton! It’s a strange colour, isn't it? That red… it’s not a true red, is it? Kind of brown-red. It's ochre, I think. I read about it. Anyway... speaking of strange things, I’m still failing to get this old Blackberry smartphone working. Honestly, voice recognition is a nightmare. It keeps interpreting "Liam" as "lion". Perhaps you  are  a lion! Very funny. It's frustrating though, especially when I'm trying to dictate a message. And speaking of frustrating, did you ever manage to find your glasses, Mum?

Oh, honestly, dreadful weather. Tarnow’s decided to embrace the grey today, hasn't it? Though, I suppose it is November. Did you see the United game yesterday? Absolutely abysmal. Just... abysmal. Aye, I did. Proper shocker, wasn't it? Didn't expect them to get hammered like that. Still, it’s football, innit? You win some, you lose some. Though I’m starting to think we’re losing a  lot  these days. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm homesick just for proper Premier League football. And a decent chippy. Homesickness. It’s a funny thing, isn't it? It’s not always about missing specific places, is it? Sometimes it’s just... a feeling. A sense of something you can't quite name. My SAD is kicking in, I think. The light here, even on a good day, is just… different. Much flatter. I know what you mean. I get it a bit too. Want another coffee? They do a wicked flat white here, seriously good. Better than anything I had back in Bury, even. And that's saying something! Thank you, dear. Yes, please. A flat white would be lovely. Tell me, how’s Piotr doing? Is he still struggling with the subjunctive? He's… having a go. Bless him. Polish grammar, eh? It’ll do you. He’s a good lad, but he gets so stressed about the exams. I feel a responsibility, you know? I want him to feel confident, but pushing too hard just makes him worse. Right, another coffee for me too, please. Absolutely. It's a burden, isn't it? That feeling of responsibility. I used to fret so much about my students, when I was teaching more regularly. Wondering if I'd prepared them enough. Though, you're far more qualified than I ever was. All that postgraduate work! Did you ever think you’d end up teaching here, in Poland? Not really, no. It was a bit of a spur-of-the-moment thing, to be honest. Needed a change, saw the advert, and thought, ‘why not?’ It’s been… interesting. I saw a notice the other day about seasonal work on farms. Picking apples and stuff. Reckon it would be good for clearing your head. Me, picking apples? I’d be more likely to trip over a root and break a hip. Though, fresh air  would  be nice. We saw a lovely spaniel today, belonging to the lady in the flat below.

Right then, this smells alright, doesn't it? Proper hearty. I reckon it'll stick to yer ribs after a day like I’ve had. Conference was a right shambles, honestly. The caterers forgot half the vegan options! Can you imagine? Half! Absolutely mental. Vegan options, eh? Sounds stressful. What happened? Did people riot? Don’t be dramatic, Liam. It wasn’t a riot. But several very disappointed delegates were definitely not impressed. Honestly, it’s my job to keep everyone happy, and I felt like I was failing miserably. The poor bloke in charge of logistics looked like he wanted to disappear into the floor. Aye, that's exactly how he looked. Proper deflated. And then the projector wouldn't work properly. Honestly, the whole thing felt cursed. I'm needing a good cuppa and a lie-down after this. Sounds rough, Maisie. At least you’re good at fixing things. I had a right bore today too. So much concrete. My back’s killing me. I’m starting to feel like one of those Roman statues, just solid and aching. You and your statues, Liam. Always so poetic. Anyway, talking about aches and pains, I had a disastrous date last night. Truly dreadful. Ooh, spill! What happened? Did he turn out to be a serial killer or just boring? Worse, Maisie. He spent the entire evening talking about his stamp collection. Stamps! Like, in excruciating detail. Watermarks, perforations, historical significance… honestly, I felt like I was trapped in a museum. Stamps? Seriously? People still collect stamps? I thought that was, like, a thing old people did. Apparently not. He was about your age, Liam, actually. And seemed perfectly normal before I arrived. I even wore that red dress I was showing you the other day, thought it might impress! Didn’t even get a compliment. Oh, the red one? That’s a stunning dress, love. He's clearly got no taste then, hasn't he? You should've just told him you were fascinated and started asking about the value of rare ones, then rolled your eyes and run off with his wallet. Just kidding! Very funny, Maisie. I didn’t go that far. I just made up an excuse about having a migraine and fled. It's back on Tinder now, I suppose. Tinder, eh? Rough. I tried that once. Waste of time. Everyone just wants something casual.

Blimey, look at those limes, eh? Proper lush this year. Reminds me a bit of a summer we had in Devon, years back. Remember that, Tom? Driving down those narrow lanes, dodging tractors… a right adventure, it was. Though, you could barely see a thing with the hedges. Vaguely. Devon was…intense, wasn't it? The navigation alone was a trial. I'm still convinced I aged five years trying to find that tiny village pub you were so keen on. Seems a world away from here, doesn’t it? All this… urban green. It does. And speaking of the world away, those Chinese guests I mentioned last week… they were quite taken with this park. Said it reminded them of some of the landscaped gardens you find around Beijing. Though, obviously, no pandas here. Pandas! Always a winner with the Chinese visitors. Makes me think about my last trip to Chengdu. The sheer scale of the panda breeding centre... astonishing. And the wildlife outside of the cities, too. I remember hiking through some forests in Sichuan - saw bears, proper brown bears, not the little black ones they have in some zoos. Crikey! Bears? Didn’t expect that. Makes you think, doesn’t it? We’re so used to seeing everything neatly contained, ‘zoos’ and ‘nature reserves’. But over there, it’s all…wilder. Saw a little boy over there trying to catch a pigeon. Rather charming, really. Kids are the same everywhere, aren't they? Always chasing pigeons. Speaking of chasing… I had a bit of a run-in with a ‘chugger’ on the way here. One of those aggressively friendly charity people. Trying to get me to sign up for something I absolutely don't need. The worst, aren't they? Just relentless. Better than eBay though, I wouldn't trust those chaps. At least with a charity, you sort of know where the money is going. Though, even that can be dubious sometimes. I've been so busy with my thesis supervision lately… it’s just a constant back and forth. Professor Davies is proving to be a bit… particular this term. Oh dear. Davies again? He's always been a bit of a stickler. What’s he nitpicking about now? The structure, mostly. Says it lacks ‘narrative cohesion’. I'm trying to explain it's a complex analysis of linguistic drift in regional dialects, not a blooming novel!

Right, so remind me again  why  I’m crammed in the passenger seat of a ridiculously posh motor, five hours from anywhere vaguely resembling civilisation? My back’s killin' me, honestly. You're crammed in a ridiculously posh motor because you agreed to help me test the new solar panel prototype, remember? It needs real-world conditions, and the Lake District ticks all the boxes: variable weather, decent sunlight potential, and… dramatic scenery. Aye, I remember  you  twisting my arm. Real-world conditions, he says. Sounds an awful lot like free labour to me. And "decent sunlight potential"? It's chucking it down with rain, Liam! I can barely see the road. Progress relies on testing in less-than-ideal circumstances, Elara. Besides, the rain is useful data. And I brought your favourite scones. Chocolate orange ones. Did you now? Chocolate orange, you say? Alright, alright, you’ve bribed me. So, this solar panel… what’s so special about it then? You've been rabbiting on about it for weeks. It’s not just a bigger version of the ones they put on garden sheds, is it? Because that wouldn’t merit a five-hour trip. No, it's significantly different. It incorporates a new type of perovskite material that allows for significantly higher efficiency in low-light conditions. The main issue with existing solar technology is it drops off dramatically when it's cloudy. This… this aims to change that. The initial simulations were incredible, but simulations are simulations. I need to see how it performs in a genuine, unpredictable environment. Perovskite, right. Sounds fancy. So, what exactly am I supposed to be  doing  while you’re fiddling with wires and taking measurements? You didn’t exactly put it in the brief. I thought my job was to provide moral support and complain about the driving. You're very good at the latter. But seriously, I need you to record observational data. Things like cloud cover, visibility, temperature, and… gut feeling. I know it sounds odd, but your intuition is surprisingly accurate. Just note down how the landscape  feels  during certain weather conditions. Anything you think might influence the panel’s performance. Plus, you can keep an eye on the data log to make sure everything's correlating. My gut feeling influencing solar panel performance? You're having a laugh, aren’t you? You know I’m a data  administrator , Liam, not some mystical weather diviner.

Cor, this chilli is reet good, ANON. Proper warming, this is. Needed it, I did. Been feeling a bit peaky all week, I have. Glad you like it, Beth. Yeah, you did look a bit washed out at the pub the other day. What’s been going on? Just a cold? It’s been a tricky week for everyone, hasn’t it? I’ve had that dodgy stomach thing swirling around, feels like I’ve been living on plain toast. ANON, you've been a lifesaver tonight, a proper comfort. Not the best timing, though, with the project deadline looming… Aye, it's more than a cold, I think. Got a right achey back, and feelin' properly drained. Mum keeps saying it’s "wear and tear" from lugging around all those exhibition stands, but I reckon it’s just me runnin' myself ragged. Conference season's a killer, innit? Wear and tear? Blimey, sounds rough. You do work ridiculous hours, Beth. Should be taking more breaks. Maybe see a doctor? I know, I know. I'm puttin' it off. Doctors are a nightmare to get hold of. And, to be honest, I’m a bit worried it’s something proper. It's that panickin’ feeling, you know? I totally get it. It's tempting to just keep ploughing on. But honestly, Beth, you're no good to anyone when you're running on fumes. I had something similar last year – kept pushing through, ended up with a full-blown migraine that lasted three days. Lessons learned, right? And ANON’s right, see a doctor. Speaking of pushing through, things are a bit mental at work. Mr. Davies is constantly on my back about the building schedule. He wants everything finished yesterday. It's a bit stressful, to be honest. Least I'm gettin' paid to potter around, I suppose. Potter around? You're doing heavy lifting and construction, Liam! Don't downplay it. It's vital work. Just try and find some downtime, even if it’s just a walk in the park. Honestly, stress hormones are brutal. Have you spoken to his wife about it? Maybe she'll give him a talking-to. That'd be somethin’, wouldn't it? Liam gettin’ a telling-off from Mr. Davies’ wife! Anyway, back to my woes... It’s been a bit rough on the relationship front too, if I’m being honest.

Honestly, I need a holiday. Like, a very long holiday. Preferably somewhere with sunshine and absolutely no spreadsheets. Rough day at the project factory, then? You sound like you’ve wrestled a badger. Worse. It was Gareth. Gareth from accounts. He’s decided he’s an expert on risk mitigation. Risk mitigation! On a project about improving the office coffee machine. The sheer audacity. Gareth? Really? He looks like he’d struggle to mitigate a paperclip jam. What was the issue? Apparently, the new coffee beans might present a “potential choking hazard” to employees. And the increased caffeine intake could lead to “unforeseen productivity fluctuations.” I kid you not. He presented a ten-page risk assessment. Ten pages! For coffee. Oh, bless his cotton socks. You’ve got to be kidding me. Honestly, some people just thrive on making things complicated. Does Mr. Gareth know he’s making himself incredibly unpopular? He seems blissfully unaware. He kept saying things like, "We need to consider all variables," and, "Due diligence is paramount." I nearly screamed. I just bit my tongue and said, "Gareth, it’s coffee. People are pretty good at avoiding choking on coffee." You handled that brilliantly. I would have just walked out. So, besides Gareth’s existential dread surrounding coffee, anything else happen? Ugh, yes. Sarah from marketing is leaving. Apparently, she’s taking a job in Bristol, working for some tech startup. Said she couldn't handle the corporate culture any longer. Oh no! Sarah? I liked Sarah. She always had the best stories about disastrous company events. What about Mark? He seemed quite fond of her. Mark’s devastated. He’s been… well, they've been a bit of a thing for months. Quietly, you know? Shared coffees at lunch, lingering glances in the meeting room. Apparently, she dumped him via email yesterday. Said she needed "emotional space" and that he was "a lovely person, but not quite what she was looking for professionally.” The email was three paragraphs long. Three paragraphs? That’s brutal! Poor Mark. He looked so smitten. Did he say anything? He's in full denial mode. He keeps saying things like, “She'll be back” and "It's just a phase." He even sent her a giant box of chocolates today. It's pitiful, honestly. And slightly embarrassing for the rest of us. Oh, Mark. He’s a good guy, really. He just needs a serious reality check.

Right, so, little ones, are you two still wrestling with this 'good versus evil' thing? It’s a bit more complicated than the stories sometimes make out, isn't it? But Miss Willow said in school that evil is  always  wrong, Mum. Like, even if you accidentally squish a ladybug, that's a tiny bit evil! But what about when you have to step on a spider? Daddy says spiders eat flies, and flies are nasty. Is Daddy doing evil then? Oh, you two are a handful! No, sweetheart, stepping on a spider to stop it from causing trouble isn't evil. It's...problem solving. Sometimes, things that seem bad – flies, for example – need to be dealt with. Evil, properly evil, is when someone  chooses  to hurt others for no good reason, to be mean just for the sake of it. It’s about greed and power, not just…getting rid of a spider. So, trolls aren’t always evil? Remember the one in the book we read? He was mean, but he liked shiny buttons. Exactly! That troll was grumpy and he liked taking things, which isn't very nice. But he wasn't inherently evil, was he? He might just have needed a friend, or a good talking to, or perhaps a very large collection of shiny buttons! That's why so many folk tales are wonderful, isn’t it? They show us that people, and even creatures, can be complicated. Think of the Green Knight in Arthurian legend. He seemed fearsome, but he was testing Arthur's bravery and honor, right? Like Robin Hood! He stole from the rich! Is  that  evil? Now that’s a good question. Robin Hood broke the law, yes. But he did it to help the poor and the oppressed. The people who were  really  doing evil were the greedy lords and barons who were squeezing everyone dry. So sometimes, breaking rules can be the  right  thing to do, even if it looks a little bit wrong. It’s about  why  you're doing something, not just  what  you're doing. So, like, if I take one of Leo’s toys to play with, that's wrong, but if I borrow it and give it back, that's okay? Precisely! Borrowing with permission is good manners, darling. Taking something without asking is…less than ideal. It's about respect and consideration. That's a form of goodness, isn’t it?

Right, so Anon’s school trip… filming a documentary about the local wildlife reserve, isn't it? Sounds… ambitious for Year 4. It does, doesn’t it? But she’s really excited, bless her. They're going tomorrow, and they’ve been learning about camera angles and sound recording all week. Mr. Davies is making a big thing of it. Wildlife! Lions! Elephants! Lions and elephants in Cambridgeshire, are they? Doubt you'll find many badgers behaving like a pride of lions, love. Still, good for her imagination. How’s her leg today? It looked a bit dodgy yesterday. It's still a bit stiff, actually. She says it hurts when she walks a lot. I’ve given her some ibuprofen, but I’m keeping an eye on it. I told the school to let me know immediately if it gets worse. I don’t want her hobbling around a nature reserve trying to film a kingfisher. Ouchie! Poor little thing. Proper nuisance, that. Always falling over. Remember that time he tried to climb the apple tree and ended up dangling by his shirt? Oh, goodness, how could I forget? Nearly gave me a heart attack. Right, well, the weather forecast is looking alright for tomorrow. Not scorching, but not chilly either. It’s been surprisingly warm at night, hasn’t it? I had to swap out the duvet for a sheet last night. Thought it would be freezing. I know! I was expecting to have to layer up, but I was practically sweating. It’s all a bit unpredictable, this weather. Speaking of unpredictable... I'm going to the gym after work today. Need to try and burn off some of this stress. They've got that new treadmill with the incline settings. Fancy trying it? Oh, I don’t know. Running on a machine just… doesn’t appeal. I prefer the elliptical. Less impact, you know? It’s kinder on my joints. Fair enough. You're the teacher, you've got more stamina than me. I’ll probably end up collapsing halfway through. I was thinking of rewarding myself with a doughnut afterwards. A doughnut? You’re trying to  burn  calories, not replace them! Don’t tell me you’re advocating a life of deprivation? One doughnut won’t hurt. Besides, I promise to do an extra ten minutes on the treadmill. Doughnut! Doughnut! Okay, okay, one doughnut. But a small one.

Honestly, Bernard, this rain. It’s been relentless this week. Makes you feel a bit…damp in the soul, doesn’t it? Damp in the soul, Arthur? You always were a poet, weren't you? It’s just rain. Good for the garden, though. Though at my age, getting down to tend it properly... that’s another matter entirely. My knees are playing up again, you know. Ah, the knees. A universal ailment for the over-sixty, it seems. I've been doing a bit of Tai Chi, actually. The doctor suggested it. Ridiculous, I thought at first, all that slow-motion waving about. But it's actually quite soothing. Helps with the back, too, which is even more troublesome. Tai Chi, eh? Never fancied it myself. Too much like interpretive dance for my liking! I’m sticking to paracetamol. And a bit of stubbornness, if I’m honest. Still got the shop to run, you know. Not exactly conducive to a relaxing life. Speaking of which, how’s the business doing? I read somewhere that independent shops are struggling terribly. Especially with all this online nonsense. It's a battle, Arthur. A constant battle. People just want the convenience, don't they? Click, click, bang, delivery. Can't compete with that. I’ve been thinking of diversifying, actually. Maybe add a few online offerings. But wrestling with websites and social media… it’s not exactly my forte. I understand. Technology has leapt forward with a frightening pace. My daughter’s constantly trying to explain things to me. "Dad, you need to engage with your audience!" Engage with my audience of retired pensioners, she means. Exactly! My daughter's the same. Always suggesting I get on TikTok or whatever it is the youngsters are doing. Though, she's also been asking about supporting the Green Party. Said they're gaining traction. The Green Party. They’ve certainly been making some noise. I’m not entirely convinced with their economic policies, mind you. Seems a bit... idealistic. But the climate crisis is undeniably the biggest issue we face. The urgency is frightening. I agree. Something has to be done. Though, idealistic or not, I'm leaning towards giving them a look. Voting Conservative all my life, and look where it's got us. A fair point. Have you been to any of those boot sales lately? Agnes found a rather lovely teapot at one last weekend.

Honestly, Liam, I still can’t get over it. Forty million quid? Just…gone? With all that talk about sustainable investing, too. It’s ridiculous. I know, Anna. It’s shocking. The Rugby Pension Fund, wasn't it? It’s just... another example of people in positions of power thinking the rules don’t apply to them. Though, to be fair, there are probably hoops they jumped through to make it appear legal. Legal doesn’t equal ethical, love. Legal doesn't mean it’s right. And it’s not like they’re starving in the streets, are they? They’re just greedy. It makes me properly angry. Makes you wonder where all our pensions are actually going. Remember Nan saying she was worried about the state pension? Always looming, isn't it? The whole thing feels intrinsically unstable. Though, the markets are volatile anyway. You can’t expect guaranteed returns. You know, I was reading this paper the other day, about how modular construction could revolutionize affordable housing… Oh, here we go with the PhD brain again! Affordable housing and revolutionary construction whilst people are losing their life savings. Priorities, Liam! Priorities! Though, seriously, tell me about the modular stuff. Sounds interesting. I need a distraction from the financial apocalypse. Alright, alright. It’s basically pre-fabricated modules, built in a factory and assembled on site. Saves time, reduces waste, potentially lowers costs… I'm looking at using 3D-printed components too, integrated within the modules. Could be a game-changer. But it needs serious investment, obviously. See? That’s what’s missing, isn't it? Investment in genuinely useful things, rather than lining pockets. Speaking of useful things, have you seen those new wide-leg trousers everyone’s wearing? I reckon I could pull them off. Wide-leg trousers? Are you serious? They remind me of the 70s. Absolutely not. Stick with your tailored cuts, you look brilliant in them. Plus, they’re far more practical. You're always tripping over things. I do not! And they're coming back around, Liam. Fashion always does! Besides, I’m thinking of getting one of those oversized, vintage blazers. You know, with the padded shoulders. Padded shoulders? Oh, for the love of... You're going full 80s on me, aren't you? It'll clash with your Sunderland accent. My accent is  charming , not clashing! And it'll be ironic, see?

Honestly, this wallpaper hasn't changed since I was a child. Still got those little ducks swimming through the reeds, doesn't it? Mum really is devoted to her aesthetic. It’s… striking. A dedication to a very particular shade of beige. So, you said today's lecture on Romanticism went well? You seemed a bit flustered when you mentioned it earlier. It did, actually, but I had a student ask the most ridiculous question. He was genuinely convinced that Wordsworth's daffodils were referencing illegal rave culture. Apparently, the 'host of golden daffodils' represented strobe lights. No! Seriously? That's brilliant, though. In a spectacularly misguided way. It shows they’re engaging, even if their interpretation is... creative. Exactly! It’s like, where did  that  even come from? I had to gently steer him back towards the pastoral poetry stuff. Though, I did briefly entertain the idea of writing an essay on Wordsworth as a proto-rave progenitor. Do it! Imagine the paper – "The Linguistic Landscape of Ecstasy: Wordsworth and the Birth of the Beat.” You’d clean up. Speaking of unconventional interpretations, I was watching that documentary about orcas last night. Absolutely breathtaking. Did you know they have their own dialects, passed down through generations? Really? Like little whale families with their own slang? That’s incredible. I’ve been meaning to look into that. It makes you think about how much communication is learned, not innate. Which, ironically, is what I was hammering home about Romantic poets today - their deliberate reclamation of language against the suffocating formality of the previous century. It’s all connected, isn’t it? And speaking of reclaiming… I was thinking about that article I read about the resurgence of squatting in London. Apparently, there’s this brilliant collective taking over abandoned buildings and turning them into art spaces. Bold. And risky. My Dad would have a heart attack if he knew I even entertained the idea when I was at university. Remember those conversations we had? "Property is sacred, Eleanor! You can’t just  take  someone’s building!" I remember. He was very passionate about adhering to the rules. But there's something undeniably compelling about using abandoned spaces for something positive. Giving them a new life. It feels… right, somehow. Though, I understand the legal complexities. It's complicated. Speaking of things that feel right, did you see that new series on Channel 4?

This Ceylon’s a bit weak, isn't it, love? Reminds me of that stuff they served at the Costessey Institute back in '68. Never could stomach it properly. Though, to be fair, not much at the Institute was worth stomachin’. You're always complaining about the tea, Arthur. It’s perfectly fine! You’ve got a face like a bulldog chewing a wasp, as always. Remember your mum’s tea? Strong enough to weld iron, that was. She’d tell you it’d cure what ails ya, even if what ails ya was just boredom. My nan used to put a dash of Worcestershire sauce in hers. Said it gave it a certain… je ne sais quoi. Bit bizarre now I think about it. Anyway, talking of bizarre, did you see that documentary on the new hostel down the road? They’re having all sorts of problems managing the… clientele. Apparently, one lad tried to rewire the light fittings himself. Rewire the light fittings? Good heavens. What were they thinkin', lettin' someone like that near a toolbox? Back in my day, a chap wouldn't dream of touchin’ electrics without proper training. Although, most lads back then were far too busy labouring, weren’t they? Hard work, that was. Honestly, my dad, he and his brother, they slogged away in their butcher's shop day in, day out. Seven days a week. Nearly killed them both, it did. My Harold was the same. Worked at the abattoir for years. Never complained, mind you. Said it was honest work. The smell, though… goodness. I could smell it on him even after he’d showered. Still, they earned an honest living, they did. Far better than sitting around all day, wouldn't you say? Definitely. And the dedication. My dad, a teacher, wouldn’t have had it any other way. He always said, shaping young minds was the most important job in the world. Though, dealing with some of those teenagers... even  I  find it a challenge! I saw some of the engineering projects they were doing though last term. Incredible stuff, really. One girl built a miniature wind turbine. Absolutely brilliant! Engineering, eh? Now that’s somethin’. Always fascinated me. Never had the knack, mind you. All those sums and calculations… gave me a headache just thinkin' about it. They used to have these fellas in Costessey, workin’ on tractors, on combine harvesters...

Honestly, David, I'm feeling quite disheartened this afternoon. This lecturer's course – you know, the one on academic literacy for new lecturers – is… well, the baseline isn't where it should be. I marked a good chunk of papers today, and a surprising number struggle with even basic paragraph construction. It’s not a lack of intelligence, I don't think, but a serious gap in their academic writing skills. Righto. Yeah, I've heard rumblings about that course. It's a bit ambitious, expecting everyone to hit the ground running with scholarly prose, isn't it? What kind of issues are you seeing specifically? Beyond the paragraphing, I mean. Oh, the usual suspects, really. A reliance on very informal language, a tendency to just  tell  rather than  show  their arguments, inconsistent referencing, and a shocking amount of passive voice. One paper read like a blog post, frankly. It was… exasperating. I mean, they’re meant to  teach  higher education students! Harsh, but fair, I reckon. It's funny, isn't it? We expect academics to be masters of their subject, but rarely do we equip them with the tools to communicate that expertise effectively in written form. It's like assuming everyone who can do the mathematics can teach it. Precisely! And what’s even more frustrating is that many of them seem to think a thesaurus is a magic wand. Throw in a load of fancy words, and suddenly you're sophisticated, apparently. It completely obscures the meaning. It reminds me rather of my own early days teaching… Oh, go on then! Spill the beans. Early days teaching? You were a teacher right out of uni? Not quite. Before I went back to postgraduate study and then into teaching here, I actually spent a significant amount of time in recruitment. It’s a world away, I know. Recruitment? Seriously? That's… unexpected. What were you recruiting for? Tech startups? Investment bankers? Initially, it was office jobs, you know, PA's, receptionists, that kind of thing. But then I moved into executive search – finding senior people for larger organisations. And that's where things got interesting. I was essentially selling people. Crafting compelling narratives, highlighting their strengths, downplaying their weaknesses. It was all about persuasion, really. Wow. So, you were basically writing mini-biographies to convince hiring managers? That’s a skill. A very transferable skill, actually. You'd be surprised how much of that translates!

Right, I’m officially brain-fried. Thermodynamics is trying to destroy me. Anyone else feelin’ the same? Nah, I’m alright. Just… lurking. Trying to look busy, ya know? Sales assistant life doesn’t exactly require intense mental gymnastics. What you studying? Engineering. So, plenty of intense mental gymnastics then. I'm Gemma, by the way. Bradford born and bred. Can’t escape the accent, sadly. Gemma! Nice to meet you. I’m Chloe. From Bolton, so a slightly less bleak landscape, apparently. Engineering, wow, that's intense. I'm doing Literature – so, basically, staring at words all day until they make sense. Hi everyone! I’m Priya. It’s lovely to meet you all too. I'm studying Computer Science, which, in its own way, is just as baffling as engineering sometimes, I think. So, Bolton's nice, Chloe? Less… industrial than Manchester? Yeah, it’s alright. Pretty quiet, mostly. I'm Liam, by the way. And Priya, Computer Science? Sounds mental. I can barely work the coffee machine at work, let alone code something. Don’t worry, Liam, most of us feel that way. Priya, is it difficult? I have a cousin doing something similar. She’s always talking about algorithms and… other things I don’t understand. It can be challenging, definitely! But it’s also really rewarding when you finally crack a problem. Like solving a really complicated puzzle. And the algorithms are just… logic, really. Once you get the hang of it. Whereabouts in Bradford are you from, Gemma? It’s a big place. Tong, near the cemetery. Not the  most  glamorous of addresses, I’ll admit. But I know every chip shop within a five-mile radius, so that’s a skill, right? It's got its perks. I always thought people from Yorkshire were incredibly witty. Is that a stereotype? Possibly. But it's a well-deserved stereotype. We have to find entertainment somehow, living so far from the sea. Being sarcastic is a national pastime. True that! My nan is a master of the cutting remark. She could deflate a balloon with a single sentence. My mum’s like that too! Indian mums have a special power to critique everything. Even when you’re doing something right. "You’re smiling too much, what are you hiding?" That's a classic. Oh my god, yes! My mum does the same! "Why are you eating so quickly?

Honestly, this hummus is banging. Proper good. You didn’t skimp on the garlic, did ya, ANON? My mam would love this. She's always moaning about having to make everything from scratch. Glad you like it, Maisie. ANON's a wizard in the kitchen, as always. I’m just wondering... you were saying earlier about your cousin joining the army? That’s quite a shift for him, isn’t it? He was always obsessed with coding, right? Aye, proper shift. He was a whizz with computers, our Liam. Building his own rigs, learnin' Python before he even got his GCSEs. Said he wanted to be a software engineer, make games or summat. Then, just…bam. Said the army offered more structure, more purpose. I dunno, love. Feels a bit… random. I get that. It’s not a decision people take lightly. My uncle joined up after his degree, initially thinking it would be a good career path. Said the training was intense and the benefits were decent. Though he ended up leaving after a few years, said it wasn't for him. What branch is Liam joining? Signals corps, apparently. Which is a bit better, innit? At least he'll be using his brain a bit. They said they need people with his skillset. Still, missin' him though. He’s meant to be at training in Aldershot next month. It's miles away. Aldershot’s rough. But Signals is definitely a good placement if he’s got a head for computers. Speaking of things miles away, did you ever find that vintage ‘Girl’s Own’ magazine I was asking about? The one with the proper adventurous heroines? Don’t remind me! I’ve been scouring eBay for a week. Proper rabbit warren, that site. Found loads of old tat, but nothing like what you’re after. There was one with a lady climbing Kilimanjaro in bloomers though – that was a right laugh. Oh, you’re terrible! I’m looking for something a bit more inspiring, honestly. Like action heroines, explorers, not… bloomers. I want to show my little niece those women were doing amazing things. It's important to counteract all the Disney princess narratives, y'know? Aye, I see yer point. Right enough. Hey, have you seen 'Dune: Part Two'? I’m proper chuffed to go. All those spaceships and giant worms... It looks brilliant. I have! It was incredible.

Honestly, Liam was just…  so . He kept talking about his crypto portfolio. Like, I get it, you're doing well, but do I really need a fifteen-minute lecture on blockchain while I'm trying to enjoy my chips? Sounds about right for Liam. Typical Londoner, eh? Always gotta show off. You'd think someone who grew up with a silver spoon would learn some manners. Remember that time he tried to convince my Nan that Yorkshire pudding wasn’t a proper dessert? Oh, don’t remind me! That was brutal. My gran nearly had a fit. She launched into a twenty-minute monologue about the history of Yorkshire pudding and how it’s absolutely, unequivocally, the pinnacle of British cuisine. Liam just looked increasingly bewildered. Exactly! It's that sense of superiority, isn't it? Like, just because you live in a trendy flat in Shoreditch, you're automatically better than everyone else. I’m starting to feel like an anthropologist studying a foreign species. Don’t even get me started on the politics these London types spout. "Oh, we need to nationalize this, privatize that..." Honestly, it’s all so detached. They've never worried about a paycheck in their lives. It's easy to throw around big ideas when you’re shielded from the consequences. Though, to be fair, the current government  is  a mess. I mean, have you seen the latest poll numbers? It's terrifying. I'm genuinely worried about what the next few years are going to look like. Tell me about it. And the cost of living... it's insane. How are people even managing? My student loan payments alone are crippling. I'm seriously considering moving back in with my parents for a bit, just to save up. You and me both. My mum keeps hinting that I should come home. Says she misses my cooking. Which, fair enough, I’m pretty decent. But I'm not ready to give up on Leeds just yet. Although… I was thinking about applying for that short film grant. They're specifically looking for projects focusing on the impact of austerity on Northern communities. That’s brilliant, Rhys! You should definitely do it. It’s such a crucial story to tell. And you’re the best person to tell it. Absolutely. You'd be amazing. It would be really powerful. Anything that gets a bit of light shone on what’s actually happening outside of the London bubble is vital.

So, what do you reckon, Dad? Bit different from your flat in London, eh? Hopefully, you both like it. Feels a bit smaller now you're actually  in  it, doesn't it, love? It's lovely, honestly! So bright and airy. And I love all the plants, Anon. You’ve really made it your own. It's much nicer than the photos suggested. Much more... lived-in, you know? Not sterile. Well, it’s… cosy. Bit cramped, perhaps. Don't get me wrong, it's clean. And that's good. London flats are often a disgrace. Though I’m wondering where you keep your… your… stuff? Everything's so... curated. He's just being a typical Londoner, dear. Always needing more space. Remember when your stairs were practically a fire hazard from all his piles of newspapers? Oh, don't remind me, Mum! It was a hazard alright. Anyway, Dad, I've made a pot of tea. Cream tea, naturally. We had a proper debate about the pronunciation of ‘scone’ the other day - apparently, it’s ‘scon’ in Kent! It is! It's how my Nan always said it. Honestly, it's scandalous to say 'skown'! It sounds…posh. ‘Scon’? Sounds barbaric, it does. Like something a pirate would utter. It’s clearly ‘skown’. It’s etymology, young lady. Right, let’s not start a war over scones. Mum, you okay? You seem a little quiet. Just thinking, dear. This visit has given me a bit of a jolt. It’s hard to believe my little Anon is all grown up, got a Master's degree, and teaching English. You've done amazingly well, love. Reminds me, I need to get around to cleaning the windows. They’re a bit streaky in the bathroom. I can do them, Mum! Really. You shouldn’t be stretching yourself. Care assistant work is tiring enough. Speaking of tiring, have you two been keeping an eye on your cholesterol? All this tea and… what are those things on the counter? Nuts? You should watch those. I read an article about the link between walnuts and diverticulitis the other day. Dreadful stuff, diverticulitis. Dad, you and your articles! Everything gives you diverticulitis! Relax, have a scone. And yes, we’re trying to eat reasonably well. Though these spices Anon bought are tempting. He's gone mad for saffron recently. Costs a fortune, you know? Don't tell him that, Dad!

Honestly, Liam, this internet's dreadful. I’ve been trying to upload a chunk of data to the corpus all morning, and it’s just crawling. Makes me want to chuck the laptop out the window, it does. Sunderland’s broadband was faster, and that’s saying something! Cambridge? Slow internet? That’s rich, coming from you. I thought this was a tech hub. Must be a dodgy connection at the cafe. Though, you're right, even back home in Pembury, we were battling with Virgin Media sometimes. It’s a national crisis, isn't it? Aye, a national disgrace! I've got all these linguists relying on me, needing their data, and I'm sat here looking like a fool. It's the pressure, see? They expect it to just  be  there, ready to go, and when it's not…well, you can imagine. Did you finish that report for Balfour Beatty then? Sounds a right headache. Nearly. Got the structural integrity analysis done, just needs a final sign-off from Mr. Harding. He’s being particularly pedantic this week. Apparently, a 0.001% margin of error is “unacceptable.” Honestly, some days I think I could build a bridge with Lego and it would meet his standards. It's good work though, building a new pedestrian bridge over the River Cam. Bit ironically scenic, really, considering the housing crisis. Don't even get me started on the housing! I was looking at some flats near the city centre – just a tiny one-bed – and they’re asking for upwards of £600,000! You’d need a trust fund to live anywhere decent around here. It's pure madness. My mam keeps saying I should just move back to Sunderland, but I need to be near the university and the resources for the corpus. It's ridiculous, isn't it? My dad's constantly complaining about it. He says he remembers when you could buy a decent house in Pembury for under £100,000. Now? Forget about it. We are seriously considering investing in a place further out, maybe somewhere in Norfolk. More space, a bit quieter, slightly cheaper. Norfolk, eh? That's a fair trek. Though, you’d need a car, wouldn’t you? Public transport out there isn’t exactly brilliant. Speaking of trekking, how was your run this morning? You were looking particularly fit on Instagram. It was brutal, actually.

Honestly, this week at the ward has been something else. Absolutely relentless.
